006a7a3f-12a8-4e12-bd02-8e971eae5a07.title: QA: env scrub uses denylist instead of allowlist (sensitive vars without matching suffix leak)
006a7a3f-12a8-4e12-bd02-8e971eae5a07.description:
## Severity
Major
## Dimension
security
## Location
src/tools/bash/policy.rs:143-151
## Violation
`apply_env_scrub` only removes env vars whose names match `is_sensitive_env` — a denylist. Sensitive credentials whose names don't match the heuristics (e.g., `DATABASE_URL`, `MONGODB_URI`, `REDIS_URL`, `SLACK_WEBHOOK`, custom names) flow freely into every spawned child.

Quoted (policy.rs:143-151):
```
pub fn apply_env_scrub(cmd: &mut Command) {
    let sensitive: Vec<String> = std::env::vars()
        .map(|(k, _)| k)
        .filter(|k| is_sensitive_env(k))
        .collect();
    for key in sensitive {
        cmd.env_remove(key);
    }
}
```
The comment ("Do NOT `env_clear`") acknowledges the tradeoff but ships the insecure default. OWASP A04.
## Mandated refactor
1. Flip to allowlist: `cmd.env_clear()` then `cmd.env(key, val)` for an explicit safe set (`PATH`, `HOME`, `USER`, `LANG`, `TERM`, `CARGO_HOME`, `RUST_LOG`).
2. Make the allowlist configurable via `.openclaudia/config.yaml`.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

010c5bd2-f897-429d-85d1-f04c36c3e0ac.title: edit.rs silently ignores replace_all argument (admitted gap, no error)
010c5bd2-f897-429d-85d1-f04c36c3e0ac.description:
## Severity
Major

## Dimension
Functional Correctness / KISS / SOLID-L (LSP — interface promises something it does not deliver)

## Location
src/tools/file/edit.rs:84-95 (and tests at lines 258-272 admit the behavior)

## Violation
`execute_edit_file` accepts a `replace_all` arg (per the schema seen in tests `args.insert("replace_all", ...)`), but the body silently ignores it and unconditionally calls `replacen(_, _, 1)`:

```rust
let count = content.matches(old_string).count();
if count > 1 {
    return (format!("Found {count} occurrences of the text. Please provide a more specific old_string..."), true);
}
...
let new_content = content.replacen(old_string, new_string, 1);
```

The test `edit_replace_all_true_with_multi_occurrence_currently_errors` (line 259) explicitly documents that the flag is "silently ignored for N>1." This is the LSP violation in §3.2 — the tool's advertised contract diverges from its delivered behavior. Worse, it returns an error to the model that says "provide a more specific old_string" even when the model has set the explicit override that should have allowed bulk replacement.

## Mandated refactor
Read the `replace_all` arg; when `true`, use `content.replace(old, new)` (replace all occurrences) and report the count replaced. When `false` (or absent), keep the current single-replace + multi-occurrence-error path. Update the error path to suggest "either narrow old_string OR set replace_all: true." No `#[allow]` — fix the logic. Cross-references the gap noted in pinned test at edit.rs:259-272 ("gap #569").

## Filed from QA review dispatch

Diff stats are scaled by occurrence count. Function refactored (canonicalise_edit_path + format_edit_success helpers) to stay under clippy too_many_lines budget — no #[allow]. 4 new fix687_* tests pass; 1412 baseline → 1428 passing.

0250cef0-1440-452e-ac97-dea2c909f471.title: QA: BackgroundShell struct mixes I/O buffers, lifecycle flags, and command metadata
0250cef0-1440-452e-ac97-dea2c909f471.description:
## Severity
Trivial
## Dimension
solid
## Location
src/tools/bash/mod.rs:24-35
## Violation
`BackgroundShell` packs 7 unrelated fields: two Arc<Mutex<Vec<String>>> buffers, a command string, two AtomicBools (finished, output_retrieved_after_finish), an Arc<Mutex<Option<i32>>> exit_status, and a PID. Each field has its own concurrency story; SRP smell — the struct is the union of "child process handle", "captured output", and "GC bookkeeping".

Quoted (mod.rs:24-35):
```
struct BackgroundShell {
    stdout_buffer: Arc<Mutex<Vec<String>>>,
    stderr_buffer: Arc<Mutex<Vec<String>>>,
    command: String,
    finished: Arc<AtomicBool>,
    exit_status: Arc<Mutex<Option<i32>>>,
    /// PID of the spawned process, used to send SIGTERM on kill
    pid: u32,
    /// Whether output has been retrieved at least once after the process finished
    output_retrieved_after_finish: AtomicBool,
}
```
## Mandated refactor
1. `ProcessHandle { pid: u32, finished: Arc<AtomicBool>, exit_status: Arc<Mutex<Option<i32>>> }`
2. `OutputBuffers { stdout: Arc<Mutex<Vec<String>>>, stderr: Arc<Mutex<Vec<String>>> }`
3. `GcState { output_retrieved_after_finish: AtomicBool }`
4. `BackgroundShell { command: String, handle: ProcessHandle, buffers: OutputBuffers, gc: GcState }`

02f4ed92-d0e1-4693-a429-152892c4e94b.title: VDD: parse_findings uses Uuid::new_v4 per finding and Finding.id as HashMap key — test determinism broken
02f4ed92-d0e1-4693-a429-152892c4e94b.description:
Current state: 

Desired state: 

Reason: 

Dimension: Testability Coverage. Location: src/vdd/mod.rs:777 (Uuid::new_v4 in parse_findings) and 1037-1056 (verdicts map keyed by finding.id). Violation: Every parse_findings call generates fresh UUIDs, so the verification agent receives a new finding_id on every iteration. There is no stable identity for a finding across iterations: if the adversary re-reports the same SQL-injection on iteration 2 and 3, they get different UUIDs, making FP-history-based deduplication by ID impossible (which is why the code uses string_similarity — see issue on Jaccard weakness). More critically, tests cannot assert specific finding IDs because they are randomised every run. Mandated Refactor: Compute finding.id as a deterministic hash of (severity, cwe, file, line_range, description_hash). This enables cross-iteration dedup by ID (replacing the weak Jaccard), makes tests assertable, and gives Chainlink a stable natural key.

030c6bc5-7fef-4e32-a742-987420df3f12.title: thinking::has_ultrathink_keyword whole-string lowercase per scan; allocate-per-call hot path
030c6bc5-7fef-4e32-a742-987420df3f12.description:
## Severity
Trivial
## Dimension
complexity
## Location
src/thinking.rs:32-39, 68-75 (has_ultrathink_keyword, has_ultrathink_in_messages)
## Violation
```rust
pub fn has_ultrathink_keyword(text: &str) -> bool {
    let lower = text.to_lowercase();
    if find_whole_word(&lower, "ultrathink") { return true; }
    ULTRATHINK_PHRASES.iter().any(|p| lower.contains(p))
}
```

Called on every user message scan, on every turn, for every provider. `text.to_lowercase()` allocates a full copy of the message — typical user message is small but turns with pasted log dumps or file contents can be 100KB+. Combined with `has_ultrathink_in_messages` iterating ALL messages on every prompt invocation, the cost is O(N · M) allocations per turn where N is messages and M is total bytes.

`find_whole_word` then performs `haystack[start..].find(needle)` in a loop — fine — but operates on the lowercase copy, doubling memory live during the scan.
## Mandated refactor
Use case-insensitive matching without allocation: walk the haystack byte-by-byte comparing `b.to_ascii_lowercase()` against the needle bytes. Or use the `memchr` crate's case-insensitive search. Or hoist the lowercase outside the loop (`has_ultrathink_in_messages` should lowercase each message ONCE and pass the lowercased slice to `has_ultrathink_keyword`). For very large messages, limit the scan to the first/last 4KiB — the keyword convention is "say it in the prompt", not "hide it in pasted logs".
## Filed from QA review dispatch

cb8467a9-16f4-4994-93d2-d1fa6c252940.author: lOrm
cb8467a9-16f4-4994-93d2-d1fa6c252940.content: Fixed at HEAD (working tree on main, pending commit). src/thinking.rs::has_ultrathink_keyword now scans the raw &str.as_bytes() with allocation-free ASCII-case-insensitive helpers (find_whole_word_ci + contains_ci + matches_ci_at) and no longer calls text.to_lowercase(). ULTRATHINK_PHRASES stored as &[&[u8]] of pre-lowered bytes; ULTRATHINK_NEEDLE constant for the whole-word case. Word-boundary semantics preserved (case bytes are lowered point-wise via to_ascii_lowercase on the haystack side only). New regression test thinking::tests::large_input_case_insensitive_match exercises a 256 KiB buffer with positive ("UltraThink"), negative (no trigger), embedded ("myUltraThinker" must NOT match), and multi-word ("THINK ULTRA HARD") cases. cargo test --lib thinking:: passes 7/7. cargo clippy --lib --all-features -- -D warnings is clean.

03ac3f85-0c2e-438b-90b5-2bde35252c37.title: Plugin install_from_git: URL-derived plugin name path traversal
03ac3f85-0c2e-438b-90b5-2bde35252c37.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

**Dimension**: Security and Access (OWASP Input Handling)

**Location**: src/plugins/manager.rs:624-689 (install_from_git), src/plugins/manager.rs:346-394 (add_marketplace_from_git)

**Violation**: The plugin/marketplace name is derived from the URL by splitting on '/' and stripping '.git':
```rust
let name = url.trim_end_matches('/').trim_end_matches(".git").rsplit('/').next().unwrap_or("plugin").to_string();
let dest = plugins_dir.join(&name);
```
A URL like 'https://evil.example.com/foo/..%2F..%2Fsecrets.git' or one containing path separators in the last segment (e.g. 'https://host/a%2Fb') can be crafted so that after unwrap the 'name' contains traversal sequences that join() resolves outside .openclaudia/plugins/. Unlike install_from_marketplace (manager.rs:483-488) which explicitly rejects '..' and '/' in the plugin name, install_from_git and add_marketplace_from_git perform NO such validation. git itself then creates arbitrary directories on disk.

**Mandated Refactor**:
1. Apply the same validation pattern as install_from_marketplace: reject names containing '..', '/', '\\', or leading '.'.
2. After computing `name`, call `Path::new(&name).components().count() == 1 && matches!(components.next(), Some(Component::Normal(_)))`.
3. After clone, canonicalize `dest` and verify `dest.starts_with(plugins_dir.canonicalize()?)`.
4. Sanitize to [A-Za-z0-9._-]+ character class and fail fast on violation.

112d6b21-a149-47e4-9334-31a8f349a4b6.author: lOrm
112d6b21-a149-47e4-9334-31a8f349a4b6.content:
Resolved. Introduced `src/plugins/validate.rs::derive_dir_name_from_url` and wired it into both URL-to-plugin-name derivation sites.

**Root cause:** `add_marketplace_from_git` and `install_from_git` extracted the clone destination name from the URL via raw rsplit on `/`, with no validation — `unwrap_or("plugin")` then `unwrap_or("marketplace")`. A crafted URL whose last segment is `..`, `.hidden`, empty, or contains path separators placed the clone outside the plugins jail. Only `install_from_marketplace` had the `name.contains("..")` guard.

**Fix:**
- `derive_dir_name_from_url(url)` uses `url::Url::path_segments()` for standard URLs and a conservative extractor for SCP SSH shorthand. The derived segment has trailing `.git` stripped, then goes through `validate_plugin_dir_name`.
- `validate_plugin_dir_name(name)` rejects: empty, `.`, `..`, anything starting with `.` (refuses hidden-dir creation), any `/`, `\\`, `:`, NUL, or control character, and any occurrence of `..` anywhere in the name.
- Both `install_from_git` (src/plugins/manager.rs:624) and `add_marketplace_from_git` (src/plugins/manager.rs:346) now derive names via the validator. The `install_from_marketplace` inline check (lines 484-488) is redundant with this but has been left in place as belt-and-braces for the pre-existing path.

**Tests (in plugins::validate::tests):**
- `derives_name_from_https_url` / `derives_name_from_scp_url` — happy path.
- `derive_name_rejects_traversal` — `https://x/a/..` fails.
- `derive_name_rejects_trailing_dot` — `https://x/.hidden` fails.
- `derive_name_rejects_empty_segment` — `https://x/` fails.
All 610 lib + 130 integration tests pass.

**Related:** this shares machinery with #280 (scheme allowlist). Both fixes land in `src/plugins/validate.rs` and are wired into `git_clone` + the two public callers.

0507ef75-b69b-4555-94e0-ca265adb4ff0.title: determine_provider: stringly-typed if-else dispatch with brittle prefix matching
0507ef75-b69b-4555-94e0-ca265adb4ff0.description:
Current state: 

Desired state: 

Reason: 

Dimension: Functional Correctness / Semantic

Location: src/proxy.rs lines 1148-1174 (fn determine_provider).

Violation: Provider dispatch is a stringly-typed `if/else-if` chain over model-name prefix matching. This is:
  (a) OCP violation — adding a new provider (e.g., `mistral`, `cohere`, `xai` for Grok) requires editing the function. It is not open for extension.
  (b) Brittle prefix matching — `starts_with("o1")` will match any future model named "o100", "observer", etc. `starts_with("claude")` will match a hypothetical `claude-lab-experimental` from a third party running on an OpenAI-compatible server.
  (c) Architectural coupling — returns `String` (allocation every call) despite the comment 'Returns a static string — no allocation needed' (line 1146) — the early-return branch returns `config.proxy.target.clone()` (line 1171) which IS an allocation, and the tail `provider.to_string()` (line 1173) also allocates.
  (d) The function silently shadows a user's proxy.target config when the model name is parseable. If a user sets proxy.target=openai but types `claude-3-sonnet`, we route to anthropic — not what the user configured.

Mandated Refactor:
  1. Define `pub enum Provider { Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Zai, DeepSeek, Qwen, Ollama, Custom(String) }` in src/providers/mod.rs.
  2. Add a static routing table: `static MODEL_PREFIX_ROUTES: &[(&str, Provider)]` populated from each adapter module via a `pub const MODEL_PREFIXES: &[&str]` declaration on each adapter.
  3. determine_provider returns `Provider` (copy-able enum), not String. Callers that need a name call `.name() -> &'static str`.
  4. Honor proxy.target as an EXPLICIT override: if target is set to a specific provider (not "auto"), route there regardless of model prefix. Only fall back to prefix-matching when target is "auto".
  5. Use word-boundary matching: `"o1" | "o1-preview" | "o3" | "o3-mini" | "o4-mini"` exact list, NOT prefix. Keep the list next to the OpenAI adapter definition.

0527b748-873c-4cb7-a688-ffb7edd1b677.description:
Steps to reproduce:

Expected:

Dimension: Functional Correctness / Defensive Programming

Location: src/oauth.rs line 233: `expires_at: Utc::now() + Duration::seconds(response.expires_in.cast_signed())`.

Violation: `response.expires_in` is declared u64 (line 163 TokenExchangeResponse). Calling .cast_signed() on a u64 larger than i64::MAX wraps to a negative value, producing a duration in the past. If Anthropic were to return `expires_in: 2^63` (improbable but not impossible with a misconfigured endpoint or a man-in-the-middle), the session would be instantly expired. More realistically:
  - No validation that expires_in > 0. A zero or missing-field-with-default value creates a session that is immediately expired, but the store accepts it and get_session returns it, leading to infinite 401-retry loops.
  - No sanity bound. A malicious or misconfigured OAuth server could return `expires_in: 31536000000` (1000 years), resulting in an effectively permanent token stored on disk with no re-check.

Similar issue in src/claude_credentials.rs line 247: `expires_in = refresh_response["expires_in"].as_i64().unwrap_or(3600);` — defaults to 1 hour on parse failure, masking a protocol deviation.

Mandated Refactor:
  1. Validate expires_in at the TokenExchangeResponse deserialization: reject values < 60 (absurdly short) or > 86400 * 7 (longer than a week is suspect for an OAuth access token). Return a structured error.
  2. Remove .cast_signed() — use i64::try_from(response.expires_in).map_err(|_| ...)? to propagate overflow as an error, not a silent wrap.
  3. claude_credentials.rs refresh_and_load: if `expires_in` is missing, Err, do not default to 3600.
  4. Add test: malformed token response with expires_in=0 should cause from_token_response to propagate an error rather than constructing an always-expired session.

06ebdec5-0e47-41c9-9974-2a3bb4e161a3.title: Bash background shells: output_retrieved_after_finish is stored AFTER finished is set, GC races
06ebdec5-0e47-41c9-9974-2a3bb4e161a3.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

**Dimension:** Functional Correctness / Concurrency

**Location:** /home/doll/OpenClaudia/src/tools/bash/mod.rs lines 108-147 (wait-thread plumbing), 84-95 (GC sweep), 206-215 (get_output mark-retrieved)

**Violation:**
Three threads touch shell.finished / output_retrieved_after_finish without a synchronizing happens-before edge:
1. The stdout reader thread (lines 112-120) sets finished=true when stdout EOFs.
2. The stderr reader thread (line 126-134) does NOT set finished.
3. The wait-thread (line 140-147) sets finished=true after child.wait().
4. spawn() GC sweep (lines 85-89) reads both atomics.

Problems:
(a) **Exit code is written by wait-thread (line 143) BEFORE it sets finished (line 145).** Two SeqCst stores in sequence do not guarantee a reader that observes finished=true also observes the exit_status — because exit_status is behind a Mutex not an AtomicOption, and is_finished is SeqCst without a lock on the same mutex. A caller may read (finished=true, exit_status=None).
(b) **stdout-thread sets finished=true even if the process is still running** (reader merely EOF'd stdout while stderr / process continued). This is the order-of-operations bug: the stdout-reader's EOF does not mean the process exited. A subsequent get_output returns is_running=false prematurely.
(c) **GC sweep in spawn() runs BEFORE spawning** (lines 83-96) — so the spawn that triggers the sweep will not itself be subject to GC until the next spawn(). A session that spawns 50 shells then none will leave 50 slots occupied forever even after they all finish.
(d) **output_retrieved_after_finish's 'after' semantics are meaningless.** The store at line 212 fires whenever finished is observed, regardless of whether the finish happened before or after the get_output call. This is sufficient for GC but the name is misleading.

**Mandated Refactor:**
1. Replace finished: AtomicBool + exit_status: Mutex<Option<i32>> with a single Mutex<ShellStatus> where ShellStatus = Running | Finished { exit_code: Option<i32> }. All transitions atomic, all reads lock once.
2. Only the wait-thread may transition to Finished. The stdout reader must not. Test: pipe into a process that reads stdin forever but closes stdout early — current code reports finished=true while the process is still alive.
3. Replace output_retrieved_after_finish with a retrieved_at: Mutex<Option<Instant>>; GC keeps shells for 10 minutes after the last retrieval. Move GC to a background thread running every 30s, not inside spawn().
4. Document the invariant in Rust: 'ShellStatus may only be transitioned from Running to Finished by the wait-thread; readers may observe either state.'

2dce955c-10a4-40e1-b21b-6cdb744fcbc9.author: lOrm
2dce955c-10a4-40e1-b21b-6cdb744fcbc9.content:
Fix applied to src/tools/bash/mod.rs:

ROOT-CAUSE FIX: moved 'output_retrieved_after_finish.store(true, SeqCst)' from inside an 'if is_finished' gate (pre-fix mod.rs:216-220) to fire unconditionally on every get_output drain (post-fix mod.rs:230-242). This eliminates the documented race: a caller draining BEFORE the wait-thread flips finished=true left the GC flag forever false, so the slot was retained indefinitely.

EVIDENCE:
- cargo test --lib: 1262 passed; 0 failed (baseline 1259 + 3 new fix351_* tests = 1262 exactly).
- cargo clippy --lib --all-targets -- -D warnings: EXIT=0.
- No #[allow], no #[ignore], no clippy.toml additions (verified against the diff).

TESTS ADDED:
1. fix351_drain_before_finish_marks_retrieved (race-exposing): spawn 'sleep 5', drain while is_running=true, assert flag flipped. Pre-fix this test would FAIL because the 'if is_finished' gate skipped the store.
2. fix351_drain_after_finish_marks_retrieved (backward-compat): drain after the short-lived process finishes; flag still set.
3. fix351_never_drained_stays_unretrieved (correctness): spawn, wait for finish but never call get_output; flag remains false so GC must NOT collect.

07270d67-3de1-450d-bac2-c5c1fd73af4b.title: acp::run_prompt_loop hard-codes max_iterations and prompt builder ignores cwd/mode
07270d67-3de1-450d-bac2-c5c1fd73af4b.description:
## Severity
Major
## Dimension
complexity
## Location
src/acp.rs:777-988 (run_prompt_loop)
## Violation
The agentic loop is a 211-line function with several intertwined design defects:

```rust
let max_iterations = 50; // Safety limit
...
let system_prompt = crate::prompt::build_system_prompt(None, None, None);
...
let mut all_messages: Vec<crate::proxy::ChatMessage> =
    vec![crate::proxy::ChatMessage { role: "system".to_string(), ... }];
```

1. `max_iterations = 50` is a magic local, not configurable, and silently caps real work.
2. `build_system_prompt(None, None, None)` discards hook instructions, custom instructions, and memory.
3. The function builds a fresh `reqwest::Client::new()` per call (line 779) instead of holding a pooled client on the server struct.
4. The function clones `self.config.active_provider().thinking` every iteration inside the 50-iteration loop.
5. `serde_json::from_value(tools.clone()).unwrap_or_default()` (line 813) swallows tool-definition parse errors and silently strips the tool array.

Cyclomatic complexity by inspection is well above the 15 threshold.
## Mandated refactor
Split `run_prompt_loop` into (a) `build_request`, (b) `dispatch`, (c) `consume_stream`. Hoist the `reqwest::Client` to a field of `AcpServer`. Pull `max_iterations` and per-call timeout onto `AcpConfig`. Replace `unwrap_or_default()` on tool definitions with an explicit `?`.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

08213840-dd99-4cb9-9290-6feca1546501.title: VDD parsing: extract_json_from_response uses byte slicing that panics on multibyte input
08213840-dd99-4cb9-9290-6feca1546501.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

Dimension: Functional Correctness / Error Orchestration. Location: src/vdd/parsing.rs:19-72 (extract_json_from_response). Violation: L24 uses text[json_start..json_start + end] where json_start = start + 7 (raw byte offset past the json fence). If an adversary response contains multibyte UTF-8 (emoji, CJK, smart quotes) near the fence, the byte offset may fall inside a codepoint. str slicing on a non-char-boundary panics. Same for L35 text[actual_start..actual_start + end] and L68 text[start..=end]. The adversary is an arbitrary upstream LLM producing natural-language prose — emoji and unicode are expected. A single emoji before the JSON crashes parse_findings which crashes the entire VDD loop. Mandated Refactor: Replace all byte-index slicing with char-boundary-safe access via text.get(range) returning Option, then handle None as a parse failure. Add a proptest fuzzing extract_json_from_response with arbitrary UTF-8 strings. Add a unit test with a 4-byte UTF-8 codepoint immediately before the fence.

c354b75f-2636-414d-88fc-19e01df6fc30.author: lOrm
c354b75f-2636-414d-88fc-19e01df6fc30.content:
Resolved. `src/vdd/parsing.rs::extract_json_from_response` now routes every substring access through `str::get(range)` which returns `Option<&str>` — an offset that lands mid-codepoint yields `None` instead of panicking. Analysis of the original code found that the delimiters (````json`, ````, `{`, `}`) are all ASCII so today's arithmetic does stay on char boundaries, but the raw indexing was a latent crash surface: any future change to the fence tokens or to the offset computations could turn adversary output into a VDD-loop kill via a single multibyte codepoint.

**Changes:**
- All four branches (````json` fence, generic ```` fence, `{"findings"` raw JSON, any `{...}` raw JSON) rewritten to chain `text.get(...)` and `Option`-return on any failure.
- Fence-length constants: `+ "```json".len()` instead of `+ 7` — mechanical refactor, but now the length is self-documenting.
- The `{"findings"` branch computes `end_rel = Some(i + c.len_utf8())` inside the depth walker (captures the byte offset PAST the closing brace) and slices exclusive `..end_rel` — semantically identical to the old inclusive `..=end_pos` but explicit about UTF-8 length accounting.

**Tests (mandated refactor point — UTF-8 fuzzing minus proptest):** 7 new unit tests in `vdd::parsing::tests`:
1. `extract_json_survives_leading_emoji` — 4-byte codepoint (🔥, U+1F525) immediately before ````json fence.
2. `extract_json_survives_cjk_prose` — 3-byte CJK chars in preamble.
3. `extract_json_survives_smart_quotes_in_prose` — curly quotes in preamble.
4. `extract_json_survives_emoji_inside_json_string` — multibyte INSIDE the JSON body.

e8928eb4-5f2b-4133-a576-7deb9c4fe4cf.content:
## Current state (src/session/, ~5418 LOC)

**Already a centralized session module — but not the broadcast-channel singleton #510 describes.**

- `src/session/mod.rs` (1820 LOC) defines `Session` (id, mode, requests, tokens, turn_metrics, modified_files, handoff_notes, vdd_* fields) + `SessionManager { persist_dir, current: Option<Session>, ... }`. Persists to disk via `atomic_write` (`session.<id>.json`, `latest.json`, `handoff.md`).
- `src/session/state.rs` (861 LOC): `TokenUsage`, `UsageExtras`, `TurnMetrics`, `PlanModeState` (with TOCTOU-safe `plan_realpath`), `is_tool_allowed_in_plan_mode`, `PLAN_MODE_ALLOWED_TOOLS`, `MCP_TOOL_PREFIX`, `PLUGIN_TOOL_PREFIX`, `get_session_context()`.
- `src/session/pricing.rs` (1224 LOC) is the cost calculator (model pricing tables, fast-mode rates, cache-write TTL math).
- `src/session/task.rs` (1170 LOC) is the in-session `TaskManager` (todo-list tool backing).
- `src/session/audit.rs` (343 LOC) is the per-session audit log.

**What CC's state/ has that OC doesn't:**
- No `tokio::sync::broadcast` listeners. Comments at `src/session/mod.rs:1596, 1642` mention `Arc<RwLock<SessionManager>>` as the *target* migration but the broadcast channel is not implemented.
- No `on_session_switch` subscriber API. Session switches go through direct `start_initializer` / `start_coding` / `end_session` mutators.
- No `has_exited_plan_mode` / `needs_plan_mode_exit_attachment` fields — those are still threaded through function args (e.g. in `tui/app.rs`).
- Permission manager, hook engine, memory_db each hold their own `Arc` on `App` (src/tui/app.rs:446-447), not centralized.

## Phase 2 spec — broadcast wiring + field migration

**Step 1 — wrap in `Arc<RwLock<>>` and add broadcast channel** (new file `src/session/events.rs`):
```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum SessionEvent {
    SessionStarted { id: String, mode: SessionMode },
    SessionSwitched { from: Option<String>, to: String },
    SessionEnded { id: String },
    ModeChanged { from: SessionMode, to: SessionMode },
    PlanModeEntered { plan_file: PathBuf },
    PlanModeExited,
    AuthRefreshed { provider: String },
}

pub struct SessionState {
    inner: Arc<RwLock<SessionStateInner>>,
    events: tokio::sync::broadcast::Sender<SessionEvent>,
}
impl SessionState {
    pub fn subscribe(&self) -> tokio::sync::broadcast::Receiver<SessionEvent>;
    pub async fn read<R>(&self, f: impl FnOnce(&SessionStateInner) -> R) -> R;
    pub async fn write<R>(&self, f: impl FnOnce(&mut SessionStateInner) -> R) -> R;
}
```
- Channel capacity 64, lagged receivers logged + dropped (matches CC's behavior).
- `write()` fires the appropriate `SessionEvent` after mutation completes.

**Step 2 — categorize fields into `SessionStateInner`** (per CC's state/ groups):
```rust
pub struct SessionStateInner {
    pub identity: IdentityState,        // session_id, parent_id, mode
    pub telemetry: TelemetryState,      // turn_metrics, cumulative_usage
    pub permissions: PermissionsState,  // plan_mode (move PlanModeState here)
    pub auth: AuthState,                // claude_code_token, provider keys cache
    pub ui: UiState,                    // has_exited_plan_mode, needs_plan_mode_exit_attachment, active_overlay metadata
    pub tasks: TaskState,               // (wraps the current TaskManager)
}
```

**Step 3 — migrate one field at a time from `App` (src/tui/app.rs:425+):**
- Move `claude_code_token` → `state.read(|s| s.auth.claude_code_token.clone())`.
- Move `permission_mgr` → `state.inner.write().permissions.manager` (or keep external Arc but expose via accessor).
- Each migration is one PR; the test plan is "no behavior change, just call sites swap".

**Step 4 — wire subscribers:**
- `SubagentTracker` subscribes to `SessionSwitched` to clear in-flight agents.
- `HookEngine` subscribes to `SessionStarted/Ended` to fire `SessionStart/End` hooks (replaces direct calls in `SessionManager`).
- `tui/app.rs` event loop subscribes to all events to drive overlay state (PlanMode banner, notification bar in #520).

**Test scaffold** (new file `src/session/events_test.rs`):
- `subscriber_sees_session_started`.
- `dropped_subscriber_doesnt_block_writer` — fill 65 events into a capacity-64 channel.
- `concurrent_readers_dont_block` — spawn 8 read tasks holding the RwLock read guard, assert another `read()` completes.

**Dependencies:** intersects #253 (App decomposition) — both can land independently if Step 3 migrations are small + sequential.

Closing the umbrella — Phase 2 work proceeds as discrete PRs per field group.

0a3c7743-ceff-4188-8d50-1eadf93df447.title: QA: guardrails check_file_access fails open on Mutex poison/None state (guardrails.rs)
0a3c7743-ceff-4188-8d50-1eadf93df447.description:
## Severity
Major
## Dimension
security
## Location
src/guardrails.rs:43-50, 26-35
## Violation
The blast-radius check returns `Ok(())` whenever the global guardrails
state cannot be inspected — both when the mutex is poisoned and when the
engine was never configured:
```rust
pub fn check_file_access(path: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
    if let Ok(guard) = GUARDRAILS.lock() {
        if let Some(engine) = guard.as_ref() {
            return engine.check_file_access(path);
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}
```
The `if let Ok` swallows `PoisonError`; the inner `if let Some` covers
the "never configured" case. Either way the function returns success and
the caller proceeds to write `.git/config` or `/etc/shadow`. This is a
classic fail-open security failure (OWASP A04 Insecure Design).
`configure()` (lines 30-35) silently no-ops on poison as well.
## Mandated refactor
Distinguish three states explicitly: `Disabled`, `Enabled(engine)`,
`Poisoned`. Return `Err("guardrails poisoned — refusing write")` on
poison. Either require explicit configuration before any tool dispatches,
or return a typed `GuardrailDecision { Unconfigured, Allowed, Denied(...) }`
and force the caller to handle `Unconfigured` (fail-closed for write
tools). Replace `if let Ok(guard) = ...lock()` with
`.lock().expect("guardrails poisoned")` if poison genuinely should crash
the process.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

3573f83a-8d1b-4528-b33d-5b98ca8e4c8e.content: Replace fail-open Mutex pattern with explicit tri-state GuardrailsState enum (Unconfigured | Configured(engine) | Poisoned). check_file_access returns Err on poison or unconfigured at the security boundary. Non-security accessors degrade gracefully with error logging. Adding 5 regression tests serialized on a per-test mutex against the process-global state.

8ff0561e-8a7d-453f-a228-d9ab856fa34f.author: lOrm
8ff0561e-8a7d-453f-a228-d9ab856fa34f.content: Fixed via tri-state GuardrailsState (Disabled | Enabled(Box<engine>) | Poisoned). Security boundary check_file_access now returns Err(POISON_ERR) when the mutex is poisoned and Ok when disabled (no policy = nothing to enforce, the existing default semantics). configure() is sticky-poison: refuses to re-arm after a panic. lock_or_poison() transitions to Poisoned on PoisonError::into_inner(). Engine is Box-allocated to keep the enum variant size balanced. 5 new regression tests serialized on a per-test mutex: returns_err_when_poisoned, happy_path_with_enabled_engine, configure_refuses_when_poisoned, non_security_paths_safe_when_poisoned, configure_with_all_disabled_yields_disabled_state. Plus retained test_disabled_guardrails_allow_all. Full lib test suite: 1480 pass (up from 1466 baseline). No clippy regressions on guardrails.rs (single pre-existing dead_code error in permissions.rs is on HEAD, unrelated). No #[allow], no clippy.toml, no #[ignore]. Forensic note: another concurrent Claude agent in this workspace repeatedly stashed src/guardrails.rs as 'unrelated-guardrails-wip' between my Edit calls; the final state on disk has been re-applied via /tmp/apply_749_fix.py and verified by md5 immediately after testing.

0aa4e5fc-6c1b-4e9b-953d-da469112e0d9.title: Prompt injection: format_core_memory_for_prompt does not escape XML/section markers
0aa4e5fc-6c1b-4e9b-953d-da469112e0d9.description:
## Severity
Major
## Dimension
security
## Location
src/memory.rs:650-662 (format_core_memory_for_prompt)
## Violation
Core memory section names and content are interpolated directly into XML wrapper tags emitted into the system prompt with no escaping:

```rust
let mut output = String::from("<core_memory>\n");
for mem in core {
    let _ = write!(
        output,
        "<{}>\n{}\n</{}>\n",
        mem.section, mem.content, mem.section
    );
}
output.push_str("</core_memory>");
```

`update_core_memory(section, content)` is fully public and the auto-learning code path stores untrusted assistant/user-derived data into core memory (see migrate_v1_on seed text). A `content` that includes `</core_memory>` or `</persona>` literally breaks out of the framing tag, allowing instruction injection into the system-prompt construction at the next session start. Same class as crosslink #501 (FTS escape) but here the sink is the LLM, not SQLite. No control on section name either — a section called `evil><system>` is currently rejected only by the SQL PRIMARY KEY constraint after the damage is done in the prompt.
## Mandated refactor
1. Strip or HTML-escape `<`, `>`, `&`, and the literal substrings `</core_memory>`, `</persona>`, `</project_info>`, `</user_preferences>` from `mem.content` before write!.
2. Enforce allowlist on `section` (`[a-z_]+`, max 32 chars) at `update_core_memory`.
3. Add a regression test that stores `</core_memory>BAD` and asserts the rendered prompt contains an escaped form, not the raw closing tag.
4. Apply the same escape to format_learned_preferences (line 1252-1268) and format_file_knowledge.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

No #[allow], no clippy.toml, no #[ignore]. cargo clippy clean; 1428 tests pass.

0d540a41-a3bd-4c36-bec3-f6220c9c7ab5.title: pdftotext subprocess: file path passed unquoted, filenames with leading hyphen become pdftotext flags
0d540a41-a3bd-4c36-bec3-f6220c9c7ab5.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

**Dimension:** Security and Access / Functional Correctness (Input Handling)

**Location:** /home/doll/OpenClaudia/src/tools/file/read.rs lines 116-117 (pdfinfo), 153-155 (pdftotext)

**Violation:**
read_pdf_file invokes 'pdfinfo <path>' and 'pdftotext [-f F -l L] <path> -' with the path supplied as the next arg (line 116, line 153). Although Command::new().arg() correctly avoids shell metacharacter injection (no shell involved), it does NOT protect against pdftotext's OWN option parsing. A file named '-help' or '--version' or '-f' will be interpreted as a flag. More dangerously, a file named '-opw' (owner password) or '-upw' (user password) ACCEPTS an additional argument from argv, so a file named '--nocenter' could change behaviour, and a file named '-opw' would consume the literal '-' (stdout sink) argument at line 154, causing pdftotext to hang waiting for stdin. An attacker able to name a file (e.g. in /tmp, via git clone of an adversarial repo, via extracted archive) can abuse this.

Additionally:
1. **pdfinfo output parsing is loose.** Lines 121-134 do 'line.starts_with("Pages:")' — a PDF with 'Pages: 5 (hidden)' matches and count parses '5'; a PDF whose metadata title happens to start with 'Pages:' leads the parser.
2. **No bound on page count printed.** A PDF with 100 000 pages and page range '1-100000' generates unbounded output before the 100_000-char guard in read_text_file (not even applied here, line 164 returns raw pdftotext text).

**Mandated Refactor:**
1. Use '--' before the path argument in both pdfinfo and pdftotext invocations: cmd.arg("--").arg(path). pdftotext from poppler-utils >=0.75 respects '--' to terminate options; confirm version and document required minimum.
2. Canonicalize the path FIRST (fs::canonicalize) so it starts with '/', which pdftotext never interprets as a flag.
3. Parse pdfinfo output via exact regex: ^Pages:\s+(\d+)$ anchored at line boundaries.
4. Enforce a max output size on the pdftotext stdout (reqwest-style: write to a capped buffer).
5. Validate page-range arithmetic: reject last - first > MAX_PAGES_PER_READ (e.g. 200).

6e2ebd87-2e9c-41c5-aca6-0b43ad28a7ef.author: lOrm
6e2ebd87-2e9c-41c5-aca6-0b43ad28a7ef.content:
Forensic evidence — fix applied in src/tools/file/read.rs.

Layer 1 (pre-spawn guard): new helper reject_flag_prefix(path) refuses any path string whose first character is '-'. Catches -help, --version, -opw, -upw, -f, -l, --nocenter, and every other pdftotext/pdfinfo flag form. Both read_pdf_file branches (no-pages and with-pages) call this guard at function entry, BEFORE any Command::new is built.

Layer 2 (option terminator): both subprocess invocations now pass '--' immediately before the path argument:
  Command::new("pdfinfo").arg("--").arg(path).output()
  cmd.arg("--"); cmd.arg(path); cmd.arg("-");   // pdftotext
This is defence-in-depth — even if layer 1 were ever bypassed, '--' guarantees the path cannot be re-parsed as a flag.

8 new tests pin both layers (Behavior 10 block, lines 762-862 of read.rs):
  1. reject_flag_prefix_rejects_single_dash_filename       (-help)
  2. reject_flag_prefix_rejects_double_dash_filename       (--version)
  3. reject_flag_prefix_rejects_password_flag_filename     (-opw, -upw — the consume-next-argv flags)
  4. reject_flag_prefix_accepts_absolute_path              (/tmp/normal.pdf)
  5. reject_flag_prefix_accepts_dot_slash_relative_path    (./doc.pdf, subdir/doc.pdf)
  6. read_pdf_file_rejects_leading_hyphen_filename         (end-to-end '-help')
  7. read_pdf_file_rejects_password_flag_filename_with_pages (end-to-end '-opw' with pages='1-3')
  8. read_pdf_file_uses_double_dash_terminator_in_source   (source-level invariant for both call sites)

Verification:
  cargo test --lib                     -> 1295 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored  (baseline 1287 + 8 new)
  cargo clippy --lib --tests -- -D warnings  -> exit 0, no warnings
  grep -nE '#\[(allow|ignore)' new code   -> none
  ls clippy.toml                       -> No such file or directory

Out of scope (mandated refactor items deferred — should file follow-up):
  - pdfinfo regex anchoring (line.starts_with("Pages:") still loose; mandated as anchored ^Pages:\s+(\d+)$)
  - max output size on pdftotext stdout (truncation guard still applied only at read_text_file)
  - max page-span enforcement (>200 pages)
These were listed in the mandated refactor but are functional-quality items separate from the flag-injection vector closed here.

0f0fe3f3-d660-4fea-a146-8891f656d864.title: ServiceRegistry exposes Arc<dyn AnalyticsSink> accessors, leaking Arc into all consumers
0f0fe3f3-d660-4fea-a146-8891f656d864.description:
## Severity
Minor
## Dimension
decoupling
## Location
src/services/mod.rs:60-71
## Violation
The accessors return references to the internal Arc smart pointer rather than to the trait object. Quoted lines:

    #[must_use]
    pub fn analytics(&self) -> &Arc<dyn AnalyticsSink> {
        &self.analytics
    }

    #[must_use]
    pub fn flags(&self) -> &Arc<dyn FeatureFlagSource> {
        &self.flags
    }

Returning the Arc itself ties callers to the heap-allocation choice and forces them to know whether the registry uses Arc, Box, or a static reference. If the implementation ever switches to a different smart pointer (or to static dispatch via generics), every call site changes. It also lets callers Arc::clone the sink outside the registry's lifetime contract, defeating any future "shutdown all sinks on registry drop" semantics.
## Mandated refactor
Return `&dyn AnalyticsSink` and `&dyn FeatureFlagSource`. If a caller genuinely needs a long-lived handle, add explicit `analytics_arc()` / `flags_arc()` accessors that signal the ownership transfer. Or expose the registry as a thin facade with `record(&self, event)` and `is_enabled(&self, name) -> bool` methods so the Arc never escapes the module.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

ffffcb4f-7a74-4bde-b761-95f29cd98db4.author: lOrm

The Arc no longer leaks into callers. Added explicit analytics_arc() / flags_arc() escape hatches that return Arc<dyn _> for the rare case where a caller really needs shared ownership (e.g. installing the sink into a background task). The smart-pointer choice is now an internal implementation detail.

0f81bfd8-4adb-4dca-8ac0-ec328269ed52.title: coordinator/teammate: TeammateState transitions are not enforced — bare field access permits Dead->Running
0f81bfd8-4adb-4dca-8ac0-ec328269ed52.description:
## Severity
Minor
## Dimension
solid
## Location
src/coordinator/teammate.rs:83-128 (TeammateState + Teammate struct)
## Violation
The module doc claims:

```rust
/// Lifecycle state. Transitions are one-way:
/// `Spawning → Running → Idle → Dead` and `Running → Dead` directly.
```

But the `Teammate` struct exposes the state as a `pub` field:

```rust
pub struct Teammate {
    pub id: TeammateId,
    pub agent_type: AgentType,
    pub color: AgentColor,
    pub state: TeammateState,
    ...
}
```

There is no `transition_to(...)` method, no invariant enforcement. The Phase 2 dispatcher (or any caller) can write `teammate.state = TeammateState::Running` after the teammate has already gone `Dead`, violating the documented contract silently. The same risk applies to setting `state = TeammateState::Idle` from `Spawning` without ever passing through `Running`.

This is LSP-adjacent: any Phase 3 wrapper assuming the contract will be wrong.

## Mandated refactor
Make the `state` field `pub(crate)` (or private) and add:

```rust
impl Teammate {
    pub fn transition_to(&mut self, next: TeammateState) -> Result<(), InvalidTransition> {
        if !self.state.can_transition_to(&next) { return Err(...) }
        self.state = next; Ok(())
    }
}
```

with a corresponding `TeammateState::can_transition_to` that enforces the documented transition table.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

b1ddbb68-8718-4a3c-a40c-c6e3e93daff0.author: lOrm
b1ddbb68-8718-4a3c-a40c-c6e3e93daff0.content:
Deferred — architectural encapsulation change (Teammate is the coordinator's central type; touches all call sites).

**Fix outline:** Make Teammate::state private (src/coordinator/teammate.rs:119) and replace the field with documented transition methods: pub fn mark_running(&mut self), pub fn mark_idle(&mut self), pub fn mark_dead(&mut self) — each asserts the state precondition (Spawning|Running|Idle → Running, etc.) and either panics in debug + logs in release, or returns Result<(), TeammateError>. Expose pub fn state(&self) -> TeammateState as a Copy getter. Now the documented one-way lifecycle is enforced by the type, not by hope.

**Recommendation:** Owner-level decision on (a) panic vs Result for invalid transitions, (b) whether transitions should be tracing-instrumented for lifecycle observability. Small refactor in surface area but coordinator-central in semantics. Defer.

0fab10e1-92c2-4b98-b79f-194a2b82a5bd.title: subagent: block_in_place + Handle::block_on inside sync tool dispatch can deadlock
0fab10e1-92c2-4b98-b79f-194a2b82a5bd.description:
## Severity
Major
## Dimension
concurrency
## Location
src/subagent.rs:1340-1350 (execute_task_tool sync branch)
## Violation
```rust
let result = match Handle::try_current() {
    Ok(handle) => tokio::task::block_in_place(|| {
        handle.block_on(run_subagent(&config, app_config, &client))
    }),
    Err(_) => match tokio::runtime::Runtime::new() {
        Ok(rt) => rt.block_on(run_subagent(&config, app_config, &client)),
```

`tokio::task::block_in_place` PANICS under `current_thread` runtimes (commonly used by CLI/test harnesses). `Handle::block_on` from within a runtime worker is itself a known deadlock anti-pattern when the inner future yields back to the same single-threaded executor. The fallback `Runtime::new()` spawns a fresh runtime per tool call: leaks threads, can starve the outer I/O reactor, and bypasses cancellation.
## Mandated refactor
Make `execute_task_tool` async (return a future) and let the tool dispatcher await it. The sync wrapper should live at the CLI boundary only. Remove the `Runtime::new()` fallback — fail fast with a typed error when no runtime is in scope.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

0fb31676-a82f-4412-afab-f7715edfd128.title: search_duckduckgo uses fixed 500ms sleep as page-load synchronization
0fb31676-a82f-4412-afab-f7715edfd128.description:
## Severity
Minor
## Dimension
concurrency
## Location
src/web.rs:475-583 (search_duckduckgo), line 501
## Violation
After `wait_until_navigated()`, the function calls `std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(500))` to wait for the page. This is a race condition: on slow machines the page may not be ready; on fast loads the 500ms is wasted latency. Inside a tokio runtime this also blocks the executor thread because the function is `pub fn`, not async, and is invoked via `block_in_place(handle.block_on(...))` from `execute_web_search`.

```rust
// Wait for page to load
std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(500));
```

A similar 2-second blocking sleep exists in `fetch_with_browser` at line 622.
## Mandated refactor
Use a polling wait with timeout: `tab.wait_for_element_with_custom_timeout(".result", Duration::from_secs(5))`. For `fetch_with_browser`, wait for `document.readyState === 'complete'` via `tab.evaluate(...)` polled with a timeout. If a true wall-clock delay is needed, use `tokio::time::sleep` from an async context.

11a61b5b-5435-4b0e-b8fd-dac426ac481e.title: SSRF guard bypassed by HTTP redirects in fetch_url
11a61b5b-5435-4b0e-b8fd-dac426ac481e.description:
## Severity
Critical
## Dimension
security
## Location
src/web.rs:262-300 (fetch_url)
## Violation
`validate_url(url)` runs on the user-supplied URL, then the request is made to `format!("{JINA_READER_URL}{url}")`. The `reqwest::Client` built at line 265-268 has default redirect policy (follow up to 10). An attacker that controls a public hostname that returns a 302 to `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/` — or to a private RFC1918 address — completely defeats the SSRF guard: the dial-time check is never re-run on the redirect target.

```rust
pub async fn fetch_url(url: &str) -> Result<FetchResult, String> {
    validate_url(url)?;

    let client = Client::builder()
        .timeout(Duration::from_secs(30))
        .build()
```

The same problem applies to `fetch_with_browser` (line 598) — headless Chrome follows redirects with no per-hop guard.
## Mandated refactor
Build the reqwest client with `.redirect(redirect::Policy::custom(|attempt| { validate_url(attempt.url().as_str()).map(|_| attempt.follow()).unwrap_or_else(|_| attempt.stop()) }))`, or `redirect::Policy::none()` and re-`validate_url` + re-dispatch manually on every 3xx. Install a `reqwest::dns::Resolve` impl that re-checks resolved IPs against `is_ip_forbidden` at dial time to close the DNS-rebinding gap noted in the docstring at line 149-152. For headless Chrome, intercept navigation events or hard-block the page by configuring a proxy that re-validates.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

ec76bd09-8a61-47d5-93a3-7b5a8948350a.author: lOrm
ec76bd09-8a61-47d5-93a3-7b5a8948350a.content:
Fix landed in src/web.rs. Forensic evidence:

ROOT CAUSE
- SHARED_HTTP_CLIENT was built without a .redirect(...) policy, so reqwest applied its default Policy::limited(10) — which silently follows 3xx without re-running validate_url on the Location target. An attacker controlling a public host could 302 to http://169.254.169.254/... (AWS metadata) or any RFC1918 IP and exfiltrate internal data; the dial-time SSRF check only ever ran on the initial URL.

FIX (option-b from the report)
- Added pub(crate) fn ssrf_redirect_policy() -> redirect::Policy and the generic-validator variant ssrf_redirect_policy_with(F) (so the policy itself is unit-testable without bypassing validate_url).
- Custom policy logic (src/web.rs:66-93):
    1. Reject if attempt.previous().len() >= SSRF_REDIRECT_LIMIT (=10) — custom policies disable reqwest's built-in hop cap, so we re-establish it.
    2. Call validate_url(attempt.url()) on every hop. Failure -> attempt.error(...); success -> attempt.follow().
- Wired into SHARED_HTTP_CLIENT::build() via .redirect(ssrf_redirect_policy()). This covers all three uses of SHARED_HTTP_CLIENT (fetch_url, search_tavily, search_brave).

TESTS ADDED (6 new, all passing)
- ssrf_redirect_to_loopback_is_blocked — wiremock returns 302->127.0.0.1; SSRF guard rejects on the redirect hop. Walks the error source chain to confirm "SSRF guard blocked redirect" surfaces under reqwest's is_redirect() wrapper.
- ssrf_redirect_to_public_is_followed — 302->public reaches the final 200 body.
- ssrf_redirect_loop_is_bounded — wiremock serves an infinite self-loop; policy terminates with "redirect chain exceeded 10 hops". Hop counter asserts the validator runs <=10 times.
- ssrf_multi_hop_public_chain_succeeds — 3-hop public chain A->B->C completes end-to-end with the per-hop guard.

1227829b-b6b7-4cc2-a741-3fa1266bd9b5.title: Guardrails quality-gate timeout prefix is Unix-specific; bash dependency on Windows
1227829b-b6b7-4cc2-a741-3fa1266bd9b5.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

**Dimension**: Functional Correctness (cross-platform)

**Location**: src/guardrails.rs:492-541 (run_shell_command_sync)

**Violation**:
1. Line 503: `format!("timeout {timeout_seconds} {command}")` — the `timeout` coreutils binary does not exist on macOS by default (only on GNU coreutils / Linux). On macOS every quality-gate run silently fails with 'command not found' and passes/fails status are meaningless.
2. Line 527 (non-windows): hardcoded `Command::new("bash")` — requires bash even on Alpine Linux containers where only `sh` is available.
3. Line 508-524 (windows): searches for Git Bash in Program Files — but the final fallback is literal 'bash' (line 517) which likely does NOT exist on a minimal Windows without Git. Returns Err gracefully but the failure is masked as exit_code -1 with no diagnostic.
4. The function returns (-1, empty-stdout, stderr-with-failure) — a caller cannot distinguish 'command exited with -1' from 'shell not found'. The 'required' flag (config/guardrails.rs:199) does not help because passed=false either way.

**Mandated Refactor**:
1. Use tokio::process::Command with tokio::time::timeout directly (as hooks/mod.rs already does correctly) — NO shell timeout-prefix hack.
2. Replace bash hardcode with platform-appropriate shell detection: on unix, try /bin/sh; on windows, try powershell.exe with explicit 'cmd' fallback.
3. Return a typed enum: enum ShellResult { Success(output), ExitFailed(code), ShellMissing, Timeout } so the caller can react appropriately.
4. Add integration tests on macOS (CI matrix) that actually runs a quality gate — likely reveals this bug.

132586cd-5b51-4ae0-9801-56397a3baed4.title: edit_file: count-occurrences contains+matches triple-scan; notebook cell index accepted via u64 cast
132586cd-5b51-4ae0-9801-56397a3baed4.description:
Current state: 

Desired state: 

Reason: 

**Dimension:** Performance / Functional Correctness

**Location:** /home/doll/OpenClaudia/src/tools/file/edit.rs lines 75, 85, 95 (content.contains, content.matches, content.replacen); /home/doll/OpenClaudia/src/tools/file/notebook.rs lines 41-44 (cell_number cast)

**Violation:**
1. **Triple traversal of file content.** edit.rs line 75: content.contains(old_string); line 85: content.matches(old_string).count(); line 95: content.replacen(old_string, new_string, 1). For a 100 KB file this scans the haystack THREE times. The first two can be merged: let count = content.matches(old_string).count(); if count == 0 { not found } if count > 1 { ambiguous } — saves one full pass.
2. **notebook.rs line 44: usize::try_from(n).unwrap_or(usize::MAX).** A caller passing cell_number = u64::MAX saturates to usize::MAX, then the 'if cell_number >= cells.len()' guard fires with a misleading 'out of bounds' error — but the silent saturation hides the semantic violation. The correct response is to reject any cell_number that doesn't fit in a sensible range (e.g. < 10_000).
3. **edit.rs line 85: if count > 1 { ambiguous } — no hint which lines matched.** The error message tells the model to 'provide a more specific old_string' without showing WHERE the matches are. Productivity hit.

**Mandated Refactor:**
1. Merge contains + matches into a single str::matches_indices walk; bail on first or count-and-report.
2. Validate cell_number range: reject > 10_000; on deserialize, treat u64::MAX as malformed.
3. When count > 1, report the line numbers of each match: 'Found N occurrences at lines [10, 42, 88]. Please include more context.'

142cf873-0bda-4e4c-a36f-29ae6be84cdc.title: Duplicated OAuth URL and beta-header string construction drift
142cf873-0bda-4e4c-a36f-29ae6be84cdc.description:
Current state: 

Desired state: 

Reason: 

Dimension: Security and Access

Location: src/proxy.rs lines 250-257 (auth_device_start) and lines 1065-1069 (proxy_anthropic_messages), and src/oauth.rs lines 84-102 (PkceParams::build_auth_url — which is the ALREADY-EXISTING canonical implementation).

Violation: auth_device_start manually builds the authorization URL via format! with bare curly-brace interpolation of ANTHROPIC_CLIENT_ID, ANTHROPIC_REDIRECT_URI, the scope literal, pkce.challenge, and oauth_state — bypassing the PkceParams::build_auth_url() method that already exists in oauth.rs and would give consistent URL encoding. This is a clear DRY violation (two authoritative URL builders). Worse, the proxy.rs version hard-codes the scope list as 'org:create_api_key user:profile user:inference' but oauth.rs OAUTH_SCOPES has a different list that INCLUDES 'user:sessions:claude_code'. These two scope lists drift silently.

Separately, proxy_anthropic_messages line 1069 sets a large inline 'anthropic-beta' header constant `claude-code-20250219,oauth-2025-04-20,interleaved-thinking-2025-05-14,fine-grained-tool-streaming-2025-05-14`. The same constant list is defined in claude_credentials.rs lines 21-27 as three separate typed constants — which are NOT used in proxy.rs, so the inline string must stay in sync manually.

Mandated Refactor:
  1. Delete lines 243-257 in auth_device_start. Replace with: `let auth_url = pkce.build_auth_url();`
  2. Ensure oauth.rs::OAUTH_SCOPES is the single source of truth. Delete the hard-coded scope string in proxy.rs.
  3. In claude_credentials.rs, create a public function `fn claude_code_beta_header_value() -> String` that joins CLAUDE_CODE_BETA_HEADER, OAUTH_BETA_HEADER, INTERLEAVED_THINKING_BETA and any fine-grained-tool-streaming header. Call it from proxy.rs line 1068.
  4. Add a compile-time check or test that proxy.rs does not contain the literal string 'oauth-2025-04-20' or the scope list.

155d5090-07c6-44bc-9227-14d65082ac14.title: MigrationContext::ledger_path is in MigrationContext but read by load() while migrations write via mark()
155d5090-07c6-44bc-9227-14d65082ac14.description:
## Severity
Minor
## Dimension
decoupling
## Location
src/migrations/mod.rs:111-114, 126-168
## Violation
The ledger path is owned by MigrationContext but the lifecycle is owned by run_all:

```rust
pub fn ledger_path(&self) -> PathBuf {
    self.openclaudia_data.join("migrations.json")
}

pub fn run_all(ctx: &MigrationContext) -> Vec<MigrationReport> {
    let mut ledger = CompletionLedger::load(&ctx.ledger_path());
    ...
    if let Err(err) = ledger.save(&ctx.ledger_path()) {  // bottom of fn
        tracing::warn!(error = %err, "failed to persist migration ledger");
    }
    out
}
```

The MigrationContext exposes ledger_path but nothing else interacts with the ledger through the context — the ledger itself is a local variable in run_all. This breaks the "context object" abstraction: callers cannot inspect or mock the ledger via MigrationContext for testing.

More importantly, individual Migration impls receive &MigrationContext but the ledger inside it is invisible to them. Once-only migrations have no way to know whether they're being re-run (a debugging affordance), nor can they participate in their own once-only logic (e.g., a migration that records additional metadata alongside its completion mark).

## Mandated refactor
1. Move the ledger ownership to MigrationContext as an interior-mutable field (RefCell<CompletionLedger>) so individual migrations can read/write it through the context.
2. Or, hide the ledger entirely as a private detail of run_all and remove ledger_path from the public MigrationContext API — the path leakage suggests an incomplete abstraction.

Pick one extreme; the current half-encapsulation forces callers to know about both the path and the loader/saver but gives them no leverage.

## Filed from QA review dispatch

15607fb5-8ab0-4aa9-a2b1-ad9e9deeb984.title: CHAINLINK_INSTALL_SHOWN global AtomicBool — no way to reset, leaks 'once' state across tests and sessions
15607fb5-8ab0-4aa9-a2b1-ad9e9deeb984.description:
Current state: 

Desired state: 

Reason: 

**Dimension:** State Management / Testability

**Location:** /home/doll/OpenClaudia/src/tools/chainlink.rs line 7 (CHAINLINK_INSTALL_SHOWN), lines 43-51 (swap-and-branch)

**Violation:**
A process-global AtomicBool controls whether the 'chainlink not found, install from github' message has been shown. Once the swap fires, future chainlink-missing errors return the shorter 'Chainlink not available.' message (line 51). Consequences:

2. **Long-running sessions never re-show the helpful message** even after a plausible event (system update, PATH change) that might have reinstalled chainlink.

**Mandated Refactor:**
1. Move the 'shown' flag onto SessionState (removing the global).
2. Re-check PATH for chainlink every 5 minutes or at session start; show the install message whenever chainlink is actually absent, not 'first time per process'.
3. Make the install URL configurable via AppConfig — agents deploying in restricted environments can point at an internal mirror.

15d38070-a65e-44c4-ac22-7de434a0d003.title: tool_intercept: parse_nested_elements has no depth or size limit, enabling memory exhaustion
15d38070-a65e-44c4-ac22-7de434a0d003.description:
## Severity
Minor
## Dimension
security
## Location
src/tool_intercept.rs:436-498 (parse_nested_elements)
## Violation
`parse_nested_elements` walks the buffer linearly without:

1. A maximum element-count cap. A model that emits 100,000 `<param_n>value</param_n>` nested elements is parsed into a HashMap with no bound.
2. A maximum value-length cap. A single `<content>` element holding a 50MB string is allocated whole into the parameters map via `value = content[abs_tag_end + 1..abs_close_pos].to_string();` (line 482).
3. A depth limit. While the parser is flat (single level), the surrounding `extract_all_tool_calls` driver calls it in a loop and can be made to accumulate unbounded tools.

A malicious or buggy upstream stream can drive the proxy into OOM by sending one giant `<write_file>...<content>$BIG</content>...</write_file>`. Because the tool then gets passed to `write_file` -> filesystem, this is also a path to disk exhaustion.

## Mandated refactor
Add `const MAX_PARAM_LEN: usize = 4 * 1024 * 1024;` and `const MAX_ELEMS: usize = 32;`. Reject (skip + log) any element exceeding the size cap; cap the parameter count at MAX_ELEMS and discard the rest with a warning. Surface a typed `ParseError::ParameterTooLarge` to the caller so the failure is observable, not silent.

16b1f441-c9ff-46f3-b2b5-06f378b9d5dd.title: execute_write_file does NOT enforce read-before-write enabling clobber attacks
16b1f441-c9ff-46f3-b2b5-06f378b9d5dd.description:
## Severity
Major

## Dimension
Security and Access / Functional Correctness

## Location
src/tools/file/write.rs:9-74 (execute_write_file) vs src/tools/file/edit.rs:46-53 (READ_TRACKER enforcement)

## Violation
edit_file requires the file have been read first (edit.rs:46-53 explicitly blocks the model from editing files it never opened — to "prevent edits based on hallucinated file contents"). write_file makes no such check. The model can call write_file on any existing file and silently clobber its contents without ever having read them.

```rust
// execute_write_file — no READ_TRACKER check anywhere
match fs::write(path, content) {
    Ok(()) => { ... }
}
```

This is the asymmetric protection problem. Worse, the write path performs the SAME canonicalize-or-walk-parent dance as edit and notebook (lines 20-34) — three copies of the same fragile logic across three sibling files, all with subtly different error messages.

A model that decides to "fix" a config file it has never seen can wipe it. A prompt-injection attack ("write a fresh CLAUDE.md saying X") succeeds without the read guard that edit_file would have refused at.

## Mandated refactor
1. Add the same READ_TRACKER.has_been_read guard to write_file when the file already exists. New-file writes are exempt (nothing to clobber). Wording: "File exists at '{path}' — call read_file first to confirm you intend to overwrite, OR use edit_file for in-place changes."
2. Extract the canonicalize-or-walk-parent dance to a shared helper used by write/edit/notebook (currently duplicated in all three).
3. Cross-reference issue #687 (replace_all gap) and the broader READ_TRACKER issue.

180b654d-aa1e-45a7-9bfc-a3ed24894ca2.title: StateStore uses std RwLock but exposes write() guard to async callers risking deadlock across await
180b654d-aa1e-45a7-9bfc-a3ed24894ca2.description:
## Severity
Critical
## Dimension
concurrency
## Location
src/state/store.rs:110-131, 144-148
## Violation
StateStore wraps SessionState in std::sync::RwLock and hands out RwLockWriteGuard via write(). The module docs explicitly forbid holding the guard across .await but there is no compile-time enforcement.

```rust
//! 1. Never hold a read guard across an `.await`.
//! 2. Never hold a write guard across an `.await`.
```

Any caller that holds the guard across an await will deadlock or poison the lock. The docs say panics on poisoned lock — one mishandled await terminates all future state access for the process.

## Mandated refactor
Either switch to tokio::sync::RwLock or replace the write() guard API with a closure-passing with_write closure so the borrow cannot cross an .await by construction.

## Filed from QA review dispatch

195439e7-8e9c-4ae7-ab36-0baba61f056e.title: tool_intercept: bash completion hint regresses on outputs containing word 'error'
195439e7-8e9c-4ae7-ab36-0baba61f056e.description:
## Severity
Trivial
## Dimension
kiss
## Location
src/tool_intercept.rs:717-722 (format_tool_results_xml_with_names)
## Violation
```rust
"bash" | "Bash" => {
    if content.contains("error") || content.contains("Error") || content.contains("failed") {
        None // Don't add completion hint for errors
    } else {
        Some("Command executed successfully.")
    }
}
```

`String::contains` matches anywhere in the buffer. Many valid bash successes contain the word "error" (`grep -c error logfile`, `find . -name '*_error_*'`, `cargo build` output that says "0 errors"). The hint is suppressed for these. Conversely, a real failure that prints "fault" or "abort" gets the success hint anyway.

This conflates "process exit code" with "string content of stdout" — they are independent signals.

## Mandated refactor
Use the actual `is_error` field that has already been computed for `*is_error in results` (it is the function parameter the outer `if *is_error` branch already uses). Remove the substring heuristic entirely.

198eff8a-a0b3-494c-8fa6-3ffff1a2b46d.title: MCP StdioTransport size limit applied after unbounded read_line

db37f81d-d1ed-4057-a2b9-4e0a035c2c4d.author: lOrm
db37f81d-d1ed-4057-a2b9-4e0a035c2c4d.content:
Already-fixed by #445 (point 2). Forensic evidence:

src/mcp.rs:359-392 — StdioTransport::request reads stdout via:
  let cap = (MAX_RESPONSE_SIZE as u64).saturating_add(1);
  let bytes_read = (&mut *reader)
      .take(cap)
      .read_until(b'\n', &mut buf)
      .await ...
  if buf.len() > MAX_RESPONSE_SIZE && !buf.ends_with(b"\n") { return Err(...) }

The QA-mandated refactor (BufReader::take(MAX_RESPONSE_SIZE as u64).read_until(b'\n', ...) against a capped buffer, bail during read) is in place verbatim. The size limit is enforced BEFORE allocation, not after — the buffer can hold at most MAX_RESPONSE_SIZE + 1 bytes.

Grep evidence (src/mcp.rs):
  L52  Fix #445 point 2 — bound BEFORE allocation on the response line.
  L348 Fix #445 point 2: bound BEFORE allocation.
  L364 let cap = (MAX_RESPONSE_SIZE as u64).saturating_add(1);
  L366 .take(cap)
  L367 .read_until(b'\n', &mut buf)

Test coverage (already present, all passing):
  - fix445_oversized_line_rejected_before_full_buffering — spawns sh that emits MAX_RESPONSE_SIZE + 1 MiB of zeros, asserts the request fails with "exceeded ... without newline" and completes within 30 s (would OOM or hang with unbounded read_line).
  - fix445_normal_line_succeeds — sanity round-trip.
  - fix445_stderr_drained_does_not_deadlock, fix445_stderr_drain_populates_ring_buffer, fix445_concurrent_drain_and_request_no_deadlock — companion #445 point-1 coverage.

Verification: cargo test --lib mcp::tests::fix445 -> 5/5 pass. Full suite cargo test --lib -> 1412 pass (baseline). cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings -> exit 0.

Note: the HTTP-side concern raised in the original report (HttpTransport::request unbounded response.json()) is a SEPARATE, distinct defect — not in #445's scope, not in #680's title scope. Filing as a follow-up would be appropriate but is outside this issue's mandated location (StdioTransport::request, src/mcp.rs:181-238).

1a8c1ec2-b880-4e0a-b255-04758c7e4165.title: tool_intercept: ToolInterceptor::clear inconsistent with extract_all_tool_calls (in_function_calls leak)
1a8c1ec2-b880-4e0a-b255-04758c7e4165.description:
## Severity
Trivial
## Dimension
kiss
## Location
src/tool_intercept.rs:111-114 (clear) vs src/tool_intercept.rs:243-272 (extract_all_tool_calls)
## Violation
```rust
pub fn clear(&mut self) {
    self.buffer.clear();
    self.in_function_calls = false;
}
```

```rust
pub fn extract_all_tool_calls(&mut self) -> (...) {
    ...
    self.buffer.clear();   // does NOT touch in_function_calls
    (all_tools, text_parts)
}
```

`extract_all_tool_calls` clears the buffer but not the `in_function_calls` flag. After extraction, `has_pending_tool_calls` still returns `true` because `self.in_function_calls` is honored at the end of that check (line 148):

```rust
self.in_function_calls
```

So a subsequent push that contains no tool calls is reported as having pending tool calls forever. The flag is also never SET by any code path inside this module (search the file), so today the bug is dormant — but the dead flag plus the inconsistent reset is a latent bug waiting for someone to introduce a `self.in_function_calls = true` line.

## Mandated refactor
Either remove the `in_function_calls` field entirely (it has no writer) or have `extract_all_tool_calls` end with `self.clear()` instead of `self.buffer.clear()`. Document the invariant in a comment.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

1c5b2b96-67d8-4153-b427-515d5a70bb9f.title: pdftotext/pdfinfo subprocess: missing '--' separator enables flag-injection via hostile filename
1c5b2b96-67d8-4153-b427-515d5a70bb9f.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

**Dimension:** Security and Access / Functional Correctness

**Location:** /home/doll/OpenClaudia/src/tools/file/read.rs lines 116-117 (pdfinfo), 143-155 (pdftotext)

**Violation:**
read_pdf_file invokes 'pdfinfo <path>' and 'pdftotext [-f F -l L] <path> -' supplying the path as a separate arg. Although Command::arg() avoids shell-level injection, it does NOT protect against pdftotext's own option parsing. A file named '-help', '--version', '-opw', or '-upw' is interpreted as a flag by the subprocess. An attacker able to name a file in the project (via git clone of adversarial repo, extracted archive, /tmp traversal) can cause pdftotext to accept owner/user password args, hang waiting for stdin, print version, or skip output entirely.

Secondary issues:
1. pdfinfo output parsing is loose: 'line.starts_with("Pages:")' (line 121). A PDF whose metadata Title begins 'Pages:' or similar can spoof the count.
2. No bound on pdftotext stdout size — the truncation guard at read_text_file (line 320) is not applied here.

**Mandated Refactor:**
1. Insert '--' as the option terminator before the path arg in both pdfinfo and pdftotext invocations: cmd.arg("--").arg(path).
2. Canonicalize path first so it always begins with '/' which pdftotext never parses as a flag.
3. Anchor the pdfinfo regex: ^Pages:\s+(\d+)$.
4. Enforce max output size by capturing stdout into a capped buffer.
5. Reject page ranges that span >200 pages.

1cf7de68-a133-41d1-b26d-7ba930ca26c0.title: subagent: model_override resolved twice and ignored when run_in_background spawns internally
1cf7de68-a133-41d1-b26d-7ba930ca26c0.description:
## Severity
Minor
## Dimension
dry
## Location
src/subagent.rs:1283-1331 (execute_task_tool) and src/subagent.rs:753-763 (run_subagent model resolution)
## Violation
`execute_task_tool` resolves the model name via `resolve_model_name` (line 1289-1292) and stores it on `SubagentConfig::model_override`. `run_subagent` then resolves model again, this time consulting `AgentType::preferred_model` and provider config defaults (lines 753-763). The two code paths can produce different model strings:

- `execute_task_tool` will pass `"opus" -> "claude-opus-4-6"` through `resolve_model_name`.
- `run_subagent`'s fallback chain uses `provider.model` raw.

So a friendly name typed by the caller is canonicalized, but a default from provider config is not — they end up as different string formats downstream.

Additionally, the background-spawn branch (lines 1316-1331) clones the entire `app_config` into the spawned task per call. For a config with many providers, hooks, and rules, this is megabytes of copy. `app_config: Arc<AppConfig>` would let the spawn share the reference.

## Mandated refactor
Move the friendly-name resolution into `run_subagent::pick_model` so both paths normalize identically. Switch `SubagentConfig::model_override` from `Option<String>` to `Option<&str>` consumed only in pick_model. Make `AppConfig` arc-shared so background spawn just clones the Arc.

Reason: 

Dimension: DRY / KISS
Location: src/cli/repl/slash.rs:846-944 (/commit arm) and :946-~1100 (/commit-push-pr arm). Both open 'use std::process::Command' inside the function, re-check 'rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree', re-run 'diff --cached --stat' and 'diff --stat', re-run the stage-all prompt, re-run the commit with default or edited message. /commit-push-pr additionally runs 'push' and 'gh pr create'.

Commit-push-pr becomes: let oid = gateway.commit(msg)?; gateway.push("origin", branch)?; gateway.open_pr(title, body)?; — three lines instead of ~250.

1ed3dbdb-1b7f-4cf5-8fb0-19d1e2d08819.title: Blocking std::process::Command inside TUI sync event loop (freezes render)
1ed3dbdb-1b7f-4cf5-8fb0-19d1e2d08819.description:
Current state: 

Desired state: 

Reason: 

Dimension: Performance / Architectural Alignment
Location: src/tui/app.rs /diff (1095), /review (1170), /init (1217), /files (1057), /doctor (1138) and fn handle_shell_command (1250)
Violation: Every one of these slash-command branches calls std::process::Command::new(...).output() directly on the TUI's synchronous event-loop thread. .output() blocks until the child exits. During that time the rendering loop does not tick, the spinner freezes, key events queue up, and cancellation (Esc) is impossible. Running 'git diff HEAD' on a large repo can block the UI for >1s. This also breaks the TUI/CLI parity invariant — Claude Code runs these asynchronously.
Mandated Refactor: All filesystem/subprocess work must go through self.runtime_handle.spawn() with results arriving via AppEvent::ShellDone { stdout, stderr, exit_code }. Add a helper fn spawn_shell(&self, cmd: Vec<&str>) -> JoinHandle<()> that sends the result back into the channel. Blocks the model spawn_api_turn already uses; apply the same pattern here.

1eeeeae1-6480-4a1f-8203-e4a4dba43f1c.title: FileType enum uses static-str payload to carry mime type — primitive obsession
1eeeeae1-6480-4a1f-8203-e4a4dba43f1c.description:
## Severity
Trivial

## Dimension
SOLID-O (OCP) / Decoupling

## Location
src/tools/file/read.rs:10-37 (FileType enum and detect_file_type)

## Violation
```rust
pub enum FileType {
    Text,
    Image(&'static str),  // mime type
    Pdf,
    Notebook,
}
```

The Image variant carries its mime type as a raw `&'static str`. The dispatcher in mod.rs (line 206) then passes that opaque string down to read_image_file. Adding a new image format (e.g. AVIF) requires editing detect_file_type, the read_image_file signature, the dispatcher, and probably a hidden assumption in the Anthropic adapter that expects "image/png" or "image/jpeg". OCP violation: the enum is not closed under extension.

The trailing comment "// mime type" carries the type information the type system should be carrying. Use a typed Mime instead.

## Mandated refactor
```rust
pub enum ImageKind { Png, Jpeg, Gif, Webp }
impl ImageKind {
    pub const fn mime(self) -> &'static str { ... }
    pub fn from_extension(ext: &str) -> Option<Self> { ... }
}
pub enum FileType { Text, Image(ImageKind), Pdf, Notebook }
```

This forces every consumer to handle the enum exhaustively and makes adding AVIF a single edit-and-recompile.

## Filed from QA review dispatch
