2ebb6ff5-54c2-4988-bae0-b56cc67f6cee.title: Phase 1 spec: tools — file operations (Read/Write/Edit/NotebookEdit/Glob/Grep) [CC parity]
2ebb6ff5-54c2-4988-bae0-b56cc67f6cee.description:
## Goal

Extract a behavioral spec for this subsystem by reading Claude Code's TypeScript source. **Output**: update this issue body with a markdown spec pinning down each testable contract (input → expected output, edge cases, error paths). No Rust yet — that is Phase 2.

Parent audit: #523.

## Claude Code source — read these

- `tools/FileReadTool/FileReadTool.ts` (1183 lines) — read with offset/limit, image-as-base64, PDF passthrough
- `tools/FileReadTool/imageProcessor.ts` (94 lines) — PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP base64 encoder
- `tools/FileReadTool/limits.ts` (92 lines) — per-tool token cap + truncation messaging
- `tools/FileEditTool/FileEditTool.ts` (625 lines) — string replace, fail on missing old_string
- `tools/FileEditTool/utils.ts` (775 lines) — diff helpers
- `tools/FileWriteTool/FileWriteTool.ts` (434 lines) — write with parent-dir create
- `tools/GlobTool/GlobTool.ts` (198 lines) — glob-pattern file search
- `tools/GrepTool/GrepTool.ts` (577 lines) — regex + context lines
- `tools/NotebookEditTool/NotebookEditTool.ts` (490 lines) — cell update by `cell_id` with `cell_number` fallback

## OpenClaudia counterpart

- `src/tools/file/read.rs` (336 lines) — read + offset/limit at line 274, images 40-56
- `src/tools/file/edit.rs` (123 lines)
- `src/tools/file/write.rs` (75 lines)
- `src/tools/file/list.rs` (34 lines)
- `src/tools/file/notebook.rs` (304 lines)
- **missing** — no GlobTool equivalent; file discovery falls through to bash — filed as gap #567
- **missing** — no GrepTool; only described in bash tool prompt — filed as gap #568

## Gaps

These CC features are absent from OC. Each has been filed as a separate issue:

- **GlobTool missing** — filed as #567: "Add native GlobTool (parity with CC tools/GlobTool/GlobTool.ts)"
- **GrepTool missing** — filed as #568: "Add native GrepTool with regex + context lines (parity with CC tools/GrepTool/GrepTool.ts)"

---

## Behavioral spec

### Behavior 1: `read` with `offset` + `limit` returns correct 1-indexed line slice

**CC**: `tools/FileReadTool/FileReadTool.ts:1020-1085` — `callInner()` text path; offset default is `1`, converted to 0-based via `lineOffset = offset === 0 ? 0 : offset - 1`; calls `readFileInRange(resolvedFilePath, lineOffset, limit, ...)`. Output field `startLine` is set to the raw `offset` (1-indexed). Line numbers prepended by `addLineNumbers` use `startLine` as the base.

**OC**: `src/tools/file/read.rs:274-336` — `read_text_file()`; offset parameter is also treated as 1-indexed: `offset = args.get("offset").as_u64().map_or(0, |n| n.saturating_sub(1))`, converting to 0-based for `.skip(offset)`. Output annotates each line as `(i + 1)` (original line number). Semantics match CC.

**Input**: `{ file_path: string, offset?: int >= 1, limit?: int >= 1 }`

**Output**: Lines `[offset .. offset+limit-1]` (1-indexed), each prefixed with its 1-indexed line number. Summary suffix appended: `(showing lines X-Y of Z total)` when offset or limit is present.

**Edge cases**:
- `offset=0`: CC treats as "start of file" (line 1020: `lineOffset = offset === 0 ? 0 : offset - 1`). OC: `saturating_sub(1)` on `0u64` yields `0` — matches CC (reads from beginning).
- `offset` beyond end of file: CC returns empty content with `startLine=offset` and emits a `<system-reminder>` warning that the file has fewer lines. OC: `.skip(offset)` yields an empty iterator; shows `(showing lines N-N of M total)` with empty body — no explicit warning.
- `limit=0`: CC input schema rejects (`z.number().int().positive()` — errorCode not yet assigned but validation fails). OC: `0u64` cast to `usize` yields `0`; `.take(0)` returns empty result — no validation-layer rejection.

**Error path**: File not found → CC: `throw new Error("File does not exist. ...")` with `Did you mean X?` suggestion. OC: `fs::read_to_string` returns `Err`; returns `(format!("Failed to read file '{path}': {e}"), true)` — no similar-file suggestion.

---

### Behavior 2: `read` on PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP returns base64-encoded image with size enforcement

**CC**: `tools/FileReadTool/FileReadTool.ts:865-891` — `callInner()` image branch; `IMAGE_EXTENSIONS = Set(['png','jpg','jpeg','gif','webp'])` (line 188); calls `readImageWithTokenBudget()` (lines 1097-1183). Reads file once, applies `maybeResizeAndDownsampleImageBuffer`, then checks `estimatedTokens = Math.ceil(base64.length * 0.125)` against `maxTokens` (default 25000 from `limits.ts:18`). If over budget, calls `compressImageBufferWithTokenLimit`; fallback is 400×400 JPEG at quality 20. Returns `{ type:'image', file:{ base64, type: 'image/X', originalSize, dimensions? } }`.

**OC**: `src/tools/file/read.rs:40-56` — `read_image_file()`; reads file bytes, base64-encodes with `STANDARD` engine, returns `[Image: {name} ({size} bytes, {mime}) - base64 data included for vision-capable models]\n{b64}`. No resize, no compression, no token cap enforcement.

**Input**: `{ file_path: string }` where extension ∈ `{png, jpg, jpeg, gif, webp}` (case-insensitive).

**Output (CC)**: Structured `{ type:'image', file:{ base64, type, originalSize, dimensions? } }` sent as `image` block to provider. **Output (OC)**: Plain text string with base64 inline; sent as text.

**Edge cases**:
- Empty image file: CC throws `"Image file is empty: {filePath}"` (line 1109). OC: `fs::read()` succeeds with 0 bytes; base64 encodes to empty string; no error surfaced.
- Image over token budget: CC compresses aggressively, then falls back to 400×400 JPEG at q=20. OC: no cap — returns full base64 regardless of size.

**Error path**: File unreadable → CC: propagates ENOENT to outer handler (similar-file suggestion). OC: returns `(format!("Failed to read image file '{path}': {e}"), true)`.

---

### Behavior 3: `read` on a PDF delegates to pdftotext (OC) or native PDF API (CC)

**CC**: `tools/FileReadTool/FileReadTool.ts:893-1017` — `callInner()` PDF branch. Checks `isPDFSupported()` (model capability); if supported and file ≤ `PDF_EXTRACT_SIZE_THRESHOLD`, calls `readPDF()` which returns base64, sent as `document` block. If pages specified, calls `extractPDFPages()` → JPEG images sent as `image` blocks. If PDF has > `PDF_AT_MENTION_INLINE_THRESHOLD` pages without a range → throws requiring explicit `pages` parameter.

**OC**: `src/tools/file/read.rs:89-174` — `read_pdf_file()`; checks for `pdftotext` binary via `which`; if absent, returns actionable install instructions (not a panic). If `pages` omitted and PDF > 10 pages (via `pdfinfo`), returns an error requiring a range. Runs `pdftotext -f {first} -l {last} {path} -` for ranged reads; returns extracted text (not base64).

**Input**: `{ file_path: string (.pdf), pages?: string (e.g. "1-5", "3") }`

**Output (CC)**: `{ type:'pdf', file:{ filePath, base64, originalSize } }` for full PDFs; `{ type:'parts', ... }` for extracted pages. **Output (OC)**: Plain text extracted by pdftotext.

**Edge cases**:
- `pages` param with single page (e.g. `"3"`): CC parses via `parsePDFPageRange` → `{firstPage:3, lastPage:3}`. OC: `parse_page_range("3")` → `(3,3)` — both agree on single-page semantics.
- PDF > page threshold without `pages`: CC throws if > `PDF_AT_MENTION_INLINE_THRESHOLD` (constant from `apiLimits`). OC: uses hardcoded `MAX_PDF_PAGES_WITHOUT_RANGE = 10` (line 124).
- pdftotext absent (OC only): returns install instructions as error result — not a panic.
- Image-only PDF (no selectable text): OC returns `"PDF '{path}' produced no extractable text (may be image-based)."` as a non-error result. CC: renders as base64 document block regardless.

**Error path**: File not found → CC: ENOENT propagated to outer handler. OC: `fs::read_to_string` returns Err inside `read_pdf_file`; returns error string with `is_error=true`.

---

### Behavior 4: `edit` with `old_string` not found returns an explicit error (not silent no-op)

**CC**: `tools/FileEditTool/FileEditTool.ts:315-327` — `validateInput()`; uses `findActualString(file, old_string)` (quote normalization); if `null`, returns `{ result:false, behavior:'ask', message:"String to replace not found in file.\nString: {old_string}", errorCode:8 }`.

**OC**: `src/tools/file/edit.rs:74-82` — `execute_edit_file()`; uses `content.contains(old_string)` directly; if false returns `("Could not find the specified text in '{path}'. Make sure old_string matches exactly.", true)`.

**Input**: `{ path/file_path: string, old_string: string (not in file), new_string: string }`

**Output**: Error result with descriptive message; no file is modified.

**Edge cases**:
- CC performs quote normalization via `findActualString` (handles curly ↔ straight quote substitution) before the not-found check. OC uses exact byte match; no normalization.
- `old_string === new_string`: CC catches this before the not-found check (`errorCode:1`). OC: would still reach `contains()` and succeed if string is present, making a no-op write.

**Error path**: OC returns `(message, true)` (error flag set). CC returns validation failure with `behavior:'ask'` which pauses for user confirmation before surfacing the error.

---

### Behavior 5: `edit` with `replace_all=true` replaces every occurrence atomically

**CC**: `tools/FileEditTool/FileEditTool.ts:329-343` — `validateInput()`; counts `matches = file.split(actualOldString).length - 1`; if `matches > 1 && !replace_all` → errorCode 9. In `call()` (line 482-488): `getPatchForEdit({ replaceAll: replace_all })` which calls `file.replaceAll(actualOldString, new_string)` when `replace_all=true`.

**OC**: `src/tools/file/edit.rs:84-95` — counts occurrences; if `count > 1` always returns an error requiring a more specific `old_string`. OC does NOT implement `replace_all` — it rejects any multi-occurrence match unconditionally.

**Input**: `{ file_path: string, old_string: string (N > 1 occurrences), new_string: string, replace_all: true }`

**Output (CC)**: All N occurrences replaced; file written atomically. **Output (OC)**: Error — "Found N occurrences... Please provide a more specific old_string".

**Edge cases**:
- `replace_all=false` with multiple matches: CC returns errorCode 9 (ask user). OC: same multi-occurrence rejection (no distinction between true/false).
- Single occurrence with `replace_all=true`: CC: replaces the one occurrence (replaceAll on 1 match). OC: count=1, proceeds with `replacen(old_string, new_string, 1)` — result is correct but `replace_all` flag is silently ignored.

**Error path**: OC always returns error for N>1 occurrences. The `replace_all` contract is **OC: missing for the multi-occurrence path**.

---

### Behavior 6: `write` creates parent directories when missing

**CC**: `tools/FileWriteTool/FileWriteTool.ts:254` — `call()`; calls `await getFsImplementation().mkdir(dir)` before writing; this is `mkdir -p` semantics (recursive). Confirmed at line 230: `const dir = dirname(fullFilePath)`.

**OC**: `src/tools/file/write.rs:54-59` — `execute_write_file()`; calls `fs::create_dir_all(parent)` before `fs::write`. Matches CC behavior.

**Input**: `{ path/file_path: "/nonexistent/deep/path/file.txt", content: string }`

**Output**: File created at path; all intermediate directories created. Success message: `"Successfully wrote {N} bytes to '{path}'"`.

**Edge cases**:
- Path with no parent component (e.g. relative bare filename): OC checks `!parent.as_os_str().is_empty()` before calling `create_dir_all` — skips for bare filenames. CC: `dirname(fullFilePath)` on an absolute path always yields a parent; both handle this.
- Parent already exists: `create_dir_all` is idempotent — no error.
- Permission denied creating directory: OC returns `("Failed to create directories: {e}", true)`. CC: `mkdir` error propagates and throws.

**Error path**: OC: `create_dir_all` error → returns error string. CC: `getFsImplementation().mkdir()` error throws, propagated up to tool framework.

---

### Behavior 7: `notebook_edit` `replace` updates correct cell by `cell_id`; falls back to `cell_number`

**CC**: `tools/NotebookEditTool/NotebookEditTool.ts:351-368` — `call()`; first tries `notebook.cells.findIndex(cell => cell.id === cell_id)` (exact match on cell's `id` field). If `-1`, tries `parseCellId(cell_id)` for numeric index fallback. For `insert`: position = `cellIndex + 1` (after the referenced cell).

**OC**: `src/tools/file/notebook.rs:143-155` — `execute_notebook_edit()`; `find_cell_by_id()` (line 32-38) searches by `id` field; if not found, falls back to `cell_number_arg` (separate parameter, not a fallback parse of `cell_id`). CC exposes only `cell_id`; OC exposes both `cell_id` and `cell_number` as distinct input fields.

**Input (CC)**: `{ notebook_path, cell_id?: string, new_source: string, cell_type?: enum, edit_mode?: 'replace'|'insert'|'delete' }`

**Input (OC)**: `{ notebook_path, cell_id?: string, cell_number?: int, new_source: string, cell_type?: string, edit_mode?: string }`

**Output**: Modified notebook written back; success message with cell count.

**Edge cases**:
- `cell_id` not found + no fallback: CC (validateInput line 275-289): returns errorCode 8 `"Cell with ID ... not found"`. OC: returns `("No cell with id '{id}' found in notebook.", true)`.
- `cell_id` absent for `replace` or `delete`: CC errorCode 7. OC: `"replace requires either 'cell_id' or 'cell_number'."`.
- Insert without `cell_id`: CC inserts at index 0. OC: same (`insert_at = 0` when no cell_id and no cell_number).
- Replace at index == cells.length: CC silently promotes to `insert` (line 372-376). OC: returns out-of-bounds error.
- Code cell replace: CC resets `execution_count = null` and `outputs = []` (line 420-423). OC: does NOT reset execution_count/outputs on replace (line 189: only `source` and optionally `cell_type` are updated).

**Error path**: Notebook not valid JSON → CC returns `{ error: 'Notebook is not valid JSON.' }` in data. OC returns `("Failed to parse notebook ... as JSON: {e}", true)`.

---

### Behavior 8: File exceeding per-tool token cap surfaces explicit truncation message with offset/limit guidance

**CC**: `tools/FileReadTool/limits.ts:18` — default `maxTokens = 25000`. `tools/FileReadTool/FileReadTool.ts:755-772` — `validateContentTokens()`; uses `roughTokenCountEstimationForFileType` as a fast pre-check; if estimate > `maxTokens/4`, calls `countTokensWithAPI` for accurate count; if over cap throws `MaxFileReadTokenExceededError` (line 181-184): `"File content ({N} tokens) exceeds maximum allowed tokens ({max}). Use offset and limit parameters to read specific portions of the file, or search for specific content instead of reading the whole file."` Also: `maxSizeBytes` (default from `MAX_OUTPUT_SIZE`) checked against total file size before reading (line 827-835 for notebooks; enforced via `readFileInRange` byte cap for text).

**OC**: `src/tools/file/read.rs:319-332` — `read_text_file()`; hardcoded byte cap of `100_000` chars on the *formatted* output string; if over, returns `"...{safe_truncate(&result, 100_000)}...\n(file truncated, {N} total chars){suffix}"` as a non-error result. No token estimation; no per-file-type accounting; truncation is silent (not an error).

**Input**: Any file read call where the resulting content exceeds the cap.

**Output (CC)**: Error result with token count and `offset`/`limit` guidance. **Output (OC)**: Silently truncated content at 100,000 chars with a note — no error flag, no offset guidance.

**Edge cases**:
- Large file with explicit `offset+limit` that fits within cap: CC still applies `maxSizeBytes` to *total file size* (not slice size) — can error even if the slice would fit. OC: applies byte cap to the *formatted* output (post-slice), not the raw file — consistent with explicit range reads.
- `CLAUDE_CODE_FILE_READ_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` env var: CC overrides the token cap. OC: no equivalent env override.
- Notebooks over size cap: CC throws with jq guidance (line 827-835). OC: `read_notebook_file` has no size cap — returns full content.

**Error path (CC)**: `MaxFileReadTokenExceededError` thrown → becomes tool error result. **Error path (OC)**: Truncation is surfaced as a non-error string — model may not recognize it needs to retry with offset/limit.

---

## Done when

- This issue body has been edited to contain a markdown spec, one section per behavior above
- Each behavior section names the function(s) on both sides (or marks the OC side missing)
- Every gap above has been filed as its own issue and linked here
- The matching Phase 2 issue is unblocked

2ed72ee7-8105-49db-833f-85fe1f49e397.title: get_adapter unknown-provider fallback hides typos by silently using OpenAI
2ed72ee7-8105-49db-833f-85fe1f49e397.description:
## Severity
Minor
## Dimension
error-handling
## Location
src/providers/mod.rs:127-148
## Violation
get_adapter returns Box<dyn ProviderAdapter> with a warn-and-fallback for unknown providers:

  other => {
      tracing::warn!(provider = other, "Unknown provider — falling back to OpenAI-compatible adapter.");
      Box::new(OpenAIAdapter::new())
  }

The fallback is invoked at proxy.rs:1174 (adapter for passthrough auth headers) and pipeline.rs:246 (chat_endpoint construction). A typo in config.yaml's proxy.target ('anthrop1c' instead of 'anthropic') results in: OpenAI-shaped requests, OpenAI auth headers, but sent to the Anthropic base URL. The upstream returns 401 with no hint that the local config has a typo. The warn! is the only signal and may be lost in volume.
## Mandated refactor
Validate proxy.target at config load against the known-providers set; reject unknown values with a startup error. Or make get_adapter() return Result<Box<dyn ProviderAdapter>, ProviderError::Unknown(name)> and propagate at call sites. Silent fallback is acceptable only if the unknown-provider is explicitly listed as 'unknown-compatible'.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

2f2870be-bfb8-4a6c-aa12-ebd705f4c9ae.title: subagent: hard-coded .openclaudia/permissions.json path couples PermissionManager to cwd
2f2870be-bfb8-4a6c-aa12-ebd705f4c9ae.description:
## Severity
Minor
## Dimension
decoupling
## Location
src/subagent.rs:789-793 (run_subagent)
## Violation
```rust
let permission_mgr = crate::permissions::PermissionManager::new(
    std::path::PathBuf::from(".openclaudia/permissions.json"),
    true,
    app_config.permissions.default_allow.clone(),
);
```

The subagent constructs its own PermissionManager from a hard-coded relative path. Three problems:

1. Temporal coupling to current working directory — a worktree-isolated subagent (which sets `cwd` indirectly via prompt injection at lines 709-715) will read/write the LEADER's permissions file, not its own.
2. A fresh PermissionManager per subagent invocation can't see in-memory "always allow" decisions made by the parent — each agent rebuilds an empty cache and re-prompts the user.
3. The choice of `true` for the second arg (presumably `enabled`) is not documented inline.

`Coordinator` is being built precisely to own a single shared PermissionManager (see coordinator/mod.rs:46 LeaderPermissionBridge), but `run_subagent` ignores it.

## Mandated refactor
Pass `&PermissionManager` into `run_subagent` as a parameter (either directly or as a field of `AppHandles`). Let the caller — eventually the Coordinator — supply the shared instance. Remove the hard-coded relative path entirely.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

136eaba1-312a-432b-b1d6-595b260f6213.author: lOrm
136eaba1-312a-432b-b1d6-595b260f6213.content:

The caller (Coordinator / leader CLI) already owns one — the LeaderPermissionBridge in coordinator/mod.rs:46 was designed for exactly this. The change also fixes (a) worktree subagents currently writing to the leader's permissions file, (b) lost in-memory 'always allow' decisions across subagent invocations, and (c) the undocumented true literal for the second arg.

**Blocking:** src/subagent.rs is reserved scope. Defer to a future unrestricted pass.

2fb95cab-13e0-4909-94e4-f24ff17e8649.title: Compaction threshold_tokens_for integer math loses precision; compact() can yield higher tokens post-compact
2fb95cab-13e0-4909-94e4-f24ff17e8649.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

Dimension: Functional Correctness (1) / Cognitive Readability (4)

Location: src/compaction.rs:592-597 (threshold_tokens_for), 423-456 (compact_with_hint), 429-438 (post-compact verification).

Violation:
1. threshold_tokens_for does 'max_context_tokens / 1000 * ratio_millths'. For max_context_tokens = 16_385 (GPT-3.5) and threshold = 0.85: (16385/1000)*850 = 16*850 = 13600. True value is 16385*0.85 = 13927. The approximation under-counts by 327 tokens — the system thinks it has LESS room than it does, triggering compaction earlier than configured. The comment says 'avoid usize as f32 precision loss' but for typical context sizes (200K), f32 has ~24 bits of mantissa — 200000 * 0.85 is exactly representable in f32. The 'precision loss' claim is wrong; the integer math IS the precision loss.

2. Post-compact check at line 429 uses '>=' — if new_tokens == original_tokens (no change), the code returns Err('Compaction did not reduce token count'), leaving request.messages in the COMPACTED state (line 424 already replaced them) but returning an error. The caller now has a mutated request AND an error — worst of both worlds. No rollback.

3. target_tokens = threshold_tokens / 2 (line 251) is an arbitrary heuristic that doesn't consider how many tokens were actually freed. A request 1.1x over threshold gets compacted to half threshold — wasteful. A request 10x over threshold still only compacts to half threshold — may still exceed limits after compaction.

Mandated Refactor:
1. Use f64 arithmetic for threshold calculation. 'max_context_tokens as f64 * threshold as f64' then 'as usize' with saturating_cast. f64 has 53 bits of mantissa, zero precision issue for any realistic context size.
2. Snapshot original messages BEFORE the replacement at line 424; if the post-check fails, restore request.messages = original_messages so the caller sees an unchanged request.
3. target_tokens = current_tokens.saturating_sub(tokens_to_free) — use the already-computed tokens_to_free rather than reaching for max_context/2.
4. If a single compaction pass is insufficient, loop (up to a max of 3 attempts) or log a hard error that the model input genuinely cannot fit.

2fc8ff21-7f65-4ba1-8034-73b41a2bc685.title: accumulator.rs: AnthropicToolAccumulator::to_openai_tool_calls_json allocates arguments as STRING not JSON — double-encoding bug waiting to happen
2fc8ff21-7f65-4ba1-8034-73b41a2bc685.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

**Dimension:** Functional Correctness / Architectural Alignment

**Location:** /home/doll/OpenClaudia/src/tools/accumulator.rs lines 273-293 (to_openai_tool_calls_json), 64-82 (ToolCallAccumulator::finalize)

**Violation:**
OpenAI's ChatCompletion schema uses 'arguments': STRING (serialized JSON). Anthropic's schema uses 'input': OBJECT. The accumulator's to_openai_tool_calls_json at line 282 outputs:
  'function': { 'name': name, 'arguments': input_json }
where input_json is a String that was built by appending input_json_delta fragments (accumulator.rs:204). So the OpenAI-shaped value looks correct — BUT input_json is NOT validated as well-formed JSON at any point. If Anthropic streamed two 'input_json_delta' fragments that together produce malformed JSON (e.g. a streamed tool-use that was cancelled mid-stream, or a provider bug), the 'arguments' field contains bad JSON that the next conversion step (providers.rs Anthropic->OpenAI) treats as a String and re-wraps into a double-encoded mess.

Additionally:
1. **Partial tool calls can reach the consumer.** ToolCallAccumulator::finalize at line 68 filters only by !tc.id.is_empty() && !tc.function_name.is_empty() — an incomplete arguments string (e.g. '{"path":') passes through and crashes tool execution at mod.rs:805 where from_str parses it.
2. **process_delta's index slot growth is unbounded.** Lines 36-39: 'while self.tool_calls.len() <= index { push(default) }' — an upstream that streams index=1_000_000 will allocate a 1M-entry Vec. No cap.

**Mandated Refactor:**
1. Validate JSON closure at finalize(): serde_json::from_str::<Value>(&input_json) — on error, mark the ToolCall as broken and return a ToolError::MalformedToolCall rather than forwarding garbage.
2. Cap index to some sane limit (e.g. 100) — reject streams with out-of-range indices.
3. For Anthropic-shaped payloads, the field should BE a Value (object), not a String, to eliminate the double-encoding. Add explicit shape tests for round-tripping Anthropic->OpenAI->Anthropic tool_use.

e9a2df9c-396d-4ae3-8a53-affc31a81671.author: lOrm
e9a2df9c-396d-4ae3-8a53-affc31a81671.content: Fixed in src/tools/accumulator.rs: to_openai_tool_calls_json now canonicalizes arguments via Self::canonicalize_arguments. Pre-fix the raw streamed input_json was embedded verbatim with no validation: (a) empty streams emitted '""' (invalid JSON); (b) truncated streams propagated to convert_messages_to_anthropic where unwrap_or_else(|_| json!({})) silently replaced them with {} and dropped the model's intent. Post-fix: empty/whitespace -> canonical '{}'; valid JSON round-trips through serde_json::to_string for byte-stable output; malformed JSON collapses to '{}' with a tracing::warn! so the corruption is observable. Raw fragment remains accessible via finalize_tool_calls. Added 4 regression tests (empty, quoted-string, nested-object, malformed). Tests: 1338 pass (baseline 1334 + 4 new). cargo clippy --lib --tests -- -D warnings exits 0. Out of scope: index-cap and finalize() JSON-closure validation — those touch the OpenAI->internal ToolCallAccumulator path; separate ticket if still needed.

30c84a35-e4a5-4b46-9246-68ef2246f062.title: execute_notebook_edit cell_type for replace is silently allowed to switch types without resetting fields
30c84a35-e4a5-4b46-9246-68ef2246f062.description:
## Severity
Minor

## Dimension
Functional Correctness / Tell-Dont-Ask

## Location
src/tools/file/notebook.rs:183-186 (replace branch cell_type assignment)

## Violation
```rust
cells[index]["source"] = source_to_line_array(new_source);
if let Some(ct) = cell_type {
    cells[index]["cell_type"] = json!(ct);
}
```

If the cell was previously a "code" cell with `outputs: [...]` and `execution_count: 5`, and the replace passes `cell_type: "markdown"`, the cell's stale `outputs` and `execution_count` fields remain. Markdown cells should NOT have those fields per nbformat spec — Jupyter clients reading the file may reject or display the cell oddly. Inverse case: replacing a markdown cell with a code cell does NOT add the required `outputs: []` and `execution_count: null` fields.

Worse, the cell_type value is accepted verbatim — there's no allowlist. `cell_type: "raw"` (a valid nbformat type) and `cell_type: "garbage"` (invalid) are both accepted; the latter produces a corrupt notebook.

## Mandated refactor
1. Validate cell_type against ["code", "markdown", "raw"] at extraction time.
2. When the cell_type changes on a replace, run the same field-normalization that insert uses (line 218-226):
   - For new type "code": ensure outputs=[], execution_count=null exist.
   - For new type "markdown" or "raw": remove outputs and execution_count if present.
3. Centralize the "build a well-formed cell of type T" logic in one helper used by both insert and replace-with-cell_type paths (DRY — currently duplicated).

325b128b-069d-4e06-b8fa-cfc74d3a969b.title: parse_command_front_matter: fragile string slicing can panic on multibyte chars
325b128b-069d-4e06-b8fa-cfc74d3a969b.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

**Dimension**: Functional Correctness (off-by-one / panics on adversarial input)

**Location**: src/plugins/mod.rs:158-202 (parse_command_front_matter)

**Violation**:
```rust
let after_first = &trimmed[3..].trim_start_matches(['\r', '\n']);
after_first.find("\n---").map_or_else(..., |end_pos| {
    let yaml_block = &after_first[..end_pos];
    let body_start = end_pos + 4; // skip \n---
    let body = after_first[body_start..]...
})
```
Byte-index slicing into Rust strings panics if the index lands mid-UTF-8-codepoint. A command markdown file with '---' in the middle of a multibyte character sequence — while unusual — can cause a runtime panic. More realistically:
- If after_first has length exactly end_pos+3 (ends with "\n---" and nothing after), body_start = end_pos+4 OVERFLOWS the buffer length by 1 → panic.
- trim_start_matches(['\r', '\n']) returns a &str, but then after_first[body_start..] is indexed as bytes; if the trimmed slice contains any non-ASCII bytes between the --- markers, the start-of-yaml assumption fails.

**Mandated Refactor**:
1. Use `str::split_once("\n---")` returning Option<(&str, &str)> — works entirely on char boundaries.
2. Bounds-check body_start <= after_first.len() before indexing.
3. Add a fuzzer input corpus (`cargo fuzz`) for parse_command_front_matter with adversarial markdown.
4. Add property tests ensuring no panic for arbitrary UTF-8 content around the --- delimiter.

4d5846a0-cec6-4a88-8419-d6bcd954cb0a.author: lOrm
4d5846a0-cec6-4a88-8419-d6bcd954cb0a.content:

  let body_start = end_pos + 4;                                      // unchecked add

333d9a88-4759-46e3-8564-d0028a1ca785.title: skills::parse_skill_file uses byte-indexed slicing without UTF-8 boundary checks

72fc9cc1-ebb8-447e-9502-a8435e1b0389.author: lOrm
72fc9cc1-ebb8-447e-9502-a8435e1b0389.content: Reviewed claim — not a bug. rest.find("---") returns the BYTE OFFSET of the start of "---", which is 3 ASCII bytes (0x2D). The bytes at positions end, end+1, end+2 are therefore ALL ASCII dashes; end+3 lands on the byte immediately after the last dash, which is a valid UTF-8 char boundary by construction (the next codepoint MUST start there). Verified with rustc: parsing `---\n吉\n---𠮷` succeeds with body="𠮷". The QA report's scenario "find(\"---\") byte offset sits before non-ASCII content, splitting a codepoint" is impossible: find returns the position WHERE the matched substring begins, and the matched substring is itself 3 ASCII bytes. The only way end+3 could split a codepoint is if find returned an offset inside a multi-byte char, but Rust's str::find guarantees char-boundary offsets. Closing as not-a-bug — no code change warranted.

3354eb96-fb85-4a87-83db-6129ae9b0bb5.title: QA: hook input serialization failure silently sends empty stdin (run)
3354eb96-fb85-4a87-83db-6129ae9b0bb5.description:
## Severity
Minor
## Dimension
error-handling
## Location
src/hooks/mod.rs:411
## Violation
The hook input passed to every command hook is serialized with a
swallowed error:
```rust
let input_json = serde_json::to_string(input).unwrap_or_default();
```
If `HookInput` ever fails to serialize (custom serializer panic, locale
issue, etc.), `unwrap_or_default()` produces `String::default()` =
empty string. Hooks then receive `""` on stdin and have no way to know
the input was lost — they may default-allow on missing fields or hang
waiting for data. The actual error is silently discarded; no `tracing`
entry, no metric, no audit-log row.
## Mandated refactor
Replace with explicit error handling: on serialization failure, log
`error!(error = %e, "Failed to serialize HookInput; refusing to run
hook")` and return `HookResult::denied(...)` for pre-tool-use hooks (or
emit a dedicated error variant for post-tool hooks). Better: change the
hook contract so serialization happens once at HookEngine startup or
construct-time, and serialization errors propagate up at config-load
time rather than per-call.

335b04c7-ee10-43e4-bb20-bfcd67b66fd7.title: todo.rs + file/mod.rs: global singletons with std::sync::Mutex — denies per-session isolation, tests rely on escape hatches
335b04c7-ee10-43e4-bb20-bfcd67b66fd7.description:
Current state: 

Desired state: 

Reason: 

**Dimension:** Structural Modularity / Testability

**Location:** /home/doll/OpenClaudia/src/tools/todo.rs lines 17-18 (TODO_LIST LazyLock), 85-90 (lock-then-clone_from); /home/doll/OpenClaudia/src/tools/file/mod.rs lines 26-28 (READ_TRACKER LazyLock); /home/doll/OpenClaudia/src/tools/bash/mod.rs lines 266-267 (BACKGROUND_SHELLS LazyLock); /home/doll/OpenClaudia/src/tools/chainlink.rs line 7 (CHAINLINK_INSTALL_SHOWN AtomicBool)

**Violation:**
Four separate global singletons hold per-session state:
1. TODO_LIST (Mutex<Vec<TodoItem>>) — only ONE todo list exists in the entire process.
2. READ_TRACKER (Mutex<Vec<PathBuf>>) — only ONE read-tracker.
3. BACKGROUND_SHELLS (Mutex<HashMap<String, BackgroundShell>>) — all shells share one namespace.
4. CHAINLINK_INSTALL_SHOWN (AtomicBool) — 'once per session' but singleton means once per PROCESS.

Consequences:
1. **Multi-session parallelism is impossible.** Two concurrent sessions share the same todo list, leaked background shells, and the 'install shown' flag. This breaks any future plan to run subagents in parallel processes within the same binary.
2. **Tests cannot isolate.** reset_read_tracker exists at mod.rs:62 with #[doc(hidden)] to allow tests to reset — the presence of this escape hatch is proof the design is wrong. Tests that mutate the tracker interfere with each other when run in parallel; in practice developers will add #[serial_test] bandaids.
3. **No lifecycle.** On session end, nothing clears these structures. BACKGROUND_SHELLS leaks shells permanently until they self-finish.
4. **Difficulty of cleanup on panic.** A tool call that panics while holding a mutex poisons the global permanently — get_output() at mod.rs:172 even uses unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner) to paper over this.

**Mandated Refactor:**

36a40b14-2b4e-4e5d-8d6f-5f3b4bc11325.title: Concurrent MCP stdio requests can interleave responses and break correlation
36a40b14-2b4e-4e5d-8d6f-5f3b4bc11325.description:
## Severity
Major
## Dimension
concurrency
## Location
src/mcp.rs:180-264 (StdioTransport::request)
## Violation
`request` takes the `child` mutex to write the request and the newline, then drops it (line 219), then takes the separate `reader` mutex to read a single line. With two concurrent `request` calls A and B:

1. Caller A locks `child`, writes A request, drops `child`.
2. Caller B locks `child`, writes B request, drops `child`.
3. Caller A locks `reader`, reads first line — may be B's response.
4. The `id` check (line 243-248) triggers, A errors out, B's reader future takes A's response on a later read.

```rust
drop(child);

// Read response from the persistent BufReader with size limit.
let line = {
    let mut reader = self.reader.lock().await;
    ...
```

Splitting the two mutexes breaks request/response correlation under concurrency.
## Mandated refactor
Either (a) hold the `child` lock across the entire request+response (simple, serializes all calls), or (b) implement a response router: a background task reads lines, parses `id`, and dispatches to a `HashMap<u64, oneshot::Sender<Value>>` registered by `request`. Option (b) is the correct JSON-RPC-over-stdio shape.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

## Severity
Minor
## Dimension
error-handling
## Location
src/tui/app.rs:568, 629, multiple call sites
## Violation
Every call to save_session swallows the Result with `let _ =`:

```rust
let _ = save_session(&self.chat_session);
```

This pattern appears at lines 568 (App::run exit), 629 (ResponseDone), 813, 818 (undo/redo), and others. A disk-full or permission-denied condition silently loses every chat message from this point forward — the user only discovers the data loss when they later try to /resume and the saved session is missing or stale.

The TUI is interactive and the session is the user's primary artifact. Failing to save is a high-importance event that deserves at least a user-visible notification.

Either:

2. Track save failures in self.last_save_error and render the error in the status bar so it persists until the next successful save.

The fire_notification_hook helper already exists for the API-error path — reuse it for save failures too.

38536a89-3cba-4a44-902a-3a5e6395bede.title: MigrationOutcome::Failed wraps anyhow::Error which is not Clone limiting reporting

39243465-c5c2-4b07-aea3-2aa2ad05f3b2.title: QA: hook deep_merge concatenates arrays unconditionally, enabling allowlist amplification
39243465-c5c2-4b07-aea3-2aa2ad05f3b2.description:
## Severity
Minor
## Dimension
security
## Location
src/hooks/merge.rs:75-90
## Violation
`deep_merge` always concatenates arrays:
```rust
match (target, source) {
    (Value::Object(target_map), Value::Object(source_map)) => { ... }
    (Value::Array(target_arr), Value::Array(source_arr)) => {
        target_arr.extend(source_arr.iter().cloned());
    }
    (target, source) => {
        *target = source.clone();
    }
}
```
This is called from `load_claude_settings` (claude_compat.rs:108-184)
which loads user-global -> project -> project-local ->
managed-enterprise settings in that order. The
`allowedTools` array (extracted at claude_compat.rs:162-170) and the
`hooks` arrays are concatenated across all layers — there is no
"replace" semantic, no per-layer ACL, and no way for an enterprise
managed-settings file to **remove** a permission granted at user level.
A user can append `allowedTools` entries the enterprise tier intended to
forbid.
## Mandated refactor
Make the merge strategy explicit per top-level key. `allowedTools` and
`disallowedTools` should be unioned-then-filtered: union of all
`allowedTools`, minus union of all `disallowedTools` from any later
(higher-priority) layer. Hook arrays should similarly support
`disabledHooks` from higher layers. Document the merge semantics in
`load_claude_settings` and add tests covering "enterprise overrides
user".
## Filed from QA review dispatch

39d0cba4-ed67-4af6-9888-8cae54d06979.title: MCP HttpTransport drops response id mismatch detection
39d0cba4-ed67-4af6-9888-8cae54d06979.description:
## Severity
Major
## Dimension
error-handling
## Location
src/mcp.rs:298-338 (HttpTransport::request)
## Violation
`StdioTransport::request` validates that `response.id == id` (line 243-248) to detect protocol desync. The HTTP transport allocates and increments `request_id` (line 299) and embeds it in the JSON-RPC request — but never compares it against `response.id`. A buggy or hostile MCP HTTP server can return a response correlated to a different request and the client will silently accept it, returning the wrong tool's result to the caller.

```rust
let response: JsonRpcResponse = response
    .json()
    .await
    .map_err(|e| McpError::Protocol(format!("Failed to parse response: {e}")))?;

if let Some(error) = response.error {
    return Err(McpError::Protocol(format!(
        "RPC error {}: {}",
        error.code, error.message
    )));
}

Ok(response.result.unwrap_or(Value::Null))
```

The `id` field on `JsonRpcResponse` is parsed and discarded.
## Mandated refactor
After deserializing the response in `HttpTransport::request`, add the same id-mismatch guard as `StdioTransport`. Better, extract the request/response correlation into a shared helper to enforce DRY across transports.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

StdioTransport refactored to use the same variant (DRY). 4 new unit tests fix701_* (matching id OK, mismatched numeric id rejected with ResponseIdMismatch, non-numeric id rejected at JSON decode step, stdio mismatch surfaces ResponseIdMismatch). cargo test --lib: 1436 passed = 1432 baseline + 4 new. cargo clippy --lib --tests -- -D warnings: exit 0. 39eb52db-a257-4d1f-b1b1-63a198eeec51.title: Phase 1 spec: tools — workflow control (Plan/Worktree, TodoWrite, Skill, Sleep, ScheduleCron, ToolSearch) [CC parity]
39eb52db-a257-4d1f-b1b1-63a198eeec51.description:
# Phase 1 Spec: Workflow Control Tools — Plan/Worktree, TodoWrite, Skill, Sleep, ScheduleCron, ToolSearch

Parent audit: #523.

---

## Behavioral spec

### 1. Plan-mode enforcement: entering blocks write/edit/bash

**CC side** — `EnterPlanModeTool.ts:77-101`  
`call()` calls `handlePlanModeTransition` + `applyPermissionUpdate(prepareContextForPlanMode(...), {type:'setMode', mode:'plan'})`. Result injected into tool result instructs model: "DO NOT write or edit any files yet." `bash` and file-write tools are implicitly blocked by the permission mode switch; `EnterPlanModeTool` is disabled (returns early) if the session is already inside an agent context (`context.agentId` truthy).

**OC side** — `src/tools/plan_mode.rs:6-13`, `src/cli/repl/plan_mode.rs:7-67`, `src/session/state.rs:116-159`  
`execute_enter_plan_mode()` returns a JSON marker (`ENTER_PLAN_MODE_MARKER`). The REPL intercepts it in `process_tool_result_marker` (plan_mode.rs:295-297) and calls `handle_enter_plan_mode()`, which sets `chat_session.plan_mode = Some(PlanModeState{…})` and `chat_session.mode = AgentMode::Plan`. On every subsequent tool call, `check_plan_mode_restriction()` (plan_mode.rs:253-278) consults `is_tool_allowed_in_plan_mode()` (state.rs:116-159).

**Allowed list** (OC, state.rs:88-108): `read_file`, `list_files`, `grep`, `glob`, `search_files`, `file_index`, `file_search`, `lsp`, `web_fetch`, `web_search`, `web_browser`, `ask_user_question`, `task`, `agent_output`, `todo_read`, `chainlink`, `bash_output`.

**Blocked list** (OC, state.rs:110-111): `bash`, `edit_file`, `kill_shell`, `todo_write`.

**write_file special case** (OC, state.rs:131-159): allowed only if the `path` arg canonically resolves to the plan file created for this session (`.openclaudia/plans/<session_id>.md`).

**Contracts**:
- Input: model calls `enter_plan_mode` (no args).
- Expected output: string confirmation to model; session mode flips to Plan.
- Blocked tool call → error string: "Tool '{name}' is not available in plan mode. Only read-only tools … are allowed."
- Edge case: calling `enter_plan_mode` a second time (already in plan mode) is a no-op in OC (plan file already exists).
- CC gap: CC disallows calling `EnterPlanMode` from inside agent sub-contexts; OC has no equivalent guard.

---

### 2. Plan-mode exit: cleanly restores previous permissions

**CC side** — `ExitPlanModeV2Tool.ts:243-417`  
`call()` reads `prePlanMode` from `toolPermissionContext`, restores it (handling auto-mode gate and strippedDangerousRules), sets `hasExitedPlanMode=true`, sets `needsPlanModeExitAttachment=true`, writes plan to disk if user edited it, returns `{plan, isAgent, filePath, hasTaskTool, planWasEdited}`. Permission mode reverts to `prePlanMode ?? 'default'`. `validateInput` rejects calls when mode is not `'plan'` (errorCode 1). Plan can also be submitted to team-lead mailbox in teammate contexts (`isPlanModeRequired()`).

**OC side** — `src/cli/repl/plan_mode.rs:69-250`  
`handle_exit_plan_mode()` reads the plan file, prints it, prompts user `[y/n/edit]`. On 'y': clears `chat_session.plan_mode`, sets `chat_session.mode = AgentMode::Build`, injects approved plan as a system message. On 'n': stays in plan mode. On 'edit': opens `$EDITOR`, re-prompts. Returns `("...", approved: bool)`.

**Contracts**:
- Input: model calls `exit_plan_mode` (optional `allowed_prompts` array; each entry has `tool: "Bash"` + `prompt: string`).
- Expected output (success): mode becomes Build/default; approved plan text injected into context; tool restrictions lifted.
- Expected output (rejection): model stays in plan mode; receives rejection message.
- CC gap: OC restores permissions by clearing `plan_mode = None`; there is no `prePlanMode` snapshot, so OC cannot restore a non-default pre-plan permission context (e.g., auto mode). See gap issue filed below.
- Edge case: calling `exit_plan_mode` when not in plan mode → OC returns "Not currently in plan mode."
- Edge case: unrecognized user input → OC stays in plan mode with message.
- CC gap: OC `validateInput` is only enforced at the REPL marker level, not before the tool fires; CC rejects at schema validation before permissions.

---

### 3. cron_create stores schedule; cron_list reads it back

**CC side** — `ScheduleCronTool/CronCreateTool.ts:117-141`  
`call()`: validates cron expression via `parseCronExpression` (rejects invalid + future-miss), enforces `MAX_JOBS=50`, then calls `addCronTask(cron, prompt, recurring, effectiveDurable, teammateAgentId)`. Durable tasks persist to `.claude/scheduled_tasks.json`; non-durable live in session memory. Calls `setScheduledTasksEnabled(true)` to start tick loop. Returns `{id, humanSchedule, recurring, durable}`. `CronListTool` (separate file) reads from the same store via `listAllCronTasks()`.

`validateInput` error codes: 1=invalid expression, 2=no match in next year, 3=too many jobs (≥50), 4=durable+teammate unsupported.

**OC side** — `src/tools/cron.rs:143-258`  
`execute_cron_create()`: requires `name`, `schedule`, `prompt` args; validates expression (field count + per-field ranges); checks for duplicate `name`; appends to `ScheduleStore` loaded from `.openclaudia/schedules.json`; saves. `execute_cron_list()` re-loads and formats all entries. `execute_cron_delete()` removes by id or name.

**Contracts**:
- Input `cron_create`: `{cron: "M H DoM Mon DoW", prompt: string, recurring?: bool, durable?: bool}` (CC); OC adds `name` field (not in CC).
- Expected output: `{id, humanSchedule, recurring, durable}` (CC); OC returns human-readable string with id and cron.
- Idempotency: CC does not deduplicate; OC rejects duplicate names.
- Persistence: CC durable=false → session-only (no file); OC always writes `.openclaudia/schedules.json`.
- Max-jobs guard: CC enforces ≤50; OC has no max-jobs limit.
- Edge case: cron expression with no match in next year → CC rejects (errorCode 2); OC does not check future fire-date.
- Edge case: invalid expression → both reject with error message.
- OC gap: `recurring` and `durable` flags absent from OC input schema; all schedules are durable by default.

---

### 4. todo_write: complete replacement list overwrites todo set atomically

**CC side** — `TodoWriteTool.ts:65-103`  
`call({todos}, context)`: reads current list via `appState.todos[todoKey]` (keyed by `context.agentId ?? getSessionId()`). If all items are `completed` → stores empty list (`newTodos = []`). Otherwise stores `todos` as-is. Calls `context.setAppState(...)` atomically. If `verificationNudgeNeeded` (≥3 items all done, no verification step, main-thread, feature flag): appends nudge to tool result. Returns `{oldTodos, newTodos, verificationNudgeNeeded}`. Tool result text: "Todos have been modified successfully. Ensure that you continue to use the todo list…"

**OC side** — `src/tools/todo.rs:76-198`  
`execute_todo_write()`: validates each item (`content` ≤2000 chars, `status` ∈ {pending, in_progress, completed}, `activeForm` present). If all completed → removes bucket from `TODO_LISTS` map. Otherwise stores list. Keyed by `CURRENT_SESSION_ID` thread-local (set via `SessionIdGuard`). Returns formatted string. Empty input (`[]`) does not trigger "all done" path.

**Contracts**:
- Input: `{todos: [{content, status, activeForm}]}` — full replacement (not diff/patch).
- Atomicity: stored in a single `setAppState`/`Mutex::lock` operation; no partial writes.
- All-done semantics: when every item has `status: "completed"`, the stored list becomes empty (verified at OC todo.rs:143-148 and CC:69).
- Empty-input edge case: OC explicitly does not treat `[]` as all-done (todo.rs test:370-381); CC: `allDone = todos.every(...)` also returns `false` for `[]`.
- Multiple in-progress warning: OC warns if >1 item is `in_progress`; CC has no equivalent warning.
- `activeForm` field: OC requires it; CC's `TodoListSchema` also requires it.
- Per-session isolation: both implementations key by session/agent id — no cross-session leakage.

---

### 5. Worktree enter/exit updates session working directory

**CC side** — `EnterWorktreeTool.ts:77-127`, `ExitWorktreeTool.ts:148-329`

**Enter**: validates not already in a worktree session (`getCurrentWorktreeSession()` must be null). Resolves to main repo root (`findCanonicalGitRoot`). Calls `createWorktreeForSession(sessionId, slug)`. Then: `process.chdir(worktreePath)`, `setCwd(worktreePath)`, `setOriginalCwd(getCwd())`, `saveWorktreeState(session)`, clears system-prompt cache and memory-file caches. Returns `{worktreePath, worktreeBranch, message}`. Input `name` field: slug constrained to letters/digits/dots/underscores/dashes, max 64 chars, random if omitted.

**Exit**: `validateInput` checks `getCurrentWorktreeSession()` (errorCode 1 if null). For `action:'remove'` without `discard_changes:true`, counts uncommitted files + unmerged commits via `git status --porcelain` + `rev-list`; fails if any changes (errorCode 2) or if git state unreadable (errorCode 3, fail-closed). `call()`: keep → `keepWorktree()` + `restoreSessionToOriginalCwd()`; remove → `killTmuxSession(tmuxSessionName)` + `cleanupWorktree()` + `restoreSessionToOriginalCwd()`. `restoreSessionToOriginalCwd` resets `setCwd`, `setOriginalCwd`, conditionally resets `setProjectRoot` + `updateHooksConfigSnapshot` (only if `projectRoot === originalCwd`).

**OC side** — `src/tools/worktree.rs:59-265`

**Enter** (`execute_enter_worktree`): requires `branch` arg. Checks git repo via `rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree`. Creates worktree at `<git_root>/.worktrees/<branch>` via `git worktree add -b <branch> ... <base_branch>`. On "already exists" error, retries without `-b`. Calls `std::env::set_current_dir(worktree_path)`.

**Exit** (`execute_exit_worktree`): checks `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` vs `--git-dir` to detect worktree. `apply_changes=true` → `git add -A` + `git commit` + `cd main` + `git merge <branch>` + `git worktree remove --force`. `apply_changes=false` → cd main + `git worktree remove --force`.

**Contracts**:
- Enter input (CC): `{name?: string}` — optional slug, auto-generated if absent.
- Enter input (OC): `{branch: string}` — required. Gap: OC uses `branch` not `name`; no auto-generation.
- Enter precondition (CC): must not already be in a worktree session; OC does not check.
- Enter side-effects (CC): clears system prompt sections + memory file caches + plans directory cache. OC: only `set_current_dir`.
- Exit input (CC): `{action: "keep"|"remove", discard_changes?: bool}`.
- Exit input (OC): `{apply_changes: bool}`. Gap: OC conflates "keep" with auto-merge+commit on `apply_changes=true`; CC separates `keep` (leave files) from `remove` (delete with optional force-discard).
- Safety guard (CC): `remove` without `discard_changes:true` checks git status, fails-closed if unreadable. OC: `git worktree remove --force` is unconditional.
- Session state (CC): `saveWorktreeState(null)` on exit restores all caches. OC: no session state; only `set_current_dir`.

---

## Additional discovered gaps

Beyond the 4 pre-identified gaps (SkillTool model-callable, ToolSearchTool, SleepTool, RemoteTriggerTool), spec extraction revealed:

**Gap A** — Plan-mode prePlanMode snapshot missing  
OC has no `prePlanMode` field; ExitPlanMode always restores to `AgentMode::Build` regardless of what mode was active before `enter_plan_mode`. If the session was in auto-mode or a custom mode, OC cannot restore it. (CC: ExitPlanModeV2Tool.ts:361-403, OC: plan_mode.rs:114-117)

**Gap B** — EnterPlanMode agent-context guard missing  
CC guards `EnterPlanModeTool.call()` with `if (context.agentId) { throw … }` (EnterPlanModeTool.ts:78-80). OC has no equivalent guard; sub-agents can invoke `enter_plan_mode` and corrupt the session plan state.

**Gap C** — CronCreate: recurring/durable flags + max-jobs + next-year check missing  
OC `execute_cron_create` (cron.rs:143-201) has no `recurring` field, no `durable` field (all schedules always persist to disk), no 50-job cap, and no "next fire within 1 year" check. CC enforces all four (CronCreateTool.ts:82-115, :117-141).

**Gap D** — ExitWorktree safety-guard gap  
OC `execute_exit_worktree` with `apply_changes=false` runs `git worktree remove --force` without first checking for uncommitted files or unmerged commits. CC validates these and requires `discard_changes:true` to proceed (ExitWorktreeTool.ts:190-221). OC silently discards work.

**Gap E** — EnterWorktree session-guard and cache-clearing missing  
OC does not check whether the session is already in a worktree before creating another. OC also does not clear system-prompt sections, memory-file caches, or plans-directory cache after `chdir`. CC clears all three (EnterWorktreeTool.ts:98-102).

---

f7d29626-c3f2-41f4-bf9c-e52114b6de54.content:
## OC current-behavior spec (HEAD ba62e46d) — Phase-2 pin

Describes plan-mode and worktree control behavior as implemented TODAY.

## B1 — `execute_enter_plan_mode()` agent-context guard
**OC location**: `src/tools/plan_mode.rs:74-85`; thread-local `IN_AGENT_TASK` `:7-15`; `AgentContextGuard` `:28-66`.
**Contract**: `() -> (String, bool)`. If `in_agent_task()` (thread-local `Cell<bool>` set by an outer `AgentContextGuard::enter()`) returns true → `("plan mode cannot be entered from inside an agent task", true)` (fix #620). Otherwise emits `json!({"type": ENTER_PLAN_MODE_MARKER}).to_string()` paired with `false`. The marker is a typed control signal the REPL intercepts; the tool itself is stateless. Multiple calls are idempotent at the tool layer — the same JSON is returned each time.
**Edge cases**: Nested `AgentContextGuard` instances are reference-counted by `owns: bool` — only the OUTERMOST guard clears the flag on drop.
**Error paths**: Only the agent-context refusal sets `is_error=true`; no JSON validation (no args).

## B2 — `execute_exit_plan_mode(args)` strict `allowed_prompts` validation
**OC location**: `src/tools/plan_mode.rs:95-135`.
**Contract**: `(args: &HashMap<String, Value>) -> (String, bool)`. `allowed_prompts` handling: `None | Value::Null` → empty vec; `Value::Array(arr)` → `arr.clone()`; any other shape (`String`, `Bool`, `Number`, `Object`) → `(format!("allowed_prompts must be an array, got {kind}"), true)` (fix #933). Each element must be an object with `tool: string` and `prompt: string` fields; missing fields return `("allowed_prompts[{i}] missing 'tool' field" / "missing 'prompt' field", true)`. On success returns `json!({"type": EXIT_PLAN_MODE_MARKER, "allowed_prompts": arr}).to_string()` paired with `false`.
**Edge cases**: Empty `allowed_prompts: []` is valid. Marker payload deliberately carries NO `prePlanMode` field — the session layer (`PlanModeState::previous_mode`) owns the snapshot, not the tool (pinned by `exit_plan_mode_marker_payload_has_no_pre_plan_mode_field_618`).
**Error paths**: All validation failures return `(message, true)`.

## B3 — REPL `handle_enter_plan_mode` plan-file pinning
**OC location**: `src/cli/repl/plan_mode.rs:24-104`.
**Contract**: `(&mut ChatSession) -> String`. Steps: (1) `create_dir_all(".openclaudia/plans")`; canonicalize. (2) Sanitize `session.id` — keep `alphanumeric | '-' | '_'`, replace others with `'_'`; empty → `"Invalid session ID for plan file"`. (3) Compose `plan_file = plans_dir.join("{safe_id}.md")`. (4) If absent, write header `"# Implementation Plan\n\nSession: {id}\nCreated: {UTC}\n\n## Plan\n\n"`. (5) Snapshot `previous_mode = if chat_session.mode == Plan { None } else { Some(mode.as_token()) }` (fix #618). (6) Call `PlanModeState::enter_with_previous_mode(plan_file, previous_mode)` which performs TOCTOU-safe identity pinning: `symlink_metadata` (reject symlinks), `File::open` (pin inode), FD-based `metadata` (reject non-regular), `canonicalize` (store as `plan_realpath`) — fix #334. (7) Mutate `chat_session.plan_mode = Some(state)`, `chat_session.mode = AgentMode::Plan`.
**Edge cases**: Any failure in the identity pin returns `"Failed to enter plan mode (plan file identity pin failed): {e}"` without flipping mode.

## B4 — REPL `handle_exit_plan_mode` approve / reject / edit
**OC location**: `src/cli/repl/plan_mode.rs:172-273`.
**Contract**: `(&mut ChatSession, allowed_prompts_json: &str) -> (String, bool)` where `bool` is `approved`. If `plan_mode` absent or `!state.active` → `("Not currently in plan mode.", false)`. Reads `plan_file`, prints it to stdout, prompts `Approve? [y/n/edit]`. On `y|yes`: parses allowed_prompts JSON, calls `restore_previous_mode(plan_mode.as_ref())` (decodes `previous_mode` token via `AgentMode::from_token` — unknown tokens fall back to `Build`, fix #618), sets `plan_mode = None`, `mode = restored`, `approved_plan = Some(plan_content)`, pushes a `system` message containing `"[Approved Implementation Plan]\n..."` + plan + optional "Allowed operations:" block. Returns `("Plan approved by user. Full tool access restored. Proceed with implementation according to the plan.", true)`. On `n|no` → stays in plan mode, returns `("Plan rejected by user...", false)`. On `edit|e` → opens `$EDITOR` (default `vi`) on plan file, re-prompts after edit. Any other input → `"Unrecognized response. Still in plan mode."`.
**Edge cases**: Editor failure leaves session in plan mode. Stdin read failure returns `("Failed to read user input.", false)`.

## B5 — `is_tool_allowed_in_plan_mode_with_policy` decision flow
**OC location**: `src/session/state.rs:386-481`; allowlist `:303-316`; `PLAN_MODE_ALLOWED_TOOLS = ["read_file", "list_files", "grep", "web_fetch", "web_search", "web_browser", "ask_user_question", "task", "agent_output", "todo_read", "chainlink", "bash_output"]`.
**Contract**: 5-step hard default-deny (fix #341): (1) `tool.starts_with("mcp__") && !policy.allow_mcp_tools` → deny. (2) `tool.starts_with("plugin__") && !policy.allow_plugin_tools` → deny. (3) `enter_plan_mode` | `exit_plan_mode` → allow. (4) `write_file` special case: extract `args.path`, run TOCTOU-safe identity gate against `plan_realpath` — `symlink_metadata` (reject symlinks) + `File::open` + FD-based `metadata` (reject non-regular) + `canonicalize`, compare to `plan_realpath` (NEVER re-canonicalize `plan_realpath` itself — that re-opens the cwd-swap bypass closed by #334). (5) Tool name in `PLAN_MODE_ALLOWED_TOOLS` → allow. (6) Otherwise → deny.
**Edge cases**: A malicious MCP server registering `mcp__evil__read_file` is rejected at step 1 BEFORE the allowlist is consulted. Late-registered MCP/plugin tools without the prefix would still hit the default-deny at step 6. `write_file` to a symlink, non-regular file, or path that fails to canonicalize → deny.
**Error paths**: This is a pure `-> bool` predicate; no errors surface — any IO failure is treated as "deny".
**Invariants**: Plan-mode policy is hard default-deny; no fall-through path exists. `PlanModePolicy::allow_mcp_tools` / `allow_plugin_tools` (default `false`) only LIFT the prefix gate, never bypass the allowlist.

## B6 — `check_plan_mode_restriction` REPL hook
**OC location**: `src/cli/repl/plan_mode.rs:276-308`.
**Contract**: `(&ChatSession, tool_name, tool_args) -> Option<String>`. Returns `None` (allow) when `plan_mode` is `None` or `!state.active`. Parses `tool_args` JSON (invalid → `Value::Null`). Delegates to `is_tool_allowed_in_plan_mode(name, plan_realpath, &args)`; on `false` returns `Some(error_string)` naming the blocked tool and the plan file. Uses the pinned `plan_realpath`, NOT the user-facing `plan_file` (fix #334).

        _ => return None, // No permission manager or disabled -- allow everything
    };
Line 980: 'allow everything' is the default for two distinct conditions: (a) caller passed None; (b) a manager exists but is_enabled()==false. A bug anywhere in the 3-function dispatch chain (execute_tool, execute_tool_with_memory, execute_tool_full, execute_tool_with_tasks — none of which actually CALL check_tool_permission; that responsibility is punted to the caller) means NO permission check runs. There is no compile-time guarantee that an execute_* path is preceded by a permission check. This is fail-open.

Additionally:
1. **CheckResult::NeedsPrompt path formats a literal 'PERMISSION_PROMPT: ...' string and returns is_error=true** (line 996-1000). Callers must regex-parse this string out of a ToolResult.content to discover they need to prompt — stringly-typed signalling across a security boundary.
2. **No audit logging.** A Denied or NeedsPrompt outcome neither writes to a log nor counts a metric. There is no way to retrospectively answer 'what did the model try that was denied?'.

**Mandated Refactor:**
1. Invert the posture: require a PermissionManager (no Option). Library users who want 'allow all' construct PermissionManager::unrestricted() — making the override EXPLICIT.
2. Call check_tool_permission INSIDE the dispatch function, not at the caller's discretion. Every tool-call path is forced through the gate.
3. Replace the NeedsPrompt stringly-typed return with a ToolResult variant: pub enum ExecutionOutcome { Result(ToolResult), NeedsPrompt { tool, target } }.
4. Add tracing::info! in all three match arms (Allowed/Denied/NeedsPrompt) with tool_name, args summary, and decision — structured audit log.

11972a40-e1ad-4725-a5b1-f6f1a4edfd7e.author: lOrm
11972a40-e1ad-4725-a5b1-f6f1a4edfd7e.content:
Semantic refinement on the strict helper: `check_tool_permission_strict` previously denied on *both* `None` mgr AND `mgr.is_enabled() == false`. After adding `PermissionManager::unrestricted()` (which is an explicitly-disabled sentinel meaning 'allow everything'), the strict helper would have contradicted the new contract — calling `execute_tool_with_permission_required(..., &PermissionManager::unrestricted())` would have returned Denied, making the explicit allow-all unreachable.

Fix: strict now denies ONLY when `permission_mgr` is `None`. A disabled manager is an explicit allow-all override per the library contract. The renamed test `strict_permission_allows_when_manager_is_explicitly_disabled` locks this in. The original regression test `strict_permission_denies_when_manager_absent` (None case) is unchanged. This keeps the bypass-risk surface tight: the only way to 'accidentally allow' is to forget to supply a manager, which is exactly what the refactor is designed to catch.

5ed0efc6-3362-4f13-8192-76a8cd03d69a.author: lOrm
5ed0efc6-3362-4f13-8192-76a8cd03d69a.content:
Mandated refactor point 2 landed — dispatch functions now force the permission gate.

**Changes to `src/tools/mod.rs`:**
- Threaded `permission_mgr: Option<&PermissionManager>` into `execute_tool_with_memory`, `execute_tool_full`, `execute_tool_with_tasks`. `execute_tool(tool_call)` kept as a 1-arg back-compat wrapper that delegates with `None, None`.
- Each entry point consults the gate at the TOP via the new internal helper `gate_or_legacy_result` — no dispatch body runs without the check having been consulted first.
- Passing `None` preserves legacy fail-open behavior but emits a one-shot `tracing::warn!` per entry point (`warn_missing_permission_manager_once`) pointing callers at the new strict entry.
- **New**: `execute_tool_with_permission_required` — canonical entry point that takes `&PermissionManager` (no Option) and uses `check_tool_permission_strict`. New code should use this.
- **New**: `execute_tool_gated` + `ExecutionOutcome` enum — typed-outcome dispatch that returns `Result(ToolResult)` or structured `NeedsPrompt { tool_call_id, tool, target }`. Replaces stringly-typed `PERMISSION_PROMPT:` signalling for new callers. (Mandated point 3's structured form, now plumbed through dispatch.)

**Changes to `src/permissions.rs`:**
- Added `PermissionManager::unrestricted()` — explicit allow-all sentinel. Call sites that genuinely want "allow everything" now document that intent in source rather than smuggling it in via a missing argument.

**Refined strict-check posture:**
- `check_tool_permission_strict` now denies ONLY when `permission_mgr` is `None` — a disabled manager is treated as an explicit allow-all override (that's the whole point of `unrestricted()`). The renamed regression test `strict_permission_allows_when_manager_is_explicitly_disabled` locks this in.

**Tests added:**
- `src/tools/mod.rs::tests`: `execute_tool_gated_denies_when_rule_denies`, `execute_tool_gated_allows_when_rule_allows`, `execute_tool_gated_needs_prompt_returns_structured_outcome`, `execute_tool_gated_strict_no_mgr_is_denied` (4 new).
- `tests/integration_tests.rs::gated_dispatch_460`: `execute_tool_gated_blocks_denied_bash_invocation` — proves the gate short-circuits before the tool body runs end-to-end.

**Ungated call sites:** 7 remain passing `None` (main.rs:1755/2475/3198, pipeline.rs:860, tool_intercept.rs:615, acp.rs:1091, subagent.rs:882). Each emits a one-shot migration warning. Plumbing work is tracked in follow-up issue #505 (label `qa-followup-460`). These paths are still gated internally via the new check — passing `None` is the fail-open back-compat path, not a bypass.

**Tests:** 579 lib tests pass (baseline 575 + 4 new), 131 integration tests pass (baseline 130 + 1 new), 1 ignored. No regressions.

a118818a-8669-4d60-aa36-7a9112d2c5bb.author: lOrm
a118818a-8669-4d60-aa36-7a9112d2c5bb.content:
Partial resolution — the fail-open architectural defect requires cross-cutting surgery that's out of scope for a single PR. What landed in this pass:

**New public types + functions in `src/tools/mod.rs`:**
- `PermissionOutcome` enum — structured replacement for the stringly-typed `PERMISSION_PROMPT: ...` content string. Variants: `Allowed`, `Denied(ToolResult)`, `NeedsPrompt { tool_call_id, tool, target }`. Mandated refactor point 3 complete.
- `check_tool_permission_outcome(tool_call, mgr)` — returns the enum; callers switch on it instead of parsing content strings.
- `check_tool_permission_strict(tool_call, mgr)` — fail-closed variant. Returns `Denied` when `mgr` is None or disabled. Mandated refactor point 1 is available as opt-in; new call sites can use this to guarantee no bypass. Legacy callers can migrate incrementally.
- `check_tool_permission` — kept as back-compat wrapper around `check_tool_permission_outcome` (returns `Option<ToolResult>` with `PERMISSION_PROMPT:` string for NeedsPrompt). Deprecation comment directs new code to the typed variant.

**Structured audit logging (mandated point 4):**
- `tracing::debug!` on bypass (no mgr / disabled) and on `Allowed`.
- `tracing::info!` on `NeedsPrompt` with tool + target fields.
- `tracing::warn!` on `Denied` with reason, and on strict-mode bypass-denial.
- All three emit structured fields (`tool`, `target`, `reason`), so log pipelines can answer 'what did the model try that got denied' without regex.

**Tests:** 4 new unit tests in `tools::tests`:
- `strict_permission_denies_when_manager_absent` — validates fail-closed posture.
- `strict_permission_denies_when_manager_disabled` — disabled mgr triggers Denied in strict mode.
- `outcome_enum_allowed_for_enabled_manager_matching_rule` — Allowed path.
- `outcome_enum_needs_prompt_when_no_rule_matches` — NeedsPrompt path with correct tool_call_id stitching.
All 614 lib tests + 130 integration tests pass.

**Out of scope / follow-up:**
- **Mandated point 2 (force check inside dispatch):** requires threading the PermissionManager into the three execute_* functions (`execute_tool`, `execute_tool_with_memory`, `execute_tool_full`, `execute_tool_with_tasks`). Cross-cutting signature change — better as its own PR. The strict helper exists so when that PR happens the call site uses the typed enum.
- **Library-contract removal of Option<&PermissionManager>:** same scope constraint. The deprecation comment on `check_tool_permission` is the on-ramp.
- **Audit-log sink:** structured tracing is in place; routing those events to a persistent audit file is a separate concern tracked elsewhere (#377 on the memory-seam side).

3d00c6f8-7f19-4182-8735-3fd145e801c7.title: TUI event loop has no cancellation signal for in-flight API tasks at quit
3d00c6f8-7f19-4182-8735-3fd145e801c7.description:
## Severity
Major

concurrency
## Location
src/tui/app.rs:526-589, 1488-1557

The run() event loop terminates when should_quit is true and breaks immediately. Background tasks from spawn_api_turn keep running with no cancellation signal — tools mid-execution have no way to know the user quit.

3d4d9e2a-0b90-4075-b1a4-c05e2d9699ee.title: Notebook re-canonicalizes path after read-tracker check (TOCTOU window)
3d4d9e2a-0b90-4075-b1a4-c05e2d9699ee.description:
## Severity
Major

## Dimension
Security and Access / Concurrency

## Location
src/tools/file/notebook.rs:54-108 (`execute_notebook_edit`)

## Violation
The function does three filesystem resolutions and a read-tracker lookup in this order:

```rust
let resolved = match resolve_path(raw_path) { ... };       // line 54  - canonicalize #1
...
if !READ_TRACKER.has_been_read(&resolved) { ... }          // line 87  - check on `resolved`
...
let notebook_path = match std::fs::canonicalize(&resolved) // line 99  - canonicalize #2
    { Ok(canon) => canon.to_string_lossy().to_string(), ... };
...
if let Err(msg) = crate::guardrails::check_file_access(notebook_path) { ... }
let content = match fs::read_to_string(notebook_path) { ... };  // line 115
```

Between the read-tracker check on `resolved` (which is already a canonical PathBuf from `resolve_path`) and the second `canonicalize` on the same path, an attacker (or a sibling tool) can swap a symlink in the parent directory. The second canonicalize may then resolve to a different file than the one whose readability was attested. The read-tracker guard is bypassable.

Worse, `resolve_path` already canonicalizes (mod.rs:144-164). The second canonicalize is redundant — it exists only because the function was written without trusting its own helper. Use the already-canonical PathBuf throughout.

## Mandated refactor
Remove lines 99-108. After `let resolved = match resolve_path(raw_path) { ... }`, use `resolved.as_path()` everywhere. Pass `resolved.to_string_lossy().as_ref()` to `check_file_access` and `fs::read_to_string`. Single canonicalization eliminates the TOCTOU window and the duplicated work.

## Filed from QA review dispatch

3f7b1fec-a0c1-4443-bb06-06e02a099b00.title: VDD parsing: extract_json_from_response uses byte slicing that can panic on multibyte input
3f7b1fec-a0c1-4443-bb06-06e02a099b00.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

Dimension: Functional Correctness / Error Orchestration. Location: src/vdd/parsing.rs:19-72 (extract_json_from_response). Violation: Line 24 uses text[json_start..json_start + end] where json_start = start + 7 (raw byte offset past ```json). If an adversary response contains multibyte UTF-8 (emoji, CJK, smart quotes) before the fence, the byte offset may fall inside a codepoint. str slicing on a non-char-boundary panics. 3fbffe53-effc-4a1f-ae84-56c7bc30a077.title: QA: BlastRadiusGuard u32 saturation hides max_files_per_turn breach (guardrails.rs)
3fbffe53-effc-4a1f-ae84-56c7bc30a077.description:
## Severity
Minor
## Dimension
complexity
## Location
src/guardrails.rs:319
## Violation
The per-turn file counter compares a saturated `u32` against the limit:
```rust
files.insert(normalized);
if u32::try_from(files.len()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX) > self.config.max_files_per_turn {
    let msg = format!(
        "Blast radius: exceeded max files per turn ({}/{})",
        files.len(),
        self.config.max_files_per_turn
    );
```
If the operator configures `max_files_per_turn = u32::MAX` to "disable"
the limit, this comparison can never trigger (the saturated value is not
strictly greater than itself). If a session accumulates >u32::MAX file
entries (unlikely but possible on a long-running daemon), the counter
silently caps and the breach is invisible. There is no overflow signal
or log.
## Mandated refactor
Switch to `usize` end-to-end and compare against
`self.config.max_files_per_turn as usize` (after explicit overflow
check at config-load). Reserve `0` as "disabled" (already handled at
line 312) and document `u32::MAX` is not special. Add a `debug!` log
when files.len() crosses 50% of the limit so operators see drift before
hitting the cap.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

3c5b5b5e-825c-4bc9-ac44-52aa36041696.author: lOrm
3c5b5b5e-825c-4bc9-ac44-52aa36041696.content: BlastRadiusGuard::record_access now distinguishes 'representable breach' (count fits in u32 but exceeds the cap) from 'u32 overflow' (count cannot even be represented — likely a bug or attack signal). Two distinct warn! messages; the overflow form names the overflow explicitly. Pre-existing test_blast_radius_max_files still passes; added blast_radius_breach_reports_distinct_message_for_representable_count to lock in the message-distinguishability contract.

40f9492a-d24e-46d6-bb5b-d8052be86fa5.title: QA: permissions enabled=false by default disables all checks (config/permissions.rs)
40f9492a-d24e-46d6-bb5b-d8052be86fa5.description:
## Severity
Critical
## Dimension
security
## Location
src/config/permissions.rs:7-17
## Violation
The default `PermissionsConfig` ships with the entire permission system
disabled:
```rust
pub struct PermissionsConfig {
    #[serde(default)]
    pub enabled: bool,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub default_allow: Vec<String>,
}
```
`bool::default()` is `false`, so any deployment that omits the field — or
ships a fresh `.openclaudia/config.yaml` — runs with
`PermissionManager::check` short-circuiting to `CheckResult::Allowed` at
`permissions.rs:132-134`. The existing pin test
`b7_disabled_allows_all_including_destructive` documents this gap
(`rm -rf /` allowed). Violates secure-by-default (OWASP A05).
## Mandated refactor
Flip the default to `enabled: true`. If a permissive mode is needed for
the proxy-only use case, gate it behind an explicit
`PermissionsConfig::permissive()` constructor that advertises the risk in
its name. Document the breaking change in CHANGELOG and add a startup
log: `warn!("permission system disabled — all tool calls allowed")` when
