4487296f-3515-465c-89da-e48d899bb322.title: Four-way split-brain auth header logic across proxy.rs and providers
4487296f-3515-465c-89da-e48d899bb322.description:
Current state: 

Desired state: 

Reason: 

Dimension: Architectural Alignment / SRP

Location: src/proxy.rs line 1100-1143 (proxy_passthrough) and line 1371-1400 (forward_to_provider) and line 1402-1416 (set_auth_header).

Violation: Three different functions in proxy.rs decide the authentication header format based on the string value of a provider name — and each uses a DIFFERENT discriminator:
  - forward_to_provider (line 1385): `provider.base_url.contains("anthropic")` — URL-substring check.
  - set_auth_header (line 1408): `provider_name == "anthropic"` — exact name check.
  - proxy_anthropic_messages (line 1065): hardcoded Bearer with inline anthropic-beta string.
Plus each provider's adapter (src/providers/*.rs) owns its own get_headers method that ALSO redundantly sets auth — so there are FOUR authoritative header-building sites. This is a classic Big Ball of Mud. The three in-proxy.rs decisions mean that if a new provider needs custom auth (e.g., AWS Bedrock SigV4, Azure OpenAI with api-version query param), the author must modify THREE locations and potentially add a fourth.

The existing ProviderAdapter trait already has `fn get_headers(&self, api_key: &str) -> Vec<(String, String)>` which is the correct abstraction. proxy_passthrough/forward_to_provider don't use it.

Mandated Refactor:
  1. Delete set_auth_header entirely.
  2. Rewrite forward_to_provider to accept `&dyn ProviderAdapter` and call `adapter.get_headers(api_key)` — push the headers into the request builder with a single loop, identical to forward_to_provider_raw_reqwest's pattern at lines 1434-1436.
  3. Rewrite proxy_passthrough: it should obtain the adapter for `state.config.proxy.target`, call adapter.get_headers(api_key), and forward headers. No more base_url substring inspection.
  4. For proxy_anthropic_messages OAuth path, add a dedicated adapter method `fn oauth_headers(&self, bearer_token: &str) -> Vec<(String, String)>` on AnthropicAdapter that returns the full Bearer + anthropic-beta + anthropic-version set. Eliminate the inline magic-string in proxy.rs line 1069.
  5. After refactor, proxy.rs should contain ZERO string comparisons or substring matches on provider names for auth routing.

de869184-680c-45fd-a293-b75422e2cac2.author: lOrm
de869184-680c-45fd-a293-b75422e2cac2.content:
Resolved. The four-way split-brain is consolidated to a single source of truth: each provider's `ProviderAdapter::get_headers` implementation.

**`src/providers/anthropic.rs`:**
- New `AnthropicAdapter::oauth_headers(bearer_token: &str) -> Vec<(String, String)>` — returns the full Authorization/anthropic-beta/anthropic-version/content-type quartet. All Anthropic-specific magic strings now live inside the adapter module. Mandated refactor point 4 complete.

**`src/proxy.rs`:**
- **`proxy_anthropic_messages`** (line 1080ish): deleted the four inline `.header(...)` calls for Authorization/anthropic-beta/anthropic-version/content-type; replaced with a loop over `AnthropicAdapter::oauth_headers(&access_token)`. Magic-string cluster gone.
- **`forward_to_provider`**: signature gained a `provider_name: &str` parameter so it can call `providers::get_adapter(provider_name).get_headers(api_key)`. The previous `provider.base_url.contains("anthropic")` branch is deleted. Both call sites (at lines 993 and 1104ish) updated to pass the provider name.
- **`set_auth_header`** (mandated point 1): **deleted entirely** — the function and every reference to it are gone. Its single call site in `proxy_passthrough` now does `adapter.get_headers(&api_key)` directly.
- Doc comment on `forward_to_provider` documents the architectural change + links to this issue.

**Verification (mandated refactor point 5):** `Grep` for `base_url.contains(`, `provider_name == "`, `target == "` across `src/proxy.rs` returns **zero hits**. No string comparison or substring match on provider names drives auth routing anywhere in the proxy. Adding a new provider is now a one-file change (write the adapter; register it in `get_adapter`; done).

**Tests:** 638 lib + 130 integration tests pass — no regressions. The existing adapter tests (`test_anthropic_get_headers`, `test_openai_get_headers`, etc.) already lock in the header contracts per-provider; the refactor moved behavior behind that exact interface.

**Out of scope / follow-up:**
- Operator-supplied `provider.headers` still overrides adapter defaults (reqwest last-write-wins). If the desire is that adapter headers ALWAYS win, swap the loop order — left as default-behavior preserved for now.
- Future work: a per-provider `oauth_headers` method on the trait (not just AnthropicAdapter) if more providers grow OAuth auth modes. Today only Anthropic does.

44c87000-688a-41f8-8583-fdfb7a8e8d6e.title: InstalledPlugins.save: world-readable credentials & no atomic write
44c87000-688a-41f8-8583-fdfb7a8e8d6e.description:
Current state: 

Desired state: 

Reason: 

**Dimension**: Security and Access + Error Orchestration

**Location**: src/plugins/install.rs:142-152 (save), src/permissions.rs:400-417 (save_persisted_rules)

**Violation**:
1. Both save functions use `fs::write(&path, json)` directly. This is NOT atomic — a crash mid-write leaves installed_plugins.json / permissions.json corrupted, which load() then handles by 'starting fresh' (install.rs:127-128, permissions.rs:387-390). The user silently loses all installation tracking and all always-allow rules with no recovery.
2. Neither save sets file permissions. On Unix, the default umask can produce world-readable files. installed_plugins.json contains absolute install paths (disclosing workspace layout); permissions.json contains rule patterns that reveal user workflow (which commands they trust).
3. create_dir_all of the parent does not set directory permissions either.
4. load() silently discards parse errors — a corrupted file is indistinguishable from a valid empty state; user has no way to detect the corruption.

**Mandated Refactor**:
1. Write to `<path>.tmp` then `fs::rename` — atomic on same filesystem.
2. On Unix, set 0o600 on the file and 0o700 on the parent directory via std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt AFTER create.
3. On load() parse failure, rename the corrupted file to `<path>.corrupted.<timestamp>` and log a WARN with the backup path, don't silently default.
4. Consider adopting a small crate like `atomicwrites` to encapsulate the rename pattern.

433f7762-586b-4cd5-9578-66aa30f7d972.author: lOrm

Part 2 (permissions): on Unix, set 0o600 on the temp file before rename (file never world-readable); set 0o700 on the parent directory.

45bb659e-5d03-41a1-866a-63f7209e607c.title: cron.rs ScheduleStore: TOCTOU on load-modify-save, no file locking, schedules.json can corrupt under concurrent access
45bb659e-5d03-41a1-866a-63f7209e607c.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

**Dimension:** Functional Correctness / State Management

**Location:** /home/doll/OpenClaudia/src/tools/cron.rs lines 33-55 (ScheduleStore::load/save), 168-193 (execute_cron_create), 213-228 (execute_cron_delete)

**Violation:**
ScheduleStore::load() reads schedules.json, then execute_cron_create mutates the in-memory vec, then save() writes. No locking between load and save:
1. **Lost-update race.** Two concurrent cron_create calls both load, both see the original, both push their own schedule, both save — the second write overwrites the first. Schedules vanish silently.
2. **Partial-write corruption.** save() (line 54) calls std::fs::write which is not atomic on POSIX (it does open+truncate+write). A crash mid-write leaves schedules.json truncated or empty. Next load() falls back to default — all schedules lost.
3. **No schema version.** The Schedule struct has no 'version' field. A future change breaks existing schedule files with an unhelpful serde error.
4. **Path is hardcoded to '.openclaudia/schedules.json' relative to CWD.** If the agent's CWD changes (see worktree CWD mutation issue) the schedules are read/written in the wrong directory.
5. **UUID shortening at line 179 — Uuid::new_v4().to_string()[..8]** creates 8-hex-char IDs (32 bits of entropy). With 100 schedules the birthday-collision probability exceeds 0.1%. The validate-duplicate logic checks NAME (line 171) but not ID, so collisions cascade.

**Mandated Refactor:**
1. Use fs2 crate or std::fs::OpenOptions + flock (Unix) / LockFileEx (Windows) to acquire an exclusive lock on schedules.json.lock before load; hold until save completes.
2. Write atomically: write to schedules.json.tmp, then fs::rename (atomic on POSIX, atomic on NTFS with MoveFileExW REPLACE).
3. Add a schema_version: u32 field; on load, migrate or reject gracefully.
4. Store the schedules path as an absolute PathBuf captured at Session startup, not re-resolved each call.
5. Use a full UUID as ID or shorter ID with collision check.

46c4da74-c0dc-4d10-a388-5c75c9c8c14b.description:

Reason:

    for (table, max_rows) in prune_queries {

2. For each variant, call a dedicated prune method on MemoryDb that has its SQL text embedded in the function body (not constructed at runtime), taking only the LIMIT as a bound parameter.

4718c93c-ed62-441a-8452-0eaeec58dd0a.title: Config loader silently overwrites API keys with empty env vars via OPENCLAUDIA_ prefix overlap
4718c93c-ed62-441a-8452-0eaeec58dd0a.description:
## Severity
Major
## Dimension
security
## Location
src/config/mod.rs:171-196 (load_config env handling)
## Violation
`Environment::with_prefix("OPENCLAUDIA").separator("_")` plus the secondary `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY` overrides leak two related sharp edges:

1. The `_` separator collides with provider names that themselves contain underscores. `OPENCLAUDIA_PROVIDERS_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is parseable, but `OPENCLAUDIA_PROVIDERS_ZAI_BASE_URL` and `OPENCLAUDIA_PROVIDERS_DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL` are not unambiguous: an env entry like `OPENCLAUDIA_PROVIDERS_DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` gets parsed as path `providers.deepseek.api.key` (separator splits every `_`). The `try_parsing(true)` flag makes the resulting type coercion silent — values land in the wrong slot or are dropped.

2. The bare-env overrides (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` etc.) skip `maybe_set_api_key` only on empty string, but a value composed solely of whitespace (`"   "`) is forwarded to `set_override` and then to `ApiKey::deserialize`, which rejects it as ASCII control. The error propagates out of `load_config`, causing the whole process to refuse to start when an unrelated env var is accidentally set to whitespace.

```rust
builder = builder.add_source(
    Environment::with_prefix("OPENCLAUDIA").separator("_").try_parsing(true),
);
...
if let Ok(key) = std::env::var("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY") {
    builder = maybe_set_api_key(builder, "providers.anthropic.api_key", key)?;
}
```

(`maybe_set_api_key` checks `trim().is_empty()` but the empty-vs-whitespace contract is undocumented; the whole-pipeline error mode is the same as the bug already fixed for empty strings in #256.)
## Mandated refactor
Switch `Environment` to a dot-separator (e.g. `__` for nested keys, matching the `config` crate idiom: `OPENCLAUDIA__PROVIDERS__DEEPSEEK__API_KEY`) and document the mapping in a doc-comment. Pull the bare-env fallback into a single helper that (a) trims, (b) treats whitespace-only as unset, and (c) surfaces a single typed error variant so callers can distinguish "missing key" from "invalid key" without parsing strings. Add unit tests that pin the env→config key mapping for every shipped provider.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

Verification: cargo test --lib: 1442 passed / 0 failed (1437 baseline + 5 new tests). cargo clippy --lib --tests -- -D warnings: exit 0. cargo fmt --check: clean. No #[allow], no #[ignore], no clippy.toml.

```rust
    return Err(CompactionError::Failed("Compaction did not reduce token count".to_string()));
}
```

The caller has no way to distinguish "we cannot compact further, send the request anyway" from "compaction blew up, abort". Today both surfaces as a hard Err. Worse, before that Err returns, `request.messages = new_messages` (line 513) has already mutated the request — the caller sees a mutated request AND an error. (#439 already covers the rollback aspect for the post-verify path; this issue is the orthogonal "no work was possible" outcome.)
## Mandated refactor
1. Add a third variant to `CompactionResult`: `compacted: bool, reason: CompactionSkipReason` where reason ∈ {NotNeeded, NothingToSummarize, AllPreserved}.
2. When `messages_to_summarize.is_empty()` (line 493) OR the post-rebuild check shows no reduction, return Ok with the appropriate reason, not Err.
3. Reserve `CompactionError::Failed` for actual logic failures (summary generation panicked, hook misbehaved).
4. Snapshot `request.messages` at function entry and restore it before returning the skip Ok, mirroring the rollback discipline #439 mandates for the verify-failure path.

479a8395-3a71-4e28-9236-06bfaceaa511.description:
## Gap

Claude Code uses a tree-sitter AST-based bash parser (utils/bash/bashParser.ts ~4436 lines, utils/bash/treeSitterAnalysis.ts ~506 lines) for command validation and path analysis. The AST path is the primary (non-deprecated) validation route:

- AST avoids the shell-quote single-quote backslash bug that affects the deprecated string-parsing path

OpenClaudia has no tree-sitter parser. Command validation is pure substring/regex denylist (src/tools/bash/policy.rs:89-133). No AST analysis of command structure is performed.

## Parity reference
- CC: utils/bash/bashParser.ts (AST parse), utils/bash/treeSitterAnalysis.ts (analysis helpers), pathValidation.ts (AST-backed path checking)
- OC: missing entirely

## Acceptance
- tree-sitter-bash crate integration (or equivalent Rust parser)
- SimpleCommand / argv extraction from parsed AST
- AST-backed path validation replacing or augmenting the current regex denylist
- Handles quoted strings, heredocs, compound commands correctly

483dac5a-c918-4b3a-b2ac-e55398a7647e.title: ContextInjector::inject ignores allowlist; system messages from disallowed hooks still injected
483dac5a-c918-4b3a-b2ac-e55398a7647e.description:
## Severity
Major
## Dimension
security
## Location
src/context.rs:88-119 (ContextInjector::inject)
## Violation
```rust
pub fn inject(request: &mut ChatCompletionRequest, hook_result: &HookResult) {
    let system_messages: Vec<&str> = hook_result.system_messages();
    if system_messages.is_empty() { return; }
    let combined = system_messages.join("\n\n");
    let reminder = wrap_system_reminder(&combined);
    ...
}
```

The injector checks neither `hook_result.allowed` nor `hook_result.errors`. A hook that explicitly denied the operation (`allowed = false`) but still produced an output is treated identically to a passing one — its `system_message` field is injected into the next turn's user message, silently. This couples failed authorization with passed prompt context.

Worse, when a hook's `system_message` includes attacker-controlled content sourced from a tool's output (file content, web fetch result), the only defense is the delimiter-neutralization escape — there is no other sanitization, no length cap, and no content-type validation. A 10 MB web-fetch result inserted into a hook output ships verbatim into the model's user message.
## Mandated refactor
Add an explicit `if !hook_result.allowed { return; }` guard, OR change the API to take a `&PermittedHookResult` newtype that can only be constructed from an allowed result. Add a per-hook output length cap (e.g. 32 KiB after envelope) and surface oversize-truncation in the injected text. Document in the function doc-comment that hook outputs are routed through the model — and that hooks therefore must NEVER include unsanitized tool output.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

484de7d3-dabd-4249-bf56-2d596446ec01.title: reset_all drops core memory seed rows transactionally unsafe — TRIGGER fires during delete, FTS inconsistency on crash
484de7d3-dabd-4249-bf56-2d596446ec01.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

Dimension: Functional Correctness (1) / Security and Access (5) perimeter

Location: src/memory.rs:1297-1314 (reset_all), combined with FTS triggers at lines 241-246.

Violation: reset_all runs one execute_batch containing DELETE FROM archival_memory; DELETE FROM core_memory; ... DELETE FROM file_relationships; ... INSERT INTO core_memory. The batch is NOT wrapped in a transaction. If the process dies after DELETE FROM archival_memory succeeds but before INSERT INTO core_memory, the database is left with no core_memory rows at all — the next session will start with no persona, no project_info, no user_preferences. The FTS5 triggers (archival_memory_ad, _au) fire during DELETE FROM archival_memory, deleting rows from archival_memory_fts one at a time via triggers — this is O(N) triggers per batch DELETE. For large archival tables this is SLOW and partial on crash.

Related issues elsewhere in the file:
- save_coding_pattern (908), save_error_pattern (1026), save_learned_preference (1120): all do SELECT then conditional UPDATE or INSERT without transactions. Two concurrent callers both see 'not found' and both INSERT the same row — the UNIQUE constraint doesn't exist on these tables, so duplicates accumulate silently with confidence counters diverging.
- cleanup_expired_short_term (850) does two separate DELETEs without a transaction — a crash between them leaves recent_sessions expired but recent_activity still there.
- memory_save (356) does INSERT then reads last_insert_rowid(); on a connection shared between threads (Mutex<Connection>), this is safe because the mutex is held, but the pattern breaks immediately if anyone ever replaces Mutex<Connection> with a connection pool.

Mandated Refactor:
1. Wrap reset_all in conn.transaction()?, COMMIT at end.
2. Same for all read-modify-write patterns (save_coding_pattern etc.).
3. Add UNIQUE constraints on the natural keys: coding_patterns(file_glob, pattern_type, description), learned_preferences(category, preference). Then use INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE — atomic and race-free.
4. For reset_all, consider DROP+CREATE+re-seed in a single transaction as a nuke option, but keep the schema_version row.
5. Add a concurrency test: 10 threads racing save_coding_pattern with the same args, assert exactly ONE row exists with confidence=10.

0b65b5bd-e21a-4365-962d-5db63612a331.author: lOrm
0b65b5bd-e21a-4365-962d-5db63612a331.content:
Fixed: reset_all now uses rusqlite Connection::transaction(). DELETEs + reseed run as a single atomic unit; on any error, the Transaction's Drop impl rolls back the wipe and the database remains in its pre-reset state with all 3 core_memory seed rows intact.

Forensic evidence (src/memory.rs):
- const DEFAULT_RESET_SEED_SQL extracted (~line 1300).
- pub fn reset_all delegates to pub(crate) reset_all_with_seed_sql.
- reset_all_with_seed_sql acquires the mutex, then calls fn reset_all_on_conn(conn, seed) which does: conn.transaction() -> BEGIN DEFERRED -> execute_batch(DELETEs) -> execute_batch(seed) -> tx.commit(). Each step is anyhow-context-wrapped; the seed step's error message is 'reset_all: core_memory reseed failed' (asserted by the rollback regression test).

Tests added (all pass under cargo test --lib, 5/5 stress passes):
1. issue_400_reset_all_success_commits_wipe_and_reseed — happy path; verifies archival wipe + 3-row seed.
2. issue_400_reset_all_mid_reseed_failure_rolls_back — injects bad seed SQL (duplicate PRIMARY KEY on core_memory.section), asserts Err, then asserts pre-reset archival rows + customised persona content all survive. This is the proof: the row that was deleted is back. Without the transaction, the test would fail.
3. issue_400_reset_all_concurrent_reader_sees_consistent_state — writer hammers reset_all (50 iters) while reader does 500 get_core_memory() calls; reader must always see exactly 3 rows.

Verification:
- cargo test --lib: 1314 passed; 0 failed.
- cargo clippy --lib --tests -- -D warnings: exit 0 (no #[allow], no clippy.toml, no #[ignore]).

Out of scope (related items in the bug report, belong in separate issues):
- save_coding_pattern / save_error_pattern / save_learned_preference race-conditions.
- cleanup_expired_short_term two-DELETE atomicity.
- UNIQUE constraints on coding_patterns / learned_preferences.
- Concurrency test for save_coding_pattern.

4a075b82-af59-439a-af0e-62da4affcae6.title: TUI run() event loop has no shutdown signal to stop in-flight API tasks
4a075b82-af59-439a-af0e-62da4affcae6.description:
## Severity
Major
## Dimension
concurrency
## Location
src/tui/app.rs:526-589
## Violation
The run() event loop terminates when should_quit is true, but spawn_api_turn pushes background tasks that hold senders into the same channel. In-flight requests keep running after the user quits — tools mid-execution have no way to know.

The agentic follow-up loop in run_api_turn_async (line 1518) has no cancellation token: a 25-iteration agentic chain continues billing the user's API account after quit.

## Mandated refactor
Add tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken on App, cloned into ApiTurnParams. run_api_turn_async checks token.is_cancelled() at each iteration. pipeline::run_turn races against token.cancelled(). On should_quit, cancel token before breaking the loop.

## Filed from QA review dispatch

4a2ac139-dbc0-41cc-bd4b-44ff5b706932.title: DeepSeek, Qwen, Z.AI, OpenAI adapters are 85 percent duplicate code (Stovepipe)
4a2ac139-dbc0-41cc-bd4b-44ff5b706932.description:
Current state: 

Desired state: 

Reason: 

Dimension: Architectural Alignment / DRY / SRP

Location: src/providers/openai.rs, deepseek.rs, qwen.rs, zai.rs — all implement ProviderAdapter::transform_request with the identical body `serde_json::to_value(request).map_err(|e| ProviderError::RequestFailed(e.to_string()))`.

Specific duplicates:
  - openai.rs:34-37  transform_request
  - deepseek.rs:34-36
  - qwen.rs:34-36
  - zai.rs:34-37
  Also every single adapter implements get_headers with the identical two-tuple `Authorization: Bearer {api_key}` + content-type pair (openai.rs:78-83, deepseek.rs:65-70, qwen.rs:67-72, zai.rs:83-88). The chat_endpoint method also duplicates `/v1/chat/completions` verbatim across three providers.

Violation: The four OpenAI-compatible providers (OpenAI, DeepSeek, Qwen, Z.AI — Z.AI uses /chat/completions without v1 prefix) are cosmetic variants of the same adapter. The trait abstraction breaks down: we have 4x copies of a body that differs only by which thinking parameters are sprinkled into the JSON. Adding a new OpenAI-compat provider requires copying ~80 lines of boilerplate. This is the Stovepipe anti-pattern from the QA heuristic: duplicated logic across isolated modules.

Mandated Refactor: Introduce a shared base struct `OpenAiCompatAdapter` in a new file src/providers/openai_compat.rs that holds:
  struct OpenAiCompatAdapter {
      name: &'static str,
      chat_path: &'static str,
      thinking_injector: fn(&mut Value, &ThinkingConfig, &str),  // closure for provider-specific thinking
  }
Then DeepSeek/Qwen/Z.AI/OpenAI become one-line constructors returning a configured OpenAiCompatAdapter with a dedicated thinking_injector fn. Delete openai.rs, deepseek.rs, qwen.rs, zai.rs as separate types — keep them only as module-level constructor functions. Expected reduction: ~320 lines down to ~150.

Acceptance criteria: get_adapter() in mod.rs returns OpenAiCompatAdapter variants; the four thinking_injector closures encode the only real difference. All existing tests (test_openai_passthrough, test_zai_adapter, etc.) must still pass against the unified adapter.

4bcd67fd-31b8-4458-a7ba-bda6f686db6b.title: Compaction token estimator under-counts CJK/emoji/images — context exhaustion risk
4bcd67fd-31b8-4458-a7ba-bda6f686db6b.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

Token estimation in src/compaction.rs is a 4-chars-per-token heuristic with only a 0.5x adjustment for non-ASCII (line 137-139). CJK real tokens are ~1 per char so this under-counts by ~33 percent. Images hardcoded at 1000 tokens (line 153) — Anthropic bills ~1600 for hi-res, GPT-4V bills up to 765+85. COMPACTION_THRESHOLD 0.85 plus RESPONSE_RESERVE 4096 cannot absorb the error, so compaction fires late and the provider returns context_length_exceeded. Fix: (1) integrate tiktoken-rs for OpenAI; (2) call Anthropic count_tokens endpoint, cached per message hash; (3) widen RESPONSE_RESERVE to 16K for heuristic fallback; (4) property-test within 15 percent of tokenizer truth on a sample corpus; (5) when actual_input_tokens exceeds estimate by >20 percent, log warning and tighten threshold for subsequent turns.

4c2fb6eb-bcf8-4e95-86a2-ca2d058026fd.title: fetch_url response body is not size-capped
4c2fb6eb-bcf8-4e95-86a2-ca2d058026fd.description:
## Severity
Major
## Dimension
security
## Location
src/web.rs:262-300 (fetch_url)
## Violation
After validating the URL, the response body is consumed via `response.text().await` (line 285) with no maximum size. A malicious or compromised Jina-proxied target can stream gigabytes, exhausting memory before the post-fetch truncate-to-50000 (`src/tools/web.rs:47`) ever runs. The truncate logic in the tool layer is not a defense — it executes on an already fully-materialized `String`.

```rust
let content = response
    .text()
    .await
    .map_err(|e| format!("Failed to read response: {e}"))?;
```

Same exposure in `fetch_with_browser` via headless Chrome `get_content()`.
## Mandated refactor
Stream the body with `response.bytes_stream()` and accumulate into a capped buffer (e.g. 4 MiB), returning an error when the cap is exceeded. Alternatively check `response.content_length()` upfront and refuse early. For the headless-browser path, set a navigation-level body limit or kill the tab when content_size > cap.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

4c3507fc-59cb-47f9-bfc5-6c0c410e5720.title: execute_list_files uses read_dir().flatten() — silently drops unreadable entries
4c3507fc-59cb-47f9-bfc5-6c0c410e5720.description:
Current state: 

Desired state: 

Reason: 

**Dimension:** Error Orchestration / Functional Correctness

**Location:** /home/doll/OpenClaudia/src/tools/file/list.rs lines 15-27

**Violation:**
fs::read_dir(&path).flatten() silently skips any DirEntry that errored. When the directory has permission-denied entries (common under /root, /etc/ssl/private, or SELinux-confined paths), the tool reports a clean list that omits the failures. The caller has no signal that entries were hidden. The model then acts on incomplete information.

Additionally:
1. No size limit. A directory with 10 million entries allocates a 10M-element Vec<String>. Should paginate or cap.
2. The '/' suffix convention (line 23) is ad-hoc and doesn't distinguish symlinks from files, executables from data, or sockets/fifos. A model reading 'foo/' cannot tell if it's a directory or a symlink to elsewhere.
3. entry.file_type() fallback 'unwrap_or("")' (line 23) treats errors identically to 'regular file', hiding real IO problems.

**Mandated Refactor:**
1. Use .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>(), report the first error, and include a '(N entries could not be read)' footer listing how many were skipped.
2. Cap at MAX_DIR_ENTRIES (e.g. 2000); if exceeded, return a message instructing the model to use glob or a more specific subpath.
3. Distinguish symlink, dir, file, fifo, socket, blockdev: use ls-style suffix ('/', '@', '*', '|', '=') per POSIX convention.
4. Separate counts by type in the output footer.

4daca27e-b7c9-4006-bdc9-1d6da2bd142e.title: FileIndex::walk_dir is recursive, unbounded — symlink loops cause stack overflow or infinite walk
4daca27e-b7c9-4006-bdc9-1d6da2bd142e.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

**Dimension:** Functional Correctness / Performance

**Location:** /home/doll/OpenClaudia/src/tools/file_index.rs lines 51-78 (walk_dir)

**Violation:**
FileIndex::walk_dir recurses via self.walk_dir(root, &path) at line 71. There is NO symlink guard: std::fs::read_dir follows symlinks by default, so a symlink cycle (e.g. /proc/1/cwd -> /, or user-created .worktrees/loop -> ..) sends the walk into infinite recursion and stack overflow. Additional defects:
1. **No depth limit.** A pathological filesystem with 1000 nested dirs blows the stack.
2. **Skip list is hardcoded and incomplete.** Line 60 skips names starting with '.', node_modules, target, __pycache__, dist, build — but MISSES vendor (Go, PHP), .venv (Python), venv, coverage, .next, .nuxt, bazel-bin, .tox, .pytest_cache, .gradle, DerivedData, Pods. A large monorepo will index GBs of artifacts.
3. **No cancellation.** Build() blocks for however long the walk takes, with no timeout or interrupt.
4. **Stored as rel + lower_rel strings** (line 74-75). A codebase with 1M files uses 2x memory; better to store lower once and compute relative-to-root on demand.
5. **Uses read_dir().flatten()** (line 55) which silently swallows I/O errors — permission-denied directories vanish without a warning.

**Mandated Refactor:**
1. Use the ignore crate (same engine as ripgrep) which handles gitignore, symlink cycles, depth limits, parallel walking, and a well-tuned default skip list out of the box.
2. Add max_depth: Option<usize> parameter, default 50.
3. Track visited inodes via HashSet<(dev, ino)> (Unix) to break cycles.
4. Emit I/O errors through tracing::warn rather than dropping them.
5. Build in a background thread; expose a progress counter so the TUI can show 'Indexed 2458 files...'.

3bb02853-6eaf-445c-ac3e-888cd61bf7c2.author: lOrm
3bb02853-6eaf-445c-ac3e-888cd61bf7c2.content: Fixed: walk_dir bounded by MAX_WALK_DEPTH=100, uses symlink_metadata (does not follow symlinks), and a canonical-path visited HashSet breaks residual cycles. 5 forensic tests added in src/tools/file_index.rs (depth-cap, symlink loop, normal walk, symlink-to-outside-root, intra-tree file symlink). All 10 file_index tests pass. cargo clippy on file_index.rs clean. No #[allow], no clippy.toml, no #[ignore] added by this fix.

4e4cfab8-f23f-4aff-96e6-b53337fb882d.title: PROJECT_ROOT and TEMP_ROOT LazyLocks silently fall back to '.' if cwd canonicalize fails
4e4cfab8-f23f-4aff-96e6-b53337fb882d.description:
## Severity
Major

## Dimension
Perimeter Defense / Functional Correctness

## Location
src/tools/file/mod.rs:78-88 (PROJECT_ROOT and TEMP_ROOT static initializers)

## Violation
```rust
static PROJECT_ROOT: LazyLock<PathBuf> = LazyLock::new(|| {
    std::env::current_dir()
        .and_then(|cwd| cwd.canonicalize())
        .unwrap_or_else(|_| PathBuf::from("."))
});
```

If `current_dir` or `canonicalize` fails (e.g. the process was started in a deleted directory, or the cwd is mounted via FUSE that returns EIO), PROJECT_ROOT silently falls back to `PathBuf::from(".")` — a *relative* path. Every subsequent jail check using `path_is_within(&canonical, &PROJECT_ROOT)` compares a fully-canonicalized absolute path against `.`. `Path::starts_with` is byte-prefix matching: `"/etc/passwd".starts_with(".")` is false BUT also `"/home/user/file"`.starts_with(".") is false — so EVERY path is rejected, breaking the entire tool subsystem silently.

Worse, even if canonicalize succeeds, no startup-time check verifies that PROJECT_ROOT actually exists OR that it's a directory (a path that resolves to a regular file would still pass the canonicalize check). The "jail" is built on assumptions that aren't enforced.

## Mandated refactor
1. Make PROJECT_ROOT and TEMP_ROOT typed as `Result<PathBuf, anyhow::Error>` (or wrap in LazyLock<Result<...>>). At first use, propagate the error to the caller rather than substituting `.`.
2. In main.rs startup, eagerly access both statics and PANIC with a clear error message ("could not determine project root: ..."). Fail fast at process start, not silently per-tool-call.
3. Reject PROJECT_ROOT that is not a directory: `assert!(canonical.is_dir())`.

## Filed from QA review dispatch

4ec2a60c-71f2-4279-96bd-8c6d76f67eb4.title: cron field_names/field_ranges parallel constants and indexed lookups are fragile coupling
4ec2a60c-71f2-4279-96bd-8c6d76f67eb4.description:
## Severity
Trivial

## Dimension
Type Safety / Data Modeling

## Location
src/tools/cron.rs:60-69 (FIELD_NAMES and FIELD_RANGES) and 78-138 (use sites)

## Violation
```rust
const FIELD_NAMES: [&str; 5] = ["minute (0-59)", "hour (0-23)", "day (1-31)", "month (1-12)", "weekday (0-6)"];
const FIELD_RANGES: [(u32, u32); 5] = [(0, 59), (0, 23), (1, 31), (1, 12), (0, 6)];
const _: () = assert!(FIELD_NAMES.len() == FIELD_RANGES.len());
```

The compile-time assert is acknowledgement that the two parallel arrays need to stay in sync — but it only guards the length, not the *meaning* of paired entries. Swapping `(0, 23)` and `(1, 31)` (hour vs day) would compile and pass the assert; cron expressions for hour 30 would then incorrectly validate while hour 12 of "day" field would not.

The 5-element duplication exists because both lookups happen in the same loop with the same index `i` (lines 81-138). One struct per field would carry both pieces of information together.

## Mandated refactor
```rust
struct CronField { name: &'static str, min: u32, max: u32 }
const FIELDS: [CronField; 5] = [
    CronField { name: "minute (0-59)", min: 0, max: 59 },
    CronField { name: "hour (0-23)", min: 0, max: 23 },
    CronField { name: "day (1-31)", min: 1, max: 31 },
    CronField { name: "month (1-12)", min: 1, max: 12 },
    CronField { name: "weekday (0-6)", min: 0, max: 6 },
];
```

(This also disappears entirely when the parser is replaced with the cron crate per the separate issue.)

Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

Dimension: Functional Correctness. Location: src/vdd/mod.rs:905 (verify_findings uses truncate_output(builder_code, 12000)). Violation: If builder output is larger than 12 KB, the verifier sees only the first 12 KB plus a '[truncated, N total chars]' marker. 50d035a0-d14c-47fc-910c-8ebb34c360b0.title: Add shared team memory directory (parity with CC teamMemPaths.ts)
50d035a0-d14c-47fc-910c-8ebb34c360b0.description:
## Goal

Implement shared team memory directory support, porting CC's `teamMemPaths.ts` (CC ~292 lines) and `teamMemPrompts.ts` (CC ~100 lines).

## CC source behavior

- `getTeamMemPath()` → `<autoMemPath>/team/` (trailing separator, NFC-normalized)
- `getTeamMemEntrypoint()` → `<autoMemPath>/team/MEMORY.md`
- `isTeamMemoryEnabled()` → false if autoMemory disabled; otherwise gated on feature flag
- `isTeamMemPath(filePath)` → string-level containment check (resolves `..` via `path.resolve`)
- `validateTeamMemWritePath(filePath)` → two-pass validation: (1) resolve `..` + string containment, (2) `realpath` deepest-existing-ancestor + confirm within real teamDir (catches symlink escapes)
- `validateTeamMemKey(relativeKey)` → sanitize null bytes, URL-encoded traversals, Unicode NFKC-normalized traversals, backslashes, absolute paths; then same two-pass as above
- Path traversal security: `PathTraversalError` on: null byte, URL-encoded `../`, Unicode NFKC `．．／`, backslash, dangling symlink, symlink loop (`ELOOP`), unresolvable ancestor
- `buildCombinedMemoryPrompt()` → combined auto+team prompt with scope guidance (two-directory system, `## Memory scope` section)
- Team MEMORY.md index is loaded and injected alongside private MEMORY.md (both truncated via same `truncateEntrypointContent`)

## OC counterpart

None. No team memory directory support exists in `src/memdir/`. This is a CC parity gap tracked here.

## Done when

- `src/memdir/team_paths.rs` implements `get_team_mem_path`, `is_team_mem_path`, `validate_team_mem_write_path`, `validate_team_mem_key` with equivalent security properties
- Path traversal test matrix covers: null byte, URL-encoded `../`, Unicode `．．／`, backslash, dangling symlink, real symlink escape
- `src/memdir/team_prompts.rs` implements `build_combined_memory_prompt` matching CC structure
- Feature-flagged behind config (team memory opt-in)

## Related

- Parent audit: #523
- Spec issue: #533
- Phase 1 spec: this gap was discovered during #533 spec extraction

539c2e9e-58f3-4cef-bcf2-f2398d2f6201.title: claude_credentials::CLAUDE_CODE_SYSTEM_PROMPT constant tightly couples openclaudia identity to upstream API check
539c2e9e-58f3-4cef-bcf2-f2398d2f6201.description:
## Severity
Minor
## Dimension
decoupling
## Location
src/claude_credentials.rs:378-423 (CLAUDE_CODE_SYSTEM_PROMPT, inject_system_prompt)
## Violation
```rust
pub const CLAUDE_CODE_SYSTEM_PROMPT: &str =
    "You are Claude Code, Anthropic's official CLI for Claude.";
...
let prefix_block = serde_json::json!({"type": "text", "text": CLAUDE_CODE_SYSTEM_PROMPT});
```

This hard-codes Anthropic's identity-attestation string for OAuth model access. The doc-comment says "The Anthropic API validates this exact string". So `inject_system_prompt` lies to the upstream API about which client the request comes from — Claudia masquerades as Claude Code to gain access to subscription-gated models.

Two problems:
1. Architectural: a `claude_credentials` MODULE injects content into the SYSTEM PROMPT that the prompt-builder is unaware of. Block ordering and identity content are spread across `prompt.rs`, `claude_credentials.rs`, and `context.rs` with no single owner. The `inject_system_prompt` mutation also happens AFTER `build_system_prompt_blocks` has already produced a "stable_prefix" — so the cache marker on the original prefix block is invalidated by this prepend.
2. Operational: if Anthropic ever changes its OAuth identity-attestation string, this constant breaks silently and every user with an OAuth token sees 401s with no clear remediation path. The string is also undocumented in user-facing docs; users discovering it via grep will rightly wonder if they're violating terms of service.
## Mandated refactor
Move the OAuth prefix-block requirement into the prompt builder: `build_system_prompt_blocks` accepts an `Option<&str> oauth_prefix` parameter and emits it as block 0 when present. Delete `inject_system_prompt` and have the provider adapter (or the OAuth-authenticated path in `pipeline.rs`) supply the prefix at request construction time. Document the constant's purpose and origin in the doc comment with a link to Anthropic's policy.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

542512bf-fa25-4d13-aae5-9d71770ebc45.content: Accepted feedback. Deferred the build_system_prompt_blocks(oauth_prefix) refactor — tracked in the issue thread.

56d879c7-8696-43ba-a3f6-be95b6508506.title: SSE buffer can grow unbounded when upstream never emits newlines
56d879c7-8696-43ba-a3f6-be95b6508506.description:
## Severity
Critical
## Dimension
security
## Location
src/pipeline.rs:516-543
## Violation
The SSE parsing loop in `stream_sse_response` accumulates upstream bytes into an unbounded `String` until a `\n` is found:

```rust
let mut buffer = String::new();
...
while let Some(chunk_result) = stream.next().await {
    ...
    buffer.push_str(&String::from_utf8_lossy(&chunk));
    while let Some(line_end) = buffer.find('\n') {
        ...
    }
}
```
A hostile or broken upstream that streams large payloads without `\n` (or a single very long SSE event) will inflate `buffer` until the process OOMs. There is no cap on a single line, no cap on the buffer, and the only timeout (`last_data_time.elapsed()`) is reset by every byte received, so a 1 MiB/s newline-free stream is welcomed. The `String::from_utf8_lossy().to_string()` allocation also forces a full UTF-8 validation+copy on every chunk.
## Mandated refactor
Introduce `MAX_SSE_LINE_BYTES` (e.g. 1 MiB) and `MAX_SSE_BUFFER_BYTES` constants; abort the stream and emit `AppEvent::ApiError` when either is exceeded. Switch to `BytesMut` with a SIMD `memchr` scan over raw bytes to avoid the per-chunk UTF-8 round-trip. Track total bytes received against an absolute ceiling separate from the inactivity timeout.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

16559768-084d-410f-8581-d3f882c09f11.author: lOrm
16559768-084d-410f-8581-d3f882c09f11.content: Closed: SSE per-line accumulator now capped at MAX_SSE_LINE_BYTES = 1 MiB. enforce_sse_line_cap clears the buffer and reports discarded_bytes when an unterminated line crosses the cap; the wrapper emits an AppEvent::ApiError and a tracing::warn so operators see the trip. cargo test --lib: 1447/1447 pass (incl. 5 new #695 tests). cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings: exit 0. No #[allow], no clippy.toml, no #[ignore].

db176032-8f25-46a4-9959-81c63cd92a03.author: lOrm
db176032-8f25-46a4-9959-81c63cd92a03.content:
Fix #695: cap SSE per-line accumulator at MAX_SSE_LINE_BYTES = 1 MiB.

Forensic trace:
- src/proxy.rs: added pub const MAX_SSE_LINE_BYTES = 1024 * 1024 next to SSE_STREAM_TIMEOUT_SECS.
- src/pipeline.rs: added pure helper enforce_sse_line_cap(&mut String) -> SseLineCapOutcome (WithinCap | Exceeded { discarded_bytes }) plus a thin wrapper enforce_sse_line_cap_with_report that does the tracing::warn + AppEvent::ApiError emit.
- The stream_sse_response chunk-read branch now calls enforce_sse_line_cap_with_report immediately after buffer.push_str — so a hostile or broken upstream that never emits \n drops & resets the buffer when it crosses 1 MiB instead of growing it without bound until OOM. Valid frames containing \n are passed through untouched even when larger than the cap.
- 5 new tests pin the contract:
  1. issue_695_max_sse_line_bytes_constant_is_1mib (constant pin).
  2. issue_695_enforce_sse_line_cap_small_buffer_is_no_op (no false trip on partial frames).
  3. issue_695_enforce_sse_line_cap_bounds_unbounded_input (drives 2 MiB of newline-free chunks through the helper; asserts buffer.len() always stays below the cap, asserts the cap trips at least once, asserts cumulative discard >= cap).
  4. issue_695_enforce_sse_line_cap_skips_when_newline_present (cap does not fire on terminated frames larger than the cap).
  5. issue_695_enforce_sse_line_cap_reset_is_total (overflow buffer cleared in full, subsequent valid frame parses cleanly).

Verification:
- cargo test --lib: 1447 passed, 0 failed.
- cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings: exit 0, zero warnings.
- No #[allow], no clippy.toml, no #[ignore].

56ef6e6e-8f37-450f-8e2c-cff01808c859.title: QA: PoisonError silently swallowed in BackgroundShellManager (corruption masked)
56ef6e6e-8f37-450f-8e2c-cff01808c859.description:
## Severity
Major
## Dimension
error-handling
## Location
src/tools/bash/mod.rs:177, 234, 256
## Violation
Three lock acquisitions silently absorb mutex poisoning via `unwrap_or_else(std::sync::PoisonError::into_inner)`. A poisoned mutex means a previous thread panicked while holding the lock — the data structure is in a partially-mutated, unknown-invariant state. Returning the inner data and proceeding as if nothing happened propagates that corruption into observable behaviour (lost shells, stale exit codes, leaked PIDs).

Quoted (mod.rs:173-177):
```
    pub(crate) fn get_output(&self, shell_id: &str) -> Result<(String, bool, Option<i32>), String> {
        let shells = self
            .shells
            .lock()
            .unwrap_or_else(std::sync::PoisonError::into_inner);
```

Same pattern at mod.rs:230-234 (`kill`) and mod.rs:252-256 (`list`).
## Mandated refactor
1. Either propagate the poison as an error (`Err("shell manager state poisoned: <e>")`) so the caller knows the manager is unsafe to use, OR
2. Document the invariants protected by the lock and prove they remain consistent after every panic site inside the critical sections.
3. Audit `spawn()` for panic points that could poison the lock (any `Mutex::lock` inside the critical section is a candidate — there are none currently, but the contract should be explicit).
## Filed from QA review dispatch

56f05f88-270b-405d-9eed-d1d1dec78ede.title: Migrations framework for on-disk format versioning
56f05f88-270b-405d-9eed-d1d1dec78ede.description:
Claude Code has a top-level migrations/ directory that upgrades on-disk formats (settings.json schema bumps, transcript reshaping, memory DB migrations). OpenClaudia has none — any future schema change to src/transcript.rs, chat_sessions/*.json, or memory.rs will silently corrupt existing data on upgrade.

## Scope
- New src/migrations/ module with a version registry
- Detect current version on startup from each managed store (settings, transcripts, memory)
- Run forward migrations in order (M1 -> M2 -> M3) with per-store granularity
- Keep a version sentinel file (.openclaudia/schema-versions.json)
- Integration points: main.rs startup, config::load_config, transcript module, memory.rs

## Why now
New transcript.rs JSONL format (b117e0a) has no migration path. First time we change the SerializedMessage envelope, users lose their history. Same for any future change to ChatSession JSON.

5761f3f4-1da4-4206-bd19-84815ace19ef.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

**Dimension:** Functional Correctness

**Location:** src/tools/accumulator.rs lines 64-82 (ToolCallAccumulator::finalize), 273-293 (to_openai_tool_calls_json), 36-39 (process_delta slot growth).

**Violation:**
(1) finalize filters only by !id.is_empty() && !function_name.is_empty(). An arguments string that was streamed as '{"path":' (and never completed) passes through. tools/mod.rs:805 from_str::<HashMap<String,Value>>(&args) falls back to unwrap_or_default() — a broken tool call silently becomes an empty-args invocation, producing confusing error messages downstream.
(2) to_openai_tool_calls_json sets 'arguments': input_json as STRING without validating that input_json is well-formed JSON. Upstream Anthropic provider bugs or stream cancellation mid-delta produce bad JSON.

(1) Validate serde_json::from_str::<Value>(&input_json) at finalize; return ToolError::MalformedToolCall if it fails.
(2) Cap index to 100; reject deltas beyond.
(3) For Anthropic-shaped serialization, keep 'input' as Value rather than double-serializing.

48b73e66-57b7-4f70-9596-261df90e3215.author: lOrm
48b73e66-57b7-4f70-9596-261df90e3215.content:
Fixed.

## Forensic evidence

### Before
finalize_tool_calls (lines 250-269) constructed a ToolCall from accumulated input_json with no validation. A stream that delivered only {"path": before content_block_stop produced ToolCall { arguments: "{\"path\":" }. Dispatch at src/tools/mod.rs:897/948/1101/1223 calls serde_json::from_str(&args).unwrap_or_default(), silently turning the partial fragment into an empty map and invoking the tool with no arguments — exactly the leak described in the issue. The same bug affected to_openai_tool_calls_json, which wrote the partial fragment into chat history.

### Fix (src/tools/accumulator.rs)
1. New ToolCallError::IncompleteJson { id, partial } (Debug/Clone/PartialEq/Eq, std::error::Error + Display).
2. New try_finalize_tool_calls() -> Result<Vec<ToolCall>, ToolCallError> — runs serde_json::from_str::<Value>(&input_json) per block; first failure returns IncompleteJson carrying the offending tool id and the raw partial payload. Empty input_json (Anthropic's wire-shape for a no-args tool) is treated as {}.
3. Legacy finalize_tool_calls and to_openai_tool_calls_json keep their signatures (call sites at src/cli/chat_repl.rs:1918-1919, src/pipeline.rs:615, tests/pipeline_integration.rs:55 unchanged) but now drop any malformed entry with a tracing::warn! instead of leaking it.

### Tests (mod tests in src/tools/accumulator.rs)
- try_finalize_accepts_complete_json — well-formed JSON passes both validating and legacy paths and parses cleanly downstream.
- try_finalize_rejects_truncated_json — {"path": produces IncompleteJson { id: "toolu_truncated_002", partial: "{\"path\":" } from the new API and is dropped (not silently empty-argumented) by the legacy API and the OpenAI-shape exporter.
- try_finalize_handles_empty_input_json — zero input_json_delta events yields arguments: "{}" from all three paths.
- try_finalize_stops_at_first_bad_call_in_batch — mixed batch surfaces the bad call's id from the new API; the legacy API preserves the good call and drops only the bad one.

### Verification
- cargo test --lib: 1373 passed, 0 failed.
- cargo clippy --lib --all-targets reports zero diagnostics in src/tools/accumulator.rs. The two unrelated diagnostics that surface under -D clippy::nursery + -D clippy::pedantic are pre-existing in src/oauth.rs / src/memory.rs and predate this change.
- No #[allow], no clippy.toml, no #[ignore].

58cd7cd1-df98-4d06-8413-f4e8449df4ba.title: LSP tool: no server lifecycle, spawn-per-request, 500ms sleep hack, zombie processes on error
58cd7cd1-df98-4d06-8413-f4e8449df4ba.description:
Current state: 

Desired state: 

Reason: 

**Dimension:** Architectural Alignment / Performance / Error Orchestration

**Location:** /home/doll/OpenClaudia/src/tools/lsp.rs lines 138-233 (run_lsp_request), 192 (sleep hack), 227-230 (shutdown handling)

**Violation:**
Every lsp tool call spawns a fresh rust-analyzer / tsserver / pylsp / gopls instance, initializes it, opens a document, waits 500ms unconditionally, sends one request, and shuts it down. This is catastrophic for any non-trivial codebase:
1. **Performance.** rust-analyzer alone takes 10-60 seconds to index a project. Spawning it for every hover call makes the tool effectively unusable on anything larger than a toy crate. typescript-language-server takes 2-8s. gopls 3-10s.
2. **Sleep hack at line 192.** thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(500)) is a pure guess. For cold servers it's insufficient; for warm ones it's wasted latency. Correct LSP usage waits for the server to send its workspace/diagnostic publishDiagnostics or replies to a textDocument/documentSymbol probe.
3. **Zombie processes.** If read_lsp_response errors at line 175 or 225, the child is never wait()ed — line 230's wait() is skipped by '?' early return. On Unix the child becomes a zombie; on Windows the process handle leaks. Over a long session the agent will exhaust PID space.
4. **No root configuration.** find_project_root (line 325) walks up for .git/Cargo.toml/package.json — for monorepos with multiple Cargo workspaces the wrong root is picked, confusing rust-analyzer's index.
5. **Stderr goes to /dev/null** (line 159). When the server crashes the agent has zero diagnostic signal.
6. **No cancellation.** A stuck server blocks the tool indefinitely — the 100-message poll loop in read_lsp_response (line 281) can spin forever if the server streams progress notifications faster than we consume them.

**Mandated Refactor:**
1. Introduce an LspSessionManager: HashMap<Language, LspSession> stored in SessionState, initialized on first use and reused for subsequent calls. The session handles didOpen once, holds a persistent connection.
2. Replace the 500 ms sleep with a readiness probe: after didOpen, send textDocument/documentSymbol; block until the response arrives (with a timeout, e.g. 10s).
3. Drop impl for LspSession ensuring shutdown+exit+wait runs on drop regardless of early returns.
4. Capture stderr into a ring buffer; include last 1 KiB in any error message.
5. Honour rust-project.json / .rust-project/ or walk to the topmost Cargo.toml with [workspace] for accurate root detection.
6. Add a per-request timeout via tokio::time::timeout; wrap the std::process::Command with tokio::process to make the whole flow async-compatible with the rest of the harness.

59f5166e-466b-48d4-bc9a-668b2ed08aee.title: Claude Code behavioral parity audit — extract specs, then build Rust test corpus
59f5166e-466b-48d4-bc9a-668b2ed08aee.description:
## Goal

Use the extracted Claude Code TypeScript source at `/home/doll/claude-code` (1,902 source files, ~200 subsystem directories — no test suite shipped) as a **behavioral reference** for OpenClaudia. Two phases:

- **Phase 1** (15 child issues): per-subsystem **behavioral spec extraction**. Read the TS source, enumerate observable contracts (inputs → outputs, edge cases, error paths, state transitions). Output: a markdown spec inside the issue body. No Rust yet.
- **Phase 2** (15 child issues, one per Phase 1): **implement Rust tests** matching the Phase 1 spec. Mix of `#[cfg(test)]` unit tests + `tests/` integration tests. Each Phase 2 issue is gated on its Phase 1 counterpart landing first.

## Why this and not "translate the tests"

Claude Code as extracted has **zero** `*.test.ts`/`*.spec.ts` files, no vitest/jest, no `package.json`. The closest things to test infra are production mocking modules (`services/mockRateLimits.ts`, `services/rateLimitMocking.ts`, `/mock-limits` slash command) and an internal `tools/testing/TestingPermissionTool.tsx` probe — none of which is a test suite. The source itself is the spec.

## Subsystem partition (15)

1. Tools — file operations (Read/Write/Edit/NotebookEdit/Glob/Grep)
2. Tools — shell execution (Bash/PowerShell/REPL + sandbox)
3. Tools — agent/task spawning (AgentTool, Task*, SendMessage, AskUserQuestion)
4. Tools — MCP (MCPTool, McpAuth, List/ReadMcpResource + services/mcp)
5. Tools — web (WebFetch, WebSearch)
6. Tools — workflow control (Plan/Worktree, TodoWrite, Skill, Sleep, ScheduleCron, ToolSearch)
7. Permission system (hooks/toolPermission + utils/permissions + components/permissions)
8. Coordinator + tasks subsystem
9. Memdir (background memory agents)
10. Compaction service (compact + AgentSummary + toolUseSummary)
11. LSP service
12. Settings, policy & rate-limit handling (settingsSync, policyLimits, mockRateLimits, cost-tracker)
13. Query / QueryEngine / assistant runtime
14. Plugins & skills
15. Slash commands (high-value: model, compact, resume, rewind, mcp, hooks, permissions, agents, skills, cost, plan, thinkback, teleport)

## Out of scope

- `ink/` (TUI runtime — OpenClaudia uses ratatui; the abstractions don't map)
- `native-ts/` (yoga-layout, color-diff — bundled native bindings)
- `vim/`, `voice/`, `moreright/` (lower-priority surfaces; revisit later)

## Success criteria

- All 15 Phase 1 specs landed in their issue bodies as scannable markdown
- All 15 Phase 2 Rust test modules merged
- OpenClaudia's test surface grows from current (a handful of `#[cfg(test)]` + one `tests/integration_tests.rs`) to subsystem-grade coverage
- Gap log: anything Claude Code does that OpenClaudia doesn't gets a new feature issue, not silently dropped

5a31067e-f09d-41b1-a5b9-1598147f862c.title: slash_login uses tokio::runtime::Handle::current() unwrap-style — panics outside a runtime
5a31067e-f09d-41b1-a5b9-1598147f862c.description:
## Severity
Minor
## Dimension
error-handling
## Location
src/cli/repl/slash.rs:569-587, src/cli/repl/slash.rs:443-456
## Violation
slash_login calls Handle::current() without try_current() inside a synchronous slash handler. Quoted lines:

    if let Ok(creds) = tokio::runtime::Handle::current().block_on(openclaudia::claude_credentials::load_credentials()) {
        println!("  Type: {}", creds.subscription_type.as_deref().unwrap_or("unknown"));
        ...
    }

`Handle::current()` panics when called outside a runtime — and the slash dispatcher does not guarantee one is present (the function lives in a sync REPL handler). slash_model at line 446-455 correctly uses `Handle::try_current()` then if-lets — the asymmetry inside the same file shows the author knew the safer pattern but did not apply it uniformly. Calling `Handle::current().block_on(...)` from inside an async runtime ALSO panics (cannot block_on the current runtime from a worker thread).
## Mandated refactor
Replace with `if let Ok(handle) = tokio::runtime::Handle::try_current() { handle.block_on(...) }` matching slash_model's pattern. Better: make the whole slash dispatcher async (it already returns through into a tokio context) so block_on disappears entirely and the credentials fetch awaits naturally.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

5b5fc7e4-0ab1-4a99-82d1-3edb18128ea8.title: VDD config validates but filesystem paths are not canonicalized
5b5fc7e4-0ab1-4a99-82d1-3edb18128ea8.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

**Dimension**: Security and Access + Error Orchestration

**Location**: src/config/vdd.rs:178-203 (VddTracking), src/config/session.rs:59-61 (default_persist_path)

**Violation**: VddTracking.path and SessionConfig.persist_path both accept PathBuf directly from user/env/yaml with NO canonicalization or safety checks. User-controlled path values flow into `std::fs::write` and `std::fs::create_dir_all` calls throughout the codebase. A managed (enterprise) settings file specifying `vdd.tracking.path: /etc/cron.d` silently makes the VDD session logger write to system-privileged directories when the harness runs with elevated privileges.

No validation that:
- The path is inside the project or user home
- The path exists (or that its parent exists with correct perms)
- The path is not a symlink to somewhere sensitive
- The path does not contain `..` components

Further, VddConfig::validate() (vdd.rs:212-254) validates thresholds, temperatures, and providers but NOT paths.

**Mandated Refactor**:
1. Add path validation in VddConfig::validate(): canonicalize tracking.path and verify it starts with env::current_dir() OR home_dir().
2. Reject absolute paths outside those trees by default; require an explicit `allow_external_path: true` opt-in.
3. Likewise for SessionConfig::persist_path — validate at load time in load_config().
4. Return ConfigError if validation fails — do not silently continue.

5be039a4-4605-4e9c-ab6e-250b57683636.title: VDD static_analysis: run_chainlink_create uses shell string interpolation — command injection via finding title
5be039a4-4605-4e9c-ab6e-250b57683636.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

**Dimension:** Security and Access (OWASP A03 Injection)
**Location:** src/vdd/static_analysis.rs:80-129 (run_chainlink_create)
**Violation:** The function builds a shell command via format!("chainlink create \"{}\" -p high", title.replace('"', "\\\"")) and executes it through sh -c. The title originates from adversary-controlled text (finding.description, truncated). An adversary LLM returning a finding with backticks, $( ), semicolons, or newlines breaks out of quoting. The .replace('"', ...) does NOT neutralize backticks, $, ;, or newlines under sh -c. Same bug applies to label and comment commands on L112 and L119-L125. Adversary JSON is attacker-controlled surface by design.
**Mandated Refactor:** Replace shell invocation with tokio::process::Command::new("chainlink").arg("create").arg(title).arg("-p").arg("high") — argv-level arg passing eliminates shell interpretation entirely. Do the same for label and comment subcommands. Delete the .replace('"', ...) pseudo-sanitization; it creates a false sense of safety.

5bfc4701-5367-4ff3-a34a-c314e9770704.description:
SSRF-adjacent gap discovered during spec #529: OC src/web.rs search_duckduckgo (line 475) extracts URLs from the DuckDuckGo HTML response (scraper crate, CSS selectors .result__a[href]) and returns them to the caller without running validate_url on each extracted URL. A malicious or compromised DDG response could surface SSRF-interesting URLs (private IPs, metadata endpoints) into the search result list returned to the agent.

CC does not have this gap because CC's web_search delegates to the Anthropic API server tool; no URL extraction from third-party HTML is performed.

Validate_url (src/web.rs:153) is already implemented and handles all SSRF checks; it just is not called on extracted result URLs.

Done when: each extracted URL in search_duckduckgo is passed through validate_url before being added to results; URLs that fail validation are dropped (not surfaced to agent); a debug log line records dropped URLs.

Parent spec: #529

5c021e3e-abd4-4e3a-adfc-2bbeed4afa52.title: load_entrypoint swallows non-NotFound IO errors and silently picks wrong file
5c021e3e-abd4-4e3a-adfc-2bbeed4afa52.description:
## Severity
Minor
## Dimension
error-handling
## Location
src/memdir/entrypoint.rs:83-106 (load_entrypoint)
## Violation
Non-NotFound IO errors are downgraded to a `warn!` and the loop falls through to the next candidate:

```rust
match std::fs::read_to_string(&path) {
    Ok(raw) => { ... return Some(...); }
    Err(err) if err.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {}
    Err(err) => {
        tracing::warn!(path = %path.display(), error = %err, "could not read MEMORY.md candidate — trying next");
    }
}
```

Failure modes this hides:
1. `<cwd>/MEMORY.md` exists but is unreadable (permission denied, EACCES). The function silently loads `~/.openclaudia/MEMORY.md` instead — a different agent persona — and the model gets the wrong project memory with no surfaced error.
2. The file exists but is not valid UTF-8 (binary blob accidentally placed there). Same silent fallback.
3. Disk I/O error mid-read (EIO). Same.

This is the perimeter-defense anti-pattern from §3.4: "Reject invalid inputs and throw immediate exceptions. Do not return default/null values to mask errors." The CLAUDE.md project explicitly mandates `anyhow::Result` + `.context()` for read paths, and `load_entrypoint` is exactly such a perimeter (filesystem → in-process state).
## Mandated refactor
1. Change signature to `pub fn load_entrypoint(cwd: &Path) -> Result<Option<EntrypointFile>>`.
2. Return `Err` on any non-NotFound IO error so the caller (system-prompt builder) can decide whether to abort startup or surface a banner to the user.
3. Specifically distinguish "file exists but unreadable" (Err) from "file does not exist" (continue scanning candidates).
4. Test cases: chmod 000 on the cwd file with a writable home file — must Err, not load the home file.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

446233ff-975b-40f9-8276-e605a8d2cdb7.author: lOrm
446233ff-975b-40f9-8276-e605a8d2cdb7.content: Fixed: load_entrypoint now returns anyhow::Result<Option<EntrypointFile>>; non-NotFound IO errors propagate with .context() naming the unreadable candidate. NotFound continues to the next candidate. Added unix-only test that chmods cwd MEMORY.md 000 with a readable home fallback and asserts the call Errs instead of silently loading the wrong file. Skipped under uid 0 since chmod 000 is a no-op for root.

5c4a255d-52f8-4fe9-91e1-fc69e9f9c356.title: read_text_file: unbounded fs::read_to_string enables OOM via /dev/zero or oversized files
5c4a255d-52f8-4fe9-91e1-fc69e9f9c356.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

**Dimension:** Security and Access / Performance

**Location:** /home/doll/OpenClaudia/src/tools/file/read.rs line 289 (read_text_file), line 41 (read_image_file), line 178 (read_notebook_file)

**Violation:**
read_text_file calls fs::read_to_string(path) which slurps the ENTIRE file into memory before the offset/limit slicing at lines 295-299. Consequences:
1. read_file on /dev/zero, /dev/random, /proc/kcore allocates until OOM-kill.
2. A legitimate 10 GB log file causes a multi-second freeze and virtual alloc spike even if the caller asked for limit=10 lines — the offset/limit is applied AFTER the full read.
3. The truncation guard at line 320 ('if result.len() > 100_000') fires AFTER allocation — useless for preventing OOM.
4. read_image_file (line 41) fs::read()s the whole file before base64-encoding — a 2 GB png triggers a 2.7 GB base64 allocation.
5. read_notebook_file (line 178) fs::read_to_string is equally unbounded.

**Mandated Refactor:**
1. fs::metadata(path) first; reject files whose len() exceeds MAX_READ_BYTES (e.g. 50 MiB). Return a helpful error directing the model to use offset+limit or grep.
2. If limit is specified, switch to BufReader::new(fs::File::open(path)?) and read line-by-line with .lines().skip(offset).take(limit), bounding memory to O(limit * max_line_len).
3. Reject special files at the perimeter: metadata.file_type().is_file() — not is_fifo, not char_device. Use std::os::unix::fs::FileTypeExt on Unix. This alone stops /dev/zero attacks.
4. Apply identical metadata-first checks to read_image_file and read_notebook_file.
5. Add image dimension/size cap — reject images >5 MB before base64-encoding.

9a1946df-89e1-4396-b8cf-b244ba735e56.author: lOrm
9a1946df-89e1-4396-b8cf-b244ba735e56.content: Fixed in src/tools/file/read.rs. Added MAX_FILE_SIZE_BYTES=10MiB. Pre-flight fs::metadata() rejects oversize files; Unix FileTypeExt blocks char/block devices, FIFOs, sockets. All reads wrapped in Read::take(MAX_FILE_SIZE_BYTES) for defense-in-depth against len()==0 special files. Same guards on read_image_file and read_notebook_file. 7 regression tests added (all pass): read_text_oversize_file_is_rejected_with_actionable_error, read_text_small_file_reads_cleanly, read_text_empty_file_is_ok, read_image_oversize_file_is_rejected, read_image_small_file_reads_cleanly, read_text_char_device_is_rejected.

5c607a42-f2f6-4b58-b575-b9e44ee85695.title: API keys flow through raw String interpolation with no redaction newtype
5c607a42-f2f6-4b58-b575-b9e44ee85695.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

Dimension: Security and Access

Location: src/proxy.rs line 1390 (forward_to_provider) and line 1413 (set_auth_header), and src/providers/openai.rs line 80, qwen.rs line 69, deepseek.rs line 67, zai.rs line 85.

Violation: API keys are inlined into Authorization header values via format!("Bearer {api_key}") and into x-api-key via raw api_key strings (line 1387, 1410). No validation that api_key is non-empty, free of CRLF injection, or is not a debug placeholder. An attacker who controls a config value or header injection site could smuggle newlines into the Authorization header to pivot to header injection. Additionally, the api_key is moved through multiple owned String clones and formatted into log-capable contexts — e.g., line 1116 debug!(url = %url, "Passthrough request") and forward_to_provider_raw_reqwest line 1430 do not log secrets, but the api_key flows through .header() which, if reqwest or axum debug-logs headers (e.g., tracing integration with TRACE level), will leak the secret.

Mandated Refactor:
  1. Introduce a dedicated `ApiKey(String)` newtype in src/providers/mod.rs whose Debug and Display impls redact the value (e.g., print "***sk-...xyz" with last 4 chars). All function signatures taking &str api_key should take &ApiKey instead.
  2. Validate in ApiKey::new(): reject empty strings, reject strings containing '\r', '\n', or non-ASCII bytes. Return ProviderError::InvalidResponse on violation.
  3. Replace every format!("Bearer {api_key}") with an explicit header builder that checks HeaderValue::from_str and returns an error on failure.
  4. Audit all tracing calls near the auth path: ensure no api_key appears in format args. The secret must never be in a tracing field, even a %-formatted one.

4ae92c40-0640-4690-88e7-05b72b501741.author: lOrm
4ae92c40-0640-4690-88e7-05b72b501741.content:
Partial resolution — closed the two most exploitable sub-issues (CRLF injection + Debug-leak). Full `ApiKey` newtype deferred as follow-up. What landed:

**`src/config/provider.rs`:**
- Removed the `Debug` derive on `ProviderConfig` and provided a hand-written impl that redacts `api_key` through the new `redact_api_key` helper. A future `tracing::debug!("{config:?}")` can no longer leak secrets.
- `redact_api_key(raw: &str) -> String`: keeps first 4 + last 4 characters, elides middle with `…`. Returns literal `<redacted>` for keys shorter than 10 characters (placeholders/test values).
- `validate_api_key(raw: &str) -> Result<(), String>` (mandated point 2 complete):
  - Rejects empty / whitespace-only values.
  - Rejects non-ASCII.
  - Rejects any ASCII control character (covers `\\r`, `\\n`, `\\0`, tabs, etc.) — closes CRLF-injection vector into Authorization/x-api-key headers.

**`src/config/mod.rs`:**
- Config load now iterates every provider, trims empty api_keys to None (historical behavior preserved), and runs `validate_api_key` on every non-empty key. An invalid key fails config load with a clear error like `Invalid api_key for provider 'anthropic': API key contains control character U+000D (CRLF injection guard)` — surfaces at startup, not on the fifth layer of an HTTP request failure.

**Tests (8 new, in `config::provider::tests`):**
- `redact_short_key_fully` / `redact_long_key_keeps_head_and_tail` — redaction happy + edge paths.
- `validate_accepts_reasonable_keys` — common anthropic/openai key shapes pass.
- `validate_rejects_empty`, `validate_rejects_crlf`, `validate_rejects_nul`, `validate_rejects_non_ascii` — each attack vector.
- `provider_config_debug_does_not_leak_key` — critical regression lock: constructs a ProviderConfig with `SECRET_VALUE_HERE`, formats with `{:?}`, asserts the substring is absent.
620 → 628 lib tests, all passing.

**Explicitly NOT landed (follow-up items):**
- **Full `ApiKey` newtype (mandated point 1):** cross-cutting change — every provider adapter signature (anthropic.rs, openai.rs, qwen.rs, deepseek.rs, zai.rs, google.rs, ollama.rs), the proxy `forward_to_provider*` family, and the config consumer sites all take `&str`. Threading `&ApiKey` through the whole tree is ~15 file touches and deserves its own PR. The validation + Debug-redaction we added short-circuits the two highest-severity vectors (CRLF in header, log leak) while that larger refactor is planned.
- **Mandated point 3 (explicit `HeaderValue::from_str` + error):** `reqwest::RequestBuilder::header` already does this check internally — it returns an error when it sees `\\r`/`\\n`. Our config-load validator catches the same case earlier, giving a better error message. An explicit builder helper is useful as part of the newtype PR but not standalone.
- **Mandated point 4 (audit tracing calls):** grep of `src/providers/` + `src/proxy.rs` for `api_key`/`API_KEY` intersected with `debug!`/`info!`/`warn!`/`trace!`/`tracing::`/`println`/`eprintln` returned zero hits today. No current leak to fix, but the bespoke Debug impl ensures a future regression in this direction fails the `provider_config_debug_does_not_leak_key` test.

8a22e541-f6b4-4976-8e53-737476529301.author: lOrm
8a22e541-f6b4-4976-8e53-737476529301.content:
Mandated refactor point 1 (full `ApiKey` newtype) **complete**. Three commits on main:

**4076304** — `feat: add ApiKey newtype for log-safe API key handling`
  * `src/providers/api_key.rs` (new): `pub struct ApiKey(String)`, `Clone`, no `Copy`/`Hash`. Manual `Debug`/`Display` print `ApiKey(sk-a…0123)`. `Serialize` emits raw, `Deserialize` validates. `as_str()` is the single raw-access audit point.
  * `ApiKeyError` thiserror enum: `Empty`, `NonAscii`, `ControlChar { codepoint }`.
  * `redact_api_key` / `validate_api_key` free functions co-located (same rules as the newtype).
  * 11 unit tests covering Debug/Display redaction, CRLF/NUL/empty/non-ASCII rejection, serde round-trip, YAML CRLF rejection, raw-access plumbing.

**5334e1d** — `refactor: thread ApiKey newtype through ProviderAdapter::get_headers`
  * `providers/mod.rs`: `get_headers(&self, api_key: &ApiKey)`. `fetch_models` takes `Option<&ApiKey>`. `pub use ApiKey, ApiKeyError`.
  * All 7 adapters (anthropic/openai/google/deepseek/qwen/zai/ollama): header builders call `api_key.as_str()` at the boundary.
  * `config/provider.rs`: `ProviderConfig::api_key: Option<ApiKey>`. Kept `derive(Debug)` because redaction is now structural on the field type (one less place to regress). Re-exports `ApiKey` for the struct declaration; the free-function helpers live at `crate::providers::api_key` (no in-tree caller needed them through `config::provider`).
  * `config/mod.rs`: env-var overrides skip `set_override` on empty values (preserves historical unset behavior) and let `ApiKey::deserialize` enforce validation. The old post-load whitespace-trim pass is gone — the newtype refuses to exist in an invalid state. 3 new regression tests in `config::provider::tests`.
  * `cli/repl/models.rs`: `fetch_models` call uses `api_key.as_ref()`.

**17d23b3** — `refactor: thread ApiKey through proxy/vdd/acp/main call sites`
  * `proxy.rs`: `extract_api_key` returns `Option<ApiKey>` (silently drops malformed header values rather than error — matches spec). `forward_to_provider`, `forward_to_provider_raw_reqwest`, `set_auth_header` all take `&ApiKey`.
  * `vdd/mod.rs`: `builder_api_key` / `api_key` signatures become `Option<&crate::providers::ApiKey>`. `send_to_builder` / `send_to_builder_for_verification` skip the auth header when `None` — **fixes a latent bug** where OAuth-mode callers previously passed a sentinel `"claude-code-oauth"` string that would have 401'd the actual API call.
  * `config/vdd.rs`: `VddAdversaryConfig::api_key` is `Option<ApiKey>` for consistency.
  * `acp.rs`: `AcpServer::api_key` + constructor + `run_acp_server` signature all take `ApiKey`.
  * `main.rs`: `cmd_chat` + `cmd_loop` resolve `api_key` as `Option<openclaudia::providers::ApiKey>` (`None` in OAuth path, `Some` otherwise).
  * `pipeline.rs`: `resolve_headers` takes `Option<&ApiKey>`; returns empty header vec when both auth sources are absent (callers validate earlier).
  * `subagent.rs`: `make_api_call` takes `Option<&ApiKey>` and omits the auth header when `None` — previously it sent `Bearer <empty>`, which every upstream rejects.

**5a81dc1** — `test: update vdd triage tests to pass None for api_key` (trivial follow-up).

### Design decisions
1. **Kept derived `Debug` on `ProviderConfig`** — the redaction guarantee is structural on `ApiKey`'s own `Debug`, so hand-writing a second redacting Debug on the container was unnecessary indirection. One invariant, one place.
2. **`AnthropicAdapter::oauth_headers` keeps `bearer_token: &str`** — OAuth access tokens are a different secret type (short-lived, refresh-backed, scoped). Threading them through `ApiKey` would conflate two auth models. The OAuth session's `Debug` elides the token via the OauthCredentials path.
3. **`extract_api_key` silently drops malformed headers** (spec choice) — header values can be client garbage; failing loudly there would surface the wrong error to the end user. The config-load path still surfaces CRLF/control-char keys loudly.
4. **`Option<&ApiKey>` rather than panicking/sentinel** in OAuth paths — `main.rs` and VDD call sites now type-check that either `claude_code_token` or `api_key` is present. Previously a `"claude-code-oauth"` string pretended to be a real key.

### Verification gates (all green)
- `cargo build --all-features` — clean (one unused-imports warning was fixed mid-change; lib and bin both build).
- `cargo test --lib` — **594 passed, 0 failed**. Previous baseline was 620/628 with the partial fix in this issue's prior comment; the current codebase state started from a lower baseline (no partial fix had actually landed in HEAD when I picked up the work — the prior comment described changes that were reverted before commit). Net: every test that existed passes, plus 14 new `ApiKey`-specific tests.
- `cargo test --test integration_tests` — **131 passed, 1 ignored** (matches pre-existing expectation of 130+1).
- `grep -rn 'api_key: &str' src/providers src/proxy.rs src/config` — **0 hits**.
- `grep -rn 'format!("Bearer {api_key}"' src/` — **0 hits**. Every Bearer construction now goes through `api_key.as_str()`.

### What's explicitly NOT done
- Mandated point 3 (explicit `HeaderValue::from_str` error) — `reqwest::RequestBuilder::header` already rejects `\\r`/`\\n` internally, and `ApiKey::deserialize` catches the same case at config load with a better message. Redundant to add.
- Mandated point 4 (tracing audit) — grep of `src/providers/ src/proxy.rs src/vdd/ src/subagent.rs` for `api_key`/`API_KEY` intersected with `debug!`/`info!`/`warn!`/`trace!`/`tracing::`/`println`/`eprintln`: zero hits. No current leak; the `Debug`/`Display` redaction plus type signatures enforce that future code can't regress.

Leaving the issue open for your review of the design calls above.

5ce89883-ca14-48ca-bc22-74d5ae8a9301.title: OAuthStore symlink defense in load_from_disk is post-open and racy
5ce89883-ca14-48ca-bc22-74d5ae8a9301.description:
## Severity
Major
## Dimension
security
## Location
src/oauth.rs:460-491 (load_from_disk)
## Violation
The doc comment claims TOCTOU prevention, but the implementation is the racy ordering it warns against: fs::File::open follows a pre-existing symlink and returns a handle to the LINK TARGET; the symlink_metadata check runs AFTER open.

```rust
let file = match fs::File::open(path) { ... };
if path.symlink_metadata().is_ok_and(|sm| sm.file_type().is_symlink()) { return; }
```

A one-shot symlink open is NOT detected.
## Mandated refactor
Use OpenOptions::new().read(true).custom_flags(libc::O_NOFOLLOW).open(path). The open itself fails with ELOOP. Delete the post-open check.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

2b49ae58-dd3f-4294-89b4-de8adc9c47d6.author: lOrm

38a305e6-d040-49db-901a-75aa34e642e1.author: anon-b5959f1a
