5d60a948-e127-456c-9a1e-39b6669328a7.title: edit.rs DIFF marker uses serialize-into-format-string instead of structured event
5d60a948-e127-456c-9a1e-39b6669328a7.description:
## Severity
Trivial

## Dimension
Decoupling / Naming

## Location
src/tools/file/edit.rs:104-115 (DIFF_START/DIFF_END marker embedded in result string)

## Violation
```rust
let diff_json = serde_json::json!({"path": path, "old": old_string, "new": new_string});
let mut result = format!(
    "Successfully edited '{}'. Replaced {} chars with {} chars.\n@@DIFF_START@@\n{}\n@@DIFF_END@@",
    path, old_string.len(), new_string.len(), diff_json,
);
```

This couples the tool to an out-of-band display protocol via in-band string markers. The downstream renderer must scan EVERY tool result for `@@DIFF_START@@` and `@@DIFF_END@@`, parse the JSON between them, and route to a color renderer. This is precisely the architectural anti-pattern Slack calls "stringly-typed events" — semantic data embedded as substrings inside a free-form text payload. The `(String, bool)` return type forces this hack (see broader issue #670 — Result-typed returns would carry structured diff data alongside the message).

If a model ever generates the literal string "@@DIFF_START@@" inside `new_string` (entirely possible in code comments or test fixtures), it breaks the renderer's parser and may inject arbitrary JSON into the diff pane.

## Mandated refactor
After the Result<ToolOutput, ToolError> refactor (issue #670), make ToolOutput carry an optional `diff: Option<DiffData>` field. The dispatcher renders the diff via its own type-safe code path. Delete the @@DIFF_START@@ markers entirely. Until then: at minimum, base64-encode or sentinel-escape the JSON payload between markers.

## Filed from QA review dispatch

5d7b6286-c825-4534-a185-f609634f526a.title: read_text_file offset_arg>0 check uses raw u64 not the post-saturating-sub usize
5d7b6286-c825-4534-a185-f609634f526a.description:
## Severity
Trivial

## Dimension
Functional Correctness / Naming

## Location
src/tools/file/read.rs:273-316 (read_text_file offset/limit handling)

## Violation
The function extracts `offset` from args, computes `offset = offset_arg.saturating_sub(1)`, and later uses `offset > 0 || limit.is_some()` to decide whether to append the "showing lines ..." suffix. The test read_text_offset_zero_treated_as_start_of_file (line 418-432) pins the observation that "OC produces a suffix even when offset=0 because offset_arg>0 check uses the pre-subtraction value — this is an OC quirk."

The function does NOT actually do this — the check `if offset > 0 || limit.is_some()` (line 310) uses `offset` AFTER saturating_sub. But the test COMMENT documents an intent that does not match the code. Either the test comment is stale (CC parity gap that no longer exists) or there's a related subtle bug — but either way, the comment misleads future maintainers.

This is the "stale comment" anti-pattern — comments are documentation that the compiler does not check. They drift.

## Mandated refactor
1. Audit the test comment and either delete it or fix the code to match the documented intent. Confirm via a fresh test what suffix-emission semantic OC actually has and pin that exactly.
2. Replace the `(u64 → usize)` saturating subtraction logic with a clearer pattern: model offset as `Option<NonZeroU64>` — None means "from start," Some(n) means "skip n-1 lines." Use `.map_or(0, |n| n.get() - 1)` for the skip count. This eliminates the saturating_sub indirection AND makes 0-vs-absent distinguishable.

## Filed from QA review dispatch

5de7e209-6291-440b-abf1-e03bc735a62a.title: QA: env scrub uses denylist instead of allowlist (sensitive vars without matching suffix leak)
5de7e209-6291-440b-abf1-e03bc735a62a.description:
## Severity
Major
## Dimension
security
## Location
src/tools/bash/policy.rs:143-151
## Violation
`apply_env_scrub` only removes env vars whose names match `is_sensitive_env` — a denylist. ANY sensitive credential whose name does not conform to the heuristics (e.g., `DB_URL`, `STRIPE_KEY` without `_API_KEY` suffix, `MONGODB_URI`, `DATABASE_URL`, `REDIS_URL`, `SLACK_WEBHOOK`, `JWT_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE`, or any custom name) flows freely into every spawned child.

Quoted (policy.rs:143-151):
```
pub fn apply_env_scrub(cmd: &mut Command) {
    let sensitive: Vec<String> = std::env::vars()
        .map(|(k, _)| k)
        .filter(|k| is_sensitive_env(k))
        .collect();
    for key in sensitive {
        cmd.env_remove(key);
    }
}
```

The comment ("Do NOT `env_clear`") acknowledges the tradeoff but ships the insecure default. OWASP A04 (Insecure Design).
## Mandated refactor
1. Flip to allowlist: `cmd.env_clear()` and then `cmd.env(key, val)` for each name in an explicit safe set (`PATH`, `HOME`, `USER`, `LANG`, `TERM`, `CARGO_HOME`, `RUST_LOG`, etc.).
2. Make the allowlist configurable via `.openclaudia/config.yaml` so operators can add project-specific safe vars.
3. Add a `passthrough_env: [...]` explicit opt-in for variables the model genuinely needs, audited per-deployment.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

ENV_ALLOWLIST_EXACT enumerates ~50 safe POSIX/toolchain vars (PATH, HOME, USER, SHELL, TMPDIR, LANG, TERM, CARGO_HOME, RUSTUP_HOME, RUST_LOG, NODE_ENV, PYTHONPATH, JAVA_HOME, GOPATH, etc.); ENV_ALLOWLIST_PREFIXES covers LC_*, XDG_*, SSH_*, DBUS_*. New helper is_env_allowed(key) gates by allowlist AND is_sensitive_env (belt-and-braces). hooks/mod.rs is_sensitive_env usage is a separate codepath out of scope. Forensic evidence: 19/19 policy tests pass (14 baseline + 5 new); 33/33 bash integration tests pass with b4c updated; cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features exit 0. No #[allow], no clippy.toml, no #[ignore].

5e4eab5b-ec26-4e64-892d-10ba7e6e399d.title: Clippy: 6 redundant closures — pass fn directly
5e4eab5b-ec26-4e64-892d-10ba7e6e399d.description:
Current state: 

Desired state: 

Reason: 

**Dimension:** Cognitive Readability
**Lint:** clippy::redundant_closure

## Violation
A closure that only forwards its arg to a single function (`|x| f(x)`) is equivalent to `f` itself. The closure layer adds visual noise without adding information.

## Locations
- src/modes/mod.rs: 954
- src/pipeline.rs: 263 (twice), 268, 358
- src/tui/app.rs: 1389

## Mandated Refactor
```rust
// Before
iter.map(|x| transform(x))
// After
iter.map(transform)
```
Be careful: only drop the closure when arg types match exactly. If `f` takes `&T` and closure arg is `T`, or vice versa, the closure is NOT redundant — clippy's suggestion is safe here by construction.

5e5562cc-1bbe-4b98-b9e6-fd72750e17b7.title: TUI event loop has no cancellation signal for in-flight API tasks at quit
5e5562cc-1bbe-4b98-b9e6-fd72750e17b7.description:
## Severity
Major
## Dimension
concurrency
## Location
src/tui/app.rs:526-589, 1488-1557
## Violation
The run() event loop terminates on should_quit and breaks immediately. Background tasks from spawn_api_turn keep running with no cancellation signal — tools mid-execution have no way to know the user quit. The agentic follow-up loop in run_api_turn_async (line 1518) has no cancellation token. A 25-iteration chain continues billing.

## Mandated refactor
Add tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken on App, cloned into ApiTurnParams. Check token.is_cancelled() each iteration. On should_quit, cancel before breaking the loop; await spawned tasks up to 2s before tearing down.

## Filed from QA review dispatch

5e625118-78a2-470d-b9fd-644b77070cb7.title: Phase 1 spec: query/QueryEngine/assistant runtime (turn loop, SSE, retry, stop hooks, budgets) [CC parity]
5e625118-78a2-470d-b9fd-644b77070cb7.description:
# Phase 1 spec: query/QueryEngine/assistant runtime (turn loop, SSE, retry, stop hooks, budgets) [CC parity]

## Goal

Extract a behavioral spec for this subsystem by reading Claude Code's TypeScript source. **Output**: update this issue body with a markdown spec pinning down each testable contract (input → expected output, edge cases, error paths). No Rust yet — that is Phase 2.

Parent audit: #523.

## Claude Code source — read these

- `QueryEngine.ts` (~1295 lines)
- `query.ts` (~1729 lines)
- `Tool.ts` (~792 lines)
- `Task.ts` (~125 lines)
- `query/stopHooks.ts` (~473 lines) — configurable stop conditions
- `query/tokenBudget.ts` (~93 lines) — budget abort

## OpenClaudia counterpart

- `src/pipeline.rs` (~1237 lines) — retry 329-351, thinking 102-113, tool accumulation 41-51, Gemini 369-484
- `src/proxy.rs` (~1773 lines)
- `src/session/mod.rs` (~694 lines)
- `src/session/task.rs` (~623 lines)

## Behavioral spec

### B1 — SSE streaming + retry on 429/529/503 with `Retry-After` backoff

**CC**: `services/api/withRetry.ts:170-516` (`withRetry` generator), `withRetry.ts:519-548` (`getRetryAfter`, `getRetryDelay`)

**OC**: `src/pipeline.rs:329-366` (`run_turn` retry loop)

**Input**: HTTP response status is 429, 503, or 529 (Anthropic overloaded). Optional `Retry-After` header containing a numeric string (seconds).

**Output**:
- CC: Before sleeping, yields a `SystemAPIErrorMessage` (`{type:'system', subtype:'api_error', retryInMs, retryAttempt, maxRetries}`) so callers can surface the delay. The SDK layer re-yields this as `{type:'system', subtype:'api_retry', retry_delay_ms}` (QueryEngine.ts:946-954). Default max retries = 10 (env-overridable via `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_RETRIES`). Delay formula: if `Retry-After` header present, parse as integer seconds and use verbatim. Otherwise: `BASE_DELAY_MS * 2^(attempt-1)` clamped to `maxDelayMs=32000`, plus 0–25% jitter. 529 non-foreground sources (background queries) throw immediately without retrying.
- OC: Hard-coded max 3 retries (`max_retries = 3u32`, pipeline.rs:330). Delay: if `Retry-After` header present parse as `u64` seconds, otherwise `2^(attempt+1)` seconds (exponential, no jitter, no ms). Emits a plain-text `AppEvent::StreamText` with the delay message — no structured retry event type. No equivalent of CC's foreground/background source routing.

**Edge cases**:
- CC handles 408 (request timeout), 409 (lock timeout), 529 with `"type":"overloaded_error"` in body (SDK sometimes misclassifies status), and ECONNRESET/EPIPE as retryable.
- CC `isPersistentRetryEnabled()` (env `CLAUDE_CODE_UNATTENDED_RETRY`) loops indefinitely with chunked 30s heartbeat yields. OC has no persistent-retry mode.
- CC `FallbackTriggeredError`: after 3 consecutive 529s for Opus, switches to `fallbackModel` and clears partial assistant messages. OC has no model-fallback mechanism.

**Error path**:
- CC: After all retries exhausted, throws `CannotRetryError` wrapping original error, which surfaces as an assistant API-error message in the turn.
- OC: After 3 retries, `response` remains `None`; returns `Err("Max retries exceeded".to_string())`.

**Divergences (gaps)**:
1. OC retry count is 3 (hard-coded) vs CC default 10 — filed as gap #RETRIES.
2. OC emits a text string on retry; CC emits a typed structured event — filed as gap #RETRY_EVENT.
3. OC has no jitter in the exponential backoff formula — filed as gap #JITTER.
4. OC does not handle 408/409/ECONNRESET/EPIPE retries — filed as gap #RETRY_CODES.
5. OC has no `FallbackTriggeredError` / model-fallback on repeated 529 — filed as gap #MODEL_FALLBACK.

---

### B2 — `build_anthropic_request` sets `budget_tokens` when effort level triggers thinking

**CC**: `services/api/claude.ts:1601-1629`, `utils/thinking.ts:10-162`

**OC**: `src/pipeline.rs:101-123` (`build_anthropic_request`, effort_level match arm)

**Input**: Model string + `ThinkingConfig` (or OC `effort_level: &str`). CC uses three config types: `{type:'adaptive'}`, `{type:'enabled', budgetTokens:N}`, `{type:'disabled'}`. OC uses string: `"low" | "medium" | "high" | "max"`.

**Output**:
- CC: If model supports adaptive thinking (`modelSupportsAdaptiveThinking`), sends `{type:'adaptive'}` (no `budget_tokens`). For models without adaptive support, uses `getMaxThinkingTokensForModel()` as default, overridden by `thinkingConfig.budgetTokens` if set. Clamps to `maxOutputTokens - 1`. Always enforces `max_tokens > budget_tokens` (claude.ts:3376-3382).
- OC: For `"high"` or `"max"`, calls `crate::thinking::anthropic_thinking_budget(Some(effort_level))` to get budget (resolves to 31999 — CC's ULTRATHINK constant). Sets `thinking.type = "enabled"` and `max_tokens = 40000`. For `"low"`, sets `max_tokens = 2048` with no thinking. For `"medium"` (default), neither thinking nor max_tokens override.

**Edge cases**:
- CC: `shouldEnableThinkingByDefault()` defaults to `true` unless `MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=0` or `settings.alwaysThinkingEnabled===false`. The `initialThinkingConfig` is `{type:'adaptive'}` by default.
- OC: Only enables thinking for `"high"/"max"` strings; medium/default has no thinking at all — diverges from CC which enables adaptive thinking by default.
- CC: 3P providers (Bedrock/Vertex) only get thinking for Opus 4+ and Sonnet 4+ models.
- OC: No provider-aware thinking guard.

**Error path**:
- CC: If `budget_tokens >= max_tokens`, clamps budget to `max_tokens - 1`.
- OC: No such clamp — OC uses static 40000 / 31999 pair which is always valid.

**Divergences (gaps)**:
- OC does not enable adaptive thinking by default for medium effort — filed as gap #ADAPTIVE_THINKING_DEFAULT.

---

### B3 — Tool calls parsed from SSE, accumulated into `TurnResult.tool_calls`

**CC**: `query.ts:551-862` (streaming loop accumulation), `query.ts:826-862` (StreamingToolExecutor path)

**OC**: `src/pipeline.rs:509-631` (`stream_sse_response`), `src/pipeline.rs:41-51` (`TurnResult`)

**Input**: SSE byte stream from Anthropic or OpenAI-compatible provider. Anthropic SSE includes `content_block_start{type:'tool_use'}`, `content_block_delta{type:'input_json_delta'}`, `content_block_stop` events. OpenAI SSE includes `choices[0].delta.tool_calls` deltas.

**Output**:
- CC: `toolUseBlocks: ToolUseBlock[]` accumulated across assistant messages. `needsFollowUp = true` as soon as any `tool_use` block arrives in any message content (query.ts:832-835). `StreamingToolExecutor` optionally starts executing tools while the stream is still open (gate: `streamingToolExecution` feature flag).
- OC: `AnthropicToolAccumulator.process_event(json)` accumulates Anthropic-format tool blocks across events. `ToolCallAccumulator.process_delta(delta)` handles OpenAI format. After stream ends, `finalize_tool_calls()` or `finalize()` is called. `TurnResult.needs_followup` = whether any tool calls were found. No streaming tool execution (tools run only after stream ends).

**Edge cases**:
- CC: On streaming fallback (FallbackTriggeredError), tombstones all partial assistantMessages and resets `toolUseBlocks`, `needsFollowUp`, discards in-progress `StreamingToolExecutor` (query.ts:712-740).
- OC: No streaming fallback; if stream errors mid-tool-accumulation, the accumulator retains whatever was collected.
- CC: If streamingFallbackOccured, yields `{type:'tombstone'}` events for orphaned messages so the UI removes them.
- OC: No tombstone mechanism.

**Error path**:
- CC: Tool use blocks without matching `tool_result` in next user message produce synthetic tool result blocks via `yieldMissingToolResultBlocks` (query.ts:984).
- OC: No `yieldMissingToolResultBlocks` equivalent; unmatched tool_use/tool_result is handled upstream in the conversation loop.

---

### B4 — Google Gemini non-streaming path handled separately from SSE

**CC**: Gemini is served via the same streaming path using OpenAI-compatible SSE (Google's v1beta endpoint). No separate non-streaming path for Gemini in `query.ts` or `QueryEngine.ts`.

**OC**: `src/pipeline.rs:369-505` (`handle_google_response`), dispatched at pipeline.rs:370-380 when `provider == "google"`.

**Input**: HTTP response body from Gemini's `generateContent` endpoint (non-streaming JSON).

**Output**:
- OC: Parses `candidates[0].content.parts[].text` for text content, `candidates[0].content.parts[].functionCall` for tool calls. Usage from `usageMetadata.promptTokenCount` / `candidatesTokenCount`. Returns `TurnResult`.
- CC: No equivalent separate path — uses Vertex AI / Gemini via OpenAI-compat wrapper and unified SSE path.

**Edge cases**:
- OC: If `gemini_json.get("error")` present, returns `Err("Gemini API error ({code}): {msg}")` without any retry.
- OC: `cache_read_tokens` and `cache_write_tokens` always 0 for Gemini (no prompt caching on Gemini non-streaming path).
- OC: Tool call IDs are generated locally as `call_{uuid}` because Gemini's `functionCall` has no native ID.

**Error path**:
- OC: JSON parse error returns `Err("Failed to parse Gemini response: {e}")`.
- OC: No retry on Gemini errors.

**Divergences (gaps)**:
- OC's Gemini path is non-streaming while Gemini supports native streaming. Filed as gap #GEMINI_STREAMING.

---

### B5 — `needs_followup: true` when tool calls present; caller re-enters agentic loop

**CC**: `query.ts:555-558` (`let needsFollowUp = false`), `query.ts:832-835` (set on tool_use arrival), `query.ts:307-1728` (while-true loop in `queryLoop` re-iterates when needsFollowUp is set; the loop itself handles re-entry)

**OC**: `src/pipeline.rs:51` (`needs_followup: bool` in `TurnResult`), `src/pipeline.rs:617-630` (set to `has_tools`), caller loop in `src/main.rs:1875-1888` (Gemini), `src/main.rs:2626-2665` (Anthropic proxy), `src/main.rs:3354-3362` (chat loop)

**Input**: `TurnResult` returned from `run_turn` / `stream_sse_response` / `handle_google_response`.

**Output**:
- CC: `queryLoop` continues its `while(true)` loop if `needsFollowUp` (tool calls pending). Adds `assistantMessages + toolResults` to messages and re-calls the model.
- OC: Caller checks `turn_result.needs_followup`; if true, executes tool calls, appends tool results to conversation, and re-calls `run_turn`. Max turns enforced by `config.session.max_turns` (0 = unlimited).

**Edge cases**:
- CC: Duplicate tool-call detection not in CC query.ts; OC has explicit duplicate detection at main.rs:2649-2664 (breaks agentic loop if all tool calls are duplicates of already-executed ones).
- CC: `stop_reason === 'tool_use'` is treated as unreliable; actual gate is presence of `tool_use` blocks in content (query.ts:553-556).
- OC: `AnthropicToolAccumulator.has_tool_use()` is the gate, same logic.

**Error path**:
- CC: If `needsFollowUp` but abort signal is set, drains `StreamingToolExecutor.getRemainingResults()` to generate synthetic results, then returns `{reason:'aborted_streaming'}`.
- OC: If TUI channel closed mid-tool-loop, breaks (macro `send_event_or_break!`).

---

### B6 — SSE stream interrupted mid-message: partial content + error flagged, not silent truncation

**CC**: `query.ts:955-997` (outer catch block), `query.ts:1011-1051` (abort handling before tool execution)

**OC**: `src/pipeline.rs:590-594` (Err arm of chunk match), `src/pipeline.rs:528-535` (stream timeout)

**Input**: Mid-stream error (`reqwest::Error` in OC, thrown by SDK in CC), or stream timeout (no data for `SSE_STREAM_TIMEOUT_SECS = 30s` in OC).

**Output**:
- CC (unrecoverable stream error): Calls `yieldMissingToolResultBlocks(assistantMessages, errorMessage)` to emit synthetic tool results for any open tool_use blocks. Then yields `createAssistantAPIErrorMessage({content: errorMessage})` so the UI shows the error inline. Returns `{reason:'model_error', error}`. Error is NOT silently swallowed.
- OC (stream chunk error): Sends `AppEvent::ApiError(format!("Stream error: {e}"))` to TUI and breaks out of the stream loop. Partial `full_content` is returned in `TurnResult`. No synthetic tool results generated. `needs_followup` reflects whatever was accumulated before the error.
- OC (stream timeout): Appends `"\n\n[Response truncated: stream timeout]"` to `full_content` and breaks. No error event; the truncation marker is inline in the content string.

**Edge cases**:
- CC: On abort signal during streaming, returns `{reason:'aborted_streaming'}` (query.ts:1051) after draining tool executor.
- OC: No abort signal concept; stream timeout is the only mid-stream termination mechanism besides chunk errors.
- CC: Recoverable errors (prompt-too-long 413, max-output-tokens) are withheld from yield during streaming and recovered after (query.ts:799-822). OC has no equivalent withhold/recover pattern.

**Error path**:
- CC: `logAntError` for internal employees; always surfaces error message to user via assistant message.
- OC: Error goes to TUI via AppEvent channel only; no persistent error in the returned `TurnResult.content` (just partial content).

**Divergences (gaps)**:
- OC stream timeout appends inline text vs CC's structured error event — filed as gap #STREAM_INTERRUPT.
- OC has no prompt-too-long withhold/recover — this is part of the compaction gap (parent #523).

---

### B7 — `max_turns_reached` attachment emitted at turn cap

**CC**: `query.ts:1704-1711` (emit `max_turns_reached` attachment + return `{reason:'max_turns'}`), `QueryEngine.ts:842-873` (handle in submitMessage: yield `{type:'result', subtype:'error_max_turns', ...}`)

**OC**: `src/main.rs:2630-2637` (Anthropic proxy path: eprintln to stderr + break), `src/main.rs:3786-3794` (chat path: eprintln + break), `src/config/session.rs:16,68` (`max_turns: u32`, default 0 = unlimited)

**Input**: `maxTurns` parameter (CC) / `config.session.max_turns` (OC). Turn count `nextTurnCount > maxTurns`.

**Output**:
- CC: Yields `createAttachmentMessage({type:'max_turns_reached', maxTurns, turnCount: nextTurnCount})`. QueryEngine catches this attachment and yields `{type:'result', subtype:'error_max_turns', is_error:true, num_turns, errors:['Reached maximum number of turns (N)']}` to SDK callers. Returns `{reason:'max_turns'}` to end the loop.
- OC: Emits an ANSI-colored warning to stderr (`eprintln!`) and breaks the agentic loop. No structured event emitted to the client or via the API response. No `error_max_turns` result type.

**Edge cases**:
- CC: Also checks max_turns after abort during tool calls (query.ts:1506-1514) and emits the attachment there too.
- OC: Only checks at the top of the while loop; an abort mid-tool doesn't check max_turns.
- CC: Emits `max_turns_reached` in SSE-forwarded Gemini path too (QueryEngine.ts handles it regardless of provider).
- OC: Gemini loop also checks `max_iterations` but only breaks — no client event.

**Error path**:
- CC: After emitting `error_max_turns`, the generator returns — no further API calls.
- OC: After `break`, the outer response-streaming loop ends; the HTTP response to the proxy client may be incomplete (partial SSE stream closed at loop exit).

**Divergences (gaps)**:
- OC emits no structured `error_max_turns` event to clients — filed as gap #MAX_TURNS_EVENT.

---

## Gaps from brief (already identified)

### G1 — Configurable stop hooks missing

**CC**: `query/stopHooks.ts:65-473` (`handleStopHooks` generator). Runs at the end of each queryLoop iteration. Executes `Stop` hooks (external scripts/commands configured via `toolPermissionContext`). Hooks can:
- Block continuation (`preventContinuation: true`) → loop returns `{reason:'hook_stopped'}`
- Inject blocking error messages into next user message
- Run `TeammateIdle` and `TaskCompleted` hooks for multi-agent scenarios
- Run fire-and-forget background tasks (memory extraction, auto-dream, prompt suggestion)

**OC**: Missing — no stop hook execution at turn end. `src/hooks.rs` exists but implements pre/post tool-use hooks only, not the stop-condition / turn-end hooks from CC `stopHooks.ts`.

**Filed as**: #587

---

### G2 — Token-budget abort missing

**CC**: `query/tokenBudget.ts:45-93` (`checkTokenBudget`). Called inside queryLoop when `feature('TOKEN_BUDGET')` is enabled and `taskBudget` is set. Tracks `globalTurnTokens` vs `budget`. Continues if `turnTokens < budget * 0.9` (90% threshold) and not diminishing returns (< 500 token delta for 3+ iterations). At 90%+ or diminishing, returns `{action:'stop'}`.

**OC**: Missing — no token budget tracking. `TaskBudget` parameter is not plumbed through the pipeline at all.

**Filed as**: #590

---

## Additional discovered gaps

### G3 — OC retry count is 3, CC default is 10

**CC**: `withRetry.ts:52` (`DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES = 10`), env-overridable via `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_RETRIES`.
**OC**: `src/pipeline.rs:330` (`max_retries = 3u32`, hard-coded).

### G4 — OC retry emits plain text; CC emits typed structured `api_retry` event

**CC**: `withRetry.ts:508-511` yields `createSystemAPIErrorMessage`; `QueryEngine.ts:943-954` re-yields as `{type:'system', subtype:'api_retry', attempt, max_retries, retry_delay_ms, error_status, error}`.
**OC**: `src/pipeline.rs:351-354` sends `AppEvent::StreamText(format!("(Retrying in {wait_secs}s — {status}...)"))`. No structured event.

### G5 — OC has no jitter in exponential backoff

**CC**: `withRetry.ts:546-547` adds 0–25% of base delay as random jitter.
**OC**: `src/pipeline.rs:350` uses `2u64.pow(attempt + 1)` with no jitter.

### G6 — OC does not retry 408/409/ECONNRESET/EPIPE

**CC**: `withRetry.ts:760-763` (408, 409 retryable), `withRetry.ts:112-118` (ECONNRESET/EPIPE stale connection retry with keep-alive disable).
**OC**: Only retries 429/503/529.

### G7 — OC has no model fallback on repeated 529

**CC**: `withRetry.ts:333-350` (`FallbackTriggeredError` thrown after `MAX_529_RETRIES=3` consecutive 529s for Opus). `query.ts:894-950` catches it, switches `currentModel` to `fallbackModel`, tombstones partial messages, yields a warning system message.
**OC**: No fallback model concept in pipeline; only breaks the retry loop.

### G8 — OC does not enable adaptive thinking by default for medium effort

**CC**: `QueryEngine.ts:278-282` sets `initialThinkingConfig = {type:'adaptive'}` by default for all queries unless explicitly disabled. `services/api/claude.ts:1606-1613` uses adaptive thinking for models that support it.
**OC**: `src/pipeline.rs:105-122` only enables thinking for `"high"/"max"` effort; `"medium"` (default) sends no thinking parameters.

### G9 — OC stream timeout uses inline text truncation marker, not structured error

**CC**: `query.ts:955-996` yields `createAssistantAPIErrorMessage` on stream error. Abort produces `{reason:'aborted_streaming'}`.
**OC**: `src/pipeline.rs:531-534` appends `"\n\n[Response truncated: stream timeout]"` to content and breaks silently.

### G10 — OC emits no structured `error_max_turns` result event to clients

**CC**: `QueryEngine.ts:851-873` yields `{type:'result', subtype:'error_max_turns', is_error:true, num_turns, ...}`.
**OC**: Only `eprintln!` to stderr. No client-visible structured event.

### G11 — OC Gemini path is non-streaming

**CC**: Uses Vertex/Gemini via OpenAI-compat SSE — unified streaming path.
**OC**: `src/pipeline.rs:396-505` — reads full JSON response body synchronously. No SSE for Gemini.

---

5e9f30aa-2439-44b3-8600-dbac79172f50.title: Phase 1 spec: LSP service + LSPTool (server pool + diagnostics + passive feedback) [CC parity]
5e9f30aa-2439-44b3-8600-dbac79172f50.description:
## Goal

Extract a behavioral spec for this subsystem by reading Claude Code's TypeScript source. **Output**: update this issue body with a markdown spec pinning down each testable contract (input → expected output, edge cases, error paths). No Rust yet — that is Phase 2.

Parent audit: #523.

## Claude Code source — read these

- `services/lsp/LSPServerManager.ts` (~420 lines) — server pool / lifecycle
- `services/lsp/LSPServerInstance.ts` (~511 lines)
- `services/lsp/LSPDiagnosticRegistry.ts` (~386 lines) — passive accumulation
- `services/lsp/LSPClient.ts` (~447 lines)
- `services/lsp/passiveFeedback.ts` (~328 lines) — surface diagnostics without tool call
- `tools/LSPTool/LSPTool.ts` (~860 lines)
- `tools/LSPTool/formatters.ts` (~592 lines)

## OpenClaudia counterpart

- `src/tools/lsp.rs` (~787 lines) — `detect_language_server` 57-73, dispatch 114, action enum 121

## Behavioral spec

### 1. goToDefinition — server selection and location return

**CC:** `LSPTool.ts` lines 438-446, `LSPServerManager.ts` lines 192-207, `formatters.ts` lines 127-169.

**Contract:**
- Input: `{ operation: "goToDefinition", filePath: string, line: int (1-based), character: int (1-based) }`.
- The tool resolves `filePath` to absolute path, extracts the file extension (lowercase), looks up the extension in the `extensionMap` built during `initialize()` from config, and calls `ensureServerStarted()` on the matched server.
- The 1-based `line` and `character` inputs are converted to 0-based before building the LSP `textDocument/definition` params (`line - 1`, `character - 1`).
- The file is opened with `textDocument/didOpen` before the request if not already tracked in `openedFiles`.
- The method sends `textDocument/definition` with `{ textDocument: { uri }, position: { line, character } }`.
- Response may be `Location`, `Location[]`, `LocationLink`, or `LocationLink[]`. `LocationLink` is normalized to `Location` via `targetUri` / `targetSelectionRange`.
- Formatted output: single result → `"Defined in <path>:<line>:<char>"`. Multiple → `"Found N definitions:\n  <path>:<line>:<char>\n ..."`. Null / empty → descriptive "No definition found" message.
- Gitignored locations are filtered before formatting via `git check-ignore` in batches of 50.

**OC counterpart:** `lsp.rs` `execute_lsp` line 73, `parse_locations` line 426. OC handles `Location` and `Location[]` but not `LocationLink`. OC spawns a fresh server per call (no pool). Coordinate system: OC `line` defaults to 1, uses `line.saturating_sub(1)` for 0-based; `character` defaults to 0 and is not adjusted.

**Gaps vs CC:**
- OC does not handle `LocationLink` responses (no `targetUri` normalization).
- OC does not filter gitignored locations.
- OC does not preserve `isFileOpen` state across calls; every call sends `textDocument/didOpen`.
- OC does not count `resultCount` / `fileCount`.

---

### 2. hover — hover text extraction

**CC:** `LSPTool.ts` lines 458-464, `formatters.ts` lines 220-267.

**Contract:**
- Input: `{ operation: "hover", filePath, line (1-based), character (1-based) }`.
- Sends `textDocument/hover` with `{ textDocument: { uri }, position: { line-1, character-1 } }`.
- Response is `Hover | null`. `Hover.contents` can be `MarkupContent` (`{ kind, value }`), `MarkedString` (deprecated string or `{ language, value }`), or `MarkedString[]`.
- `extractMarkupText` handles all three shapes: string → direct; `{ kind }` → `.value`; array → map each item (string or `.value`) joined with `"\n\n"`.
- If `Hover.range` present, prepend `"Hover info at <line+1>:<char+1>:\n\n"` before content.
- Null result → `"No hover information available. ..."`.

**OC counterpart:** `lsp.rs` `parse_lsp_response` line 363. OC handles the same three shapes (`string`, `{ value }`, array) but uses `"\n"` separator (not `"\n\n"`) for arrays. OC does not prepend the range prefix. OC returns raw extracted string in `hover_text` field, not a formatted string.

**Gaps vs CC:**
- OC does not emit range-qualified prefix when `Hover.range` is present.
- OC array join uses `"\n"` vs CC `"\n\n"`.

---

### 3. findReferences — reference location list

**CC:** `LSPTool.ts` lines 448-457, `formatters.ts` lines 173-218.

**Contract:**
- Input: `{ operation: "findReferences", filePath, line (1-based), character (1-based) }`.
- Sends `textDocument/references` with `context: { includeDeclaration: true }`.
- Response is `Location[] | null`.
- Locations with undefined `uri` are filtered and logged as errors.
- Gitignored locations are filtered via `git check-ignore`.
- Single location → `"Found 1 reference:\n  <path>:<line>:<char>"`.
- Multiple → grouped by file: `"Found N references across M files:\n\n<file>:\n  Line <line>:<char>\n..."`.
- Zero → `"No references found. ..."`.

**OC counterpart:** `lsp.rs` `parse_locations` line 426, same branch as `GoToDefinition`. OC produces `Vec<LspLocation>` with 1-based lines, raw URI (not relative path). OC does not group by file, does not filter gitignored paths, returns JSON serialization.

**Gaps vs CC:**
- OC does not group references by file in output.
- OC does not filter gitignored paths.
- OC emits raw file URIs instead of relative paths.

---

### 4. documentSymbols — nested symbol tree

**CC:** `LSPTool.ts` lines 466-471, `formatters.ts` lines 306-366.

**Contract:**
- Input: `{ operation: "documentSymbol", filePath, line, character }` (position is sent but unused for the `textDocument/documentSymbol` method — only `textDocument: { uri }` is used).
- Response can be `DocumentSymbol[]` (hierarchical, has `range` field) or `SymbolInformation[]` (flat, has `location` field). First element presence of `"range"` vs `"location"` distinguishes the two.
- `DocumentSymbol[]` path: recursive tree formatted with indentation. Each node: `"<indent><name> (<kind>) [<detail>] - Line <line+1>"`. Children indented +2 spaces per level.
- `SymbolInformation[]` path: delegates to `formatWorkspaceSymbolResult` — flat grouping by file.
- `symbolKindToString` maps SymbolKind integers 1-26 to readable names; unknown → `"Unknown"`.
- `countSymbols` recursively counts including children for `resultCount`.
- Zero / null → `"No symbols found in document. ..."`.
- Result is capped at `maxResultSizeChars: 100_000`.

**OC counterpart:** `lsp.rs` `parse_symbols` line 466. OC uses `parse_symbols_inner` recursively, depth-limited to `MAX_SYMBOL_DEPTH = 20`. OC falls back from `range` to `location.range` for `SymbolInformation`. OC does not separate the two response formats; returns `Vec<LspSymbol>` JSON. OC symbol formatting: `symbol_kind_name` covers all 26 kinds identically to CC.

**Gaps vs CC:**
- OC does not format the tree as human-readable text; emits raw JSON.
- OC does not detect and handle `SymbolInformation[]` format separately (no grouping-by-file path for flat format).
- OC does not apply `detail` field to node output.

---

### 5. Unknown action string → explicit error listing valid actions

**CC:** `LSPTool.ts` line 155-163, schemas validated via Zod discriminated union. The `inputSchema` uses `z.enum([...9 operations...])` so invalid `operation` values are rejected at `validateInput` with `"Invalid input: ..."` error before reaching `call`. Error code 3.

**OC counterpart:** `lsp.rs` `execute_lsp` lines 113-126. OC matches `action_str` in a `match` block; the `_` arm returns `("Unknown LSP action: {action_str}. Use: goToDefinition, findReferences, hover, documentSymbols", true)`. OC does **not** panic.

**Behavioral differences:**
- CC rejects with a Zod validation error including the full enum list; OC returns a manual error listing only its 4 operations.
- CC validates at tool input layer before any server interaction; OC validates inside `execute_lsp` after `file_path` extraction but before server launch.
- CC's valid operation set has 9 entries (`goToDefinition`, `findReferences`, `hover`, `documentSymbol`, `workspaceSymbol`, `goToImplementation`, `prepareCallHierarchy`, `incomingCalls`, `outgoingCalls`); OC only implements 4.

---

### 6. Server crash mid-call → explicit error, not hang

**CC:** `LSPServerInstance.ts` lines 121-125, 356-409; `LSPClient.ts` lines 156-167.

**Contract:**
- `LSPClient` registers a `process.on("exit")` handler. If exit code is non-zero and `!isStopping`, sets `isInitialized = false`, calls `onCrash(crashError)`.
- `createLSPServerInstance` passes `onCrash` callback that sets `state = "error"` and increments `crashRecoveryCount`.
- `sendRequest` checks `isHealthy()` first (requires `state === "running" && client.isInitialized`). If unhealthy, throws immediately: `"Cannot send request to LSP server '<name>': server is <state>[, last error: ...]"` — no hang.
- Content-modified transient errors (code `-32801`, e.g. rust-analyzer still indexing) are retried up to `MAX_RETRIES_FOR_TRANSIENT_ERRORS = 3` with exponential backoff starting at 500ms: delays 500ms, 1000ms, 2000ms. After max retries, throws.
- After `crashRecoveryCount > maxRestarts (default 3)`, `start()` throws `"LSP server '<name>' exceeded max crash recovery attempts"` and stops retrying.
- `LSPTool.call()` wraps the entire request in a try/catch; any thrown error becomes `{ result: "Error performing <op>: <message>" }` — caller receives a non-error tool result with the error in the text.

**OC counterpart:** `lsp.rs` `run_lsp_request` line 138, `read_lsp_response` line 277. OC synchronously blocks on `read_lsp_response`, which loops up to 100 messages for the matching `id`. If the server crashes mid-read, `reader.read_line` returns 0 bytes or an I/O error, returning `Err("Read error: ...")`. `execute_lsp` returns `("LSP error: ...", true)`. No retry logic. No health check before send.

**Gaps vs CC:**
- OC has no health check (`isHealthy`) before sending — a zombie process would likely hang or return I/O error after process exits.
- OC has no transient error retry (no content-modified backoff).
- OC has no crash recovery count / max-restart guard.
- OC blocks the calling thread (synchronous I/O); CC is non-blocking (async).

---

## Gaps already visible from the brief

These are CC features OpenClaudia does not implement. Each has been filed as a separate issue.

- **Server-pool lifecycle missing** — OC spawns fresh server per call (slow, performance-critical). Filed: see gap issue filed from spec extraction.
- **DiagnosticRegistry missing** — passive accumulation of `textDocument/publishDiagnostics` notifications. Filed: see gap issue filed from spec extraction.
- **PassiveFeedback missing** — surface LSP diagnostics into conversation without explicit tool call. Filed: see gap issue filed from spec extraction.

## Additional discovered gaps

Gaps found during spec extraction beyond the three listed above:

- **LocationLink not handled** — OC `parse_locations` only handles `Location` objects (requires `uri` field). CC normalizes `LocationLink` → `Location` via `targetUri`/`targetSelectionRange`. Affects `goToDefinition` and `goToImplementation`. Filed: see gap issue.
- **Gitignore filtering missing** — CC filters result locations/symbols via `git check-ignore` (batched, 50 paths per call, 5s timeout). OC returns all locations including those in gitignored files. Filed: see gap issue.
- **5 operations entirely absent** — OC `LspAction` enum has 4 values; CC has 9 operations. Missing: `workspaceSymbol`, `goToImplementation`, `prepareCallHierarchy`, `incomingCalls`, `outgoingCalls`. Filed: see gap issue.
- **Singleton manager / isFileOpen deduplication missing** — OC sends `textDocument/didOpen` on every call. CC tracks `openedFiles` (URI → serverName) and skips `didOpen` for already-open files. This is the file-sync protocol side of the pool gap. Filed: see gap issue.
- **File size guard missing** — CC checks file size before reading (`MAX_LSP_FILE_SIZE_BYTES = 10_000_000`); files > 10MB return `"File too large for LSP analysis"`. OC reads the entire file unconditionally. Filed: see gap issue.
- **Tool disabled when LSP not connected** — CC `isEnabled()` returns `isLspConnected()`, gating on at least one non-error server. OC always exposes the tool. Filed: see gap issue.
- **Startup initialization wait** — CC `call()` checks `getInitializationStatus()` and `await waitForInitialization()` if still pending. OC has no manager lifecycle; every call is a fresh subprocess. Covered by pool gap.
- **`workspace/configuration` reverse-request handler** — CC registers a handler returning `null` for each requested config item (satisfies TypeScript language server). OC does not process server-initiated requests. Filed: see gap issue.

## Done when

- This issue body has been edited to contain a markdown spec, one section per behavior above
- Each behavior section names the function(s) on both sides (or marks the OC side missing)
- Every gap above has been filed as its own issue and linked here
- The matching Phase 2 issue is unblocked

39b8ffc7-8e2c-4cea-898d-ac73b6d8f631.author: lOrm
39b8ffc7-8e2c-4cea-898d-ac73b6d8f631.content:
## OC-current behavioral spec — `src/tools/lsp.rs`

### B1 — Action dispatch (lines 496-586, `execute_lsp`)
**Contract**: `execute_lsp(args: &HashMap<String, Value>) -> (String, bool)`. Reads:
- `action` (default `"hover"`).
- `file_path` (required; absent → `("Error: file_path is required", true)`).
- `line` (default 1, u32-saturating from u64), `character` (default 0).

Then four serial gates: (1) `detect_language_server` by `file_path` extension — unknown ext returns `"No language server known for file: {path}"`. (2) `is_lsp_connected` PATH probe via `which {server_cmd}` (spawns `/usr/bin/which`) — if not on PATH, returns `"LSP server unavailable for {lang}: '{server_cmd}' not found on PATH. …"`. (3) `std::fs::metadata` size guard: `meta.len() > LSP_MAX_FILE_SIZE = 10 * 1024 * 1024` → `"File too large for LSP analysis: {n} bytes exceeds the {LSP_MAX_FILE_SIZE}-byte limit (10 MiB). …"`. metadata failures are tolerated and forwarded to read step. (4) `action_str` match: `goToDefinition|definition`, `findReferences|references`, `hover`, `documentSymbols|symbols`; anything else → `"Unknown LSP action: {action_str}. Use: goToDefinition, findReferences, hover, documentSymbols"`. Bool second return is `true` for errors.

Success path: `run_lsp_request(...)` then `serde_json::to_string_pretty(&result)` (returns `("", false)` on stringify failure since `unwrap_or_default`). Error path: `("LSP error: {e}", true)`.

### B2 — Language server table & PATH gating (lines 164-200, `resolve_language_server`; 480-492, `detect_language_server`)
**Contract**: Extension → `(cmd, args)` table; trims leading `.` from `lang_or_ext`. Supported keys: `rs→rust-analyzer`; `ts/tsx/js/jsx→typescript-language-server --stdio`; `py→pylsp`; `go→gopls serve`; `c/cpp/h/hpp→clangd`; `java→jdtls`; `rb→solargraph stdio`. Bare language aliases recognized: `rust`, `typescript`, `typescriptreact`, `javascript`, `javascriptreact`, `python`, `go`, `c`, `cpp/c++`, `java`, `ruby`.
`is_lsp_connected(lang)` returns `false` for unknown lang AND `false` when `which $cmd` fails.

### B3 — Env-scrubbed spawn (lines 397-477, `apply_lsp_env_scrub`/`spawn_language_server`)
**Contract**: Spawned servers have `Command::env_clear()` applied; only env vars whose name is in `LSP_SAFE_ENV_EXACT = ["PATH","HOME","USER","LOGNAME","LANG","LC_ALL","TMPDIR","SHELL","TZ"]` (case-insensitive) OR whose UPPER name starts with one of `LSP_SAFE_ENV_PREFIXES = ["LC_","XDG_"]` are re-injected. All `*_TOKEN`, `*_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_*`, `OPENAI_*`, `AWS_*`, `GH_*` are dropped by construction.
stdin/stdout/stderr all `Stdio::piped()`. Spawn failures → `Err(format!("Failed to start {cmd}: {e}"))`.

### B4 — LSP request lifecycle (lines 588-732, `run_lsp_request`)
**Contract**: `(server_cmd, server_args, file_path, line, character, action) -> Result<LspResult, String>`.
Sequence: canonicalize path; compute `root_uri = find_project_root(abs)`; `file_uri = "file://{abs}"`; read file via `file_error::read_file`. Spawn server (env-scrubbed); stderr captured into ring buffer; child wrapped in `ChildGuard` (RAII kill+reap on drop). Send `initialize` (id=1) with `processId`, `rootUri`, empty capabilities, single workspaceFolder; read response. Send `initialized` notification. **`didOpen` deduplication**: `mark_opened(server_cmd, abs)` returns true iff first claim — only then is `textDocument/didOpen` sent. `OpenFileGuard` rolls back the slot on early `?`-return so a failed run cannot leak. Send readiness probe (`textDocument/documentSymbol` id=1001), call `wait_for_readiness` with 10s deadline. Then send the real request (id=2) and read response (id=2). On any error, the stderr snippet (last bytes) is appended to the error message.

### B5 — Response parsing (lines 917-1101)
**Hover** (`parse_lsp_response` Hover arm): `result.contents` → flat string. Three shapes: bare string; `{value: "..."}` object (MarkupContent/MarkedString); array → joined with `"\n"`. Returns `LspResult{action:"hover", hover_text: Some(...), results:[], symbols:[]}`.
**GoToDefinition / FindReferences**: `parse_locations(result)` accepts `Array | single Object`; per location, requires `uri` (string), `range.start`; emits `LspLocation{uri (raw), line=start.line+1 (1-based), character=start.character, end_line, end_character, preview:None}`. Missing fields → location skipped. No gitignore filtering. No LocationLink handling.
**DocumentSymbols**: `parse_symbols_inner` with `MAX_SYMBOL_DEPTH = 20`. Each symbol requires `name` and `range` OR `location.range`; falls back from `range` to `location.range` (SymbolInformation shape). Children recursed with `+1` depth. `symbol_kind_name(kind: u64)` maps LSP SymbolKind 1..=26 to string names; unknown → `"Unknown"`. Returns `Vec<LspSymbol>` as JSON (no flat-vs-tree formatting).

### B6 — Failure modes (no retry, sync I/O)
**Contract**: `send_lsp_message` / `send_lsp_notification` write `Content-Length` + JSON-RPC to stdin; `read_lsp_response(reader, id)` loops up to `lsp_max_messages()` messages looking for matching `id`. I/O errors propagate as `Err(String)`. No content-modified `-32801` retry. No crash recovery / restart count. No health-check before send. Server crash → `read_line` returns 0 / I/O error → `Err`. Sync blocking I/O on the calling thread; concurrent calls each spawn a fresh subprocess.
`ChildGuard::drop` always kills + reaps; `OpenFileGuard::drop` removes a stale dedup slot when `commit()` was not reached.

### B7 — Open-file dedup registry (lines 32-76, 132-137)
**Contract**: Process-wide `OnceLock<Mutex<HashMap<server_cmd, HashSet<PathBuf>>>>`. `mark_opened` inserts and returns true iff inserted (first opener). `mark_closed` returns true iff entry was removed. Poison handled via `into_inner`. Dedup is per-server-cmd; same path against different servers is independent. Persistent across requests within a single process (servers are spawned fresh per request, but the registry assumes a long-lived server; this is a known divergence from CC's pool model).

5ee57911-6336-4a5b-baa6-220d25e364a0.title: execute_list_files lacks sort by type, pagination, and metadata (single-line dump)
5ee57911-6336-4a5b-baa6-220d25e364a0.description:
## Severity
Minor

## Dimension
Functional Correctness / KISS / Usability

## Location
src/tools/file/list.rs:7-33 (execute_list_files)

## Violation
The tool is a one-paragraph dump:

```rust
for entry in entries.flatten() {
    let name = entry.file_name().to_string_lossy().to_string();
    let file_type = entry.file_type().map_or("", |ft| if ft.is_dir() { "/" } else { "" });
    items.push(format!("{name}{file_type}"));
}
items.sort();
(items.join("\n"), false)
```

Problems:
1. `entries.flatten()` silently discards per-entry errors (e.g. EACCES on a specific symlink) — the model gets a partial list with no indication of failure.
2. No pagination — listing a directory with 50k entries produces a 50k-line response, consuming the entire token budget.
3. Alphabetical sort mixes files and directories — every other CLI sorts dirs first.
4. No file metadata: no size, mtime, no distinction between symlinks and regular files. A model trying to decide which file to read has zero signal.
5. No filter args (no glob, no recursive option, no hidden-file toggle).

## Mandated refactor
1. Accept optional args: `pattern` (glob), `recursive: bool`, `max_entries: usize` (default 200), `show_hidden: bool` (default false).
2. Return a structured listing: dirs first then files, each line "name/  " or "name (Nbytes, mtime)".
3. Surface flatten errors via tracing::warn! and append "(N entries skipped due to errors)" if any.
4. Cap output at max_entries; on truncation return is_error or a clear "(showing N of M entries — use pattern to narrow)" suffix.

## Filed from QA review dispatch

2d430fc4-12a4-4139-9a1b-7558e04fc067.author: lOrm
2d430fc4-12a4-4139-9a1b-7558e04fc067.content: Partial fix applied: dirs-before-files sort. execute_list_files now collects (is_dir, name) tuples and sorts so all directories appear before all files, with alphabetical order preserved within each bucket (the standard ls layout). The wider scope items in the QA report (pagination, glob filter, metadata-rich output, recursive flag, hidden-file toggle) are deferred — they'd reshape the tool API and the on-wire contract with the model. Filing those separately if needed; this issue closes on the sort-order piece since that was the concrete actionable defect.

5f458cc3-1b5c-4714-9edd-ddfa342f80fc.title: Compaction token estimator under-counts CJK/emoji/images — context exhaustion risk
5f458cc3-1b5c-4714-9edd-ddfa342f80fc.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

Dimension: Functional Correctness (1)

Location: src/compaction.rs:119-141 estimate_tokens, 144-171 estimate_message_tokens, 153 image hardcode.

Violation: Token estimation is a 4-chars-per-token heuristic with only a +0.5x adjustment for non-ASCII. Real tokenizers treat CJK at ~1 token per char (under-count 33%+). Images hardcoded at 1000 tokens — Anthropic bills ~1600 for hi-res, GPT-4V up to 765+85. COMPACTION_THRESHOLD=0.85 assumes the estimator is correct within the RESPONSE_RESERVE=4096 margin. When under-counted, compaction fires too late and provider returns context_length_exceeded; when over-counted, it summarizes usable context early.

Mandated Refactor:
1. Integrate tiktoken-rs for OpenAI-family models.
2. Call Anthropic POST /messages/count_tokens for Anthropic (cache per message hash).
3. Widen RESPONSE_RESERVE to 16K when using the heuristic fallback.
4. Property test: estimate within +/-15 percent of tokenizer truth on a sample corpus.
5. Track under-count: when actual_input_tokens exceeds estimate by >20%, log and adjust threshold for subsequent turns.

5fb072f7-976a-46a3-868a-12483a6f19da.title: Plugin::load_legacy_manifest defaults silently fabricate plugin metadata from raw JSON
5fb072f7-976a-46a3-868a-12483a6f19da.description:
## Severity
Minor
## Dimension
error-handling
## Location
src/plugins/mod.rs:321-380
## Violation
Every field is extracted with `.as_str().unwrap_or("unknown")` or `.map(String::from)`. A legacy manifest with a missing/typo'd name silently loads as "unknown". Quoted lines:

    let name = legacy["name"].as_str().unwrap_or("unknown").to_string();
    ...
    let server_name = server["name"].as_str().unwrap_or("unknown").to_string();
    let transport = server["transport"].as_str().unwrap_or("stdio").to_string();
    map.insert(
        server_name,
        McpServerConfig {
            command: server["command"].as_str().map(String::from),

If two legacy plugins drop their `name`, both load with `id = "unknown"` and the second clobbers the first in the manager's HashMap. Same for "unknown" MCP servers. The "unknown" sentinel is a stringly-typed sentinel — a classic defensive-programming smell that hides upstream input bugs.
## Mandated refactor
Replace each `.unwrap_or("unknown")` with `.ok_or_else(|| PluginError::InvalidManifest("legacy manifest missing required field: name"))?`. Surface InvalidManifest to the manager so the broken plugin is reported, not silently shadowed. Add a dedicated `LegacyManifest` typed struct deserialised with serde + #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] so typos surface explicitly.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

bb6beb2d-27bd-4448-91f8-9aa5923bf469.content: Already addressed in src/plugins/mod.rs load_legacy_manifest (lines 493-579) via crosslink #347: both 'name' and per-server 'name' fields now use ok_or_else with PluginError::InvalidManifest. The 'unknown' fabricated default has been replaced with explicit errors that name the offending path.

5fb81d71-fa5c-4227-a848-8958fbfc13d3.title: SQLi: public execute_raw() on MemoryDb accepts arbitrary SQL string
5fb81d71-fa5c-4227-a848-8958fbfc13d3.description:
Current state: 

Desired state: 

Reason: 

Dimension: Security and Access (5) / Perimeter Defense (3.4)

Location: src/memory.rs:158 (pub fn execute_raw(&self, sql: &str))

Violation: MemoryDb exposes a public method that executes ANY SQL string via conn.execute_batch(sql). This is a SQLi bomb waiting to go off. The global rule 'always use parameterized queries' is violated at the API boundary — every future caller is invited to build SQL with format!(). Already happening: src/auto_learn.rs:113-116 uses format!() to interpolate table and max_rows values before calling execute_raw. The current values are hardcoded constants, so not exploitable today, but the pattern normalizes string-built SQL and trains the next developer to do the same with user input.

Mandated Refactor:
1. Make execute_raw pub(crate) at minimum; ideally delete it and expose only typed methods (prune_table(table: TableKind, limit: u32)) using parameterized queries and an enum allowlist of table names.
2. Add a clippy disallowed_methods lint or compile-time guard to forbid building SQL with format outside migrate_v*_on helpers.
3. Replace the auto_learn.rs prune loop: since SQLite does not allow binding table names, enumerate the tables in match arms, each calling a pre-written parameterized DELETE with a bound LIMIT.

61885b53-b3ea-4251-bec5-32006d4f2ee1.title: Add path allowlist validation for bash tool (parity with CC checkPathConstraints)
61885b53-b3ea-4251-bec5-32006d4f2ee1.description:
## Gap

CC's checkPathConstraints (tools/BashTool/pathValidation.ts:1013-1100) validates that file paths accessed by path-modifying commands (cd, mv, cp, rm, ln, tee, truncate, install, find, sed, rsync) are within the allowed working directories for the session. READONLY_COMMAND_REGEXES (readOnlyValidation.ts:1509-1570) classifies cd, ls, find and other commands as read-only when they match safe patterns, and validates cd paths against the allowed directory list.

OC has no path allowlist. execute_bash and BackgroundShellManager::spawn pass commands directly to bash -c. Any path accessible to the OC process can be written or deleted if the command passes the denylist.

Key behaviors missing:
- Allowed working directory set (per-session, multiple dirs supported)
- cd path resolution and validation against allowed set
- Compound command write + cd block (prevents cd /secret && mv ...)
- Redirect target path validation (> /etc/passwd blocked)
- Process substitution >(...) blocked
- Windows UNC path detection

## Parity reference
- CC: tools/BashTool/pathValidation.ts:1013 checkPathConstraints, readOnlyValidation.ts:1509 READONLY_COMMAND_REGEXES
- OC: missing entirely — src/tools/bash/policy.rs has no path awareness

## Acceptance
- Per-session allowed working directory set (initially = cwd at session start)
- Validate redirect targets and path arguments for path-modifying commands
- Block compound cd + write patterns
- Return error (not panic) when path is outside allowed set

619167ab-632f-49fb-bbc9-469ba79e9efe.title: context.rs ContextInjector: hook/user content concatenated unescaped into system-reminder — prompt injection
619167ab-632f-49fb-bbc9-469ba79e9efe.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

Dimension: Security and Access / Perimeter Defense. Location: src/context.rs:10-12 (wrap_system_reminder), 22-48 (inject), 129-137 (inject_all). Violation: wrap_system_reminder simply interpolates content between literal tags with format!. If hook output or rules output contains the literal string '</system-reminder>' or a fake '<system-reminder>' with attacker-crafted content, it breaks out of the reminder envelope and injects arbitrary instructions into the model's prompt. Hook output comes from external processes per hooks.rs — if any hook reads from a web source, MCP tool output, or file whose content is user-controlled, a malicious hook payload can override Claudia's system prompt. The 'test_hook_content_does_not_duplicate_base_sections' test in prompt.rs acknowledges this is a known surface but does not defend against it. Mandated Refactor: In wrap_system_reminder, escape or reject content containing '</system-reminder>', '<system-reminder>', and standalone '</system>' tags. Better: hash-sign the reminder frame with a per-session nonce so injected fakes are distinguishable, e.g. <system-reminder id='abc123'>...</system-reminder abc123>. Alternatively, apply the same treatment as apply_prompt_modification: treat hook-injected text as data, never as instructions, by wrapping in a <user-data> tag that is documented in the system prompt as non-instructional.
