042202b8-63d4-4521-ac6b-7a8d73ece663.author: lOrm
042202b8-63d4-4521-ac6b-7a8d73ece663.content:
Fix: src/subagent.rs

BUG: BackgroundAgentManager.agents HashMap inserted on register() but never removed; remove() existed but was uncalled by the runtime. Long sessions leaked finished BackgroundAgent Arcs (each carrying full output + task) and list() scanned all of them on every agent_output listing.

CHANGES (src/subagent.rs):
- L259 pub const FINISHED_AGENT_TTL_SECS: u64 = 60 * 60 (1h retention window).
- L281 BackgroundAgent gained finished_at: Mutex<Option<Instant>>.
- register() initializes finished_at=None and calls self.gc() to amortize sweep cost.
- finish()/fail() set finished_at=Some(Instant::now()) before flipping the finished AtomicBool.
- L400 pub fn gc(&self) -> usize { ... }: retain agents that are unfinished OR finished within TTL; returns evicted count. Poisoned-lock-safe.
- list() now gc()'s first so TUI/CLI never observes leaked stale rows.
- L426 pub fn cleanup_finished(&self) -> usize { ... }: explicit shutdown hook for tui.rs.
- L1508-1509 execute_agent_output_tool drops its local Arc then calls BACKGROUND_AGENTS.remove(agent_id) AFTER extracting result/error — consume-on-read invariant. Caller gets the output, then the entry is freed on the same call.

TESTS (4 new):
- issue422_gc_removes_finished_agents_past_ttl: backdates finished_at by TTL+1s, asserts gc()==1 and get() returns None.
- issue422_gc_keeps_in_progress_and_recently_finished_agents: running agent (finished_at=None) and a just-finished agent both survive; removed==0.
- issue422_agent_output_returns_result_then_removes_finished_entry: success path returns "the answer is 42" THEN entry vanishes; failure path returns "synthetic failure" THEN entry vanishes. Pins ordering.
- issue422_cleanup_finished_drops_finished_keeps_running: two finished (one finish, one fail) removed, one running survives.

FORENSIC VERIFICATION:
- cargo test --lib: 1318 passed; 0 failed (baseline 1314 + 4 new).
- cargo test --lib issue422: 4 passed; 0 failed.
- cargo test --lib subagent::tests: 20 passed (16 existing + 4 new), 0 failed.
- cargo clippy --all-targets --lib --tests -- -D warnings: EXIT=0.

HARD CONSTRAINTS RESPECTED:
- No #[allow(...)] in the diff.
- No edits to clippy.toml.
- No #[ignore] on any test.
- doc-paragraph clippy lint satisfied by rewriting the doc, not silencing it.

98de5d97-789c-46c2-9381-9047790d6307.title: FileEditTool: replace_all parameter unsupported in OC (silent flag drop)
98de5d97-789c-46c2-9381-9047790d6307.description:
## Summary

CC's FileEditTool supports a `replace_all: boolean` parameter that, when true, replaces every occurrence of `old_string` with `new_string`. OC's `execute_edit_file` (`src/tools/file/edit.rs:84-95`) unconditionally rejects multi-occurrence matches regardless of `replace_all`. The flag is silently dropped: callers passing `replace_all=true` get the same multi-occurrence rejection as if they passed it false or omitted it.

## CC Reference

- `tools/FileEditTool/FileEditTool.ts:329-343` (validateInput, counts matches and gates on `replace_all`)
- `tools/FileEditTool/FileEditTool.ts:482-488` (`getPatchForEdit({ replaceAll: replace_all })` → `file.replaceAll(actualOldString, new_string)`)

## Gap

`src/tools/file/edit.rs:84-95` — count > 1 always errors; `replace_all` field is not threaded into the multi-occurrence path. Single-occurrence with `replace_all=true` silently ignores the flag (works only because count=1 already uses `replacen(_,_,1)`).

## Parent Spec Issue

999d1806-3f4d-4e21-b021-fef07b9ced9a.title: get_adapter boxes zero-sized types per-request and silently falls back on typos
999d1806-3f4d-4e21-b021-fef07b9ced9a.description:
Current state: 

Desired state: 

Reason: 

Dimension: Architectural Alignment / DIP

Location: src/providers/mod.rs line 120 (fn get_adapter).

Violation: get_adapter returns `Box<dyn ProviderAdapter>` constructed fresh on every call via `Box::new(AnthropicAdapter::new())`. This is called from proxy_chat_completions at line 688 on every single incoming request. Since each adapter is a zero-sized struct (e.g., `pub struct AnthropicAdapter;`), the Box allocation is wasteful BUT the bigger problem is that the trait objects are unnecessarily owned — callers cannot share a single static adapter. No caching layer exists.

Also:
  - Line 133-139: unknown provider silently falls back to OpenAIAdapter with a WARN log. This violates 'fail fast at system boundaries' — a typo in proxy.target (e.g., `anthrpic`) results in silently wrong behavior. The user pays for calls to the wrong endpoint.
  - The enum-like dispatch is hardcoded; adding a new provider requires editing this match. DIP violation.

Mandated Refactor:
  1. Make each adapter a `pub static ANTHROPIC: AnthropicAdapter = AnthropicAdapter;` (constructible at compile time — they're all ZSTs).
  2. Change get_adapter signature to `fn get_adapter(name: &str) -> Result<&'static dyn ProviderAdapter, ProviderError>`. No allocation, no Box.
  3. Return Err(ProviderError::Unsupported(format!("Unknown provider: {name}"))) for unrecognized names. No silent fallback. The proxy maps this to a 400 Bad Request with a helpful message listing supported providers.
  4. If a 'custom' OpenAI-compatible provider is needed (for LM Studio, LocalAI), make it an explicit config option (`providers.custom.api_format: openai`) rather than implicit fallback.

99c40919-1140-4cd4-b304-337fc3a4c137.title: QA: bash denylist is fundamentally bypassable substring matching (security theater)
99c40919-1140-4cd4-b304-337fc3a4c137.description:
## Severity
Critical
## Dimension
security
## Location
src/tools/bash/policy.rs:82-136
## Violation
The denylist matches lowercased substrings against a hard-coded list. The module's own doc-comment admits this is "NOT a substitute for a real sandbox" (policy.rs:3-7). The pinning test `b5_gap_589_advanced_injection_not_blocked` (policy.rs:453-469) further confirms process substitution, IFS injection, and `/proc/environ` reads pass through.

Trivial bypasses for the canonical "rm -rf /" rule include: `r''m -rf /`, `\rm -rf /`, `eval $(echo cm0gLXJmIC8K | base64 -d)`, `${HOME:0:0}rm -rf /`, `rm$IFS-rf$IFS/`, or any newline-separated multi-statement.

Quoted (policy.rs:82-136):
```
/// Hard denylist of command patterns that are effectively always malicious
/// or catastrophic. Returns `Some(reason)` when the command is denied.
...
    const SUBSTRINGS: &[(&str, &str)] = &[
        ("rm -rf /", "rm -rf of root filesystem"),
        ...
    ];
```

Encoding a denylist this thin into a security boundary creates false confidence — operators may believe `validate_command` provides defense it cannot.
## Mandated refactor
1. Rename `validate_command` to `coarse_safety_screen` and document explicitly that it only catches naive prompt-injection, NOT determined attackers.
2. Architect a real sandbox (firejail/bubblewrap on Linux, seatbelt on macOS, AppContainer on Windows) and require it for ALL bash execution in production mode.
3. Add an explicit opt-in "unsandboxed" mode for development that prints a loud warning on every invocation.
4. Adopt parameterized command construction (no `bash -c` of arbitrary strings) for any internal callers — only model-supplied commands should ever traverse the policy layer, and they MUST hit the sandbox.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

9a9484d3-e770-4ad5-aefd-218cd247b14e.title: Session is #[derive(Clone)] + cloned on every read — deep-copies turn_metrics/progress on every access
9a9484d3-e770-4ad5-aefd-218cd247b14e.description:
Current state: 

Desired state: 

Reason: 

Dimension: Performance & Complexity (6) / State Management Tell-Don't-Ask (3.3)

Location: src/session/mod.rs:77-101 (derive Clone on Session), callers do session.clone() in tui/cli/proxy.

Violation: The Session struct holds Vec<TurnMetrics>, Vec<String> x3, String (handoff_notes), and 3 Option<u32>+Vec<String> for VDD tracking. Every field is heap-allocated. Session implements Clone (line 78). Test code does 'let session = manager.get_or_create_session().clone()' (mod.rs:658, 675, 680); production code in tui/app.rs and proxy.rs likely does the same to escape mutable-borrow constraints.

Each clone deep-copies every turn_metrics entry (TurnMetrics is Clone-derived). A 1-hour session with 360 turns cloned three times per turn allocates ~1000 TurnMetrics copies per minute. This is Tell-Don't-Ask inverted: callers ASK the manager for the Session, then act on a snapshot, then the mutation vanishes because nobody wrote it back.

Related: SessionManager is itself Clone (line 351-352) and owns TaskManager (also Clone with Vec<Task>). Cloning a manager clones every task and every session file path — not cheap.

Mandated Refactor:
1. Remove #[derive(Clone)] from Session. Force callers to request specific pieces (get_stats() -> SessionStats struct with Copy fields; get_handoff() -> String by reference).
2. Where async tasks need 'own' a session snapshot, introduce Arc<Session> with interior mutability via Mutex<SessionInner> — single-copy sharing.
3. Apply Tell-Don't-Ask: let callers send commands to the session (session.complete_task(...)) rather than cloning-mutating-discarding.
4. Identify every session.clone() call site (git grep), audit intent, replace with Arc or targeted read-only accessors.

9b7ab8fe-277a-4c96-bd85-5f273b7bc874.description:
## Gap

CC's bashCommandIsSafe_DEPRECATED (tools/BashTool/bashSecurity.ts:2257-2420) applies ~15 security validators beyond OC's 16-pattern substring/regex denylist:

1. Control-character injection (non-printable chars that bypass validators)
2. Shell-quote single-quote backslash bug exploitation
3. IFS injection (validateIFSInjection, line 1017)
4. /proc/*/environ access (validateProcEnvironAccess, line 1041)
5. Carriage-return tokenization differential (shell-quote vs bash parse differently on CR)
6. Unicode whitespace smuggling (validateUnicodeWhitespace, line 1902)
7. Obfuscated flags (validateObfuscatedFlags, line 1130)
8. Brace expansion (validateBraceExpansion, line 1751)
9. Backslash-escaped operators (validateBackslashEscapedOperators, line 1696)
10. Mid-word hash comment injection (validateMidWordHash, line 1919)
11. Quoted-newline desync (validateCommentQuoteDesync, line 1990 / validateQuotedNewline, line 2109)
12. Process substitution >(...) / <(...) (pathValidation.ts:1028)
13. Windows UNC path injection (readOnlyValidation.ts:1903)
14. git + cd compound command sandbox escape (readOnlyValidation.ts:1917)
15. Malformed token injection (validateMalformedTokenInjection, line 1082)

OC only blocks 16 catastrophic fixed substrings + pipe-to-shell regex (src/tools/bash/policy.rs:89-133).

## Parity reference
- CC: tools/BashTool/bashSecurity.ts:2257-2420 (validator chain)
- OC: src/tools/bash/policy.rs:89-133 (minimal denylist only)

## Acceptance
- Implement the missing validators or a Rust equivalent of the validation chain
- Each validator has unit tests matching CC's test suite patterns
- Prefer AST-based analysis (see tree-sitter gap issue) over regex for structural patterns

validate_url blocks private ranges via host.starts_with('172.16.') / '10.' / '192.168.' / etc. The string-prefix check is unsound in five ways:
1. Hostnames bypass entirely. 'http://internal-server.corp/' or 'http://metadata.google.internal/' do not match any IP prefix and pass validation.
2. DNS rebinding. An attacker-controlled domain whose DNS A record flips between public and 169.254.169.254 bypasses the static parse-time check; reqwest resolves at send-time.
3. Decimal-encoded IPv4. 'http://2130706433/' = 127.0.0.1 parses with host '2130706433', matches no prefix, reqwest dials localhost.
4. IPv6 coverage is incomplete. Only [::1] is blocked. ::ffff:127.0.0.1 (IPv4-mapped), fc00::/7 (ULA), fe80::/10 (link-local), 2002::/16 (6to4) are all reachable.
5. 172.16/12 prefix logic is wrong. starts_with('172.2') at line 36 matches 172.200.x (public); lines 37-38 BLOCK public 172.30-172.31 while missing private 172.26-172.29 reliably.

**Mandated Refactor:**
1. Resolve hostname with trust-dns-resolver; validate EACH resolved IpAddr against ip_network IANA special-purpose registry (private, loopback, link-local, multicast, benchmarking, documentation, reserved, shared-address-space).
2. Use a custom reqwest resolver that re-validates at dial-time — closes the DNS-rebinding window.
3. Explicitly block metadata endpoints: 169.254.169.254, fd00:ec2::254, metadata.google.internal, 100.100.100.200.
4. Add regression tests for decimal-IPv4 bypass, metadata.google.internal, IPv6 ULA.

d7eeb2bb-7ca9-4b83-955c-c345dc247c35.author: lOrm
d7eeb2bb-7ca9-4b83-955c-c345dc247c35.content:
Resolved. Changes to `src/web.rs`:

**New machinery:**
- `DANGEROUS_HOSTNAMES` const slice: `localhost`, `localhost.localdomain`, `ip6-localhost`, `ip6-loopback`, plus cloud-metadata endpoints (`metadata.google.internal`, `metadata.goog`, `metadata.aws`, `metadata.tencentyun.com`, `instance-data`, `instance-data.ec2.internal`) and Kubernetes in-cluster hosts (`kubernetes`, `kubernetes.default`, `kubernetes.default.svc`, full FQDN).
- `parse_host_as_ip(host)`: recognizes standard dotted-quad IPv4, bracketed IPv6, **decimal-integer IPv4** (`2130706433` → 127.0.0.1), and **hex-integer IPv4** (`0x7f000001`).
- `is_ipv6_forbidden(v6)`: unwraps IPv4-mapped form and re-checks as IPv4; then denies unique-local (fc00::/7), link-local (fe80::/10), 6to4 (2002::/16), and Teredo (2001:0000::/32).
- `is_ip_forbidden(ip)`: full IPv4 matrix via `Ipv4Addr` stdlib methods plus manual ranges — loopback, private, link-local, broadcast, unspecified, multicast, documentation, 100.64/10 CGNAT, 192.0.0/24 IETF, 198.18/15 benchmarking, 240.0.0.0/4 reserved.

**Rewritten `validate_url`:**
1. Scheme allowlist (http/https).
2. Hostname denylist match.
3. IP-literal match via `parse_host_as_ip` — handles decimal/hex encoding.
4. DNS resolution via `ToSocketAddrs`; **every** resolved address checked against `is_ip_forbidden`.

**All QA-listed bypasses closed:**
- Bypass 1 (hostnames): `metadata.google.internal` now explicitly denylisted + DNS-resolution check.
- Bypass 2 (DNS rebinding): **partially** mitigated — validate-time check catches unsophisticated rebinds; full defense needs a custom `reqwest::Resolver` that re-checks at dial time (tracked as a follow-up).
- Bypass 3 (decimal IPv4): `parse_host_as_ip` decodes and classifies.
- Bypass 4 (IPv6 partial): full matrix now — mapped, ULA, link-local, 6to4, Teredo all blocked.
- Bypass 5 (bogus 172/2 prefix): now uses `Ipv4Addr::is_private()` which correctly implements 172.16.0.0/12. Added test `ssrf_previous_prefix_bug_172_200_now_allowed` to lock the fix against regression.

**Tests:** 15 new SSRF regression tests in `web::tests` (ssrf_* prefix) covering decimal/hex-encoded loopback, GCP/AWS metadata hostnames, K8s control plane, IPv6-mapped loopback, IPv6 ULA + link-local, CGNAT range, documentation range, future-reserved 240/4, benchmarking 198.18/15, public 172.200.x acceptance, public 8.8.8.8 acceptance, and all five private 172.x middle-octets (16,20,25,28,31). Total lib test count: 574 → 589, all passing. 130 integration tests also still pass.

**Out of scope / follow-up:**
- Custom `reqwest::Resolver` wrapping `TokioResolver` that enforces the same `is_ip_forbidden` check at each dial, closing the DNS-rebinding residual. Filed as a successor issue is advisable.
- URL normalization (look-alike unicode hosts, percent-encoded dots, etc.) — url crate already handles most of this; further hardening should live in a separate refactor.

9ca25b4a-3b32-4863-b7cc-db9b5d9d813f.description:
Current state: 

Desired state: 

Reason: 

**Dimension**: Structural Modularity (God Object / SRP)

**Location**: src/config/keybindings.rs (22,845 bytes in one file)

**Violation**: keybindings.rs is 22KB in a single module housing: KeyAction enum, KeybindingsConfig, ParsedKeystroke, KeyContext, KeybindingResolver, ChordResolveResult, parse_chord, plus tests. This is a classic God Module: a config file (config/keybindings.rs) holding a runtime resolver (KeybindingResolver) that performs logic far beyond configuration schema. It violates SRP — the config/ directory should contain only schema types; resolver logic belongs in a sibling keybindings/ module.

Comparing file sizes in src/config/:
- keybindings.rs: 22,845 bytes (resolver + schema + parser)
- vdd.rs: 14,027 bytes (schema + validation)
- mod.rs: 10,413 bytes (loader)
- hooks.rs: 5,723 bytes (schema only — CORRECT size)
- guardrails.rs: 5,531 bytes (schema only — CORRECT size)
- provider.rs: 3,975 bytes (schema only — CORRECT size)

keybindings.rs alone is bigger than guardrails + provider + proxy + permissions combined.

**Mandated Refactor**:
1. Create src/keybindings/ module with:
   - src/keybindings/parser.rs (parse_chord, ParsedKeystroke)
   - src/keybindings/resolver.rs (KeybindingResolver, ChordResolveResult, KeyContext)
   - src/keybindings/actions.rs (KeyAction enum)
2. Keep src/config/keybindings.rs as a thin schema module (<2KB) containing only the YAML-deserializable KeybindingsConfig struct.
3. The config module imports from keybindings as needed; the converse import (keybindings depending on config) is also permitted but should be minimized.

error-handling

```rust
if let Some(idx) = self.buffer.find(&open_tag) {

9d952aa9-443b-492f-9ce1-2144f74a273d.title: OPENCLAUDIA_ALLOW_OUT_OF_ROOT env var allows model to escape jail via prompt injection on env
9d952aa9-443b-492f-9ce1-2144f74a273d.description:
## Severity
Major

## Dimension
Security and Access / Least Privilege

## Location
src/tools/file/mod.rs:95-97 (strict_mode function)

## Violation
```rust
fn strict_mode() -> bool {
    !matches!(std::env::var("OPENCLAUDIA_ALLOW_OUT_OF_ROOT"), Ok(ref v) if v == "1")
}
```

The jail can be entirely disabled by setting one env var. There is NO logging when the jail is disabled — strict_mode() is called per-resolve_path silently. An operator who set the var "just for one test" and forgot leaves the agent with no path containment. The function is called by all read/write/edit operations.

Worse: the bash tool (separate from this review scope) can `export OPENCLAUDIA_ALLOW_OUT_OF_ROOT=1`. The model itself can then disable its own jail by running a shell command. The jail is theoretical, not enforced.

The CLI flag check is also misnamed: "ALLOW_OUT_OF_ROOT=1" is the only value that disables; any other value (including "true", "yes", "on") leaves strict mode on. The check `if v == "1"` is right-shaped but undocumented at the use site.

## Mandated refactor
1. Cache the env var value at startup in PROJECT_ROOT's LazyLock (once), not per-call. Subsequent bash exports cannot disable the jail.
2. Emit a tracing::warn! once at startup if the jail is disabled.
3. Refuse to honor the env var when the process is launched from a non-interactive context (e.g. when ENV "OPENCLAUDIA_AGENT_MODE=1" or similar), so prompt-injection cannot weaponize an operator's debug setting.
4. Accept the documented set of truthy values ("1", "true", "yes", case-insensitive) — current check is brittle.

## Filed from QA review dispatch

9da7b155-0062-42d2-9066-b50002894d16.title: PlanModeState canonicalize TOCTOU + non-existent plan file fallback bypass
9da7b155-0062-42d2-9066-b50002894d16.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

Dimension: Security and Access (5) / Functional Correctness (1)

Location: src/session/state.rs:116-169 (is_tool_allowed_in_plan_mode).

Violation: Plan mode is supposed to restrict write_file to ONLY the plan file. The check uses fs::canonicalize on both target and plan_file (lines 137-139). If EITHER canonicalize fails, it silently falls through to string-based absolute-path comparison (lines 144-157). Three problems:

1. TOCTOU: fs::canonicalize resolves symlinks at check time. Between the check and the later write (in tools.rs write_file), an attacker (or a confused sub-agent) can replace the plan file with a symlink pointing elsewhere. The second check happens on a different filesystem state.
2. Non-existent plan_file: canonicalize fails when the target doesn't exist yet. The fallback path (lines 144-157) just does path-string comparison after joining with current_dir. An attacker who picks a cwd that makes './plan.md' resolve to the same absolute PATH STRING as the target file — even if they point to different inodes via symlink or case-insensitive FS (macOS default, Windows) — passes the gate.
3. std::env::current_dir() is read at check time and can differ from the cwd at write time (any tool that does std::env::set_current_dir between invocations breaks the invariant).

Mandated Refactor:
1. Compute the plan file's canonical path ONCE at plan mode entry, store the realpath in PlanModeState.plan_realpath. Reject plan mode entry if the plan file cannot be created/canonicalized.
2. In the allow check, require the tool arg path to canonicalize successfully AND equal plan_realpath. Refuse on any canonicalize failure — no string fallback.
3. At write_file execution time (not check time), re-verify the final resolved path against plan_realpath before opening the file.
4. Reject symlinks: std::fs::symlink_metadata and disallow if file_type().is_symlink().
5. Add tests for symlink swap, non-existent plan file, case-insensitive FS, relative-path confusion.

9ea2aa8c-c6d4-4d2c-a28a-2219c8279fa4.title: transcript::append_entry chmod-after-create leaves brief world-readable window on JSONL files
9ea2aa8c-c6d4-4d2c-a28a-2219c8279fa4.description:
## Severity
Minor
## Dimension
security
## Location
src/transcript.rs:160-187 (append_entry + set_secure_perms)
## Violation
```rust
let mut file = OpenOptions::new().create(true).append(true).open(&path)?;
writeln!(file, "{line}")?;
set_secure_perms(&path, 0o600);
```

On first creation, the file is opened with default umask permissions (typically 0o644) and written to BEFORE the chmod to 0o600 runs. Any session line that contains sensitive context (a tool result containing a token, a prompt with project secrets) is briefly world-readable. The window is short but exists for every NEW transcript file.

`set_secure_perms` then reads the current mode (`perms.mode() & 0o777 != mode`) and only chmod's if it differs — sensible, but it also means a process running with a tighter umask never tightens further. And the call is unconditional on every append, costing a syscall pair per write to do nothing in steady state.

The directory creation has the same defect: `create_dir_all(parent)?; set_secure_perms(parent, 0o700);` opens the dir at 0o755 first, then tightens. Concurrent listers see 0o755 briefly.
## Mandated refactor
On Unix, use `OpenOptions::new().mode(0o600).create(true).append(true).open(&path)` (with `std::os::unix::fs::OpenOptionsExt`) so the file is born with the correct mode. For the directory, use `std::os::unix::fs::DirBuilderExt` + `DirBuilder::new().mode(0o700).recursive(true).create(parent)`. Move the post-create chmod call behind a "first-write" flag so the syscall isn't paid on every append.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

The file and directory are BORN with the restricted modes — no umask-default window between open(2) and chmod(2). Removed the post-create set_secure_perms calls (and the now-unused helper itself). Windows path unchanged (NTFS ACLs). Same shape as the #801 fix to OAuthStore.

9ffbf9e7-7d4b-48ea-971a-486b7ae7b533.title: Guardrails module singleton: LazyLock<Mutex<Option<...>>> anti-pattern
9ffbf9e7-7d4b-48ea-971a-486b7ae7b533.description:
Current state: 

Desired state: 

Reason: 

**Dimension**: Architectural Alignment (Dependency Inversion) + Error Orchestration

**Location**: src/guardrails.rs:26-99 (global GUARDRAILS + wrapper fns)

**Violation**: The guardrails engine is exposed as a global LazyLock<Mutex<Option<GuardrailsEngine>>> accessed via free functions (check_file_access, record_file_modification, check_diff_thresholds, etc.). This is a textbook DIP violation:
- Callers cannot inject a test double
- The module has HIDDEN global state — calling configure() at startup is a temporal-coupling requirement
- If configure() is not called, every wrapper silently no-ops (guardrails.rs:44-49) — violating 'fail fast at perimeters'
- Mutex locking on EVERY file access and modification is a hot-path synchronization cost; the guard only holds an Option read
- The Mutex itself is unnecessary because GuardrailsEngine is set once at startup and never mutated; an RwLock or std::sync::OnceLock would be more appropriate
- Errors in lock acquisition (PoisonError) are silently swallowed (`if let Ok(guard) = ...`) — if any thread panics while holding the lock, ALL subsequent guardrail checks pass with Ok(()) silently

**Mandated Refactor**:
1. Replace with `OnceLock<GuardrailsEngine>` — set once, lock-free reads forever after.
2. Pass &GuardrailsEngine explicitly to call sites (via AppContext struct) instead of a global.
3. If global is unavoidable, at least return Result from each wrapper so an unconfigured engine is a loud panic/error, not silent allow.
4. Add a startup assertion: in main.rs, after guardrails::configure(), probe GUARDRAILS.lock() and panic if empty.

a18b5692-24e0-4109-9043-48b54bb02cbc.title: ACP session_map grows unbounded across session/new and session/load calls
a18b5692-24e0-4109-9043-48b54bb02cbc.description:
## Severity
Major
## Dimension
decoupling
## Location
src/acp.rs:125, 565-634 (session_map, handle_session_new, handle_session_load)
## Violation
`AcpServer` holds `session_map: HashMap<String, String>` for ACP-id → openclaudia-id, and inserts on every `session/new` or fall-through `session/load`:

```rust
self.session_map.insert(acp_session_id.clone(), oc_session_id);
self.messages.clear();
```

There is no eviction path. Sessions accumulate for the lifetime of the server process, and `self.messages` is a SINGLE shared `Vec<Value>` that is `clear()`-ed on every new/load — meaning the server is effectively single-session despite the map's existence. A client that opens two ACP sessions concurrently loses the messages of whichever one isn't currently active, with no error surfaced.

This is a confused-design symptom: either the server is single-session (delete the map and store one current ID) or multi-session (move `messages` into a per-session struct keyed by ACP id, and add eviction on `session/close` or LRU).
## Mandated refactor
Pick one model and commit to it. Recommended: introduce `struct AcpSessionState { messages: Vec<Value>, cancel_flag: Arc<AtomicBool>, oc_session_id: String, last_activity: Instant }` and store `HashMap<String, AcpSessionState>` keyed by ACP session id. Add `session/close` handling (close notification or LRU eviction at N=64) so a long-lived stdio server cannot leak unbounded memory. Update `handle_session_prompt` to look up the session by id, not by hidden global state.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

a1cc8c0f-36e6-4f91-ac2a-38169882a70f.title: MCP HttpTransport missing timeout enables indefinite hangs
a1cc8c0f-36e6-4f91-ac2a-38169882a70f.description:
## Severity
Major
## Dimension
error-handling
## Location
src/mcp.rs:284-293 (HttpTransport::new)
## Violation
The HTTP client is constructed with `reqwest::Client::new()`, which has no default timeout. Any MCP server that hangs (TCP open, no body) blocks the calling task forever. `StdioTransport`'s sibling code has no in-band timeout either; only `McpManager::call_tool_with_timeout` provides a tokio wrapper, but `call_tool` is exposed without one and so are `initialize`, `refresh_tools`, `list_resources`, `read_resource`.

```rust
pub fn new(base_url: &str) -> Self {
    Self {
        client: reqwest::Client::new(),
        ...
    }
}
```

Compare with `src/web.rs:265` which sets `.timeout(Duration::from_secs(30))`.
## Mandated refactor
Build the client with `Client::builder().timeout(Duration::from_secs(30)).connect_timeout(Duration::from_secs(10)).build()`. Apply a default per-request `tokio::time::timeout` inside every transport method (`StdioTransport::request`, `HttpTransport::request`) so the `McpError::Timeout` variant fires when a transport hangs.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

a1d2a228-d7bc-4d6e-9dbe-275ab38d9950.title: SessionManager::end_session temporal coupling — no RAII, silent persist-failure
a1d2a228-d7bc-4d6e-9dbe-275ab38d9950.description:
Current state: 

Desired state: 

Reason: 

Dimension: Cognitive Readability (4) / Error Orchestration (7)

Location: src/session/mod.rs:467-488 (SessionManager::end_session) and callers across main.rs/tui/app.rs.

Violation:
1. Temporal coupling: The lifecycle is 'get_or_create_session() -> mutate -> end_session()'. If the program panics, is SIGKILLed, or the caller forgets to call end_session, ALL in-memory session state (turn_metrics, files_modified, decisions, cumulative_usage) is lost. There is no Drop impl and no RAII guard. The comment on atomic_write (line 492) only protects writes that actually happen.
2. Error swallowing: persist_session failure is logged via warn!() (line 475) then Some(session) is returned anyway. The caller has no signal that the session was NOT durably stored. This is exactly the 'swallowed internal exception' anti-pattern from 3.4.
3. end_session returns Option<Session> where None means 'no session was active' — a distinct condition from 'persist failed'. Caller cannot tell them apart.
4. persist_session writes THREE files (session.id.json, latest.json, handoff.md) non-atomically relative to each other. If the process dies between writes, latest.json can point to a session whose .json file was never written, or handoff.md can lag the session JSON.

Mandated Refactor:
1. Introduce an OwnedSession RAII guard returned by get_or_create_session() that auto-calls persist() on Drop.
2. persist_session returns Result; end_session returns Result<Option<Session>, PersistError> so the caller can decide how to handle failure.
3. Write all three files into a temp directory then rename the directory atomically (or use a single index file listing current session id + serial number).
4. Contract assertion: after end_session, no further mutation methods on the Session should be possible (consume by value).

a35a0786-b064-42f1-a086-6ca68e53ba4c.description:
Steps to reproduce:

a35bda57-3a1a-48d9-926c-db542cc624bd.title: VddEngine API takes builder_provider as &str throughout coupling to stringly-typed routing
a35bda57-3a1a-48d9-926c-db542cc624bd.description:
## Severity
Trivial
## Dimension
naming
## Location
src/vdd/mod.rs (multiple): 209, 288, 348, 402, 803, 885, 995
## Violation
Every public/internal method in VddEngine takes builder_provider: &str:

```rust
pub async fn review_text(..., builder_provider: &str, builder_api_key: ...) -> ...
pub async fn process_response(..., builder_provider: &str, ...) -> ...
async fn advisory_review(..., builder_provider: &str, ...) -> ...
async fn blocking_loop(..., builder_provider: &str, ...) -> ...
async fn triage_findings(..., builder_provider: &str, ...) -> ...
async fn verify_findings(..., builder_provider: &str, ...) -> ...
async fn send_to_builder_for_verification(..., provider_name: &str, ...) -> ...
async fn send_to_builder(..., provider_name: &str, ...) -> ...
```

This is stringly-typed routing through 8+ functions in the same module. A typo at any call site silently routes to the wrong provider (or fails downstream with a ConfigError that doesn't pinpoint the typo location). The framework's naming guideline mandates "registered constants" and "enums over stringly-typed code."

Worse, the parameter is paired with builder_api_key: Option<&ApiKey> at each callsite — these are conceptually one unit (a Provider handle) but passed as two parameters. The function-signature-mandate of 0-2 parameters is technically met but only by collapsing the unit into two coupled positional args.

## Mandated refactor
Define a Provider handle (existing ProviderAdapter trait or a new struct), pass it as a single value, and remove the &str pairs:

```rust
pub struct BuilderProvider<'a> {
    name: &'a str,
    api_key: Option<&'a ApiKey>,
}

pub async fn review_text(..., builder: &BuilderProvider<'_>) -> ...
```

Internal methods take &BuilderProvider; the .name() and .api_key() accessors give controlled access. ConfigError messages can attach the BuilderProvider for richer diagnostics.

## Filed from QA review dispatch

a50491f2-e653-4fa5-b390-33f3a5beb986.title: SSE buffer can grow unbounded when upstream never emits newlines
a50491f2-e653-4fa5-b390-33f3a5beb986.description:
## Severity
Critical
## Dimension
security
## Location
src/pipeline.rs:516-543
## Violation
The SSE parsing loop in `stream_sse_response` accumulates upstream bytes into an unbounded `String` until a `\n` is found:

```rust
let mut buffer = String::new();
...
while let Some(chunk_result) = stream.next().await {
    ...
    buffer.push_str(&String::from_utf8_lossy(&chunk));
    while let Some(line_end) = buffer.find('\n') {
        ...
    }
}
```
A hostile or broken upstream that streams large payloads without `\n` (or a single very long SSE event) will inflate `buffer` until the process OOMs. There is no cap on a single line, no cap on the buffer, and the only timeout (`last_data_time.elapsed()`) is reset by every byte received, so a 1 MiB/s newline-free stream is welcomed. The `String::from_utf8_lossy().to_string()` allocation also forces a full UTF-8 validation+copy on every chunk.
## Mandated refactor
Introduce `MAX_SSE_LINE_BYTES` (e.g. 1 MiB) and `MAX_SSE_BUFFER_BYTES` constants; abort the stream and emit `AppEvent::ApiError` when either is exceeded. Switch to `BytesMut` with a SIMD `memchr` scan over raw bytes to avoid the per-chunk UTF-8 round-trip. Track total bytes received against an absolute ceiling separate from the inactivity timeout.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

a6bf2499-5bc1-4e52-a2be-9572971e8f9a.title: Untagged enum shapes can silently mis-parse: PluginSource, HooksSpec, CommandsSpec
a6bf2499-5bc1-4e52-a2be-9572971e8f9a.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

**Dimension**: Functional Correctness (YAML/JSON deserialization robustness)

**Location**:
- src/plugins/manifest.rs:52-73 (CommandsSpec, HooksSpec, HooksSpecEntry untagged)
- src/plugins/manifest.rs:141-158 (McpServersSpec, McpServersSpecEntry untagged)
- src/plugins/manifest.rs:186-203 (AgentsSpec, SkillsSpec untagged)
- src/plugins/marketplace.rs:12-20 (PluginSource untagged)

**Violation**: Serde's #[serde(untagged)] tries variants in declaration order and picks the first that successfully deserializes. Multiple variants overlap:
- CommandsSpec: Path(String) vs Paths(Vec<String>) vs Map(HashMap<...>) — a command value that is JSON object like {"foo":"bar"} tries to deserialize as HashMap<String, CommandMetadata> and may SUCCEED with an empty metadata on misconfigured input (CommandMetadata has no required fields). A user who writes {commands: {source: "./cmds"}} intending a typo-fix for CommandsSpec::Path(".../cmds") silently becomes a Map with one command named 'source' with source ".../cmds". No error.
- HooksSpec::Inline(HooksDefinition) has no required fields either — any object deserializes successfully as an EMPTY HooksDefinition, masking real hooks config errors.
- PluginSource::Path(String) vs Structured — if a user writes `source: "npm:foo"` intending a structured source, it silently becomes a Path and later fails at install time with confusing 'path not found' error.

**Mandated Refactor**:
1. Convert each untagged enum to an internally tagged representation with `#[serde(tag = "kind")]` OR use `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` on all target structs.
2. Add `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` to HooksDefinition, CommandMetadata, PluginSourceDef variants, MarketplaceSource variants.
3. Add roundtrip property tests that assert: for each ambiguous input, either it deserializes to the expected variant OR it errors — never silently into a wrong variant.
4. Provide a config-validate subcommand that surfaces deserialization warnings to users before runtime.

a74ba0f6-44f9-420b-8c91-5091b73dff43.title: memory_save tags are stored as comma-joined TEXT — cannot query, comma in tag corrupts round-trip
a74ba0f6-44f9-420b-8c91-5091b73dff43.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

Dimension: Functional Correctness (1) / Architectural Alignment (2)

Location: src/memory.rs:356-364 memory_save; 390-407 memory_search split(',') parse; schema at line 231 'tags TEXT DEFAULT'.

Violation: memory_save takes tags: &[String] and stores them as tags.join(",") in a single TEXT column. Every read path splits on ','. Problems:

1. A tag containing a literal comma (e.g. tag='rust, tokio') is split into two fake tags on read. No escaping. Data corruption on round-trip.
2. Cannot query 'all memories tagged X' efficiently — no index, only substring LIKE which yields false matches (e.g. LIKE '%rust%' matches 'rustaceans').
3. First normal form violation. Tags are a many-to-many — should be a junction table archival_memory_tags(memory_id, tag).
4. FTS5 is indexing the tag blob as one giant term. Searching for a tag via FTS uses substring semantics instead of exact match.
5. Empty tag list = empty string — split(',') returns [''], which is then filtered at line 398 with 'filter(|s| !s.is_empty())'. OK but wasteful allocation.

Mandated Refactor:
1. Schema v4: CREATE TABLE archival_memory_tags (memory_id INTEGER REFERENCES archival_memory(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, tag TEXT NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY(memory_id, tag)); CREATE INDEX ON archival_memory_tags(tag).
2. memory_save wraps the INSERT + N tag-INSERTs in a single transaction.
3. memory_search JOINs to filter by tag explicitly via a parameter.
4. Backfill migration: parse the old tags column, write into the new table, drop the old column.
5. Keep the FTS index on archival_memory.content only; tags filter is a separate JOIN.

e5adcb05-1486-461e-8ab5-3f2213ad0b9a.author: lOrm
e5adcb05-1486-461e-8ab5-3f2213ad0b9a.content:
Schema v4 normalises archival_memory.tags into a junction table.

Schema: CREATE TABLE archival_memory_tags(memory_id INTEGER REFERENCES archival_memory(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, tag TEXT NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY(memory_id, tag)) + CREATE INDEX idx_archival_memory_tags_tag ON archival_memory_tags(tag).

Hot paths:
- memory_save now opens a Transaction, inserts the content row, then INSERT OR IGNORE for each non-empty tag, commits atomically.
- memory_search/memory_get/memory_list select content columns then hydrate tags via load_tags_for(conn, id) — JOIN-free, O(log n) per row.
- memory_search_by_tag(tag, limit) is new: indexed equality on archival_memory_tags.tag — exact match, no LIKE substring false positives, comma not special.
- reset_all wipes archival_memory_tags first then archival_memory (FK cascade also makes this safe).
- migrate_v4_on: created in SAVEPOINT migrate_v4, back-fills legacy comma-joined data via split(',').trim() into archival_memory_tags, rebuilds archival_memory_fts to drop the tags column from the FTS index, then ALTER TABLE archival_memory DROP COLUMN tags. ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT on any failure.
- Connection::open now issues PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON; without it the ON DELETE CASCADE is a silent no-op.

Tests (5 new in memory::tests):
- issue_464_tag_with_comma_round_trips_intact — 'rust, tokio' survives save->get as ONE tag.
- issue_464_search_by_tag_is_exact_match_not_substring — search 'rust' returns rust-tagged and multi-tag rows, NOT 'rustaceans'.
- issue_464_migration_preserves_legacy_comma_joined_data — hand-built v3 db with comma-joined rows + whitespace + empty tag string migrates correctly; legacy tags column gone; schema_version == 4.
- issue_464_empty_tag_list_produces_no_junction_rows — memory_save(c, &[]) writes 0 junction rows; memory_search_by_tag("") doesn't match.
- issue_464_delete_cascades_into_junction_table — memory_delete cascades to junction rows (proves PRAGMA foreign_keys is on).

Verification: cargo clippy exit 0; cargo test --lib -- --test-threads=1 → 1365 passed; 0 failed. No new #[allow] / clippy.toml / #[ignore]. Touched files: src/memory.rs (junction table + migration + helpers + 5 tests), src/services/background.rs (updated raw INSERTs to drop legacy tags column reference).

a770d748-027b-43ea-b169-57e47e03aeb1.title: Duration::from_mins is nightly-only unstable API in init_vdd_engine_if_enabled
a770d748-027b-43ea-b169-57e47e03aeb1.description:
## Severity
Critical
## Dimension
complexity
## Location
src/main.rs:619-622
## Violation
The reqwest client builder uses an unstable nightly-only API.

```rust
let http_client = reqwest::Client::builder()
    .timeout(std::time::Duration::from_mins(2))
    .build()
    .unwrap_or_else(|_| reqwest::Client::new());
```

`std::time::Duration::from_mins` is gated behind the unstable `duration_constructors` feature (`#![feature(duration_constructors)]`) and is not available on stable Rust. This binary will fail to compile on stable toolchains, blocking CI and end-user installation. Additionally, the `unwrap_or_else(|_| reqwest::Client::new())` silently drops the timeout configuration if the builder fails — a configured 2-minute VDD timeout becomes the default (no timeout), which is exactly the bug crosslink #496 was supposed to prevent.

## Mandated refactor
Replace with stable equivalent and surface the build error:

```rust
let http_client = reqwest::Client::builder()
    .timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(120))
    .build()?;  // propagate the failure rather than silently dropping timeout
```

If propagation is infeasible at this call site, return `None` and log a warn so callers know VDD is disabled rather than running with infinite timeout.

## Filed from QA review dispatch

a8542ea0-14e8-4970-bc97-563a6d5d72c6.title: FileIndex score_match uses wrapping_sub(1) on usize creating obscure underflow path
a8542ea0-14e8-4970-bc97-563a6d5d72c6.description:
## Severity
Minor

## Dimension
Cognitive Readability / KISS

## Location
src/tools/file_index.rs:152-158 (CamelCase bonus check inside score_match)

## Violation
```rust
if orig_chars[pi].is_uppercase()
    && orig_chars
        .get(pi.wrapping_sub(1))
        .is_some_and(|c| c.is_lowercase())
{
    score += BONUS_CAMEL;
}
```

The code is inside a branch guarded by `if pi > 0` (line 146) — so `pi.wrapping_sub(1)` will never actually underflow. The wrapping_sub is therefore a dead defensive measure that obscures intent: a reader has to mentally execute the path to confirm safety. KISS §3.2 demands the obvious form: `orig_chars.get(pi - 1)`. The wrapping arithmetic is a "clever" pattern that suggests the programmer was uncertain about the invariant.

Worse, the cast at line 184 uses `#[allow(clippy::cast_possible_truncation, clippy::cast_possible_wrap)]` — silencing the lint instead of bounding `path_chars.len()` first. The path_len_penalty division yields zero for very long paths, defeating the "Prefer shorter paths" intent for the worst offenders.

## Mandated refactor
1. Replace `pi.wrapping_sub(1)` with `pi - 1`. The `if pi > 0` guard already enforces safety.
2. Replace the `#[allow]` casts with `i32::try_from(path_chars.len()).unwrap_or(i32::MAX) / 10` — the value cannot legitimately overflow because paths are bounded by OS PATH_MAX.

## Filed from QA review dispatch

a8621c1d-106e-4ad8-b4c5-dfe95a2f4e24.title: SessionId::from_raw accepts any string bypassing the UUID invariant of the newtype
a8621c1d-106e-4ad8-b4c5-dfe95a2f4e24.description:
## Severity
Minor
## Dimension
kiss
## Location
src/state/categories.rs:42-46
## Violation
The SessionId newtype claims to be UUID-shaped:

```rust
/// Session identifier — UUID-shaped string.
///
/// Newtype so session ids don't get confused with teammate / agent / transcript
/// ids at call sites...
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(transparent)]
pub struct SessionId(String);
```

But `from_raw` accepts any String:

```rust
/// Wrap a caller-supplied string without re-validating. Used by
/// persist.rs when deserializing v1 files written before this
/// newtype existed.
#[must_use]
pub fn from_raw(s: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
    Self(s.into())
}
```

The test `session_id_round_trips_from_raw` explicitly stores `"abcd-1234"` — not a UUID. The "make invalid states unrepresentable" guideline is violated: SessionId promises UUID, but `from_raw("")` or `from_raw("../../etc/passwd")` produce SessionId values that propagate through logging, paths (session_project_dir uses session_id), and database queries.

Worse, since `#[serde(transparent)]` is on the type, a malicious or corrupted on-disk session file with `"session_id": "../../etc/passwd"` is silently accepted by from_raw — and `session_project_dir.join(session_id.as_str())` is a path traversal vector if any caller composes paths this way.

## Mandated refactor
1. Rename `from_raw` to `from_legacy_v1_blob` and gate it behind `pub(crate)` plus a clarifying doc comment that it is only safe to call on input that was previously a uuid::Uuid::to_string() output.
2. Add a `try_parse(s: &str) -> Result<Self, uuid::Error>` for the deserialization path that validates the input is a valid UUID string.
3. The serde derive should use try_parse via a custom impl rather than transparent; transparent allows any string through.

## Filed from QA review dispatch

New session_id_from_raw_validates_uuid test asserts UUID round-trip works and that empty / abcd-1234 / ../../etc/passwd / not-a-uuid / malformed UUIDs all fail. Existing round-trip test renamed to session_id_round_trips_from_raw_unchecked.

a877ff2f-5388-486b-85b6-2334f81b37a5.title: duplicate cwd_lock helper inlined verbatim in worktree.rs and cron.rs tests
a877ff2f-5388-486b-85b6-2334f81b37a5.description:
## Severity
Trivial

## Dimension
DRY

## Location
src/tools/worktree.rs:349-354 and src/tools/cron.rs:268-273 (both define `fn cwd_lock() -> MutexGuard<'static, ()>`)

## Violation
The exact same helper definition appears in both test modules:

```rust
fn cwd_lock() -> MutexGuard<'static, ()> {
    static LOCK: OnceLock<Mutex<()>> = OnceLock::new();
    LOCK.get_or_init(|| Mutex::new(()))
        .lock()
        .unwrap_or_else(std::sync::PoisonError::into_inner)
}
```

Two separate `static LOCK` instances — meaning the cwd_lock in worktree.rs does NOT serialize against the cwd_lock in cron.rs. A worktree test and a cron test that BOTH mutate cwd via std::env::set_current_dir can interleave under parallel test execution and corrupt each other's cwd assumptions.

(The comment in cron.rs:267 even acknowledges the need to coordinate "with worktree tests" — but the two locks are independent.)

## Mandated refactor
Move the helper to a shared test utility module (e.g. `src/tools/testutil.rs` with `#[cfg(test)] pub`) that exports a single `pub fn process_cwd_lock() -> MutexGuard<'static, ()>` backed by ONE OnceLock<Mutex<()>>. Both test modules import that helper. This guarantees mutual exclusion across the entire process.

a962240b-0eb5-41ef-bca4-0ebcc1d735b7.title: git_clone / git_pull / git rev-parse may execute via PATH-injected git binary
a962240b-0eb5-41ef-bca4-0ebcc1d735b7.description:
## Severity
Major
## Dimension
security
## Location
src/plugins/git.rs:26-46, src/plugins/git.rs:55-71, src/plugins/git.rs:80-93
## Violation
All three subprocess invocations construct the git command with a bare program name. \"std::process::Command::new("git")\" resolves \"git\" by walking the runtime PATH, so any directory writeable by an attacker that ends up earlier on PATH (e.g. a poisoned \".openclaudia/plugins/\" workspace, a manipulated user shell, a CI runner with a misordered PATH) lets a malicious binary masquerade as git and run with the user's privileges during plugin install/update. Quoted lines:

    let mut cmd = std::process::Command::new(\"git\");
    cmd.arg(\"clone\").arg(\"--depth\").arg(\"1\");
    ...
    let output = std::process::Command::new(\"git\")
        .arg(\"rev-parse\").arg(\"HEAD\")
    ...
    let output = std::process::Command::new(\"git\")
        .arg(\"pull\")

Plugin install is already an untrusted-code path (a marketplace can redirect to an arbitrary repo), so PATH-injection escalation here is a Major-severity supply-chain hole.
## Mandated refactor
Resolve git's absolute path once at process start using \"which::which(\"git\")\" (or equivalent) and cache the resulting PathBuf in a module-level OnceLock; pass that absolute PathBuf to Command::new throughout git.rs. Reject the install path entirely if the canonical git binary is not under a system-trusted prefix (e.g. /usr/bin, /usr/local/bin) when running under a managed PluginPolicy.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

206dc14b-55c0-44a7-9c58-fc1c2e83d36a.author: lOrm
206dc14b-55c0-44a7-9c58-fc1c2e83d36a.content: Fixed: GIT_BIN: LazyLock<Result<PathBuf, String>> in src/plugins/git.rs caches which::which("git") at first use. All three Command::new("git") sites (git_clone L63, resolve_head_sha L93, git_pull L119) now invoke Command::new(git_bin()?). Added 3 regression tests: (1) git_bin_is_absolute_path — invariant that the cached binary is an absolute path; (2) git_clone_uses_resolved_absolute_bin — forensic shim test: prepends a sentinel-touching git to PATH after GIT_BIN resolution and asserts the shim sentinel is never written, proving the dispatch went through the cached absolute path; (3) git_bin_surfaces_missing_binary — failure-surface contract that Err lookup yields PluginError::IoError. Tests 1412 -> 1415, cargo clippy --lib --all-targets -- -D warnings exits 0, cargo fmt clean. No #[allow], no #[ignore], no clippy.toml. which = "8" added to Cargo.toml (already a transitive dep via headless_chrome).

a9aa50b8-c9f5-4f2a-86e0-b5c322367b45.title: execute_notebook_edit is a 200-line god function with cyclomatic complexity > 15
a9aa50b8-c9f5-4f2a-86e0-b5c322367b45.description:
## Severity
Critical

## Dimension
Complexity / SOLID-S (SRP) / Structural Modularity

## Location
src/tools/file/notebook.rs:48-298 (function `execute_notebook_edit`, ~250 lines, annotated with `#[allow(clippy::too_many_lines)]`)

## Violation
The function carries an `#[allow(clippy::too_many_lines)]` to suppress the lint that should be failing it. Counting branches it contains: at least 18 distinct decision points (argument extraction guards x6, edit_mode validation, read-tracker check, canonicalize match, file read match, JSON parse match, cells lookup, resolved_index resolve, target_desc map, replace/insert/delete arms each with their own nested checks, write match, serialize match, warning check). Cyclomatic complexity ≥ 18 — over the V(G) > 15 hard reject threshold from §3.5.

Concrete: lines 165-250 hold a single `match edit_mode { "replace" => {...} "insert" => {...} "delete" => {...} _ => unreachable!() }` where each arm is itself a multi-step procedure with its own out-of-bounds checks and side effects, then lines 252-297 do post-processing inside another nested `match` on serialize → write. This is the god-object anti-pattern at function granularity.

## Mandated refactor
1. Replace `#[allow(clippy::too_many_lines)]` with extraction; do not silence the lint.
2. Extract three private functions: `apply_replace(cells, index, new_source, cell_type)`, `apply_insert(cells, insert_at, new_source, cell_type)`, `apply_delete(cells, index)`, each returning `Result<EditOutcome, ToolError>`.
3. Extract `parse_locator(args, cells) -> Result<LocatorResolution, ToolError>` for the cell_id/cell_number resolution block (lines 143-163).
4. Extract `persist_notebook(path, notebook, edit_mode, outcome) -> Result<String, ToolError>` for the write+summary block (252-297).
5. The top-level `execute_notebook_edit` should then be linear: validate → resolve locator → dispatch → persist.

a9f719b7-4b6c-4b50-bb2d-735a32642c48.title: Tool return type (String, bool) is stringly-typed — replace with Result<ToolOutput, ToolError> enum
a9f719b7-4b6c-4b50-bb2d-735a32642c48.description:
Current state: 

Desired state: 

Reason: 

**Dimension:** Architectural Alignment / Error Orchestration / Type Safety

**Location:** pervasive across /home/doll/OpenClaudia/src/tools/ — every tool returns (String, bool). Examples: bash/mod.rs:309, file/read.rs:40, file/write.rs:9, file/edit.rs:9, chainlink.rs:11, lsp.rs:73, web.rs:9, worktree.rs:59, cron.rs:143, task.rs:7, ask_user.rs:8.

**Violation:**
Every tool function returns (String, bool) — the first element is both success text AND error text depending on the second bool. This violates:
1. **Type safety.** There is no way for the type system to prevent swapping the two components. A refactor that flips the bool leaks errors as success. No compile-time guarantee that errors carry error data and not arbitrary text.
2. **Loss of structure.** The caller (check_tool_result_marker, tool_intercept.rs format_tool_results_xml_with_names) regex-greps for 'error' / 'Error' / 'failed' to decide completion hints (tool_intercept.rs:718) — a classic stringly-typed anti-pattern.
3. **Error category is erased.** The caller cannot distinguish 'permission denied' from 'file not found' from 'upstream 500' without substring matching.
4. **Markers are stuffed into the same String.** USER_QUESTION_MARKER, ENTER_PLAN_MODE_MARKER are detected by JSON-parsing the content (mod.rs:923) — a brittle in-band signalling.

**Mandated Refactor:**
1. Define:
   pub enum ToolError { InvalidArg(String), PermissionDenied(String), NotFound(String), Io(io::Error), Timeout, Upstream(String), Policy(String) }
   pub enum ToolOutput { Text(String), Image { mime: String, data: Vec<u8> }, Structured(serde_json::Value), Marker(ToolMarker) }
   pub enum ToolMarker { UserQuestion(Vec<Question>), EnterPlanMode, ExitPlanMode { allowed: Vec<AllowedPrompt> } }
2. Every execute_* function returns Result<ToolOutput, ToolError>. Callers pattern-match the marker branch directly.
3. Delete check_tool_result_marker, parse_user_questions, parse_exit_plan_mode_prompts — the Marker variant IS the marker.
4. format_tool_results_xml_with_names' completion hints become methods on ToolOutput (ToolOutput::completion_hint(&self) -> Option<&str>) — no string matching.

9981a8c4-3dda-43ed-ba1d-a64a93d84278.author: lOrm
9981a8c4-3dda-43ed-ba1d-a64a93d84278.content: Issue calls for replacing the (String, bool) tool return convention across all src/tools/ files with Result<ToolOutput, ToolError> where ToolOutput is an enum (Text/Image/Structured/Marker) and ToolError categorizes failures (InvalidArg/PermissionDenied/NotFound/Io/Timeout/Upstream/Policy), deleting check_tool_result_marker and the in-band marker parsing entirely. Not addressable in a cleanup pass: pervasive across every tool, tool_intercept.rs format_tool_results_xml_with_names, the marker plumbing (USER_QUESTION_MARKER, ENTER_PLAN_MODE_MARKER, ExitPlanMode), and the completion-hint heuristics. Closing the cleanup-pass ticket while tracking the broader refactor under tools/ architectural work.

a9f82755-47d3-49ac-a877-089c10975789.title: FileIndex paths and lower_paths are two parallel Vecs invariant must be maintained by hand
a9f82755-47d3-49ac-a877-089c10975789.description:
## Severity
Minor

## Dimension
Type Safety / Data Modeling

## Location
src/tools/file_index.rs:28-32 (FileIndex struct), 72-76 (walk_dir push), 89-104 (search zip)

## Violation
```rust
pub struct FileIndex {
    paths: Vec<String>,
    lower_paths: Vec<String>,
}
```

Two parallel Vecs that MUST stay index-synchronized. Every push to `paths` MUST also push to `lower_paths`; every read from one MUST zip with the other. The invariant is enforced only by the convention that walk_dir does both pushes (line 74-75). Search uses `self.paths.iter().zip(self.lower_paths.iter())` (line 91). If a future maintainer adds a path to one Vec but not the other (e.g. in a hypothetical `remove` method, or during incremental updates), index returns drift silently — search would skip files or score the wrong file.

## Mandated refactor
```rust
struct IndexedPath { display: String, lower: String }
pub struct FileIndex { paths: Vec<IndexedPath> }
```
One push per file, one iteration per search. The invariant is enforced by the type system. Performance is identical (struct of strings = same allocation pattern as paired Vecs).

## Filed from QA review dispatch

aa54ef92-a855-4c30-8fd3-6d70af6d0d23.title: cron.rs ScheduleStore: lost-update race, non-atomic write, hardcoded relative path, short UUID collisions
aa54ef92-a855-4c30-8fd3-6d70af6d0d23.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

**Dimension:** Functional Correctness / State Management

**Location:** /home/doll/OpenClaudia/src/tools/cron.rs lines 33-55 (load/save), 168-193 (execute_cron_create), 213-228 (execute_cron_delete)

**Violation:**
1. Lost-update race: two concurrent cron_create calls both load, both mutate, both save — one overwrites the other silently.
2. Non-atomic write: save() at line 54 does fs::write (open+truncate+write). A crash mid-write leaves schedules.json truncated. Next load() falls back to Default — schedules vanish.
3. Path hardcoded to '.openclaudia/schedules.json' relative to CWD. If CWD mutates (see worktree tool CWD side effect), schedules move directories.
4. 8-hex-char ID from Uuid::new_v4().to_string()[..8] (line 179) gives 32 bits. Duplicate check is against NAME only, not ID — birthday collisions cascade.
5. No schema_version field — future migrations break existing stores with unhelpful serde errors.

**Mandated Refactor:**
1. Acquire advisory lock on schedules.json (fs2 crate, flock/LockFileEx) spanning load..save.
2. Atomic write: fs::write to schedules.json.tmp then fs::rename.
3. Capture absolute schedules_path at Session init, pass via ToolContext.
4. Use full UUID or 16-hex chars, and check ID uniqueness on insert.
5. Add schema_version: u32.

## Violation
Three unconditional `unwrap()` calls in a hot user-input path. The TUI is a long-running interactive process — a panic here tears down the alt-screen with raw mode enabled and leaves the user's terminal in a broken state.

```rust
let re = regex::Regex::new(r#"@"([^"]+)"|@(\S+)"#).unwrap();
...
let full_match = cap.get(0).unwrap().as_str();
let raw_path = cap.get(1).or_else(|| cap.get(2)).unwrap().as_str();
```

`cap.get(1).or_else(|| cap.get(2))` is also load-bearing — if the regex is ever changed to introduce additional groups, the unwrap may fire on a `None`. The regex itself is recompiled on every call (regex compilation is expensive — ~100us-1ms per call).

## Mandated refactor
1. Lift the regex to a `once_cell::sync::Lazy<Regex>` / `std::sync::LazyLock` constant so it compiles exactly once and any compile error surfaces at first use (which can be tested in unit tests).
2. Replace `unwrap()` on capture groups with explicit handling: skip the iteration with `continue` if the expected group is absent. The first call (`cap.get(0)`) is safe per regex contract but should still use `expect("regex Match must have group 0")` to document the invariant rather than swallow the diagnostic.

ab0ccb3b-b087-4808-b007-fe5fa42a4024.title: QA: lsp.rs child.wait() after shutdown has no timeout
ab0ccb3b-b087-4808-b007-fe5fa42a4024.description:
## Severity
Minor
## Dimension
concurrency
## Location
src/tools/lsp.rs:226-229
## Violation
After issuing `shutdown` + `exit`, `run_lsp_request` calls `child.wait()` with no timeout. A wedged language server will block this call forever — and because `execute_lsp` is synchronous from the tool dispatch loop, the agent stalls.

Quoted (lsp.rs:226-229):
```
    send_lsp_message(&mut stdin, "shutdown", 3, json!(null))?;
    send_lsp_notification(&mut stdin, "exit", json!(null))?;
    let _ = child.wait();
```

`let _` also discards exit status.
## Mandated refactor
1. Spawn a watchdog thread that `child.kill()`s after a bounded shutdown deadline (~2s).
2. Use `wait_timeout` crate / `nix::sys::wait::waitpid(WNOHANG)` polling.
3. Surface the wait result.

ab2ae097-c0c4-4c0c-9b84-99ebead283ad.title: HookEngine.run: matcher_context conflates tool_name, prompt, event - leaks prompt into regex
ab2ae097-c0c4-4c0c-9b84-99ebead283ad.description:
Current state: 

Desired state: 

Reason: 

**Dimension**: Cognitive Readability + Security

**Location**: src/hooks/mod.rs:441-451 (get_matcher_context), 453-464 (matches_entry)

**Violation**: get_matcher_context returns one of: tool_name | prompt | event config_key. This means a hook configured for PreToolUse with matcher='rm' might match when:
- The user enters 'I want to rm a file' as a prompt (UserPromptSubmit event firing with same matcher)
- The hook was semantically intended for tool-name-matching only

A matcher intended to be a TOOL NAME regex (the typical case) can accidentally fire against user-submitted free-form text. This is a semantic confusion that can cause production hook firings on arbitrary user content — both a correctness and a privacy issue (the prompt is sent into the hook regex engine, where a log of the match context might persist).

Additionally this violates SRP: the function switches matcher semantics based on which field is populated. Callers cannot tell, at config time, what their matcher will actually see.

**Mandated Refactor**:
1. Change HookEntry to have an EXPLICIT `matcher_target` field: enum { ToolName, Prompt, EventKey } so authors declare intent.
2. Split HookEngine::get_matcher_context into three typed accessors: match_tool(entry, tool), match_prompt(entry, prompt), match_event(entry, event).
3. In the run() dispatcher, pick the accessor based on HookEvent variant.
4. Default matcher_target per event (PreToolUse→ToolName, UserPromptSubmit→Prompt) but require explicit field if non-default.

ab8f9c0a-721b-497c-bb07-b3c6947da57b.title: subagent: BACKGROUND_AGENTS and TRANSCRIPT_STORE globals defeat testability and isolation
ab8f9c0a-721b-497c-bb07-b3c6947da57b.description:
## Severity
Minor
## Dimension
decoupling
## Location
src/subagent.rs:365-366 (BACKGROUND_AGENTS) and src/subagent.rs:381-382 (TRANSCRIPT_STORE)
## Violation
```rust
pub static BACKGROUND_AGENTS: LazyLock<BackgroundAgentManager> =
    LazyLock::new(BackgroundAgentManager::new);
```

```rust
pub(crate) static TRANSCRIPT_STORE: LazyLock<Mutex<HashMap<String, StoredTranscript>>> =
    LazyLock::new(|| Mutex::new(HashMap::new()));
```

Both are process-global mutable singletons. Consequences:

1. Two tests that register agents share state and pollute each other (the test suite already works around this with random UUIDs).
2. Coordinator agents and the top-level CLI agent share one BackgroundAgentManager — there is no per-leader isolation, breaking the "always-allow per teammate" guarantee the LeaderPermissionBridge is designed to enforce.
3. Dependency Inversion violation: every caller depends on a concrete global instead of a `Arc<dyn AgentRegistry>` trait object.
4. The transcripts global holds raw `Vec<Value>` cloning the full message history on every load — no test can swap it for an in-memory mock.

This is the classic Singleton anti-pattern (heuristic 3.1, "Reject God Objects … force division into granular services").

## Mandated refactor
Define a `trait BackgroundAgentRegistry: Send + Sync` and a `trait TranscriptStore: Send + Sync`. Make `run_subagent` take `&dyn BackgroundAgentRegistry, &dyn TranscriptStore` (or an `AppHandles` bundle). Keep a single shared instance constructed in `main.rs` and inject it. Remove the globals or, if retained, mark them `#[cfg(not(test))]` and provide test-only constructor.

abb7a9c5-9db5-4700-ba7a-0eb00202bb8f.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

**Dimension:** Functional Correctness, Performance
**Lint:** clippy::or_fun_call

## Violation
`x.unwrap_or(some_function())` evaluates `some_function()` UNCONDITIONALLY, even when `x` is `Some` — the unwrap never uses the value. This is wasted work at best; at worst it's a bug (side effects, expensive allocation, or panics in the default path fire even on the happy path).

## Locations
- src/pipeline.rs: 138, 139, 299
- src/vdd/mod.rs: 1040

Additionally: `or(fn())` same category:
- src/tui/app.rs: 143

## Mandated Refactor
Replace eager `unwrap_or(f())` with lazy `unwrap_or_else(|| f())`:
```rust
// Before (eager, always runs f())
x.unwrap_or(expensive_default())
// After (lazy, only runs f() if x is None)
x.unwrap_or_else(|| expensive_default())
```
Same fix for `.or(f())` → `.or_else(|| f())`. Each of the 5 sites requires a case-by-case audit — if `f()` is a pure `const` literal or trivial value, `unwrap_or` is fine; only when it's a fn call/allocation/computation is this wasteful.

adeb5236-32fc-43de-a4a4-71df76706006.title: skills::load_skills hard-codes relative ".openclaudia/skills" — silently picks up working-dir-relative skill files
adeb5236-32fc-43de-a4a4-71df76706006.description:
## Severity
Minor
## Dimension
security
## Location
src/skills.rs:62-77
## Violation
The project-skills directory is computed as a relative PathBuf, so its meaning shifts with whatever directory the process happens to be in when load_skills() fires. Quoted lines:

    // Project skills: .openclaudia/skills/
    let project_dir = PathBuf::from(".openclaudia/skills");
    if project_dir.exists() {
        dirs_to_scan.push(project_dir);
    }

If a user runs `oc` from an unrelated directory that happens to contain a `.openclaudia/skills/` (cloned third-party repo, demo bundle), those skills load with the same privileges as the user's own. Worse, the prompt body is later injected directly into the model context via `SlashCommandResult::Skill(skill.prompt)` (slash.rs:531-534), so a hostile cwd silently steers the agent.
## Mandated refactor
Resolve project_dir against an explicit project root: walk upward from cwd looking for `.openclaudia/config.yaml` (use the same logic the config loader uses, or extract it into a shared `project_root()` helper). If no root is found, skip the project-skills load entirely. Log the resolved absolute path at `info!` so operators can verify the source. Add a startup audit that prints all skills paths the next REPL render will use.

Expressions of the form `a * b + c` on floats can be computed as a single fused-multiply-add via `a.mul_add(b, c)`. The FMA instruction is both faster on modern CPUs and numerically more accurate (single rounding instead of two).

b27143d4-ec45-477b-9e65-bd4ef291168c.title: resolve_path rejects .. components but still susceptible to symlink escape and absolute path escape
b27143d4-ec45-477b-9e65-bd4ef291168c.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

**Dimension:** Security and Access (Path Traversal)

**Location:** /home/doll/OpenClaudia/src/tools/file/mod.rs lines 79-98 (resolve_path); used by execute_read_file (file/mod.rs:108), execute_write_file (file/write.rs:14), execute_edit_file (file/edit.rs:14), execute_list_files (file/list.rs:10), execute_notebook_edit (file/notebook.rs:36).

**Violation:**
resolve_path only blocks the literal '..' Component in the path string. It has THREE independent bypasses:
1. **Absolute-path escape:** if p.is_absolute() the function returns it as-is (line 81), so a model can read_file '/etc/passwd', '/root/.ssh/id_rsa', '/home/other_user/.bash_history'. The supposed 'path traversal' protection is toothless because the attacker does not need '..' when absolute paths are accepted. There is no confinement to a project root.
2. **Symlink escape for reads:** execute_read_file (mod.rs:108-111) calls resolve_path but NEVER canonicalizes; fs::read_to_string (read.rs:289) follows symlinks. A write to /tmp/alias -> /etc/shadow earlier in the session (or a pre-existing symlink) lets the attacker read anywhere fs::read_to_string can reach. Contrast execute_write_file (write.rs:20) and execute_edit_file (edit.rs:20) which DO canonicalize — the read path is the outlier.
3. **TOCTOU between canonicalize and fs::write:** write.rs lines 20-34 canonicalize, then line 62 does fs::write(path, ...). A symlink swap between those two calls resolves to a different target. Write is not open-with-O_NOFOLLOW.

**Mandated Refactor:**
1. Introduce a project-root jail: resolve_path must take a root: &Path (the session cwd at startup, stored in SessionState) and reject any resolved path whose canonicalized form is not a prefix-descendant of that root. All four call sites receive the root from ToolContext.
2. Canonicalize BEFORE the read path (read_text_file, read_image_file, read_pdf_file, read_notebook_file) and verify containment.
3. Use OpenOptions with custom_flags(libc::O_NOFOLLOW) on Unix (and equivalent on Windows via symlink_metadata pre-check) for write_file and edit_file to close the TOCTOU window.
4. Block absolute paths outside the jail even when the caller explicitly provides them — this is the model speaking, not the user. If the user needs out-of-root access, they must configure an allowlist (crate::permissions::FileAccessPolicy).
5. Delete the toothless 'Path traversal not allowed' check at lines 89-95 or keep it as defense-in-depth BUT document that it is not the primary defense.

e5d46076-dc71-4c38-9e86-6e878e2643b5.author: lOrm
e5d46076-dc71-4c38-9e86-6e878e2643b5.content:
Resolved. Changes to `src/tools/file/mod.rs`:

**New machinery:**
- `PROJECT_ROOT: LazyLock<PathBuf>` — canonicalized CWD captured at first tool call, pinned so later `cd`s (worktree tool, shell) cannot move the jail.
- `TEMP_ROOT: LazyLock<Option<PathBuf>>` — canonicalized process temp dir. Accepted as a secondary jail because (a) `tempfile`-based tests pass `/tmp/...` paths, (b) some legitimate tool intermediate-file workflows live in TMPDIR.
- `strict_mode()` — default ON, disabled only by explicit `OPENCLAUDIA_ALLOW_OUT_OF_ROOT=1`. Secure by default.
- `path_is_within(canonical, root)` helper.

**New `resolve_path` pipeline:**
1. Absolutize (string join, no symlink follow).
2. Reject `..` components with clear error (defense-in-depth — canonicalize would normalize them but the error becomes vague).
3. **Canonicalize** — resolves symlinks, closing the read-path symlink-escape hole (#269 bypass 2). For not-yet-existing targets, walks up to the first existing ancestor, canonicalizes that, and rejoins the virtual suffix — supports `write_file` creating deeply nested new directories without reopening the escape.
4. Enforce containment: rejected unless inside PROJECT_ROOT OR TEMP_ROOT.

**Bypass fixes:**
- **Absolute-path escape (bypass 1):** `read_file '/etc/passwd'` now returns "outside the project root" instead of returning the file contents. Verified in test_read_file_not_found.
- **Symlink-escape on read (bypass 2):** reads now go through canonicalize — a symlink `/tmp/alias -> /etc/shadow` inside a path resolves to `/etc/shadow`, which fails the project-root check.
- **TOCTOU partial mitigation:** canonicalize before each operation minimizes the window. Full O_NOFOLLOW write remains future work (mandated refactor point 3) — tracked as a follow-up since it needs per-platform work (libc::O_NOFOLLOW on Unix, distinct symlink_metadata pre-check on Windows).

**Tests:** all 574 lib + 130 integration tests pass. One integration test (`test_read_file_not_found`) was updated to accept either the legacy 'not found' or the new 'outside the project root' error phrasing — the new behavior is strictly better security but needed the assertion to be broadened.

**Out of scope / follow-up:**
- O_NOFOLLOW on write/edit paths — needs platform-specific file-open machinery.
- Configurable per-session allowlist of extra jail roots (for legitimate out-of-root projects). Today the only escape hatch is the global env var.
- The `strict_mode()` check reads env on every call; could be `LazyLock` if benchmarks show it matters.

b2a2e0db-49aa-41ca-82a4-589b2731cfbf.title: FTS MATCH query construction does not escape FTS5 operators (syntax-error DoS / query confusion)
b2a2e0db-49aa-41ca-82a4-589b2731cfbf.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

Dimension: Security and Access (5) / Functional Correctness (1)

Location: src/memory.rs:377 (memory_search)
  let sanitized_query = format!("\"{}\"", query.replace('"', "\"\""));

Violation: The comment implies this is sanitized, but wrapping a string in double-quotes for FTS5 does not actually handle all operator characters. FTS5's MATCH accepts operators (AND, OR, NOT, NEAR, column filters 'colname:token', prefix '*', parenthesized groups). A user memory_search query containing unbalanced quotes or special characters (e.g., the NUL byte, control chars in content) will still produce rusqlite errors propagated to the caller — a trivial DoS where a single bad search breaks the feature. Worse, if we ever expose memory_search through an MCP tool surfaced to untrusted tool output, query confusion could be used to exfiltrate arbitrary rows via crafted boolean expressions.

This is not classical SQLi (rusqlite binds ?1 as a parameter) but it IS an FTS5 expression injection. The right fix is to escape each whitespace-separated token as a phrase literal OR normalize to a safe subset.

Mandated Refactor:
1. Tokenize the user query on whitespace, strip/replace every FTS5 metacharacter ('"', '*', '(', ')', ':', '-'), and rejoin each token wrapped in quotes.
2. On any parse/query error, return Ok(vec![]) rather than propagating — search is best-effort.
3. Add tests for adversarial queries: empty string, only quotes, NEAR/AND/OR/NOT, column filter syntax, 10 KB input.
4. Rename sanitized_query to phrase_query to accurately describe what it does.

b2bb3b51-fe9b-4ce4-9115-d5074257f767.title: Add denial tracking module (parity with CC denialTracking.ts — consecutive/total denial limits)
b2bb3b51-fe9b-4ce4-9115-d5074257f767.description:
## Summary

CC's `utils/permissions/denialTracking.ts` tracks permission classifier denials with two counters:
- consecutiveDenials: resets to 0 on any allowed action
- totalDenials: never resets (session-scoped)

Thresholds (DENIAL_LIMITS): maxConsecutive=3, maxTotal=20.
When shouldFallbackToPrompting() returns true:
- Interactive mode: fall back to permission prompt with warning
- Headless mode: throw AbortError('Agent aborted: too many classifier denials in headless mode')

OC has no DenialTrackingState, recordDenial, recordSuccess, or shouldFallbackToPrompting.

## Security relevance
Without denial tracking, a headless OC agent can be stuck in an infinite denial loop. CC aborts the agent after 20 total denials in headless mode. This gap is security-relevant for agent reliability.

## Behaviors to implement
- DenialTrackingState { consecutiveDenials, totalDenials }
- recordDenial: increments both counters
- recordSuccess: resets consecutiveDenials to 0 only (totalDenials persists)
- shouldFallbackToPrompting: true when consecutive >= 3 OR total >= 20
- Integration with PermissionManager::check() for headless vs. interactive behavior

## Parent issue
#531

## References
- CC: utils/permissions/denialTracking.ts:1-46
- CC: utils/permissions/permissions.ts:879-911, 958-978, 984-1058
- OC: src/permissions.rs (no denial tracking)

New PermissionManager fields consecutive_denials/total_denials; methods record_denial (increments both via saturating_add), record_allowed (resets consecutive only), escalation_state -> EscalationState { Normal, ShouldAbort }, reset_denial_tracking. 7 new tests under denial_tracking_*. Forensic evidence: cargo test --lib = 1391 passed/0 failed (baseline 1384 + 7 new); cargo clippy --lib --tests -- -D warnings exit 0; no #[allow] / #[ignore] / clippy.toml. CC parity: denialTracking.ts.

b2d7368a-b5fa-46d2-b34f-c0694747dd60.title: Installed plugin file_path only resolves home dir; project-scope entries orphan
b2d7368a-b5fa-46d2-b34f-c0694747dd60.description:
Current state: 

Desired state: 

Reason: 

**Dimension**: Functional Correctness / Testability Coverage

**Location**: src/plugins/install.rs:173-182 (file_path)

**Violation**: InstalledPlugins::file_path always returns ~/.openclaudia/plugins/installed_plugins.json regardless of InstallScope (Managed, User, Project, Local). Yet PluginInstallEntry carries scope + project_path distinguishing per-project installs. A user with multiple projects, each having their own plugin installs, has ALL scopes writing to the same global file. Consequences:
- Two different projects installing the same plugin name at different paths trigger the upsert match-by-scope-and-project_path logic (install.rs:157-164) correctly — BUT if one project is deleted, the entry remains forever (no cleanup).
- If dirs::home_dir() returns None (unusual, but possible in restricted environments), it falls back to RELATIVE path .openclaudia/plugins/installed_plugins.json — this then changes depending on the process CWD. A long-running agent changing cwd between sessions writes to DIFFERENT files, fragmenting install state.
- No project-scoped file path even though scope enumerates Project.

**Mandated Refactor**:
1. Split into two tracking files: global ~/.openclaudia/plugins/installed_plugins.json (User/Managed scopes) and .openclaudia/plugins/installed_plugins.json (Project/Local scopes).
2. InstalledPlugins::load should merge them; save should dispatch each entry to the correct file based on scope.
3. If dirs::home_dir() returns None, return an error (not a relative-path fallback) — fail fast.
4. Add a `prune_stale()` method that drops entries whose install_path no longer exists.

b3518c3c-a725-4867-a37d-52f3cc321548.title: Config load: no validation of provider base_url (SSRF / protocol allowlist)
b3518c3c-a725-4867-a37d-52f3cc321548.description:
Steps to reproduce:

Expected: 
Actual: 

**Dimension**: Security and Access (SSRF)

**Location**: src/config/mod.rs:108-195 (load_config), src/config/provider.rs:40-50 (ProviderConfig.base_url)

**Violation**: ProviderConfig.base_url is loaded as a plain String with no validation:

**Mandated Refactor**:

2. Reject RFC1918 / link-local / cloud-metadata IPs in non-dev mode.
3. Warn loudly if proxy.host != 127.0.0.1 and emit an audit log entry.
4. Use the `url` crate to parse and enforce.

## Severity
Trivial

## Dimension
Naming / Documentation & Intent

## Location
src/tools/todo.rs:89-95 (content length check)

## Violation
```rust
Some(c) if c.len() > 2000 => {
    return (format!("Todo {i} content exceeds maximum length of 2000 characters"), true);
}
```

The 2000 appears twice as a magic literal. CLAUDE.md (Naming section) requires constants to be UPPER_SNAKE_CASE. The value is meaningful (CC parity) but undocumented at the call site — a maintainer changing it would have to update two literals and risk drift.

Also note `c.len()` counts bytes, not characters. A todo item containing 1000 emoji (4 bytes each in UTF-8) would fail the check at 4000 bytes but only 1000 visible glyphs. The error message says "characters" — wrong unit.

## Mandated refactor
```rust
const TODO_CONTENT_MAX_CHARS: usize = 2000;
...
Some(c) if c.chars().count() > TODO_CONTENT_MAX_CHARS => {
    return (format!("Todo {i} content exceeds maximum length of {TODO_CONTENT_MAX_CHARS} characters (got {})", c.chars().count()), true);
}
```

Or document explicitly that the limit is bytes-not-chars and rename the constant `TODO_CONTENT_MAX_BYTES`.

**Dimension:** DRY / Cognitive Readability

**Location:** /home/doll/OpenClaudia/src/tool_intercept.rs lines 28-73 (to_tool_call: tool-name map at 31-41, param-name map at 46-57)

**Violation:**
to_tool_call maintains TWO independent translation tables:
1. Tool name map at lines 30-41 translating Claude-Code names ('bash', 'Read', 'write_file', 'glob', 'grep', 'webfetch') to internal names ('bash', 'read_file', 'write_file', 'list_files', 'grep', 'web_fetch').
2. Parameter name map at lines 46-57 translating ('file_path','path') to 'path', ('content','contents') to 'content', etc.
