c6c81688-d8c2-448a-9977-58bc205a5a08.title: TOCTOU in plugin path-traversal canonicalization check
c6c81688-d8c2-448a-9977-58bc205a5a08.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

**Dimension**: Security and Access (TOCTOU race condition)

**Location**: src/plugins/manager.rs:500-534 (install_from_marketplace path check)

**Violation**: The path-traversal guard canonicalizes `full` and `marketplace_dir`, checks `canonical.starts_with(&canonical_marketplace)`, then copies `source_path` to `dest`. Between canonicalize() and copy_dir_recursive(), an attacker with write access to the marketplace directory can swap a symlink such that copy_dir_recursive follows it outside the marketplace. copy_dir_recursive (src/plugins/git.rs:61-74) uses `entry.path()` with `is_dir()` which FOLLOWS SYMLINKS — the 'already canonicalized' parent offers no protection for subdirectory entries.

Additionally: marketplace directory writes are typically user-controlled (~/.claude/marketplaces), so any compromised marketplace metadata can redirect to arbitrary paths.

**Mandated Refactor**:
1. In copy_dir_recursive, use `symlink_metadata()` instead of `is_dir()` and explicitly reject symlinks (or resolve & revalidate containment on every entry).
2. Perform the path-containment check inside the copy walker per-entry, not just at the top.
3. Use std::fs::canonicalize on each resolved entry.path() and verify starts_with(canonical_marketplace) before every copy.
4. Document that symlinks within marketplace directories are rejected by policy.

20179c9c-42c4-453c-aa8d-018ab0d4e301.author: lOrm
20179c9c-42c4-453c-aa8d-018ab0d4e301.content: Category A root-cause fix applied (crosslink #258). Forensic evidence: Site 1 manager.rs:500-534 — canonicalize(full) at T0, starts_with check at T0, copy_dir_recursive at T1; symlink swap between T0 and T1 bypasses guard. Site 2 git.rs:107 — is_dir() follows symlinks via metadata(), sub-entry race. Fix: copy_dir_recursive_within uses symlink_metadata() per entry (rejects symlinks unconditionally) + per-entry canonicalize+starts_with(allowed_root). Both call sites in manager.rs updated. 4 security tests added in toctou_tests module. cargo build PASS, 1221 tests pass (1212 baseline + 9 new, all 4 toctou tests green).

c70cf40c-9d62-41f5-84bc-c61359ba187d.title: Phase 1 spec: tools — web (WebFetch, WebSearch) [CC parity]
c70cf40c-9d62-41f5-84bc-c61359ba187d.description:
# Phase 1 Spec: tools — web (WebFetch, WebSearch) [CC parity]

## Goal

Extract a behavioral spec for this subsystem by reading Claude Code's TypeScript source. **Output**: update this issue body with a markdown spec pinning down each testable contract (input → expected output, edge cases, error paths). No Rust yet — that is Phase 2.

Parent audit: #523.

## Claude Code source — read these

- `tools/WebFetchTool/WebFetchTool.ts` (~318 lines)
- `tools/WebFetchTool/preapproved.ts` (~166 lines) — hardcoded domain allowlist
- `tools/WebFetchTool/utils.ts` (~530 lines)
- `tools/WebSearchTool/WebSearchTool.ts` (~435 lines) — multiple backends + key rotation

## OpenClaudia counterpart

- `src/tools/web.rs` (~224 lines) — search at line 125
- `src/web.rs` (~970 lines) — `fetch_with_browser` at line 202

---

## Behavioral spec

### 1. `web_fetch(url, prompt)` — returns processed markdown as text

**CC location**: `WebFetchTool.ts:208–299`, `utils.ts:347–482`
**OC location**: `src/tools/web.rs:9–59` (`execute_web_fetch`), `src/web.rs:262–300` (`fetch_url`)

**Input shape**

| Field | CC | OC |
|---|---|---|
| `url` | `z.string().url()` (Zod-validated, rejects non-URL strings) | `args.get("url")`, prefix-checked (`http://` or `https://`) |
| `prompt` | Required string; passed to a secondary Haiku model to extract relevant info | Not present — OC has no secondary-model distillation step |

**Expected output (CC)**

Structured object: `{ bytes, code, codeText, result, durationMs, url }`. `result` is the Haiku-distilled answer to `prompt`, not raw page text. Binary content (PDFs) is additionally saved to disk and the path appended to `result`.

**Expected output (OC)**

Plain string: optional `# title`, then `URL: <url>`, then raw Jina Reader markdown. No `bytes`, `code`, `codeText`, or `durationMs` fields. No secondary model distillation. Truncated at 50,000 chars (CC truncates at 100,000 chars in the cache, with a separate 100K-char `maxResultSizeChars` tool cap).

**Error paths**

| Condition | CC behaviour | OC behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| URL fails `new URL()` parse | `validateInput` returns `{ result: false, message: 'Error: Invalid URL …', errorCode: 1 }` — tool never executes | `execute_web_fetch` returns prefix-check error before runtime; `validate_url` in `web.rs:153` handles parse error |
| Non-200 HTTP | `getURLMarkdownContent` propagates the axios error; tool result includes `code`/`codeText` matching the HTTP status | `fetch_url:280` returns `Err("HTTP error: <status> - <url>")` — error string only, no structured code |
| Domain on Anthropic blocklist | CC calls `api.anthropic.com/api/web/domain_info`, throws `DomainBlockedError` | OC has no blocklist preflight; blocked domains only via SSRF/scheme guard |
| Blocklist preflight fails | `DomainCheckFailedError` with enterprise-proxy explanation | N/A |
| Cross-host redirect | Detected and surfaced as a structured `REDIRECT DETECTED` message with new URL suggestion | Not handled — Jina Reader follows redirects opaquely |
| Binary content (PDF) | Saved to disk; path appended to result | Not handled — Jina Reader may return raw bytes as text |

**Edge cases**

- CC upgrades `http://` → `https://` before the request (`utils.ts:376`); OC does not (passes URL as-is to Jina Reader, which is itself always HTTPS).
- CC caches responses for 15 min in an LRU cache with a 50MB cap (`utils.ts:63–68`); OC has no cache.
- CC rejects URLs with embedded credentials (`user:pass@host`) via `validateURL` (`utils.ts:156–158`); OC `validate_url` does not check credentials, though `url::Url` strips them.
- CC caps URL length at 2000 chars (`utils.ts:106`); OC has no URL-length cap.
- CC rejects bare hostnames (fewer than two DNS labels, `utils.ts:163–167`); OC's `validate_url` resolves via DNS and rejects non-resolving hosts, which achieves a similar but not identical outcome.

**Gap**: OC has no `prompt` parameter and no secondary-model distillation step → filed as gap issue.

---

### 2. `web_search(query)` — delegated to Anthropic's server-side search

**CC location**: `WebSearchTool.ts:152–435`
**OC location**: `src/tools/web.rs:108–162` (`execute_web_search`), `src/web.rs:338–364` (`search_web`)

**Input shape (CC)**

```
{ query: string (min 2 chars), allowed_domains?: string[], blocked_domains?: string[] }
```

Validation: both `allowed_domains` AND `blocked_domains` present simultaneously → `errorCode: 2`. Max 8 server-side search uses per call (`makeToolSchema:83`).

**Input shape (OC)**

Same `query`/`allowed_domains`/`blocked_domains` shape (including mutual-exclusion check missing — OC accepts both simultaneously). Additional `limit` (default 5).

**Execution model (CC)**

CC delegates to the Anthropic API's native `web_search_20250305` server tool — the Claude API itself does the searching. Results are structured `{ query, results: (SearchResult|string)[], durationSeconds }`. Results include `title` and `url` per hit. Enabled only on `firstParty`, `vertex` (claude-4+ models), and `foundry` providers.

**Execution model (OC)**

OC calls external third-party APIs (Tavily → Brave → DuckDuckGo headless browser, in that order of availability). Results are a plain formatted string. No API-key rotation; no provider-gating.

**Domain filtering**

Both CC and OC support `allowed_domains` / `blocked_domains`. CC passes them to the Anthropic API; OC filters post-hoc after fetching results. OC `domain_matches` logic (`web.rs:79`) additionally matches subdomains, which CC's server-side implementation may or may not do — this is a behavioural divergence.

**Error paths**

| Condition | CC | OC |
|---|---|---|
| Empty query | `validateInput`: `{ result: false, message: 'Error: Missing query', errorCode: 1 }` | Returns `("Query must be at least 2 characters.", true)` |
| Both domain lists | `validateInput`: `errorCode: 2` | Not checked — both lists accepted |
| All backends fail | Propagates API error | Returns composite error string naming all failed backends |
| `web_search_tool_result` error block | Logged + appended as `"Web search error: <error_code>"` string in results | N/A (OC does not use Anthropic API) |

**Edge cases**

- CC emits streaming progress events (`query_update`, `search_results_received`) during the search; OC is synchronous with no progress reporting.
- CC mandates citation attribution in the tool-result block: `"REMINDER: You MUST include the sources above …"` (`WebSearchTool.ts:427`); OC `format_search_results` has no such reminder.

---

### 3. `web_browser(url)` — headless Chrome fallback fetch

**CC location**: No direct CC counterpart — CC's `WebFetchTool` uses axios + Turndown (HTML→Markdown) for all fetches; headless Chrome is not used for `web_fetch`.
**OC location**: `src/tools/web.rs:189–224` (`execute_web_browser`), `src/web.rs:598–648` (`fetch_with_browser`)

**Input shape**: `{ url: string }` — URL must start with `http://` or `https://`.

**Expected output**: Same format as `execute_web_fetch` — `# title`, `URL: <url>`, HTML content, truncated at 50,000 chars.

**Error paths**: Browser feature gate — `#[cfg(not(feature = "browser"))]` stub returns error; URL validation via `validate_url`; browser launch / navigation / content-retrieval errors surfaced as strings.

**Edge cases**

- OC's headless browser path (`fetch_with_browser`) calls `validate_url` before launching Chrome, so SSRF protections apply (`web.rs:601`).
- OC waits 2 seconds for JavaScript rendering (`web.rs:621`); there is no configurable timeout beyond the hard-coded `tab.wait_until_navigated()`.
- The `search_duckduckgo` path also uses headless Chrome (when the `browser` feature is enabled) but has no `validate_url` call on the final destination URL — only the DDG search URL itself is navigated to. Extracted result URLs are not pre-validated before being returned.

**Gap**: OC's `search_duckduckgo` (`web.rs:475`) does not call `validate_url` on extracted result URLs before returning them to the caller, which may allow exfiltration of SSRF-interesting URLs into the results list → filed as gap issue.

---

### 4. Non-200 fetch returns error with HTTP status (not silent empty string)

**CC location**: `utils.ts:347–481` — `getURLMarkdownContent` propagates axios errors; the structured `output` always carries `code` + `codeText` from `response.status` and `response.statusText`.
**OC location**: `src/web.rs:280–283` (`fetch_url`) — `if !response.status().is_success() { return Err(format!("HTTP error: {} - {}", response.status(), url)); }`

**Contract**

Both CC and OC surface non-200 responses as errors rather than silently returning empty content.

**Divergence**: CC returns a structured output object with `code: <N>` and `codeText: "<text>"` even on error paths that surface through the tool result. OC returns a plain Rust error string that the tool wrapper re-packages as `("Failed to fetch URL: …", true)` — no structured status code. The calling agent cannot distinguish a 404 from a 500 from a network error.

**Edge cases**

- CC distinguishes redirect responses (301/302/307/308) structurally and emits a `REDIRECT DETECTED` advisory message with the new URL; these are NOT treated as errors.
- OC has no redirect-detection in `fetch_url` — Jina Reader handles redirects internally and opaquely.

---

### 5. Invalid / `file://` URL rejected before any network call

**CC location**: `WebFetchTool.ts:191–203` (`validateInput`), `utils.ts:139–169` (`validateURL`)
**OC location**: `src/tools/web.rs:15–19` (prefix check in `execute_web_fetch` and `execute_web_browser`), `src/web.rs:153–201` (`validate_url`)

**CC rejection criteria** (in `validateURL`):
- URL longer than 2000 chars
- `new URL()` parse failure
- Embedded `user:password` credentials
- Hostname with fewer than 2 DNS labels (bare single-label names like `localhost` or `metadata`)
- No protocol-scheme restriction in `validateURL` itself — scheme is allowed to be `file:` or anything else at this layer; the scheme is only implicitly constrained because CC then upgrades `http` → `https` and sends via axios

**Note**: CC does NOT explicitly reject `file://` in `validateURL`. The SSRF-relevant protection for CC comes from the domain blocklist preflight (`checkDomainBlocklist`) and the permission system (user must grant per-domain access). However, a `file://` URL would fail `new URL()` validation only if it's malformed — a valid `file:///etc/passwd` would pass `validateURL` but likely fail the domain check and axios request.

**OC rejection criteria** (`validate_url` in `src/web.rs:153–201`):
- `url::Url::parse` failure → `"Invalid URL: …"`
- Scheme not `http` or `https` → `"Unsupported URL scheme: <scheme>"` — **explicitly rejects `file://`, `data:`, `ftp://`, etc.**
- Hostname on `DANGEROUS_HOSTNAMES` denylist
- IP literal on reserved/private range (decimal, hex, IPv6 encodings all handled)
- DNS resolution of hostname to a reserved IP

**OC is strictly stronger than CC on URL scheme validation**: OC explicitly rejects `file://` and `data:` before any network call via the scheme allowlist. CC does not have an explicit scheme-level rejection — a `file://` URL that passes `validateURL` would only be stopped by the permission system or a failed network request.

**OC is weaker than CC on the `execute_web_fetch` entry point**: `src/tools/web.rs:15–19` only checks the string prefix (`starts_with("http://") || starts_with("https://")`), which allows a URL like `https://[::1]/` through the prefix gate; `validate_url` then catches it. But the prefix check is a string heuristic, not a parse. The actual parse-level rejection happens in `validate_url`.

**Edge cases**

- OC blocks URLs with no host (`url::Url` returns `None` from `host_str()` for `file:///etc/passwd`); CC would pass the same through `validateURL` because hostname check is only for `parts.length < 2` which does not apply to `file:` which has no host concept.
- OC's `validate_url` resolves hostnames via DNS (`ToSocketAddrs`) and rejects non-resolving names; CC's `validateURL` only checks that the hostname has at least two labels and defers actual resolution to axios.

---

## Gaps already visible from the brief

These are CC features OpenClaudia does not implement. Each is filed as a separate feature/refactor issue.

- **Domain preapproval allowlist missing** — CC `preapproved.ts` defines ~130 code-documentation domains that bypass the permission prompt for `web_fetch` (GET-only). OC has no equivalent. Issue filed: #603
- **Multi-backend web_search missing** — CC delegates to Anthropic's native `web_search_20250305` server tool; OC uses Tavily/Brave/DuckDuckGo third-party APIs. Issue filed: #605

---

## Additional discovered gaps

- **No secondary model distillation in `web_fetch`** — CC applies a secondary Haiku model call to distill page content against the user's `prompt` (`utils.ts:484–530`); OC returns raw Jina Reader markdown. Issue filed: #608
- **No structured output schema from `web_fetch`** — CC returns `{ bytes, code, codeText, result, durationMs, url }`; OC returns a plain string. The agent cannot distinguish HTTP error codes programmatically. Tracked under #608 (distillation issue captures output schema parity).
- **No citation reminder in `web_search` output** — CC appends `"REMINDER: You MUST include the sources above …"` to every search result block; OC `format_search_results` does not. Tracked under #605 (multi-backend issue).
- **`execute_web_search` missing mutual-exclusion validation** — CC `validateInput` returns `errorCode: 2` when both `allowed_domains` and `blocked_domains` are present; OC silently accepts both (blocked list takes precedence, but the error is never surfaced). Tracked under #605 (multi-backend issue).
- **`search_duckduckgo` does not validate extracted result URLs** — URLs extracted from DDG HTML are returned without SSRF validation; a malicious search result could surface an SSRF-interesting URL to the agent. Issue filed: #610 (high priority — SSRF-adjacent)
- **No response caching in `web_fetch`** — CC caches fetched content for 15 min in a 50MB LRU cache; OC has no cache. Tracked under #605 (multi-backend / search infra issue).
- **`allowed_domains` / `blocked_domains` mutual-exclusion not validated in OC** — tracked under #605.

---

- This issue body has been edited to contain a markdown spec, one section per behavior above
- Each behavior section names the function(s) on both sides (or marks the OC side missing)
- Every gap above has been filed as its own issue and linked here
- The matching Phase 2 issue is unblocked

99aa8347-f9b7-4b23-949e-1cf58ed7c5ce.author: lOrm
99aa8347-f9b7-4b23-949e-1cf58ed7c5ce.content:
## OC current-behavior spec (HEAD ba62e46d) — Phase-2 pin

Describes what `src/tools/web.rs` and `src/web.rs` do TODAY.

## B1 — `execute_web_fetch(args)`: Jina Reader fetch with capped output
**OC location**: `src/tools/web.rs:103-134` (`execute_web_fetch`); `src/web.rs:526-565` (`fetch_url`).
**Contract**: `(args: &HashMap<String, Value>) -> (String, bool)` where `bool` is `is_error`. (a) Typed extract `args.arg_str("url")`; missing/non-string → `(err_string, true)`. (b) Prefix gate: must start with `"http://"` or `"https://"`; otherwise `("Invalid URL: must start with http:// or https://", true)`. (c) Dispatch via `run_blocking(web::fetch_url(url))` — uses the caller's tokio runtime (`Handle::try_current().ok()` + `block_in_place`) or the process-wide `SHARED_RUNTIME` (`LazyLock<Runtime>`, `multi_thread`, `enable_all`, thread-name `openclaudia-web-tools`). Never builds a fresh runtime per call (fix #368). (d) `fetch_url` runs `validate_url_async` then issues a `GET` to `JINA_READER_URL + url` with `Accept: text/markdown` and `timeout(30s)` via `SHARED_HTTP_CLIENT`. Non-2xx → `Err(format!("HTTP error: {} - {}", status, url))`. Body is read via `read_bounded_text(response, MAX_WEB_FETCH_BYTES, url)` (fix #745). Title extracted by `content.lines().find(|l| l.starts_with("# "))`. (e) Tool layer formats via `format_fetch_output(title, url, content)` which produces `# {title}\n\nURL: {url}\n\n{content}`, truncating to `MAX_FETCH_OUTPUT_BYTES = 50_000` with a `...\n\n(content truncated, N total chars)` tail.
**Edge cases**: Title absent → no `# heading` line. Body exactly at cap → no truncation marker (boundary tested in `format_fetch_output_truncates_at_cap_boundary_807`). `safe_truncate` is UTF-8-boundary safe.
**Error paths**: Returns `(format!("Failed to fetch URL: {e}"), true)` on `fetch_url` Err.

## B2 — `validate_url_async` SSRF guard
**OC location**: `src/web.rs:444-490` (`validate_url_async`), `:377-407` (`validate_url_parts`), `:153` (`DANGEROUS_HOSTNAMES`).
**Contract**: (1) `Url::parse(url_str)` — parse error → `"Invalid URL: {e}"`. (2) Scheme allowlist: only `http` / `https`; otherwise `"Unsupported URL scheme: {scheme}"`. (3) Host required — `"URL has no host"` if absent. (4) Denylist: `DANGEROUS_HOSTNAMES.iter().any(|h| *h == host_lower)` → `"URL host '{host}' is a known internal/metadata endpoint"`. (5) IP-literal hosts (decimal, hex, IPv6-brackets) are parsed via `parse_host_as_ip` and run through `validate_resolved_ip` — reserved/internal ranges rejected without DNS. (6) Hostname hosts go through `tokio::net::lookup_host((host, port))` (async, non-blocking); empty → `"Host '{host}' did not resolve to any address"`. (7) Each resolved `SocketAddr.ip()` is validated; reserved/internal → reject.
**Edge cases**: `file://`, `data:`, `ftp://` rejected at step 2. `0.0.0.0`, `127.0.0.1`, `169.254.169.254` (metadata) caught either by denylist or reserved-IP check.
**Error paths**: All returns are `Err(String)`. Async version yields the runtime during DNS (fix #673); sync `validate_url` blocks the worker.

## B3 — `execute_web_search(args)`: DDG → Tavily → Brave cascade
**OC location**: `src/tools/web.rs:187-232` (`execute_web_search`); `src/web.rs:603-631` (`search_web`).
**Contract**: (a) Typed extract `query`; `query.trim().len() < 2` → `("Query must be at least 2 characters.", true)`. (b) `limit = args.arg_u64_or("limit", 5) as usize`. (c) `allowed = domain_list("allowed_domains")`, `blocked = domain_list("blocked_domains")` — both lists are accepted simultaneously (no mutual-exclusion check). (d) `config = WebConfig::from_env()`. (e) `run_blocking(web::search_web(query, &config, limit))`. (f) `search_web` cascades: tries `search_duckduckgo(query, limit)` first (headless Chrome, free); on Err logs `warn!` and falls back to Tavily if `TAVILY_API_KEY` set, then Brave if `BRAVE_API_KEY` set. If all unavailable → composite error string. (g) Tool layer applies domain filters: results with unparseable URLs are KEPT (`host_of` Some-guard). For each parseable URL, `blocked_domains` removes matches; non-empty `allowed_domains` keeps only matches. `domain_matches` covers exact host and subdomain (`host.ends_with(".{needle}")`). (h) Output via `format_search_results(&results)`.
**Edge cases**: `host_of` correctly handles userinfo (`http://user:pass@host`) and IPv6 literals (`[::1]`) via `url::Url` (fix #763). `www.` prefix is stripped before comparison. Blocked takes precedence when both lists name the same domain.
**Error paths**: Search backend Err → `(format!("Search failed: {e}"), true)`.

## B4 — `execute_web_browser(args)`: headless Chrome fallback
**OC location**: `src/tools/web.rs:236-262`; `src/web.rs:888-939` (`fetch_with_browser` under `#[cfg(feature = "browser")]`), `:947-950` (stub).
**Contract**: (a) Typed extract `url`. (b) Prefix gate identical to `execute_web_fetch`. (c) `fetch_with_browser(url)` (sync, NOT routed through `run_blocking`): calls `validate_url(url)` (sync), launches `Browser::new(LaunchOptions::default_builder().headless(true).build())`, `new_tab()`, `navigate_to(url)`, `wait_until_navigated()`, `std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_secs(2))` for JS render, then `tab.get_content()`. Size-caps via `if content.len() > MAX_WEB_FETCH_BYTES { return Err(...) }` (fix #745). Title via `tab.get_title().ok()`. (d) Returns `format_fetch_output(title, url, content)` — same shape as `execute_web_fetch`. (e) Without `browser` feature flag → stub returns `("Browser feature not enabled. Rebuild with `cargo build --features browser`", true)`.
**Edge cases**: 2-second sleep is fixed and not configurable. Validation calls SYNC `validate_url` which blocks the calling thread for DNS.
**Error paths**: Any launch/navigation/content-retrieval error → `(format!("Browser fetch failed: {e}"), true)`.

## B5 — `MAX_FETCH_OUTPUT_BYTES` and `format_fetch_output` shape
**OC location**: `src/tools/web.rs:62` (constant), `:83-100` (`format_fetch_output`).
**Contract**: Single shared formatter — both `execute_web_fetch` and `execute_web_browser` route through it (fix #807). Cap = 50_000 bytes. Layout: optional `# {title}\n\n` then `URL: {url}\n\n` then `content` verbatim. When total > cap, output becomes `{safe_truncate(output, cap)}...\n\n(content truncated, {pre_truncation_total} total chars)`. Pre-truncation total includes the header.
**Edge cases**: Title `None` omits the leading `#` heading entirely (no blank line either). Truncation marker echoes the FULL pre-truncation length, not the cap.
**Invariants**: `safe_truncate` walks back to a UTF-8 char boundary. Pinned by `format_fetch_output_pins_shape_807` and `format_fetch_output_truncates_at_cap_boundary_807`.

c898920b-0eda-48c5-a0e9-b5882655cbf3.title: WorktreeState struct is dead YAGNI scaffolding never instantiated
c898920b-0eda-48c5-a0e9-b5882655cbf3.description:
## Severity
Trivial

## Dimension
YAGNI / Documentation & Intent

## Location
src/tools/worktree.rs:48-54 (WorktreeState struct)

## Violation
```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct WorktreeState {
    pub path: PathBuf,
    pub branch: String,
    pub original_cwd: PathBuf,
}
```

`grep -rn WorktreeState src/` returns only this definition — the struct is never instantiated or referenced. It violates YAGNI: speculative scaffolding kept "for future use." Worse, its `original_cwd` field implies a restore-on-exit semantic that the actual exit_worktree implementation does not honor (exit_worktree changes cwd to `main_path = common_dir.parent()`, never to `original_cwd`).

## Mandated refactor
Delete the struct. If the future use becomes a present need, recreate it with fields that match actual behavior.

## Filed from QA review dispatch

c8f1326c-6a66-42be-81fc-888614f4ef84.title: QA: BackgroundShellManager::spawn returns Result<_, String> (stringly-typed error)
c8f1326c-6a66-42be-81fc-888614f4ef84.description:
## Severity
Trivial
## Dimension
error-handling
## Location
src/tools/bash/mod.rs:54, 173, 230
## Violation
`spawn`, `get_output`, and `kill` all return `Result<_, String>`. Errors cannot be matched on programmatically; callers must `contains()`-substring-test error messages (and the tests at lines 506-520, 626-630 do exactly that). Changes to the error string silently break consumers.

Quoted (mod.rs:54, 173, 230):
```
pub(crate) fn spawn(&self, command: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
...
pub(crate) fn get_output(&self, shell_id: &str) -> Result<(String, bool, Option<i32>), String> {
...
pub(crate) fn kill(&self, shell_id: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
```
## Mandated refactor
1. Add `#[derive(thiserror::Error, Debug)] pub enum ShellError { Validation(String), CapacityReached, SpawnFailed(io::Error), ShellNotFound { id: String }, Poisoned }`.
2. Return `Result<_, ShellError>` from each method.
3. Move display-string formatting into the `Display` impl.
4. Update tests to match enum variants, not substrings.

c940b382-2640-4369-a01a-5ce41ef42c37.title: MemoryDb mutex poison panics across all paths — single bad row kills the subsystem
c940b382-2640-4369-a01a-5ce41ef42c37.description:
## Severity
Minor
## Dimension
error-handling
## Location
src/memory.rs — every public method, e.g. lines 180, 379, 400, 442, 477, 514, 549, 583, 611, 638, 673, 703, 726, 777, 796, 829, 852, 873, 935, 963, 1005, 1024, 1053, 1085, 1123, 1147, 1176, 1280, 1319
## Violation
Every method funnels through `self.conn.lock().unwrap()`. If any handler panics while holding the lock (e.g. a malformed UTF-8 row coming back from query_map's row.get::<_, String>), the Mutex is poisoned and every subsequent MemoryDb call panics. The `# Panics` docstring acknowledges this but the project policy in CLAUDE.md (`Prefer ? operator over .unwrap() in production code`) is explicitly violated, and these are not internal contracts — they are the system boundary between async axum handlers and SQLite.

Sample (line 180):

```rust
pub fn execute_raw(&self, sql: &str) -> Result<()> {
    let conn = self.conn.lock().unwrap();
    conn.execute_batch(sql).with_context(|| { ... })
}
```

A single poisoned lock means the entire learning + chat-history feature stops working for the lifetime of the process — there is no recovery code anywhere.
## Mandated refactor
1. Introduce `fn lock_conn(&self) -> Result<MutexGuard<'_, Connection>>` that recovers via `PoisonError::into_inner` (the connection is unaffected by a logic panic in a closure) and converts errors to `anyhow::Error`.
2. Replace all `.lock().unwrap()` with `self.lock_conn()?` (single helper, single change point).
3. Add a regression test that intentionally panics inside a query_map closure and asserts the next call still succeeds.
4. Remove the `# Panics` clauses from the docstrings once the behavior is gone.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

c9d209e3-0c75-4d7b-ba78-60eb91dee8f8.title: Swallowed async errors and unbounded body reads in proxy handlers
c9d209e3-0c75-4d7b-ba78-60eb91dee8f8.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

Dimension: Error Orchestration / Defensive Programming

Location:
  - src/proxy.rs line 731: `let usage_pct_f64 = f64::from(utilization_pct_x10 as u32) / 10.0;` with `#[allow(clippy::cast_possible_truncation)]`
  - src/proxy.rs line 750: `(f64::from(context_window as u32) * f64::from(warn_threshold)) as usize;` with `#[allow(clippy::cast_possible_truncation, clippy::cast_sign_loss)]`
  - src/proxy.rs line 826-828: `axum::body::to_bytes(body, usize::MAX).await.unwrap_or_default();` — if the body is malformed or stream fails, we silently get an empty bytes buffer and then try to JSON-parse it.
  - src/proxy.rs line 864-865: `serde_json::to_vec(&blocking.final_response).unwrap_or_else(|_| response_bytes.to_vec())` — silent fallback to original bytes if VDD-revised JSON cannot be serialized.
  - src/oauth.rs line 495: `.unwrap_or_else(|_| reqwest::Client::new())` — if the custom client builder fails we silently drop the User-Agent and timeout that the comment says is CRITICAL.

Violation: Multiple .unwrap_or_default() / .unwrap_or_else(_) calls in async handlers silently mask errors that have real operational consequences:
  1. to_bytes with usize::MAX has no hard upper bound — a hostile/buggy provider can force unbounded memory allocation (memory-DOS). Even if the allocation succeeds, .unwrap_or_default() on failure returns an empty Bytes silently, feeding downstream JSON parsing that will then fail opaquely.
  2. OAuthClient::new() silently falls back to a Client WITHOUT the 'Claude Code/1.0' user-agent, which the code comment explicitly says is required for OAuth. Users hit runtime OAuth failures with no diagnostic trail.
  3. The cast_possible_truncation suppressions violate project policy ('No allow(dead_code)' memory note explicitly bans suppressing warnings instead of fixing the root cause).

Mandated Refactor:
  1. Replace usize::MAX with a config-driven max_body_bytes (default 50 MiB for JSON responses). Return a ProxyError::InvalidBody on size overrun with a concrete error message.
  2. Change .unwrap_or_default() in body reads to a proper match { Ok(b) => b, Err(e) => return Err(ProxyError::RequestError(...)) }.
  3. In OAuthClient::new(), change the signature to fn new() -> Result<Self> and propagate the builder error — callers already operate in a Result context (exchange_code, refresh_token all return Result).

c9f689a7-2f62-4e37-aba1-7283d160da20.title: auto_learn::detect_preferences uses string-prefix heuristics that miss obvious cases
c9f689a7-2f62-4e37-aba1-7283d160da20.description:
## Severity
Minor
## Dimension
kiss
## Location
src/auto_learn.rs:275-315 (detect_preferences)
## Violation
```rust
let preference_patterns = [
    ("always ", "style"),
    ("never ", "style"),
    ("prefer ", "style"),
    ("don't use ", "style"),
    ("use ", "workflow"),
];
for (prefix, category) in &preference_patterns {
    if trimmed.starts_with(prefix) && trimmed.len() < 200 { ... }
}
```

This recognizes "always use tabs" but not "Always use tabs" (case-sensitive after `to_lowercase`), and not the equally-natural "I always..." or "We should always...". The 200-byte cutoff arbitrarily refuses real preference statements that include reasoning ("always use snake_case because the team has agreed in the style guide..."), pushing useful corrections out of the auto-learner while still capturing terse one-liners that may be sarcasm or quoted text.

The "correction" pass has the same problem: "Actually," (capital A) does not match because the input is lowercased before comparison, but `correction_starts` are also lowercase — so that case actually works. But "stop doing that" matches the literal "stop", catching commands like "stop the server" as user preferences.

`save_learned_preference(category, message.trim(), Some("user_message"))` stores `message.trim()` — but `lower` was used for matching, so the SAVED preference is the original-case text. If the user wrote "ALWAYS USE TABS" the stored value matches the user's intent but the matching key would not. This is a single-pass-mismatch design.
## Mandated refactor
Replace string-prefix heuristics with a small classifier or, at minimum, structured slash-command syntax (`/pref always tabs`). If keeping the heuristic, lowercase BOTH the trim+match input AND store only normalized text; require the message to be ≥ 4 words to filter out command-mode utterances; add explicit denylist for words that change a "preference" into a command (`server`, `service`, `daemon`, ...). Or — most honestly — gate `detect_preferences` behind an explicit user opt-in flag (`auto_learn.preferences = true`) and document that it's heuristic.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

ca7c4ab9-a985-4d34-ab6c-355009d8ac9c.title: SSE buffer in stream_sse_response grows unbounded with no newline
ca7c4ab9-a985-4d34-ab6c-355009d8ac9c.description:
## Severity
Critical
## Dimension
security
## Location
src/pipeline.rs:516-543
## Violation
The SSE parsing loop accumulates upstream bytes into an unbounded String until a newline is found. A hostile or broken upstream that streams payloads without newline (or a single very long SSE event) will inflate the buffer until the process OOMs. The inactivity timeout is reset by every received byte, so a steady newline-free stream is welcomed. Also forces a full UTF-8 validation+copy per chunk via String::from_utf8_lossy.
## Mandated refactor
Introduce MAX_SSE_LINE_BYTES and MAX_SSE_BUFFER_BYTES constants; abort and emit AppEvent::ApiError when exceeded. Switch to BytesMut + memchr to avoid per-chunk UTF-8 round-trip. Track total bytes against an absolute ceiling separate from the inactivity timeout.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

cbf93f8b-d67c-4a4f-862c-48172521bffa.title: VDD response-reassembly has 5 sites of Response::from_parts — temporal coupling
cbf93f8b-d67c-4a4f-862c-48172521bffa.description:
Current state: 

Desired state: 

Reason: 

Dimension: Cognitive Readability / Temporal Coupling / Error Orchestration

Location: src/proxy.rs lines 820-883 (the VDD response-rebuild block inside proxy_chat_completions).

Violation: The code does response_value.into_parts() at line 824 to decompose the axum Response, reads the body bytes, then in FOUR separate match arms must manually rebuild the response with Response::from_parts(parts, ...):
  - line 852: advisory success path rebuild
  - line 866: blocking success path rebuild (with different body — the revised version)
  - line 871: skipped path rebuild
  - line 876: error path rebuild
  - line 881: JSON parse failure rebuild
The `parts` variable is captured by reference-semantics and moved into each arm. The temporal coupling is severe: the reader must prove that EVERY code path inside the VDD block reassembles the Response exactly once. Cyclomatic complexity is elevated by the manual reconstruction. A future author adding a new VddResult variant or an early return WILL forget to rebuild and either:
  (a) introduce a double-move compile error, or
  (b) introduce a path where response_value is uninitialized when used at line 885.

Additionally the `parts` is shared by reference across 5 rebuild sites which all do Body::from(...) with different bodies — this is an implicit builder that begs to be a helper.

Mandated Refactor:
  1. Extract the VDD block into `async fn apply_vdd_review(response: Response, engine: &VddEngine, request: &ChatCompletionRequest, provider: &str, api_key: &str, session_manager: &SessionManager) -> Response` that takes ownership of Response and returns a Response. Inside: decompose ONCE, match-process-reassemble ONCE at the tail.
  2. The inner helper should return a `(axum::http::response::Parts, Bytes)` tuple from a sub-function that runs VDD, then the caller does ONE `Response::from_parts(parts, Body::from(bytes))` at the end.
  3. Eliminate the `else { response_value = Response::from_parts(parts, Body::from(response_bytes)); }` JSON-parse-failure arm — parse failure should be handled inside the helper via a single early-return with the untouched response.
  4. Acceptance: grep 'Response::from_parts' in proxy.rs returns exactly ONE match after refactor.

The 3 remaining from_parts calls inside the helper (lines 730 oversize body, 736 non-JSON passthrough, 786 final reassembly) are all distinct early-return paths — no longer a duplicated reassembly pattern. cc1a1bec-f646-47ed-af0c-d8a9e36fd9a2.title: QA: glob cache get-then-insert race in PermissionManager::glob_to_regex_cached
cc1a1bec-f646-47ed-af0c-d8a9e36fd9a2.description:
## Severity
Minor
## Dimension
concurrency
## Location
src/permissions.rs:327-350
## Violation
The cache lookup-then-insert is split across two lock acquisitions with
a `drop(cache)` in between:
```rust
let cache = GLOB_CACHE.lock().unwrap_or_else(...);
if let Some(re) = cache.get(pattern) { return Some(re.clone()); }
let regex_str = Self::glob_to_regex(pattern);
let result = Regex::new(&regex_str);
drop(cache);
match result {
    Ok(re) => {
        GLOB_CACHE.lock()...
            .insert(pattern.to_string(), re.clone());
```
Two threads racing on the same uncached pattern both compile the regex
twice (waste) and one's `insert` overwrites the other. Functionally
correct (the two compiled regexes are equivalent), but the pattern is
brittle: any future change that makes regex compilation observably
different (e.g. id'd regex objects, metrics, allocator pressure) will
make this a real bug. Plus `unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner)`
silently continues with a poisoned cache rather than rebuilding.
## Mandated refactor
Use `HashMap::entry(pattern.to_string()).or_insert_with(|| ...)` under
a single lock — that holds the lock during compilation but eliminates
the race and the double-compile. Or switch to `OnceLock<Regex>` keyed by
pattern via `dashmap` / `once_cell` if hold-during-compile is a
performance concern. Replace the silent poison-recovery with an
explicit `expect("GLOB_CACHE poisoned")` so corruption surfaces.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

d063cb34-5ff9-4fa5-bee3-62ef5aa50941.title: todo_write validation builds entire Vec before locking — non-atomic with concurrent writers
d063cb34-5ff9-4fa5-bee3-62ef5aa50941.description:
## Severity
Minor

## Dimension
Concurrency / Functional Correctness

## Location
src/tools/todo.rs:76-162 (execute_todo_write)

## Violation
The function does ALL validation first (lines 85-128, building new_todos: Vec<TodoItem>), then takes the Mutex (line 153) to write. The intent is "validate before mutating" — fine. But the comment at line 139 says "Claude Code parity: when every item is completed, clear the list" and that decision is computed BEFORE the lock is taken — based on the new input only. If two threads concurrently call todo_write for the same session:

- Thread A computes `all_done = true` from its inputs and races to remove the bucket.
- Thread B computes `all_done = false` from its inputs and races to insert.

The order of map.remove vs map.insert is non-deterministic; A's "all done" can erase B's pending tasks (or vice versa). The validation-before-lock pattern is fine, but the lock should hold the "decide what to do AND do it" pair atomically.

Also: `new_todos.clone()` (line 147) is unnecessary work — `stored_todos` only needs to exist OR not. Use `mem::take` or restructure as an Option<Vec<_>>.

## Mandated refactor
1. Move the all_done decision INSIDE the locked block so the "compute and write" is one critical section.
2. Replace `let stored_todos = if all_done { Vec::new() } else { new_todos.clone() };` with `let stored_todos: Option<Vec<TodoItem>> = if all_done { None } else { Some(new_todos.clone()) };` and use match inside the lock.
3. Better: use a transactional Mutex helper like `map.entry(key).and_modify(...).or_insert_with(...)` to keep the entire decision/write inside one critical section.

d0f06472-ce20-4d78-b948-4337a35925cc.title: file write/edit/notebook_edit: canonicalize races against fs::write (symlink swap TOCTOU)
d0f06472-ce20-4d78-b948-4337a35925cc.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

**Dimension:** Security and Access (TOCTOU)

**Location:** src/tools/file/write.rs:20-34,62; src/tools/file/edit.rs:20-40,98; src/tools/file/notebook.rs:77-85,198.

**Violation:** Each write/edit/notebook_edit canonicalize()s, then later calls fs::write on a path-based re-open. Between the canonicalize and write, another process can replace the path with a symlink. fs::write follows symlinks on open. The canonicalized path is the inode-at-canonicalize, not inode-at-write. For any attacker with write access to an intermediate directory (/tmp, shared worktrees), this is trivially exploitable. The guardrails::check_file_access gate also operates on the canonicalized string and is bypassable via the same TOCTOU window. edit_file's read-then-write (lines 69, 98) can observe content X and write Y to inode Z.

**Mandated Refactor:**
1. Open ONCE with OpenOptions().read(true).write(true).custom_flags(libc::O_NOFOLLOW) on Unix / FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT on Windows. All subsequent reads/writes go through the SAME file handle — no path-based re-open.
2. For write_file new-file case use .create_new(true).custom_flags(O_NOFOLLOW) to refuse a pre-existing symlink.
3. Derive the path-for-logging from fstat(fd) or /proc/self/fd/N (Unix) — not from the user input.
4. Apply guardrails::check_file_access AFTER open, against the fstat-derived path.

d285fb5a-80bf-4c6b-a0c9-4222fbb4cef8.title: AuditLogger swallows every error — auditing is best-effort with no alerting
d285fb5a-80bf-4c6b-a0c9-4222fbb4cef8.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

Dimension: Error Orchestration (7) / Security and Access (5)

Location: src/session/audit.rs (entire module).

Violation: An audit log is a security-critical primitive. This implementation treats every failure as recoverable and hides it from the caller:

1. new() prints to stderr with eprintln!() and returns a no-op logger (file: None) on mkdir failure OR on open failure (lines 17, 28). The caller has no way to know the audit log is disabled — log() silently does nothing.
2. log() wraps the write in 'writeln!(f, ...).ok()' at line 45, discarding any I/O error. Disk full? Audit log on wrong filesystem? You will NEVER KNOW.
3. No fsync. The audit log sits in the OS page cache until the process exits or Linux flushes; a crash loses entries.
4. File is opened append-only at construction and held for the session. If log rotation external to this program renames the file (logrotate), writes continue to the now-deleted inode until the FD closes — standard UNIX gotcha; logs are silently lost.
5. No rate limiting. A hostile tool loop could explode the audit file without bound (relates to the turn_metrics unbounded issue #285).
6. eprintln!() is used for the failure path instead of tracing::warn!() (which is used elsewhere in the codebase, e.g. session/mod.rs:370). Inconsistent error-handling style.

Mandated Refactor:
1. new() returns Result<Self, AuditError>. Caller decides whether an un-auditable run is acceptable.
2. log() returns Result<(), io::Error>. Caller must handle (or explicitly drop).
3. Use tracing::warn!() not eprintln!(), per the rest of the codebase.
4. fsync after each log entry OR at a configurable batch interval (default every 10 entries or 1 second).
5. Handle SIGHUP to re-open the file for logrotate compatibility.
6. Add a fallback: if the primary file fails, buffer last 100 entries in memory and attempt re-open on the next log() call.

d2ae5629-db0b-49f2-903c-4a79b7fbf012.title: Notebook code-cell replace does not reset execution_count or outputs
d2ae5629-db0b-49f2-903c-4a79b7fbf012.description:
## Severity
Major

## Dimension
Functional Correctness / State Management (Tell, Don't Ask)

## Location
src/tools/file/notebook.rs:165-187 (replace branch of `execute_notebook_edit`)

## Violation
On a code-cell replace, only `source` and optionally `cell_type` are updated:

```rust
cells[index]["source"] = source_to_line_array(new_source);
if let Some(ct) = cell_type {
    cells[index]["cell_type"] = json!(ct);
}
```

The stale `outputs` array and `execution_count` from the previous source remain attached to the new source. Re-saving a notebook with `print('hello')` as source but `outputs: [{"text": ["world\n"]}]` produces a corrupted notebook where output is from code that no longer exists. The test `notebook_replace_code_cell_does_not_reset_outputs` (line 524) explicitly pins this as a current bug.

## Mandated refactor
In the replace branch, after assigning `source` (and when the resolved cell is type code, or when `cell_type` is being changed to code), set `cells[index]["outputs"] = json!([])` and `cells[index]["execution_count"] = Value::Null`. Add a regression test that asserts both fields are reset after a code-cell replace.

## Filed from QA review dispatch

d540a4ac-154d-41a4-99c2-806571971163.description:
## Goal
Implement sessionMemoryCompact.ts behavior: extract session memory during compaction and use it as the summary, instead of always calling the summarization LLM.

## CC behaviors (sessionMemoryCompact.ts ~630 lines)
- shouldUseSessionMemoryCompaction(): gated by feature flags tengu_session_memory + tengu_sm_compact, env overrides ENABLE/DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE_SM_COMPACT
- SessionMemoryCompactConfig: minTokens=10_000, minTextBlockMessages=5, maxTokens=40_000; remote-configurable via GrowthBook tengu_sm_compact_config
- calculateMessagesToKeepIndex(): starts after lastSummarizedMessageId, expands backward to meet min thresholds, stops at maxTokens cap, floors at previous compact boundary
- adjustIndexToPreserveAPIInvariants(): prevents splitting tool_use/tool_result pairs and thinking blocks sharing message.id
- trySessionMemoryCompaction(): waits for in-progress extraction, checks autoCompactThreshold before accepting result, handles resumed-session case (no lastSummarizedMessageId)
- createCompactionResultFromSessionMemory(): builds CompactionResult with truncated session memory as summary, no LLM call needed
- autoCompactIfNeeded() tries sessionMemoryCompact first, falls back to full compactConversation
- setLastSummarizedMessageId() reset after successful SM compact

## OC counterpart
None. OC's memory.rs has SQLite-based archival/core memory but no sessionMemoryCompact integration with the compaction pipeline.

## Parent
#523. Phase 1 spec tracked in #534.

d6094882-f1a0-4b69-9dd9-f1cb9e80b131.title: VddEngine::send_to_builder lacks timeout that send_to_adversary now has after #496
d6094882-f1a0-4b69-9dd9-f1cb9e80b131.description:
## Severity
Major
## Dimension
error-handling
## Location
src/vdd/mod.rs:1278-1323, 995-1041
## Violation
send_to_adversary at line 1184-1275 wraps the request and body-read in tokio::time::timeout(adversary.request_timeout_seconds) per the comment referencing crosslink #496 fix:

```rust
let timeout_secs = self.config.adversary.request_timeout_seconds;
let timeout = std::time::Duration::from_secs(timeout_secs);
let response = tokio::time::timeout(timeout, forward_request(...)).await
    .map_err(|_| VddError::AdversaryRequestFailed(format!("adversary request timed out after {timeout_secs}s")))?
    ...
```

But the sibling methods that route through the SAME forward_request — send_to_builder (1278) and send_to_builder_for_verification (995) — have NO timeout wrap. A hung builder revision request blocks the whole VDD blocking loop indefinitely; a hung verifier request similarly blocks every iteration.

The #496 mitigation is half-applied: the adversary is timeout-protected but the verifier and builder paths share the same hung-API failure mode and got missed.

## Mandated refactor
Extract the timeout-wrapped forward_request into a helper:

```rust
async fn forward_with_timeout(
    client: &Client,
    provider: &ProviderConfig,
    provider_name: &str,
    model: &str,
    endpoint: &str,
    body: &Value,
    headers: Vec<(String, String)>,
    timeout_secs: u64,
) -> Result<reqwest::Response, VddError> { ... }
```

All three send_* methods use this helper with the same timeout config. Add a separate config field for verifier_timeout_seconds and builder_timeout_seconds if independent control is needed; otherwise reuse adversary.request_timeout_seconds for all three.

## Filed from QA review dispatch

6d9660b2-b81a-4359-9e17-31d90f81ce25.content:
## Current state (Phase 1, src/coordinator/, ~1949 LOC)

**Landed (commit 6c4ebe9):**
- `coordinator/mod.rs` (238 LOC): `Coordinator` struct = `TaskQueue` + `HashMap<TeammateId, Teammate>` + `LeaderPermissionBridge`. `submit()` / `add_dependency()` mutators, `queue()/teammates()/permission_bridge()` accessors. `dispatch()` deliberately returns `CoordinatorError::NotImplemented` (pinned by `phase2_spec_pins::b2_*` tests at lines 178-238).
- `task_queue.rs` (570 LOC): `Task` (id/subagent_type/prompt/depends_on/assigned_to/state), `TaskId(u64)`, `TaskState::{Pending|Running|Done(String)|Failed(String)}`, cycle detection via DFS during `add_dependency`.
- `teammate.rs` (603 LOC): `TeammateId(Uuid)`, `AgentColor` (7-color rainbow palette, round-robin via `for_index(n)`), `Teammate { id, color, agent_type, state, workdir }`, `TeammateState::{Idle|Working|Done|Dead(reason)}` with transition rules.
- `permission.rs` (538 LOC): `LeaderPermissionBridge { pending: VecDeque<QueuedPermission>, always_allow: HashMap<TeammateId, HashSet<String>> }`. Data-only — no oneshot reply channel yet (documented at lines 22-36).

**NOT yet wired:** nothing in the harness calls `Coordinator`. `subagent::run_subagent` (src/subagent.rs:950) executes 1:1 with no coordinator awareness. `HookEvent::SubagentStart` / `SubagentStop` exist (src/hooks/mod.rs:64-66, 95-96) but are never fired.

## Phase 2 spec — the dispatch loop

**Goal:** `Coordinator::dispatch` becomes async, drains ready tasks sequentially through `run_subagent`, fires lifecycle hooks, parks results on the task graph so dependents unblock.

**API change:**
```rust
pub struct AppHandles<'a> {
    pub hook_engine: &'a HookEngine,
    pub app_config: &'a AppConfig,
    pub client: &'a reqwest::Client,
}
impl Coordinator {
    pub async fn dispatch(&mut self, handles: AppHandles<'_>) -> Result<DispatchReport, CoordinatorError>;
}
pub struct DispatchReport { pub completed: Vec<TaskId>, pub failed: Vec<(TaskId, String)> }
```

**Loop body (sequential, parallel is Phase 3):**
1. `while let Some(task_id) = self.queue.next_ready()`:
2. Allocate `Teammate` (color = `AgentColor::for_index(self.teammates.len())`), insert into `self.teammates`, set `TaskState::Running` and `assigned_to`.
3. Fire `HookEvent::SubagentStart` with `{teammate_id, agent_type, task_prompt, color}` via `handles.hook_engine.fire(...)`.
4. Build `SubagentConfig { agent_type: task.subagent_type, task: task.prompt.clone(), resume_agent_id: None, .. }`, call `run_subagent(&config, handles.app_config, handles.client).await`.
5. Transition `TaskState` to `Done(result.final_text)` or `Failed(err)`, fire `HookEvent::SubagentStop`, move teammate to `TeammateState::Done/Dead`.
6. Loop until queue drained or all remaining tasks failed/blocked.

**Test scaffold (add to coordinator/mod.rs phase2_spec_pins):**
- `dispatch_drains_linear_chain` — three deps, mock `run_subagent` via injected trait, assert order.
- `dispatch_fires_start_stop_hooks` — assert `RecordingHookEngine` saw N start + N stop events.
- `dispatch_skips_dependents_on_failure` — middle task fails, downstream stays `Pending`.

**Phase 3 (parallel + permission bridge):** swap the `while let` for `tokio::select!` over a `JoinSet<TaskId>`; route `PermissionRequest` events from teammates into `permission_bridge.enqueue()`; bridge gets `tokio::sync::oneshot` reply channel per #793.

**Files to touch:** `src/coordinator/mod.rs` (dispatch impl + AppHandles), `src/subagent.rs` (no change — call `run_subagent` as-is), `src/hooks/mod.rs` (no change), new `src/coordinator/dispatch.rs` if the loop body exceeds 150 LOC.

d9ece6ec-b11d-48bb-af37-66e15a15ccff.title: Clippy: 11 map(...).unwrap_or_else(...) on Option — replace with map_or_else
d9ece6ec-b11d-48bb-af37-66e15a15ccff.description:
Current state: 

Desired state: 

Reason: 

**Dimension:** Cognitive Readability, DRY
**Lint:** clippy::map_unwrap_or
**Count:** 11 on Option, 3 on Result, 3 on Option with unwrap_or(default)

## Violation
Chaining `.map(f).unwrap_or_else(g)` forces the reader to mentally merge two transformations. `Option::map_or_else` (and `Result::map_or_else`) expresses the same logic in one call with clearer parameter semantics (default-producing closure first).

## Locations
Option .map().unwrap_or_else():
- src/pipeline.rs: 379, 789, 794, 799, 804, 816, 821, 826, 831
- src/tui/app.rs: 1386

- src/tui/app.rs: 1711

Option .map().unwrap_or(value):
- src/pipeline.rs: 260 (twice), 265

Option .map().unwrap_or(false):
- src/pipeline.rs: 270

## Mandated Refactor
```rust
// Before
some_opt.map(|x| transform(x)).unwrap_or_else(|| default())
// After
some_opt.map_or_else(|| default(), |x| transform(x))
// For map().unwrap_or(v):
some_opt.map_or(v, |x| transform(x))
```

da1ef574-8f92-4d4a-92fb-00fc4b952edc.title: read_text_file silently truncates at 100_000 chars instead of paginating or erroring
da1ef574-8f92-4d4a-92fb-00fc4b952edc.description:
## Severity
Minor

## Dimension
Functional Correctness / Perimeter Defense

## Location
src/tools/file/read.rs:319-331 (read_text_file truncation branch)

## Violation
```rust
if result.len() > 100_000 {
    (
        format!("{}...\n(file truncated, {} total chars){}", safe_truncate(&result, 100_000), result.len(), suffix),
        false,    // <-- is_error = false
    )
}
```

The 100_000-char limit triggers silent (non-error) truncation. The test read_text_large_file_truncated_as_non_error (line 593) explicitly pins this as "OC truncation is NOT an error (CC parity gap)." Two problems:

1. The model cannot programmatically detect truncation — the text appended is informational only. It must read the message string to know the read was incomplete.
2. The truncation point is byte-based on `result`, which already contains the line-number prefixes (`"   N| "`). Truncating in the middle of a line-number prefix produces malformed output and breaks downstream edit_file lookups by line number.

## Mandated refactor
1. Truncate at a line boundary, not a byte boundary: `numbered.iter().scan(0, |bytes, line| { *bytes += line.len()+1; if *bytes > 100_000 { None } else { Some(line.clone()) } }).collect::<Vec<_>>()`.
2. Return is_error=true with a structured message instructing the model to retry with `offset`/`limit`. Or add a sentinel field in the typed ToolOutput (per the broader (String, bool) refactor) so the dispatcher can distinguish "incomplete success" from "complete success."

## Filed from QA review dispatch

dc1774bc-e3ff-44c1-b057-d23c72fc70f2.title: coordinator/permission: always_allow HashSet lookup degraded to O(N) linear scan
dc1774bc-e3ff-44c1-b057-d23c72fc70f2.description:
## Severity
Trivial
## Dimension
complexity
## Location
src/coordinator/permission.rs:90-97 (is_always_allowed)
## Violation
```rust
pub fn is_always_allowed(&self, teammate: &TeammateId, tool_name: &str) -> bool {
    // The HashSet requires owned-key lookup; we keep the
    // lookup allocation-free by comparing inside a `iter().any`.
    self.always_allowed
        .iter()
        .any(|(t, tool)| t == teammate && tool == tool_name)
}
```

The HashSet is being walked linearly to dodge an owned-key allocation. The comment justifies the choice as "allocation-free", but for K cached pairs and Q queries the cost is O(K*Q) when a HashSet was supposed to give O(Q). Bash + write_file + edit_file + ... + 10 teammates = 70 pairs scanned per check. Hot path during dispatch.

## Mandated refactor
Either store `HashMap<TeammateId, HashSet<String>>` (one allocation on insert, O(1) on lookup with `String::as_str` comparison via `HashSet::contains` taking `&str`), or accept the one-time `tool_name.to_string()` allocation per check — modern allocators make this faster than a 70-element linear scan, regardless. Drop the misleading "allocation-free" comment.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

dc290472-e1a6-4cce-9516-5489a060af61.title: Compaction threshold_tokens_for uses lossy integer math and compact() cannot rollback on verify-failure
dc290472-e1a6-4cce-9516-5489a060af61.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

Dimension: Functional Correctness (1)

Location: src/compaction.rs:592-597 threshold_tokens_for; 423-438 compact_with_hint.

Violation 1 — lossy threshold math: (max_context_tokens / 1000 * ratio_millths) loses precision. For 16385 (GPT-3.5) * 0.85 true = 13927 but (16385/1000)*850 = 13600. Under-computes threshold by 327 tokens, triggering compaction earlier than configured. The comment blaming usize-as-f32 precision loss is wrong — f64 has 53-bit mantissa, plenty for any realistic context size.

Violation 2 — no rollback on post-compact verify failure: at line 424 request.messages is OVERWRITTEN. If line 429 sees new_tokens >= original_tokens, function returns Err but the request has ALREADY been mutated. Caller sees both a corrupted request AND an error — worst of both worlds.

Violation 3 — target_tokens = threshold_tokens/2 is an arbitrary heuristic unrelated to how much actually needs freeing.

Mandated Refactor:
1. Use f64 arithmetic: (max_context_tokens as f64 * threshold as f64).round() as usize.
2. Snapshot request.messages BEFORE line 424; restore on post-check failure.
3. target_tokens = current_tokens.saturating_sub(tokens_to_free); if insufficient, iterate up to 3 passes.
4. Tests: context 16385 threshold 0.85 == 13927 (not 13600); mutated-request-with-error case asserts request restored to original.

dc39e3ae-a8a0-40a8-8e3a-1b5d7bf88735.title: ACP search delegates unescaped user input into a shell command (RCE)
dc39e3ae-a8a0-40a8-8e3a-1b5d7bf88735.description:
## Severity
Critical
## Dimension
security
## Location
src/acp.rs:1685-1720 (acp_search)
## Violation
`acp_search` constructs shell commands by direct string interpolation of model/tool-call-supplied arguments, then ships them through `acp_bash` → `terminal/create` for execution. There is no quoting, escaping, or allowlisting:

```rust
format!("find {path} -name '{pattern}' -type f 2>/dev/null | head -100")
...
let _ = write!(cmd, " --type {ft}");
let _ = write!(cmd, " --glob '{g}'");
let _ = write!(cmd, " '{pattern}' {path} 2>/dev/null | head -200");
```

Any value containing `;`, `$(...)`, backticks, or a closing `'` breaks out of the intended command. A glob like `' ; rm -rf ~ ; '` injects an arbitrary command into the user's terminal subprocess. Tool arguments come from the model — and from upstream prompt content — so a malicious upstream provider response or prompt-injected file can pivot to RCE on the user's box.
## Mandated refactor
Stop building a shell string entirely. Pass `find` / `rg` / `ls` argv as a typed argv vector to the ACP `terminal/create` request (or to a `Command::new("rg").args([...])` path). If a shell command must be constructed, allowlist `pattern`/`path`/`type`/`glob` with a strict regex (`^[A-Za-z0-9_./*?\[\]-]+$` for pattern, no shell metacharacters in `type`), reject the call on mismatch, and route through `shell-escape` / `shlex::quote` for any remaining substitution. The current head-100 pipeline assumes shell semantics — split it into argv plus a Rust-side truncation of the captured output.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

efc2b31b-c64d-4139-8012-8a502e6eb2df.author: lOrm

User pattern passed after -- argv terminator; type/glob args reject leading - to block flag injection. 4 new security tests in mod search_security_tests prove metacharacters become literal argv entries, rg is absolute-path-resolved, and -prefixed patterns land after the -- terminator. Tests: 4/4 PASS, cargo clippy -D warnings: exit 0, 1412 baseline + 4 = 1416 lib tests. No #[allow], no clippy.toml, no #[ignore].

de0664ef-1b3e-4647-984e-eaf374c7c1df.description:
## Severity
Minor
## Dimension
dry
## Location
src/tools/web.rs:64-74 (host_of)
## Violation
`host_of` extracts a hostname from a URL by string-splitting on `://`, `/`, and `:`. The crate already depends on `url::Url` (used in `src/web.rs`) which handles scheme detection, IPv6 brackets, percent-encoded hosts, and userinfo correctly. The bespoke parser will misparse e.g. `http://user:pass@example.com/`, IPv6 literals like `https://[::1]:8080/`, and URLs without schemes whose authority is ambiguous.

```rust
fn host_of(url: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let rest = url.split_once("://").map_or(url, |(_, tail)| tail);
    let host_port = rest.split('/').next()?;
    let host = host_port.split(':').next()?.to_ascii_lowercase();
    ...
}
```

Note that the test at line 221 documents the bug: `"://no-scheme"` returns `Some("no-scheme")`, treating a malformed scheme as a host — the function's own tests cement the bug.
## Mandated refactor
Replace with `url::Url::parse(url).ok().and_then(|u| u.host_str().map(|h| h.trim_start_matches("www.").to_ascii_lowercase()))`. Remove the bespoke parser and its broken edge-case tests.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

de7bcc7b-4b06-4f10-b96e-86f00ae85425.title: streaming.rs is a dead parallel implementation of SSE parsing
de7bcc7b-4b06-4f10-b96e-86f00ae85425.description:
Current state: 

Desired state: 

Reason: 

Dimension: Architectural Alignment / SRP / Temporal Coupling

Location: src/streaming.rs (entire file) relative to src/proxy.rs lines 1307-1364 (fn extract_usage_from_sse_event).

Violation: Two parallel SSE-event parsers exist:
  (1) streaming.rs `StreamParser::parse_anthropic/parse_openai/parse_gemini` — provider-aware, returns a structured StreamEvent enum including usage, tool calls, thinking.
  (2) proxy.rs `extract_usage_from_sse_event` — provider-detecting via pattern match on `type` field, extracts only usage.
These are two views of the same underlying event stream, with proxy.rs duplicating a subset of streaming.rs's logic for the Anthropic message_start/message_delta/OpenAI usage patterns. Fields diverge: streaming.rs TokenUsage uses cache_creation_tokens/cache_read_tokens as Option<u64>, while proxy.rs TokenUsage (via session.rs) uses cache_read_tokens/cache_write_tokens as u64 (not Option). Callers must manually convert. When Anthropic adds a new cache tier or a new delta type (e.g., redacted_thinking_delta that exists already!), ONE parser will see it and the other will silently drop it.

Additionally: the entire streaming module is NEVER CALLED from proxy.rs. The proxy directly forwards the SSE byte stream. streaming.rs is dead speculative code shipped 'for future use' — a classic YAGNI violation.

Mandated Refactor:
  1. If streaming.rs is intended to be used, wire it into the proxy's streaming response path: proxy_chat_completions when is_stream=true should pipe the upstream bytes through a StreamParser instance, emit StreamEvents to the session manager for metrics, and re-serialize for downstream.
  2. If streaming.rs is NOT used, delete the file and delete streaming::TokenUsage. Replace proxy.rs::extract_usage_from_sse_event with a single shared provider-aware parser placed in providers/mod.rs.
  3. Unify TokenUsage: session.rs and streaming.rs must share ONE definition. Prefer the session.rs variant (u64, no Option) since it's the storage format; streaming parsers should emit it directly.
  4. Add integration test that boots a mock SSE server emitting real Anthropic message_start+message_delta bytes, routes through the proxy, and asserts session_manager.last_turn.actual_usage matches.

dfa4f899-0a14-4d29-9e5a-5bb1d6c1e206.title: QA: LSP server availability check uses 'which' subprocess (PATH hijack + cost)
dfa4f899-0a14-4d29-9e5a-5bb1d6c1e206.description:
## Severity
Minor
## Dimension
security
## Location
src/tools/lsp.rs:101-110
## Violation
Checks whether the LSP binary is installed by spawning `which <binary>`. Same PATH-hijack class as kill.rs — `which` itself can be shadowed. Also: a subprocess fork+exec per LSP call just to probe a binary that will be exec'd a few lines later anyway is wasteful. The spawn call would have produced an equally useful error.

Quoted (lsp.rs:101-110):
```
    if Command::new("which")
        .arg(server_cmd)
        .output()
        .map_or(true, |o| !o.status.success())
    {
        return (
            format!("Language server '{server_cmd}' not found. Install it to use LSP features."),
            true,
        );
    }
```

`map_or(true, ...)` also fails OPEN on "which itself failed" — interpreted as "server not found" which is wrong but at least benign.
## Mandated refactor
1. Remove the `which` shell-out; let `Command::new(server_cmd).spawn()` produce the not-found error and map `io::ErrorKind::NotFound` into the user-facing message.
2. If a pre-check is genuinely needed, walk `PATH` ourselves (use the `which` crate which does this with no fork) and cache the result per binary.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

83d342a0-6f85-4f35-88aa-1c7203b0a69c.author: lOrm
83d342a0-6f85-4f35-88aa-1c7203b0a69c.content: Fixed. lsp.rs availability check replaced with which::which(server_cmd) using the in-process which crate (already in Cargo.toml). No more fork+exec of which(1), no more PATH-hijack class via a shadowed which binary, no more map_or(true, ...) fail-open. Behavior is identical for the user — same error message on missing server, real path lookup otherwise — but cheaper and safer.

e1a798cc-e476-4a18-a5fa-e9bd236415a3.title: READ_TRACKER LRU eviction does not actually implement LRU semantics (insertion-order only)
e1a798cc-e476-4a18-a5fa-e9bd236415a3.description:
## Severity
Trivial

## Dimension
Naming / Documentation & Intent

## Location
src/tools/file/mod.rs:29-55 (ReadFileTracker — comment says LRU-ordered)

## Violation
```rust
pub struct ReadFileTracker {
    /// LRU-ordered list: most recently read files at the end.
    /// When capacity is exceeded, oldest entries (front) are evicted.
    read_files: Mutex<Vec<PathBuf>>,
}

pub(crate) fn mark_read(&self, path: &Path) {
    ...
    files.retain(|p| p != &resolved);
    files.push(resolved);
    ...
}
```

Calling `mark_read(p)` after `has_been_read(p)` returns true does promote `p` to most-recent. But `has_been_read(p)` itself does NOT promote — it only reads. So a file that is *frequently checked* but never *re-marked* will be evicted while a file that was marked once 10k entries ago and never touched again gets kept (until something else pushes 10k more entries). The doc says LRU; the implementation is "insertion order, MRU on re-insert." These are different policies.

The distinction matters because edit_file calls has_been_read(); a session that does many edits but few reads can have its frequently-edited file evicted while a never-touched file blocks the slot.

## Mandated refactor
Either:
1. Make the policy match the docs: have has_been_read also promote (turn it into &mut self and acquire the write lock — currently it only takes the lock; turn it from `contains` to a remove-then-push-at-end).
2. OR fix the docs to say "insertion order with most-recent-touch promotion on mark_read" and explicitly document that has_been_read does not promote.

Cross-references issue #787 (READ_TRACKER global mutex) — the right fix is to use a real LRU container (linked_hash_map) so the policy is mechanical.

## Filed from QA review dispatch

e1b8ef4e-4979-461c-940d-472e372de917.title: Anthropic adapter has TWO message converters; transform_request uses the broken one
e1b8ef4e-4979-461c-940d-472e372de917.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

Dimension: Structural Modularity / DRY

Location: src/providers/anthropic.rs has TWO independent message-conversion paths:
  (1) AnthropicAdapter::convert_messages (private, lines 37-79) — takes `&[ChatMessage]`, used by AnthropicAdapter::transform_request.
  (2) convert_messages_to_anthropic (pub fn, lines 338-445) — takes `&[Value]`, used by... (per Grep unused internally — it's re-exported from mod.rs line 32 for external consumers).

These two functions do the SAME job (OpenAI -> Anthropic message format) with different input types and DIFFERENT behaviors:
  - (1) doesn't handle role='tool' as tool_result — it bucket-maps everything non-assistant to 'user' with plain text.
  - (2) DOES handle role='tool' with tool_use_id / tool_result blocks, assistant tool_calls split into tool_use content blocks.
The path actually used for Anthropic requests (AnthropicAdapter::transform_request line 123) calls the simpler (1), which silently DROPS tool-result semantics. Any agentic loop where a model produces tool_calls and the next turn sends back role='tool' messages will be mis-translated: the tool result becomes a bare 'user' message with no tool_use_id linkage. Anthropic rejects this with a 400 error ('each tool_use must have a matching tool_result').

Mandated Refactor:
  1. Delete AnthropicAdapter::convert_messages (private). Route through the public convert_messages_to_anthropic, converting ChatMessage to Value via serde_json::to_value first (or by reading the ChatMessage directly — prefer a typed path).
  2. Better: change the signature of convert_messages_to_anthropic to take &[ChatMessage] and eliminate the Value intermediary. Keep the richer behavior.
  3. Add integration test: simulate a full agentic loop round trip: user query -> Anthropic tool_use -> our proxy returns assistant with tool_calls -> client sends role='tool' message -> proxy's transform_request -> body that Anthropic accepts.

52ac9f35-980e-4038-9ac9-30b2958f5ea0.author: lOrm
52ac9f35-980e-4038-9ac9-30b2958f5ea0.content:
Resolved. Changes to `src/providers/anthropic.rs`:

**`AnthropicAdapter::convert_messages`** — was 42 lines of its own lossy logic; replaced with a 5-line delegation:
```rust
fn convert_messages(messages: &[ChatMessage]) -> Vec<Value> {
    let as_values: Vec<Value> = messages
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|m| serde_json::to_value(m).ok())
        .collect();
    convert_messages_to_anthropic(&as_values)
}
```
`ChatMessage` already derives `Serialize`, so the `to_value` hop is a straightforward serde roundtrip. The hot path (`transform_request`) now goes through the richer converter that handles `role="tool"` → `tool_result` blocks with `tool_use_id` linkage and assistant `tool_calls` → `tool_use` blocks.

**Mandated refactor point 1 complete** (single converter). Point 2 (native `&[ChatMessage]` in `convert_messages_to_anthropic`) is deferred: the Value-based converter is also used by external callers (re-exported from `providers/mod.rs:32`) that pass raw JSON, so changing its signature is cross-cutting; the serde hop is essentially free since it's in-memory JSON with no allocation beyond the cloning that was already happening.

**Tests (mandated refactor point 3 — integration test):** 3 new unit tests in `providers::anthropic::tests`:

1. **`tool_result_role_becomes_tool_result_block_with_id`** — the direct regression test for this issue. Constructs a 3-turn conversation (user, assistant with `tool_calls`, tool response), runs `AnthropicAdapter::transform_request`, and asserts:
   - Assistant message has a `tool_use` content block with `id="toolu_abc"`, `name="calc"`, `input.expr="2+2"`.
   - Tool-result message has `role="user"` with a `tool_result` block whose `tool_use_id` matches "toolu_abc" and content is "4".
   The old implementation would have produced a bare `{role:"user", content:[{type:"text", text:"4"}]}` with no linkage — which this test now catches.
2. **`plain_text_user_message_still_works`** — smoke test that the common non-tool path is preserved.
3. **`image_content_part_preserved`** — multimodal: text+image parts survive the new converter route. The richer converter preserves array content as-is, so base64 image content blocks pass through.

631 lib tests pass.

**Impact:** any agentic tool-loop using Anthropic via this proxy would previously have failed after the first tool call with a 400 `"each tool_use must have a matching tool_result"` error. That's now fixed.
