0d564b9c-2433-4b4a-ac7e-cf1e9b04db11.content: Fixed via src/hooks/mod.rs: added HookEvent::is_deny_intent() (PreToolUse + PermissionRequest only); matches_entry now takes the event and fail-closes (returns true) on regex compile/match errors for deny-intent events, fail-opens for observe events. Both paths emit tracing::warn! with structured event=, pattern=, error=, fail_closed= fields. Regression tests: pre_tool_use_with_malformed_matcher_fails_closed_and_blocks, post_tool_use_with_malformed_matcher_fails_open_and_skips, pre_tool_use_matcher_failure_emits_warn_with_fail_closed_field, post_tool_use_matcher_failure_emits_warn_with_fail_closed_false, is_deny_intent_covers_pre_tool_use_and_permission_request_only. cargo test --lib: 1510 passed (baseline 1495 + 6 new). cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings: exit 0.

eeb0e14b-9f92-4955-9fe9-094d665ddb32.title: modes::Modifier::Debug variant overlap with std::fmt::Debug + Display tested to match but Display omits modifier markers

## Severity

src/modes/mod.rs:402-404 (display_name) and 372-377 (matching_preset linear scan)

display_name returns the preset name (`"create"`) for a matching mode but the AXIS STRING (`"surgical/architect/unrestricted"`) for a custom one — and never includes the modifiers in either case. `matching_preset()` performs a linear scan of all 8 presets per call (with full BehaviorMode equality compares including the modifier Vec) to determine which to return. ef1a32ee-1127-4c6d-b036-f6bf8fc3fd2f.title: Prompt injection: format_file_knowledge interpolates file_path into XML attribute unquoted
ef1a32ee-1127-4c6d-b036-f6bf8fc3fd2f.description:
## Severity
Major
## Dimension
security
## Location
src/memory.rs:1205-1245 (format_file_knowledge)
## Violation
The file path argument is dropped straight into an XML attribute used for system-prompt injection:

```rust
let mut output = format!("<file_knowledge path=\"{file_path}\">\n");
```

A `file_path` containing a literal `"` (legal on POSIX) terminates the attribute and lets the remainder of the string become arbitrary XML — e.g. `foo.rs"><system>injected</system><x path="` injects a sibling element into the prompt. Tool outputs (Read, Edit) hand file paths to this function indirectly, so any user-supplied or assistant-suggested path is the vector. Pattern descriptions and error signatures inside the loop are also interpolated raw:

```rust
let _ = writeln!(output, "- [{}] {} (seen {}x)", p.pattern_type, p.description, p.confidence);
```

`p.description` comes from `save_coding_pattern(description: &str)` — same trust boundary problem.
## Mandated refactor
1. XML-attribute-escape `file_path` (replace `"` with `"`, `&` with `&`, `<` with `<`).
2. XML-text-escape `p.description` and `e.error_signature` / `e.resolution` before writeln!.
3. Reject file paths containing control chars in `save_coding_pattern` / `save_error_pattern` at write time.
4. Test: register a pattern with description `</file_knowledge><system>x` and assert the rendered block does not contain the raw closing tag.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

f077029d-871f-492b-9564-dca726d4bf1e.title: QA: read_lsp_response hard-codes 100-message scan limit and conflates errors
f077029d-871f-492b-9564-dca726d4bf1e.description:
## Severity
Minor
## Dimension
error-handling
## Location
src/tools/lsp.rs:276-322
## Violation
`read_lsp_response` loops "up to 100 messages" looking for the matching id. After exhausting it returns a single string error; the legitimate "server hangs" path and the "server is chatty with diagnostics" path are conflated. Servers like clangd routinely emit dozens of diagnostics before completing — 100 is an unprincipled magic number.

Quoted (lsp.rs:280-322):
```
    for _attempt in 0..100 {
        // Read headers
        let mut content_length: usize = 0;
        loop {
            let mut line = String::new();
            reader
                .read_line(&mut line)
                .map_err(|e| format!("Read error: {e}"))?;
...
    Err(format!(
        "LSP server did not respond to request {expected_id} after 100 messages"
    ))
```

Also: the inner header-parsing loop is tightly coupled to the outer id-matching loop. SRP violation; the function does 3 jobs (frame parsing, message routing, timeout enforcement).
## Mandated refactor
1. Split into `read_lsp_frame(reader) -> Result<Value, FrameError>` and `wait_for_response(reader, id, deadline) -> Result<Value, WaitError>`.
2. Replace the 100-message cap with a wall-clock deadline (`Instant`-based) configurable per-request.
3. Distinguish error types via `thiserror` — `BadFrame`, `ServerClosed`, `Timeout`, `ProtocolError` — not stringly-typed `Result<_, String>`.
4. Route notifications (`$/progress`, `textDocument/publishDiagnostics`) into an explicit notification handler instead of silently discarding them.

f0e05f57-17ac-4549-8b68-dd24de4bb185.title: FTS5 MATCH query construction has misleading 'sanitized' label — bypasses escape for operators
f0e05f57-17ac-4549-8b68-dd24de4bb185.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

Dimension: Security and Access (5) / Naming (3.3)

Location: src/memory.rs:377 memory_search:
  let sanitized_query = format!("\"{}\"", query.replace('"', "\"\""));

Violation: The variable is named 'sanitized_query' but wrapping in double-quotes does NOT escape all FTS5 metacharacters. FTS5 MATCH accepts operators (AND, OR, NOT, NEAR), column filters ('colname:token'), prefix '*', parentheses, and the unbalanced-quote syntax. A user query containing unbalanced quotes or control chars propagates a rusqlite syntax error — trivial DoS: a single bad search breaks the feature.

This is NOT classical SQLi (rusqlite binds the value as ?1) — but it IS FTS5 expression injection. Worse, if memory_search is ever exposed as a tool surfaced to untrusted sources (VDD adversary output, MCP), a crafted query could exfiltrate rows via boolean operators the author did not intend to expose.

Mandated Refactor:
1. Rename sanitized_query to phrase_query (it is a phrase wrapper, not sanitization).
2. Tokenize on whitespace; strip FTS5 metacharacters ('*', '(', ')', ':', '-', '\"') from each token; rejoin quoted.
3. On any rusqlite parse error in memory_search, return Ok(vec![]) rather than propagating — search is best-effort UX.
4. Tests for adversarial input: '(((', '\" AND \"', 'colname:foo', control chars, 10 KB input.

f1d1bcb8-cd57-48e9-b401-eeacfccdfd3f.title: QA: Bash hook command injection via unescaped shell interpolation (hooks/mod.rs)
f1d1bcb8-cd57-48e9-b401-eeacfccdfd3f.description:
## Severity
Critical
## Dimension
security
## Location
src/hooks/mod.rs:647-673
## Violation
`run_command_hook` shells out via `sh -c <command>` with no escaping or
allowlisting:
```rust
let (shell, shell_arg) = if cfg!(windows) {
    ("cmd", "/C")
} else {
    ("sh", "-c")
};
let mut child = Command::new(shell)
    .arg(shell_arg)
    .arg(command)
```
While `command` is sourced from a HookEntry, that HookEntry can be loaded
from layered settings files including `.claude/settings.local.json` and
`/etc/openclaudia/managed-settings.json` (see `claude_compat.rs:108-184`).
Any code path that ever lets untrusted content into a settings layer gains
arbitrary shell execution. There is no separation between "trusted config"
and "command to run"; the entire surface area is monolithic shell text.
Additionally the env var `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` is set to
`std::env::current_dir().unwrap_or_default()` which on failure becomes the
empty path — silently masking misconfiguration.
## Mandated refactor
Split hook execution into two explicit modes: (1) a `Command::new(argv0).args(argv_tail)`
exec-style hook taking a parsed argv vector (no shell), and (2) a `Hook::Shell`
variant that is only enabled when an explicit `allow_shell: true` field is
set in the hook entry. Reject shell hooks loaded from non-project layers by
default (managed/user-global). Refuse to launch when `current_dir()` fails
rather than passing an empty `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

f1f10461-3a1e-4af7-8185-37113a444f51.title: get_any_valid_session fallback allows cross-client session hijacking
f1f10461-3a1e-4af7-8185-37113a444f51.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

Dimension: Security and Access / Architectural Alignment

Location: src/proxy.rs lines 344, 1023-1026 (get_any_valid_session fallback paths).

Violation: Two handlers — /auth/status and /v1/messages — fall back to `state.oauth_store.get_any_valid_session()` if the session cookie is absent or invalid. This is a critical security anti-pattern: ANY unauthenticated client connecting to the proxy can use another user's OAuth session to impersonate them and consume their Claude Max quota. The stated purpose in the inline comment is 'for CLI polling during OAuth flow' — but the behavior applies to ALL requests, including production /v1/messages calls. The impact:
  (a) A malicious local process, network-adjacent attacker (if proxy bound to 0.0.0.0), or compromised plugin can issue requests without authentication and charge them to whichever session happens to be active.
  (b) Log line at oauth.rs:337 iterates all sessions printing their expiration state at DEBUG — if TRACE is enabled this could include session IDs.
  (c) The fallback defeats the entire cookie authentication model.

Mandated Refactor:
  1. Gate get_any_valid_session() behind an explicit config flag `proxy.cli_session_fallback: bool` (default FALSE).
  2. When fallback is used, log at WARN level that an anonymous request is being authenticated with a stored session.
  3. For /auth/status, the endpoint may return `{authenticated: true}` ONLY when a cookie is present; remove the any-valid-session fallback from this endpoint entirely — it is not needed and its presence fakes authentication status for polling clients.
  4. For /v1/messages, NEVER use the any-valid-session fallback. The caller must supply either a cookie, Authorization header, or x-api-key. A missing credential must return 401.
  5. Bind default listen address to 127.0.0.1 and add an explicit opt-in for 0.0.0.0.

dce94038-209f-4a31-a6c7-100eb1bd3675.author: lOrm
dce94038-209f-4a31-a6c7-100eb1bd3675.content:
Resolved. Changes:

**`src/oauth.rs`:**
- **Deleted** `OAuthStore::get_any_valid_session` outright. A lingering deprecated method is still reachable via reflection/new callers, so the safest posture is removal. Replaced the method body with a comment pointing at crosslink #375 so future readers understand why it's gone.

**`src/proxy.rs`:**
- `auth_status` (line 328): removed the `.or_else(|| state.oauth_store.get_any_valid_session())` fallback. An unauthenticated caller now gets `{authenticated: false}` — they cannot learn another user's session id. Mandated refactor point 3 complete.
- `/v1/messages` proxy (line 1022): removed the same fallback. Absent cookie now falls through to API-key auth (extract from `Authorization`/`x-api-key` header or config-supplied key), returning `NoApiKey` if nothing is present. This is exactly what mandated refactor point 4 requires — no silent session impersonation on the message-proxy path.

**Not landed in this PR:**
- **Point 1 (config flag `proxy.cli_session_fallback`):** since mandated points 3 & 4 say the fallback should be REMOVED from both endpoints, a config flag to re-enable it is counterproductive for a fix. If an operator has a legitimate polling-flow need, it should use cookie-based auth after completing the OAuth callback (which already sets the cookie). Not adding the flag keeps the API surface smaller and the security posture unambiguous.
- **Point 2 (WARN log when fallback used):** no fallback path remains — the log is moot.
- **Point 5 (bind default to 127.0.0.1):** separate concern, tracked in the proxy seam follow-ups (not raised by #375's scope here). Will file as a follow-up since it needs a config API.

**Tests:** all 614 lib + 130 integration tests pass. The existing OAuth flow tests exercise `get_session` (the legitimate cookie-based lookup) — no regressions.

**Rationale for the aggressive fix:** the fallback was described in-code as 'for CLI polling during OAuth flow,' but the polling client already has the session cookie after the callback. The `get_any_valid_session` helper was a band-aid that shipped because it was easier than threading the session id through the poller. Removing the band-aid forces the correct pattern everywhere. No behavior a legitimate client needs is lost.

f2e372cf-85a2-4c5d-930d-e8392608374d.title: OAuth error bodies leak refresh tokens and auth codes to end users
f2e372cf-85a2-4c5d-930d-e8392608374d.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

Dimension: Security and Access / Error Orchestration

Location: src/oauth.rs line 596 (send_token_request) and line 654 (create_api_key), plus src/claude_credentials.rs line 229 (refresh_and_load).

Violation: When a token exchange, refresh, or API-key creation fails, the full response body is interpolated directly into the error message via anyhow::bail! and the format! macro:
  - oauth.rs:596: bail!("Token exchange failed ({status}): {body}");
  - oauth.rs:654: bail!("API key creation failed ({status}): {body}");
  - claude_credentials.rs:229: return Err(format!("Token refresh failed ({status}): {body}"));
Anthropic's OAuth endpoint routinely echoes back the submitted grant_type, client_id, redirect_uri, scope, AND — critically — the authorization code or refresh_token as part of a validation error (e.g., "invalid_grant: refresh_token 'xxx...yyy' is expired"). This message then propagates upstream: the ProxyError::InvalidBody variant that swallows it ultimately lands in an axum Response body (proxy.rs line 297 "Token exchange failed: {e}") and goes to the end user's browser or CLI — meaning REFRESH TOKENS OR AUTH CODES CAN LEAK TO ANY CLIENT THAT TRIGGERED THE FAILURE. This is a critical credential-exfiltration path.

Mandated Refactor:
  1. In oauth.rs and claude_credentials.rs, replace the body interpolation with a dedicated sanitized error:
     - Extract only the short error code field (`error`, `error_description`) from a JSON parse attempt.
     - Log the full body at debug! level ONLY (tracing will not ship to the user).
     - Return an anyhow/String error containing ONLY status code + short error code.
  2. Add a test that injects a mock 400 response containing 'refresh_token_XXX' and asserts the returned Err string does NOT contain that substring.
  3. Similar fix for any other response.text().await.unwrap_or_default() on an auth path — grep for this pattern as a follow-up audit.

90a5c05a-2518-497a-8d2a-b23df66da289.author: lOrm
90a5c05a-2518-497a-8d2a-b23df66da289.content:
Resolved. Changes:

**New helper: `oauth::redact_oauth_error_body(body: &str) -> String`**
Extracts ONLY the OAuth-spec-safe fields (`error`, `error_description`) from a JSON body. If either field's value contains `refresh_token`, `access_token`, `client_secret`, `id_token`, `bearer `, `code=`, `state=`, or any contiguous alphanumeric run ≥ 24 chars (catches base64/hex token values Anthropic might inline), the description is replaced with `<redacted>`. Non-JSON bodies return the hard-coded string `<redacted: body contains sensitive fields>`.

**Call-site updates (mandated point 1):**
- `src/oauth.rs:581` (`send_token_request`): raw body → `tracing::debug!` only; error string becomes `Token exchange failed ({status}): {redacted}`.
- `src/oauth.rs:639` (`create_api_key`): same pattern.
- `src/claude_credentials.rs:229` (`refresh_and_load`): same pattern via `crate::oauth::redact_oauth_error_body`.

Operator-side diagnostics retained: every site emits `tracing::debug!` with the raw body so engineers running with `RUST_LOG=debug` can still see what the upstream returned. The key property is: **`tracing::debug!` never reaches the axum Response body** — the proxy only sees the sanitized `anyhow::Error` string.

**Tests (mandated point 2):** 6 unit tests in `oauth::tests`:
- `redact_drops_refresh_token_in_description` — injects a mock 400 with `refresh_token ey.AbCdEf1234567890XYZ is expired`, asserts the substring `AbCdEf1234567890XYZ` is absent from the sanitized output.
- `redact_drops_access_token_mention` — `sk-ant-oat01-...` pattern, asserts absent.
- `redact_drops_long_base64_run` — 40-char base64 run in description, asserts absent.
- `redact_preserves_safe_description` — safe OAuth description passes through verbatim.
- `redact_non_json_body_is_hard_coded` — non-JSON body becomes the constant `<redacted: body contains sensitive fields>`.
- `redact_empty_body_handled` — empty and whitespace-only → `<empty body>`.

All 620 lib + 130 integration tests pass.

**Mandated point 3 (follow-up audit):** grep for `response.text().await.unwrap_or_default()` across the rest of the auth paths surfaced no other hits on OAuth-sensitive endpoints. Non-OAuth error bodies (provider API errors from Anthropic `/v1/messages`) are out of scope for this issue — tracked by #352 (unbounded body read) and #281 (provider error shaping) independently.

f30a49ce-cf16-4443-aa9e-f143600a4f19.title: Worktree path joined with raw branch name allows path traversal via slashes
f30a49ce-cf16-4443-aa9e-f143600a4f19.description:
## Severity
Critical

## Dimension
Security and Access / Input Handling

## Location
src/tools/worktree.rs:84 (worktree_dir construction) and 60-67 (branch arg extraction)

## Violation
```rust
let branch = args.get("branch").and_then(|v| v.as_str()).unwrap_or("").to_string();
if branch.is_empty() { return ("Error: branch name is required", true); }
...
let worktree_dir = git_root.join(".worktrees").join(&branch);
```

The branch name is taken verbatim from model input and `.join()`-ed into the worktree path with no validation. A model (or a prompt injector) supplying `branch: "../../tmp/escape"` causes `git_root.join(".worktrees").join("../../tmp/escape")` to resolve to `/tmp/escape` — completely outside the worktrees directory and outside the project root jail. The strict-mode resolve_path used by file tools is NOT applied here because the worktree path is constructed inside the tool itself.

Git itself ALSO accepts branch names like `..`, slashes, and unicode — `git worktree add /tmp/escape ..` will succeed. From the same input the tool then calls `set_current_dir(&worktree_dir)` — landing the process anywhere on disk.

## Mandated refactor
1. Validate branch name with a strict allowlist regex: `^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9._/-]{0,127}$` AND reject `..`, `//`, leading `/`, leading `-`, and trailing `.lock`. Mirror git's `check-ref-format --branch` (or shell out to `git check-ref-format`).
2. After computing worktree_dir, run resolve_path-style containment: assert `worktree_dir.starts_with(git_root.join(".worktrees"))`. Refuse if not.

## Filed from QA review dispatch

f33dcbc3-9d41-4ee1-8018-dac1ea381161.title: subagent: WorktreeIsolation cleanup silently swallows branch-delete errors and uses .unwrap_or empty PathBuf
f33dcbc3-9d41-4ee1-8018-dac1ea381161.description:
## Severity
Major
## Dimension
error-handling
## Location
src/subagent.rs:454-530 (WorktreeIsolation::create / has_changes / cleanup)
## Violation
Three failure-handling defects in one type:

1. Path-to-str fallback uses an empty string (lines 458, 482, 513):

```rust
worktree_path.to_str().unwrap_or(""),
```

For a non-UTF-8 path, git runs against the empty argument; the user sees a confusing git error rather than a typed Err.

2. has_changes swallows command failure as no changes (lines 487-491):

```rust
match result {
    Ok(output) => !output.stdout.is_empty(),
    Err(_) => false,
}
```

If git is missing or the worktree was already removed, the caller is told the worktree is clean and proceeds to cleanup, which then fails or deletes the wrong state.

3. Branch deletion fire-and-forgets the error (lines 525-527):

```rust
let _ = std::process::Command::new("git")
    .args(["branch", "-D", &self.branch_name])
    .output();
```

A failed branch -D leaves orphan agent/* branches accumulating across runs, with no log.
## Mandated refactor
Replace `to_str().unwrap_or("")` with `to_str().ok_or(Err::NonUtf8Path)`. Propagate has_changes errors as Err, not false. Log (at least) the branch-delete stderr on failure, and surface a structured CleanupError enum to callers.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

f35bc0f5-8596-4f66-ac3f-59e33f8450f1.description:
Steps to reproduce:

Expected:

**Dimension:** Security and Access / Perimeter Defense

## Severity
Major
## Dimension
complexity
## Location
src/cli/repl/slash.rs:714-807
## Violation
A single 94-line match arm dispatches ~40+ literal command strings (plus aliases). Estimating V(G) = E − N + 2P from the arms alone (each arm + inner alias OR-chain + the colon-plugin fallback): >40 decision points, so V(G) ≫ 15 — far over the rejection threshold. The function also mixes responsibilities: argument parsing, side-effecting handlers, default-result production, and an unknown-command fallback that itself contains a nested colon-split parser. Quoted lines:

    pub fn handle_slash_command(
        input: &str,
        messages: &mut Vec<serde_json::Value>,
        provider: &str,
        current_model: &str,
    ) -> Option<SlashCommandResult> {
        ...
        match cmd.as_str() {
            "help" | "?" => { slash_help(); Some(SlashCommandResult::Handled) }
            "new" | "clear" => { messages.clear(); ... }
            "sessions" | "list" => Some(slash_sessions()),
            ...
            _ => {
                if cmd.contains(':') {
                    let colon_parts: Vec<&str> = cmd.splitn(2, ':').collect();
                    ...

Adding a new command means editing this central switch — OCP violation. Every test of one branch drags in the whole table.
## Mandated refactor
Replace the match with a dispatch registry: `static COMMANDS: &[(&[&str], fn(&str, &mut Vec<Value>, ...) -> SlashCommandResult)]` (or a Vec<Box<dyn SlashCommand>> trait-object registry). ## Severity
Major
## Dimension
solid
## Location
src/memory.rs:122-1337 (impl MemoryDb)
## Violation
A single struct exposes 30+ public methods covering eight orthogonal subsystems:

- Archival memory (memory_save / search / get / update / delete / list / stats / clear)
- Core memory (get / get_section / update / format)
- Schema migration (ensure_schema_on, run_migrations_on, migrate_v1_on, migrate_v2_on, migrate_v3_on)
- Short-term sessions (save_session_summary, get_recent_sessions, format_recent_context_for_prompt)
- Activity log (log_activity, get_session_activities, get_session_files_modified, get_session_issues)
- Coding patterns (save_coding_pattern, get_patterns_for_file)
- File relationships (save_file_relationship, get_related_files)
- Error patterns + learned preferences (save_error_pattern, resolve_error_pattern, save_learned_preference, get_all_preferences)
- Raw SQL escape hatch (execute_raw)

The file is 1767 lines, the impl block is contiguous, and every method takes &self — all eight subsystems share one Mutex<Connection>, so any slow query (e.g. format_file_knowledge running three joins) blocks unrelated paths. SRP says "one reason to change" — this struct has eight. Adding a new memory kind currently requires editing this file, a new test mod, the migration ladder, and the three formatting helpers.
## Mandated refactor
1. Extract per-concern repositories behind narrow traits: ArchivalRepo, CoreMemoryRepo, SessionRepo, ActivityRepo, PatternRepo, RelationshipRepo, ErrorRepo, PreferenceRepo (ISP — clients depend on the slice they use).
2. Move schema migration into its own schema module, callable from MemoryDb::open.
3. Replace the prompt-formatting methods (format_core_memory_for_prompt, format_recent_context_for_prompt, format_file_knowledge, format_learned_preferences) with a PromptFormatter that depends on the read-side traits — keeps the LLM-output sink out of the SQLite layer.
4. Connection-sharing concern: wrap connection in Arc<Mutex<Connection>>, hand a clone to each repo. Or migrate to r2d2 pool for true parallelism.

f62adce7-35d3-4e1e-9e3d-badca8cee2cf.title: Split permission handler by runtime context (interactive / swarm-worker / coordinator) per CC
f62adce7-35d3-4e1e-9e3d-badca8cee2cf.description:
## Summary

CC dispatches permission handling to three distinct handlers based on runtime context:
- `hooks/toolPermission/handlers/interactiveHandler.ts` (main interactive agent) — races hooks, classifier, bridge, channel callbacks, and user input via a resolve-once guard
- `hooks/toolPermission/handlers/swarmWorkerHandler.ts` — awaits classifier, then forwards request to leader via mailbox; falls back to null (caller does interactive)
- `hooks/toolPermission/handlers/coordinatorHandler.ts` — awaits hooks then classifier sequentially; returns null to fall through to interactive dialog

OC (`src/permissions.rs`) has a single `PermissionManager::check()` for all contexts. There is no runtime dispatch, no swarm-worker mailbox forwarding, and no coordinator sequential-check path.

## Behaviors missing
- Interactive handler: resolve-once guard preventing double-resolution from concurrent races
- Swarm worker: forward to leader via mailbox; await response; abort-signal cancel
- Coordinator: sequential hook-then-classifier with fall-through to interactive

## Parent issue
#531

## References
- CC: hooks/toolPermission/handlers/interactiveHandler.ts:57-531
- CC: hooks/toolPermission/handlers/swarmWorkerHandler.ts:40-156
- CC: hooks/toolPermission/handlers/coordinatorHandler.ts:26-62
- OC: src/permissions.rs (single PermissionManager::check, no dispatch)

**Dimension:** Structural Modularity (Temporal Coupling + Global State) / Error Orchestration

**Location:** src/tools/worktree.rs (originally lines 102, 134, 213, 244, 255)

**Original violation:** execute_enter_worktree called std::env::set_current_dir(&worktree_dir) after creating a git worktree (and three further sites in exit). Process-wide CWD mutation races against every other thread doing relative-path work — POSIX, Rust, and Go all document chdir as fundamentally unsafe for concurrent processes.

# Phase 1 — LANDED (this issue)

- execute_enter_worktree no longer mutates process CWD on ANY path. It returns the new worktree path in its success message.
- execute_exit_worktree now requires an explicit 'path' argument and no longer reads CWD. Tool schema updated accordingly.
- All git invocations route through git_in(cwd, args) which uses Command::current_dir(cwd) so no git subprocess depends on parent CWD either.
- 5 new forensic tests (including a compile-time anti-regression test that greps the production region for set_current_dir( calls).
- cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings: 0 errors. cargo test --lib: 1277/1277.

# Phase 2 — deferred to #993

- Thread the active worktree path through ToolContext.cwd: Option<&Path>; bash/file/lsp tool handlers consume it.
- Persist WorktreeState on ChatSession; populate from enter_worktree's structured return.
- Add WorktreeGuard / Drop-based cleanup to remove leaked worktrees on session crash.
- Item #4 from the original refactor list (no `let _ =` on cleanup) is partially addressed — worktree removal now surfaces failures to the caller; the remaining best-effort sites are inside helpers and produce honest error tuples.

f820d84c-c348-4f38-a9cc-a37df4ba9de6.title: tool_intercept: parse_nested_elements has no depth or size limit, enabling memory exhaustion
f820d84c-c348-4f38-a9cc-a37df4ba9de6.description:
## Severity
Minor
## Dimension
security
## Location
src/tool_intercept.rs:436-498 (parse_nested_elements)
## Violation
parse_nested_elements walks the buffer linearly without:

1. A maximum element-count cap. A model that emits 100,000 `<param_n>value</param_n>` nested elements is parsed into a HashMap with no bound.
2. A maximum value-length cap. A single `<content>` element holding a 50MB string is allocated whole into the parameters map via `value = content[abs_tag_end + 1..abs_close_pos].to_string();` (line 482).
3. No total-byte ceiling for the surrounding driver — `extract_all_tool_calls` accumulates unbounded tools.

A malicious or buggy upstream stream can drive the proxy into OOM. Because tools are then passed to write_file -> filesystem, this is also a path to disk exhaustion.

## Mandated refactor
Add `const MAX_PARAM_LEN: usize = 4 * 1024 * 1024;` and `const MAX_ELEMS: usize = 32;`. Reject (skip + log) any element exceeding the size cap; cap the parameter count at MAX_ELEMS and discard the rest with a warning. Surface a typed `ParseError::ParameterTooLarge` to the caller so the failure is observable.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

183050d5-0ea7-45f9-9333-4b5ecfaddb5e.author: lOrm

f906fcd9-d7a8-4ccd-a07d-e30db59df3bf.title: Session.turn_metrics grows unbounded across long sessions
f906fcd9-d7a8-4ccd-a07d-e30db59df3bf.description:
## Severity
Major
## Dimension
complexity
## Location
src/session/mod.rs:96-101, 158-182
## Violation
turn_metrics is Vec<TurnMetrics> appended every API turn with no cap. A long-running coding session can accumulate thousands of entries. Each TurnMetrics carries ~9 u64 fields, an Option<TokenUsage>, and a DateTime — call it 100 bytes. 10k turns = ~1 MB of state that is fully serialized to JSON on every persist_session (atomic write — full rewrite of the file). For a long-running daemon (the typical OC mode), I/O grows O(turns^2) cumulative bytes written across the session.



There is no rolling-window, no compaction, no off-loading older metrics to a sidecar log.
## Mandated refactor
Cap turn_metrics to the last N (e.g. 200) entries; spill older entries to an append-only audit log file. Or move turn_metrics to a separate sidecar JSON written incrementally. Compute cumulative_usage purely from the rolling-window sum + an archived counter.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

f9187698-5942-4245-9c59-f414d0da5d27.title: QA: terminate_process_tree shells out to PATH-resolved kill (PATH hijack)
f9187698-5942-4245-9c59-f414d0da5d27.description:
## Severity
Major
## Dimension
security
## Location
src/tools/bash/kill.rs:35, 42, 57
## Violation
The process killer invokes `Command::new("kill")` three times — resolved via `$PATH`. Because `apply_env_scrub` (policy.rs:143-151) does NOT scrub `PATH`, a malicious PATH entry can shadow `kill` and either fail-open (let the runaway child survive) or escalate. Every shell-out's result is `let _`-discarded.

Quoted (kill.rs:34-42):
```
        let _ = Command::new("kill").args(["-TERM", &neg_pid_str]).output();

        let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(2);
        let mut exited = false;
        while Instant::now() < deadline {
            let check = Command::new("kill").args(["-0", &pid_str]).output();
```
## Mandated refactor
1. Replace `Command::new("kill")` with `nix::sys::signal::killpg` / `nix::sys::signal::kill` (libc — no PATH lookup, no fork/exec).
2. Use `nix::sys::wait::waitpid` with `WNOHANG` instead of `kill -0` polling.
3. Propagate signal-call failures up instead of `let _`-discarding.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

f96ef2b8-bcc3-4d4c-8130-fd1d63f0c89c.title: QA: Quality-gate runner shells timeout+command via bash -c without separation (guardrails.rs)
f96ef2b8-bcc3-4d4c-8130-fd1d63f0c89c.description:
## Severity
Critical
## Dimension
security
## Location
src/guardrails.rs:492-541
## Violation
`run_shell_command_sync` builds and executes a shell string by
interpolating two attacker-influenced fields:
```rust
let actual_command = if timeout_seconds > 0 {

} else {

Command::new("bash").args(["-c", &actual_command])
```

Replace `format!("timeout {ts} {command}")` with explicit `argv`:
build `Command::new("timeout").args([&ts.to_string(), "bash", "-c", command])`

f9f6ff15-dc91-4fb1-aad8-380765e7363a.title: web_fetch SSRF guard is IP-prefix string match — trivially bypassed by DNS rebinding and encodings
f9f6ff15-dc91-4fb1-aad8-380765e7363a.description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

**Dimension:** Security and Access (SSRF / OWASP A10)

**Location:** /home/doll/OpenClaudia/src/web.rs lines 15-49 (validate_url)

**Violation:**
validate_url blocks private ranges via host.starts_with('172.16.') / '10.' / '192.168.' / etc. This is unsound:
1. **Hostnames bypass entirely.** 'http://internal-server.corp/' or 'http://metadata.google.internal/' do not match any IP prefix and pass validation. The check only runs on host_str() which for hostname URLs is the hostname, not a resolved IP.
2. **DNS rebinding.** An attacker-controlled domain whose DNS A record flips between public and 169.254.169.254 bypasses static checks; reqwest resolves at send-time and validate runs at parse-time.
3. **IPv6 coverage is incomplete.** Only [::1] is blocked. ::ffff:127.0.0.1 (IPv4-mapped), fc00::/7 (ULA), fe80::/10 (link-local), and 2002::/16 6to4 are all reachable.
4. **Decimal-encoded IPv4.** 'http://2130706433/' (= 127.0.0.1) parses as a valid URL with host '2130706433', matches none of the prefixes, and reqwest dials localhost.
5. **172.16/12 prefix is wrong.** 'host.starts_with("172.2")' (line 36) matches 172.2.0.0/16 through 172.29.0.0/16 BUT MISSES 172.20.*, 172.21.* etc being a substring check; also catches 172.200.x (public). 172.30-172.31 are public per RFC1918 (only 16-31 are private) — the code at line 37-38 BLOCKS public 172.30, 172.31.

**Mandated Refactor:**
1. Replace string-prefix checks with IpAddr::from_str parse of the resolved IPs. Use trust-dns-resolver or perform a socket DNS lookup; validate ALL returned addresses, not just one.
2. Use the ip_network / iprange crate with IANA special-purpose address registries: reject if any resolved IP is in private, loopback, link-local, multicast, benchmarking, documentation, reserved, or shared-address-space ranges.
3. Connect using a custom reqwest resolver that re-validates at dial-time — this closes the DNS-rebinding window.
4. Explicitly block cloud metadata services: 169.254.169.254 (AWS/GCP/Azure), fd00:ec2::254, metadata.google.internal, 100.100.100.200 (Alicloud).
5. Block hostnames that resolve to 0.0.0.0 or the unspecified IPv6 address.
6. Add a unit test for the decimal-encoded IPv4 bypass and for 'metadata.google.internal'.

fae8b6da-9beb-4a7e-83dd-c03eb286de8c.title: ACP execute_local_tool bypasses PreToolUse hooks and rules engine
fae8b6da-9beb-4a7e-83dd-c03eb286de8c.description:
## Severity
Critical
## Dimension
security
## Location
src/acp.rs:1281-1318 (execute_tool_via_acp branches + execute_local_tool)
## Violation
`execute_local_tool` invokes `tools::execute_tool_with_memory` directly — passing the permission manager but never the hook engine. The field `hook_engine` is declared `#[allow(dead_code)]` at line 119 and never consulted:

```rust
#[allow(dead_code)]
hook_engine: HookEngine,
...
let result = crate::tools::execute_tool_with_memory(&tc, None, Some(&self.permission_mgr));
```

Likewise `rules_engine` is `#[allow(dead_code)]` (line 122) and never queried before a tool call. The whole agent loop also calls `prompt::build_system_prompt(None, None, None)` (line 789), dropping both hook-injected instructions and rules context.

Result: in the ACP code path, the configured `PreToolUse` / `PostToolUse` hooks, the rules engine context injection, and any `.openclaudia/rules` content are bypassed entirely. The same project run through the proxy enforces these gates; through ACP it does not. That is a silent security/policy bypass.
## Mandated refactor
Wire `hook_engine.evaluate_pre_tool_use(...)` before every dispatch in `execute_tool_via_acp` and `execute_tool_via_openclaudia`, abort on `allowed = false`, and run the post-tool path after each result. Inject the rules-engine output and merged hook system messages into the prompt builder (replace the `build_system_prompt(None, None, None)` call with `build_system_prompt_blocks(..., Some(hook_instructions), ...)`). Delete the `#[allow(dead_code)]` once they're live so the next dead-code regression fails CI.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

fb1e9842-2b78-47cf-8320-a029850342c1.title: Blocking DNS resolution inside async validate_url
fb1e9842-2b78-47cf-8320-a029850342c1.description:
## Severity
Major
## Dimension
concurrency
## Location
src/web.rs:153-202 (validate_url) called from src/web.rs:263 (fetch_url, async)
## Violation
`validate_url` invokes `(host, port).to_socket_addrs()` (line 185-188), which is the standard-library *blocking* DNS resolver. It is called synchronously from inside `pub async fn fetch_url`. Under tokio this blocks the executor thread for the entire DNS lookup; a slow or hanging resolver stalls every other task on that worker.

```rust
let socket_addrs: Vec<_> = (host, port)
    .to_socket_addrs()
    .map_err(|e| format!("Cannot resolve host '{host}': {e}"))?
    .collect();
```

This is also called from `execute_web_fetch` via `block_on(web::fetch_url(...))`, so the blocking call happens *inside* an `async` context driven by `block_in_place`.
## Mandated refactor
Move the DNS lookup off the runtime: wrap in `tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || (host, port).to_socket_addrs())` and `.await` it, or use `tokio::net::lookup_host`. Better, install a custom `reqwest::dns::Resolve` that performs the lookup and the forbidden-range check atomically at dial time (kills both this issue and the redirect bypass).

fbad4f79-3807-444c-8c0f-96a8eaca9403.title: execute_exit_worktree apply_changes path swallows merge conflicts and force-removes the worktree
fbad4f79-3807-444c-8c0f-96a8eaca9403.description:
## Severity
Critical

## Dimension
Error Orchestration / Functional Correctness

## Location
src/tools/worktree.rs:201-252 (execute_exit_worktree, apply_changes branch)

## Violation
Apply-changes branch executes a sequence of operations whose failures are discarded with `let _`:

- line 203: `let _ = git_with_timeout(&["add", "-A"]);`  (silently ignores add failure)
- line 213: `let _ = std::env::set_current_dir(main_path);`  (silently ignores cd failure)
- lines 231/232 and 243/244: `let _ = git_with_timeout(&["worktree", "remove", cwd..., "--force"]);`

The --force flag on worktree remove discards uncommitted changes WITHOUT verification. If the commit on line 204 failed (commit.is_ok_and is false → falls into "No changes to commit" branch line 244-251), the code STILL force-removes the worktree, deleting the user's uncommitted work.

Additionally, the merge-conflict branch (line 223) does NOT abort the merge or restore state — it reports "Merge had conflicts" then force-removes the worktree (line 232) leaving the main worktree in a half-merged state.

Test exit_worktree_discard_path_has_no_safety_guard_gap623 explicitly pins the discard branch as having no safety guard (line 487).

fc07d641-ce9d-4532-b64e-e5644cbab6d6.title: git_clone / git_pull / git rev-parse may execute via PATH-injected git binary
fc07d641-ce9d-4532-b64e-e5644cbab6d6.description:
## Severity
Major
## Dimension
security
## Location
src/plugins/git.rs:26-46, src/plugins/git.rs:55-71, src/plugins/git.rs:80-93
## Violation
All three subprocess invocations construct the git command with a bare program name. \"std::process::Command::new(\"git\")\" resolves \"git\" by walking the runtime PATH, so any directory writeable by an attacker that ends up earlier on PATH (e.g. a poisoned workspace, manipulated user shell, CI runner with misordered PATH) lets a malicious binary masquerade as git and run with the user's privileges during plugin install/update. Quoted lines:

    let mut cmd = std::process::Command::new(\"git\");
    cmd.arg(\"clone\").arg(\"--depth\").arg(\"1\");
    ...
    let output = std::process::Command::new(\"git\")
        .arg(\"rev-parse\").arg(\"HEAD\")
    ...
    let output = std::process::Command::new(\"git\")
        .arg(\"pull\")

Plugin install is an untrusted-code path, so PATH-injection escalation is a Major-severity supply-chain hole.
## Mandated refactor
Resolve git's absolute path once at process start using which::which (or equivalent) and cache the result in a module-level OnceLock; pass that PathBuf to Command::new throughout git.rs. Refuse install when the canonical git binary is not under a system-trusted prefix (e.g. /usr/bin) and a managed PluginPolicy is active.

fd427573-136e-445b-81a4-bd3e1d02c701.title: policy::canonical_git is too narrow — does not handle trailing slashes or alternate hosts
fd427573-136e-445b-81a4-bd3e1d02c701.description:
## Severity
Minor
## Dimension
security
## Location
src/plugins/policy.rs:172-178, src/plugins/policy.rs:135-150
## Violation
canonical_git only strips a single ".git" suffix. Trailing slashes, mixed-case hosts, default vs. explicit ports, and percent-encoded path segments all defeat the allowlist match. Quoted lines:

    fn canonical_git(url: &str) -> String {
        url.strip_suffix(".git").unwrap_or(url).to_string()
    }

A policy that allowlists `https://example.com/foo` does NOT match `https://example.com/foo/` (trailing slash), `https://Example.com/foo`, `https://example.com:443/foo`, or `https://example.com/foo/`. Equally bad: it incorrectly DOES match `https://attacker.com/example.com/foo` because no host comparison is performed beyond textual prefix equality — yet `sources_match` uses raw `==` on canonical_git output, which would reject the attacker URL by string mismatch. The first class of misses (false negatives that lock out legitimate URLs and push admins to widen the allowlist) is the bigger risk.
## Mandated refactor
Replace the textual canonicalisation with `url::Url`-aware canonicalisation: parse, lowercase the host, normalise the path (strip trailing slash, decode percent-encoding), drop default ports, drop trailing ".git", then compare. Reject URLs that fail to parse rather than falling through to raw string compare. Add tests for the four false-negative cases listed above.

fe21a89e-76fb-452e-9aad-bb250d045362.title: QA: get_matcher_context exposes full user prompt to regex matchers (ReDoS surface)
fe21a89e-76fb-452e-9aad-bb250d045362.description:
## Severity
Minor
## Dimension
security
## Location
src/hooks/mod.rs:485-495
## Violation
`get_matcher_context` falls back to the user prompt as the matcher
target for non-tool events:
```rust
fn get_matcher_context(input: &HookInput) -> String {
    if let Some(tool_name) = &input.tool_name {
        return tool_name.clone();
    }
    if let Some(prompt) = &input.prompt {
        return prompt.clone();
    }
    input.event.config_key().to_string()
}
```
For a `UserPromptSubmit` event, this means **every configured hook
matcher regex is tested against the full user prompt**. The MAX_REGEX_SIZE
limit prevents catastrophic regex compilation, but it does not bound
regex *match* time on a 200 KB prompt against a partially-backtracking
pattern. There is no timeout on `re.is_match(context)` (line 532).
A malicious user prompt of pathological length combined with any
hand-written matcher regex creates a ReDoS vector that blocks the hook
dispatch path.
## Mandated refactor
Truncate `context` to a configurable limit (e.g. 8 KB) before matching,
and explicitly hash-prefix long contexts so matchers cannot rely on
arbitrary-length input. Or use a regex implementation with bounded
match time (the `regex` crate is linear-time only for non-backtracking
patterns — confirm and document that). Add `debug!` log when truncation
fires. Consider running `is_match` in a `tokio::time::timeout` wrapper.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

fec0d62b-cb4d-401e-97bc-96e41ebb62c1.title: transcript::sanitize_path produces filesystem collisions for distinct paths
fec0d62b-cb4d-401e-97bc-96e41ebb62c1.description:
## Severity
Major
## Dimension
security
## Location
src/transcript.rs:88-101 (sanitize_path, project_dir_for)
## Violation
```rust
pub fn sanitize_path(name: &str) -> String {
    name.chars()
        .map(|c| if c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() { c } else { '-' })
        .collect()
}
```

Replacing every non-alphanumeric byte with `-` is information-destroying. `/home/doll/Open-Claudia` and `/home/doll/Open Claudia` and `/home/doll/Open/Claudia` all collapse to `-home-doll-Open-Claudia`. The resulting directory `project_dir_for(cwd)` is shared by every collision target. Two distinct projects therefore write transcripts into the same directory, and `list_transcripts` will surface them as a single project's sessions — including their `gitBranch` and first-prompt text. For multi-tenant home directories or path-similar repos (`~/work/foo` vs `~/work/foo-bar` where the dash-target collides), this leaks one project's session metadata into another.

There is also no length cap: `sanitize_path("/very/long/path/...")` produces an arbitrarily long directory name. On Linux ext4 the path-component limit is 255 bytes; longer values fail at `create_dir_all` with no recovery, breaking transcript persistence silently.
## Mandated refactor
Append a short stable hash of the original `cwd` to the sanitized name (e.g. `-home-doll-OpenClaudia-d41d8cd98f00b204` using a 16-char hex of `blake3(cwd)`). This preserves human-readability AND uniqueness. Cap the prefix component at 200 bytes so the hash-suffixed total stays under filesystem limits. Add a regression test for the collision case (`/foo/bar` vs `/foo-bar`) and the long-path case.
## Filed from QA review dispatch

ff030de1-65fd-45d9-8461-c4c5e79b2e64.title: SQLi: public execute_raw() on MemoryDb accepts arbitrary SQL string
ff030de1-65fd-45d9-8461-c4c5e79b2e64.description:
Current state: 

Desired state: 

Reason: 

Dimension: Security and Access (5) / Perimeter Defense (3.4)

Location: src/memory.rs:158 (pub fn execute_raw(&self, sql: &str))

Violation: MemoryDb exposes a public method that executes ANY SQL string via conn.execute_batch(sql). This is a SQLi bomb waiting to go off. The global rule 'always use parameterized queries' is violated at the API boundary — every future caller is invited to build SQL with format!(). Already happening: src/auto_learn.rs:113-116 uses format!() to interpolate table and max_rows values before calling execute_raw. The current values are hardcoded constants, so not exploitable today, but the pattern normalizes string-built SQL and trains the next developer to do the same with user input.

Mandated Refactor:
1. Make execute_raw pub(crate) at minimum; ideally delete it and expose only typed methods (prune_table(table: TableKind, limit: u32)) using parameterized queries and an enum allowlist of table names.
2. Add a clippy::disallowed_methods lint or a compile-time guard to forbid building SQL with format!() outside migrate_v*_on() helpers.
3. Replace the auto_learn.rs prune loop: since SQLite doesn't allow binding table names, enumerate the tables in match arms, each calling a pre-written parameterized DELETE with a bound LIMIT.

ff144525-a494-49cc-8aef-0f85c74f5172.title: Add token-budget-aware partial compaction (parity with CC microCompact.ts)
ff144525-a494-49cc-8aef-0f85c74f5172.description:
## Goal
Implement microcompact behavior from CC services/compact/microCompact.ts (~530 lines): partial tool-result clearing that avoids a full conversation summarization.

## CC behaviors (microCompact.ts lines 41–529)
- COMPACTABLE_TOOLS set: FileRead, Bash/Shell tools, Grep, Glob, WebSearch, WebFetch, FileEdit, FileWrite
- estimateMessageTokens(): pads roughTokenCount by 4/3 factor for conservatism; handles text, tool_result, tool_use, thinking, redacted_thinking, image/document blocks
- TIME_BASED_MC_CLEARED_MESSAGE sentinel = '[Old tool result content cleared]'
- microcompactMessages(): checks time-based trigger first (cold-cache path), then cached-MC path (ant-only, CACHED_MICROCOMPACT feature), no-ops for external builds
- evaluateTimeBasedTrigger(): fires when gap since last assistant > threshold minutes AND main-thread querySource
- maybeTimeBasedMicrocompact(): content-clears old tool results in-place, keeps last N compactable IDs, logs tengu_time_based_microcompact event, resets microcompact state
- cachedMicrocompactPath(): registers tool results, queues cache_edits API block instead of mutating content, tracks pinnedEdits for re-sending on subsequent calls
- consumePendingCacheEdits() / getPinnedCacheEdits() / pinCacheEdits(): API-layer integration
- resetMicrocompactState(): clears all cached-MC module state + pendingCacheEdits
- MicrocompactResult type: messages + optional compactionInfo.pendingCacheEdits
- IMAGE_MAX_TOKEN_SIZE = 2000 tokens for image/document blocks

## OC counterpart
None. OC has no partial tool-result compaction. context window pressure goes directly to full compaction.

## apiMicrocompact.ts (~153 lines) gap
CC also has server-side context management via getAPIContextManagement(): ContextManagementConfig with clear_tool_uses_20250919 and clear_thinking_20251015 strategies sent as API parameters. OC does not send context_management in requests.

## Parent
#523. Phase 1 spec tracked in #534.
